Description/content.value:
Digital transformation touches almost every area of an organisation. Therefore, students can be employed in a variety of roles after graduation. The programme aims to impart application-oriented knowledge relating to the digital transformation of business processes in conjunction with technical implementation.
Graduates will be able to coordinate digital transformation in companies and act as an interface between IT and other business areas such as production, marketing or purchasing. Specialist knowledge in the areas of information technology, engineering and business management is taught in an application-oriented manner in the context of digitalisation and applied practically by the students.
Companies in Germany currently need more than one hundred thousand employees (according to various studies). The demand for qualified employees in the field of digitalisation is expected to grow exponentially in the coming years, such that in just a few years, more than four times as many positions will need to be filled as there are today. Digitalisation affects all industries and sectors and is one of the central issues of the future. By choosing this degree, you will become a sought-after specialist and be able to pursue the role that best suits you in the future.
Perspectives after Graduation
To remain competitive, global manufacturing companies must meet the challenges of digitalisation. The successful transfer of previous economic and technical processes to digital processes requires the know-how of specialists. The bbw University has developed the Business Engineering in Digital Transformation Master's programme in order to provide companies with future specialists who are well prepared for global competition in the area of digitalisation of business processes. The broad spectrum of the course allows you to specialise in different areas of the company. Students are equipped with skills that are useful in both small and medium-sized enterprises as well as large corporations.
Mechanical Engineering
Automotive Industry
Medical Sector
Automation Technology and Robotics

Description/content.value:
In this three-semester programme, students don't just learn how to communicate science well; they also learn to distinguish good from bad quality research and how to communicate uncertainty and the process of scientific discovery as an honest broker, without under- or overstating scientific findings.
Beyond that, students
learn both strategic and journalistic communication of findings not only from natural sciences, but also from social sciences and humanities;
study and practice traditional communication through text, audio and video, as well as innovative approaches such as data visualisation, virtual reality, or game and exhibition design;
learn to find ways to connect with audiences who are sceptical of the findings of credible science;
learn to make their own communication more reliable, for example by pre-publication fact checking or by addressing biases or conflicts of interest;
understand how to involve their audience through public engagement projects, and explore what communication research has found about which communication strategies are the most effective.
Case studies and international guest speakers will connect what students have learned to the real world and show them the many possible career paths.
In their Master’s thesis in the third semester, students either showcase what they have learned in a larger communication project, or they conduct an academic study to answer a communication research question with practical relevance for working journalists or science communicators.
As a result, the programme prepares graduates for the international science communication job market in areas including the following:
Science journalism
Public relations for companies, non-profits, think tanks or governments
Advertising in areas that use scientific knowledge (for example medical)
Science diplomacy
Exhibition design in places like museums
SciArt (communicating science through art)
Public engagement
Game design

Description/content.value:
As the largest liquid freshwater reservoir on earth, groundwater has both a huge environmental and economic value, and will be an essential resource for adaptation to climate change and reduction of socio-economic vulnerability, particularly in regions where freshwater availability is highly variable and frequently limited.
Several factors foster the need for a more comprehensive and multidisciplinary educational groundwater programme.
First, groundwater is a component of the water cycle interacting with all other components at various temporal and spatial scales.
Second, groundwater systems are largely interdependent with socio-economic development. The presence of important and productive aquifers can boost socio-economic development and alleviate poverty in low-income countries by providing water for public supply and sustainable irrigation, increasing (environmental-friendly) land use efficiency.
On the other hand, the continuous growth of the world population and the socio-economic development of many countries has already caused, and will continue to cause, large impacts on freshwater (including groundwater) systems through uncontrolled exploitation, causing depletion, seawater intrusion, reduction in baseflows in rivers and ecological flows sustaining freshwater ecosystems, or land subsidence.
Third, climate change is foreseen to affect freshwater availability globally, with several hotspots, among which many areas that currently already suffer periods of severe droughts and freshwater scarcity, such as the Mediterranean area of southern Europe and Northern Africa, north-east China, northern and south-western Latin America, large parts of Australia and the western United States, among others.
Fourth, important feedback mechanisms exist between groundwater (and its use), climate and global change, which vary in time and space.
GroundwatCh addresses the current gaps in higher education with regard to the understanding of the complex interactions between groundwater, surface water, climate and global change, and how we should consider these, and can benefit from them, for the implementation of adaptation solutions. Embracing the central theme of Groundwater and Global Change – Impacts and Adaptation, we have linked it to six major thematic fields:
Hydrological flow and ecosystems (A)
Groundwater quality and pollution (B)
Groundwater and climate (C)
IWRM and sustainable development (D)
Water infrastructure (E)​
Monitoring, data and modelling (F)​

Third, climate change is foreseen to affect freshwater availability globally, with several hotspots, among which many areas that currently already suffer periods of severe droughts and freshwater scarcity, such as the Mediterranean area of southern Europe and Northern Africa, north-east China, northern and south-western Latin America, large parts of Australia and the western United States, among others.

Fourth, important feedback mechanisms exist between groundwater (and its use), climate and global change, which vary in time and space.

GroundwatCh addresses the current gaps in higher education with regard to the understanding of the complex interactions between groundwater, surface water, climate and global change, and how we should consider these, and can benefit from them, for the implementation of adaptation solutions. Embracing the central theme of Groundwater and Global Change – Impacts and Adaptation, we have linked it to six major thematic fields:

  • Hydrological flow and ecosystems (A)
  • Groundwater quality and pollution (B)
  • Groundwater and climate (C)
  • IWRM and sustainable development (D)
  • Water infrastructure (E)​
  • Monitoring, data and modelling (F)​

Course organisation.value:
As a GroundwatCh student, you will start the academic year at ULisboa IST in September, where you will start with the QGIS introductory (certified) course during the first semester, followed by the mandatory courses addressing core competences in thematic areas A-D, and elective courses in E-F (see https://www.groundwatermaster.eu/about), totalling (at least) 30 ECTS (as you are free to select more elective courses). In February, still in Portugal, you will take preparatory training in interdisciplinary science and fieldwork to prepare for the interdisciplinary project taking place at IHE Delft in the second semester. At the end of February, you will move to IHE Delft, where you will acquire (at least) 30 ECTS in the second semester, taking mandatory and elective courses within all thematic areas. Among the elective courses, you can opt for an ECTS-credited internship at any of the associated partners (APs). Following conclusion of the second semester at the end of July, you can continue your internship if desired, or have a summer break before moving to TU Dresden mid-September, where you will start your third semester with summer school courses and a thematic seminar. Subsequently, you will obtain training (at least 30 ECTS) in thematic areas A, C and F, through compulsory courses in climate modelling and groundwater-soil-land-climate feedback mechanisms as well as a study project and elective courses that can also cover the other thematic areas.
At the end of the third semester, in March of the second academic year, you will start your thesis study (30 ECTS), optionally together with an AP. You will conduct research under the guidance of a professor from one of the full partner universities, and lecturers or researchers from APs can be your mentors. We aim at a balanced distribution of MSc thesis projects and students amongst the three partner universities. The thesis has to be defended at the university where the student is registered, i.e. the university of the supervising professor, in agreement with local institutional regulations.

Description/content.value:
The international Master’s programme in Medical Physics and Physics of Living Systems at TU Dortmund University offers interdisciplinary training at the intersection of physics, biology and medicine.
Students acquire advanced scientific skills and learn to apply physical principles to biomedical challenges – from diagnostics to biotechnology and health technology.
The programme offers two specialisation tracks:
Track A – Medical Physics:
This track prepares students for a career as a Medical Physics Expert (MPE) in hospitals or for work in the healthcare industry and related research. The track benefits from strong collaborations with clinics and medical research institutions.
Track B – Physics of Living Systems:
This track focuses on applying physics to understand biological systems. Students deepen their knowledge in areas like neuroinformatics, biochemistry, and modern life science methods.
Description/content.html:
The international Master’s programme in Medical Physics and Physics of Living Systems at TU Dortmund University offers interdisciplinary training at the intersection of physics, biology and medicine.

Students acquire advanced scientific skills and learn to apply physical principles to biomedical challenges – from diagnostics to biotechnology and health technology.

The programme offers two specialisation tracks:

  • Track A – Medical Physics:
    This track prepares students for a career as a Medical Physics Expert (MPE) in hospitals or for work in the healthcare industry and related research. The track benefits from strong collaborations with clinics and medical research institutions.

  • Track B – Physics of Living Systems:
    This track focuses on applying physics to understand biological systems. Students deepen their knowledge in areas like neuroinformatics, biochemistry, and modern life science methods.

Course organisation.value:
The programme runs for two years.
In the first three semesters, students will attend courses corresponding to approx. 30 CP (both the first and second semester) and approx. 15 CP (third semester). These courses include synchronisation courses (9 CP), fundamentals (14 CP), specialisation (39 CP) and elective courses (13 CP).
In the third semester, students will start the transition into the research phase and spend approximately half of their time on their research project (research lab) and the other half in courses.
The fourth semester is dedicated to research for the Master's thesis.
Details about the courses offered can be found here.

Description/content.value:
Mathematics and Computer Science is an interdisciplinary Master's programme with an equal share of mathematics and computer science, and it provides the opportunity to combine the two disciplines in seminars and project modules.
Recent developments in both fields show that they are increasingly interrelated. For example, mathematics involving algorithms (optimisation, statistics and data science, scientific and high-performance computing, image processing, etc.) or computer science requiring mathematical background (machine learning, computer vision, process mining, quantum computing, etc.).
The Master's programme is designed for people with a Bachelor's degree in mathematics or computer science, or related fields at the interface. We expect a solid background knowledge in the foundations of both fields, which have to be documented during the application procedure.
We promise cutting-edge training in both fields, individualised learning with 1:1 supervision, an application-oriented focus and excellent career prospects in Germany and abroad. With their mix of mathematical foundations and programming project experience, alumni have all the tools to be pioneers of digital transformation.

Academic admission requirements.value:
Admission is possible for students with a (nearly completed) Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Computer Science and related areas. Applicants undergo an aptitude test.
The application must be accompanied by the following documents:
Curriculum Vitae
Bachelor's or comparable university degree certificate (if the diploma cannot be presented by the application deadline, a transcript of records must be submitted, certifying that the candidate has passed the exams to date)
Documentation of qualification (please follow the instructions in the VIBS portal)
Note that during the application process you will be asked to present evidence of your background knowledge of mathematics and computer science
In this context, you will have to prove that your Bachelor's degree(s) (or other qualifications) encompass either 60 ECTS in Mathematics and 30 ECTS in Computer Science or 30 ECTS in Mathematics and 60 ECTS in Computer Science.
APS certificate for certificates from China, Vietnam and India
For more details please see our FAQ at https://www.uni-augsburg.de/en/fakultaet/mntf/math/studium/studiengaenge/mathe-info-master/#FAQ_MI.

Description/content.value:
The MBA distance learning programme in Innovation Management programme is designed for professionals aiming to drive change and growth in their organisations through systematic innovation strategies. It combines theoretical knowledge with practical methods and tools to empower students to successfully lead innovation processes and develop new business models.
Key focus areas include:
General Management and Business Fundamentals
Innovation Management in Companies: process design, business model innovation, open innovation approaches, frugal innovation, and intellectual property management
Building an Innovation-Oriented Culture: leadership skills, creativity methods, organisational design (New Work), and values-based innovation
Systematic Innovation Methods: TRIZ, design thinking, trend analysis, and other methods for structured idea generation and problem-solving
Digitalisation and Sustainability: integration of digital transformation and sustainable practices as essential drivers of innovation
Case studies and real-world insights: analysis of successful innovative companies and participation in international conferences such as the ISPIM Innovation Conference
This MBA course of study enables students to develop a deep understanding of the role of innovation as a core competitive advantage, equipping them to shape and implement successful innovation strategies across diverse industries.
Students can take advantage of intensive support and develop their know-how in the environment of a cooperative working atmosphere.
Description/content.html:
The MBA distance learning programme in Innovation Management programme is designed for professionals aiming to drive change and growth in their organisations through systematic innovation strategies. It combines theoretical knowledge with practical methods and tools to empower students to successfully lead innovation processes and develop new business models.

Key focus areas include:

  • General Management and Business Fundamentals
  • Innovation Management in Companies: process design, business model innovation, open innovation approaches, frugal innovation, and intellectual property management
  • Building an Innovation-Oriented Culture: leadership skills, creativity methods, organisational design (New Work), and values-based innovation
  • Systematic Innovation Methods: TRIZ, design thinking, trend analysis, and other methods for structured idea generation and problem-solving
  • Digitalisation and Sustainability: integration of digital transformation and sustainable practices as essential drivers of innovation
  • Case studies and real-world insights: analysis of successful innovative companies and participation in international conferences such as the ISPIM Innovation Conference

This MBA course of study enables students to develop a deep understanding of the role of innovation as a core competitive advantage, equipping them to shape and implement successful innovation strategies across diverse industries.

Students can take advantage of intensive support and develop their know-how in the environment of a cooperative working atmosphere.

Course organisation.value:
The programme is divided into four semesters:
Semesters 1 & 2: Business fundamentals, including management frameworks, financial and quantitative methods, marketing, communication, and leadership
Semester 3: Specialised modules on innovation management, leadership in innovation-friendly cultures, and systematic innovation methods
Semester 4: Master’s thesis, accompanied by participation in an international seminar and presentation of research outcomes
The structure and teaching methods follow a hybrid and blended learning approach, combining self-study, online/face-to-face teaching on three to four weekends per semester. In small groups, the learning content can be deepened.
Self-directed study with comprehensive learning materials (learning letters) designed for independent and flexible learning
Online courses and digital learning platforms, allowing students to study from anywhere and at their own pace
Intensive use of applied teaching methods such as simulations, group projects, and presentations to prepare students for real-world challenges
The types of assessment are written examinations, seminar papers, project presentations, Master's thesis, and colloquium.
This structure is specifically designed to allow students to continue working alongside their studies, offering maximum flexibility and practice-oriented learning.
You will be supported by a team of professors with practical experience and numerous company contacts, as well as executives and experts in specialist lectures.
With this and the contact to fellow students, you will build up an excellent network. Use this opportunity as a booster for your professional networking and development!

Description/content.value:
The MBA Motorsport Management is a unique distance learning programme designed to provide professionals with advanced knowledge and practical skills in management within the motorsport industry. Participants gain in-depth insights into the structures and processes of international motorsport, covering topics from team and event management to motorsport marketing and logistics.
Key areas of study include:
General Management and Business Fundamentals: business administration, finance, economics, quantitative methods, and strategic marketing to build a strong managerial foundation
Motorsport Organisation and Governance: structures and regulations in motorsport series, team and personnel management, logistics, and track and event operations
Motorsport Marketing and Sponsorship: motorsport-specific marketing strategies, sponsorship and financing, public relations, social media, and brand management
Legal and Regulatory Aspects: understanding the legal frameworks and compliance requirements that shape the global motorsport environment
Practical Motorsport Management Skills: hands-on insights into event planning, team leadership, and operational management through case studies and real-world projects
International Networking and Exposure: participation in international seminars and conferences, such as the FIA Sport Conference, providing valuable industry connections and global perspectives
The programme is delivered via a blended learning approach, combining self-study materials, online modules, and an interactive seminar at the FIA conference. This format enables students to integrate studies with their professional careers.
Students can take advantage of intensive support and develop their know-how in the environment of a cooperative working atmosphere.

Semester 3: Organisation and governance in motorsport, personnel and project management, motorsport logistics, event and track management, Sponsorship, social media, public relations, brand and innovation management, legal frameworks
Semester 4: Students complete a Master's thesis and attend international conferences such as the FIA Sport Conference to enhance their global network and practical exposure

A detailed overview:

  • Semesters 1 & 2: General management modules (economics, quantitative analysis, financial management, and strategic marketing)
  • Semester 3: Organisation and governance in motorsport, personnel and project management, motorsport logistics, event and track management, Sponsorship, social media, public relations, brand and innovation management, legal frameworks
  • Semester 4: Students complete a Master's thesis and attend international conferences such as the FIA Sport Conference to enhance their global network and practical exposure

The structure and teaching methods follow a hybrid and blended learning approach, combining self-study, online/face-to-face teaching on three to four  weekends per semester. In small groups, the learning content can be deepened.

  • Self-directed study with comprehensive learning materials (learning letters) designed for independent and flexible learning
  • Online courses and digital learning platforms, allowing students to study from anywhere and at their own pace
  • Intensive use of applied teaching methods such as simulations, group projects, and presentations to prepare students for real-world challenges
  • The types of assessment are written examinations, seminar papers, project presentations, Master's thesis and colloquium.

This structure is specifically designed for working professionals, providing maximum flexibility while ensuring a high degree of practical relevance and direct application to the motorsport industry.

You will be supported by a team of professors with practical experience and numerous company contacts, as well as executives and experts in specialist lectures.

With this and the contact to fellow students, you will build up an excellent network. Use this opportunity as a booster for your professional networking and development!

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value: International students at Hochschule RheinMain can find part-time work such as student assistant positions, jobs in retail or hospitality through the university's job portal, the Career Hub and the student services. Students from outside the EU or EEA are allowed to work for a maximum of 140 full working days or 280 half days within one calendar year without a separate work permit. Working as a student assistant may allow more flexible arrangements. The Career Hub and the International Career Service RheinMain provide targeted support including job listings, workshops and networking events such as Matching Week. More information is available on the Hochschule RheinMain Career Hub and the Hochschule RheinMain international student website.

Students from outside the EU or EEA are allowed to work for a maximum of 140 full working days or 280 half days within one calendar year without a separate work permit. Working as a student assistant may allow more flexible arrangements. The Career Hub and the International Career Service RheinMain provide targeted support including job listings, workshops and networking events such as Matching Week. More information is available on the Hochschule RheinMain Career Hub and the Hochschule RheinMain international student website.

The Digital Media Manager Master’s degree programme offers you the ideal basis for your dream job in the digital sector. You will learn how to develop (digital) business models and what role the analysis of target groups plays in this. You will learn which media formats are used by whom and how you can identify and develop new business fields. You will further expand the expertise you have acquired in one of the two specialisations – be it in the field of project management in combination with another foreign language to qualify for international projects and negotiations; or in the field of the digital workplace with a clear focus on creating organisational structures and teaching leadership skills.

Description/content.value:
The English-taught study programme BEng Mechatronics and Automation addresses students of all nationalities, offering an ideal opportunity to get to know “technology made in Germany”. The degree programme is additionally offered as a work- integrated variant.
Combining elements from mechanical engineering, electrical engineering and computer science, the programme enables students to enhance technical systems’ performance during their development and production. In addition, they will learn how to bring complex technical systems into operation, to service and optimise them. To round off the training, strong project management skills and successful teamwork, also in international teams, are imparted.
As the programme is taught in English, intercultural aspects are embedded into its contents and students from different cultural backgrounds work together, students are enabled to work in international company projects in an increasingly globalised world. In addition, the English-language programme is intended to prepare international students for the German labour market and to facilitate their access to it.
Students enrolled in the work-integrated study programme are employed by a company at the same time. This is what sets the work-integrated programme apart. Students receive financial remuneration for their employment in the company. The work experience that is integrated into the programme is beneficial for both the student and the company, providing a solid foundation for a possible permanent position in the company after obtaining the Bachelor’s degree.
Starting in the (non-work-integrated) degree programme and switching to the work-integrated version later on is possible, as the courses of study are largely identical.
Please find further information on the BEng Mechatronics and Automation (work-integrated) on our website. Instructions on how to apply for the work-integrated degree programme can be found here.
For information on the regular study programme BEng Mechatronics and Automation (without a company), please check this website. Please find instructions on how to apply for the regular degree programme here.

Description/content.value:
Shaping Secure Systems for a Connected World
The English-taught Master's programme in Sociotechnical Cybersecurity at the Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt (THI, Technical University of Applied Sciences) prepares you specifically for a career in one of the most important future fields of our time: the protection of complex technical systems from attacks.
Interdisciplinary. International. Impact-oriented.
Cybersecurity has long been more than just technology – it affects people, organisations, and entire societies. Our programme combines technical excellence with a solid understanding of social science. You will learn how to prevent attacks on systems, how to develop security architectures, and how human behaviour, management structures, and cultural factors influence security.
Technical depth meets industry focus
Unlike general cybersecurity programmes, this Master's programme provides domain-specific security expertise in the three key sectors of mobility, industry, and healthcare.
For the cybersecurity of tomorrow
We train you today for the cybersecurity of tomorrow. You will explore technologies that will shape the future – such as post-quantum cryptography, quantum key distribution, and AI-based security mechanisms. Additionally, you will acquire scientific and analytical skills applicable to both research and industry.
Personal. Practical. Future-proof.
We actively encourage your involvement in the cybersecurity community through international projects, participation in competitions, and practical research. Thanks to small groups and individual support, you will develop into a professional who understands technology, people, and organisations equally – and can thus shape cybersecurity holistically.
Learning in a high-tech environment
You will study in one of Germany's leading mobility and technology regions in direct contact with partners such as Audi, Airbus, MBDA, and numerous innovative start-ups. THI offers an ideal learning environment with modern laboratories and innovative teaching methods.

Costs of living.value:
In addition to tuition fees, students face the following fixed monthly living costs:
- Health insurance: approx. 150 EUR
- Liability insurance: approx. 10 EUR
- Accommodation: approx. 500 to 650 EUR
- Internet and mobile phone: approx. 25 EUR
- Food: approx. 200 to 300 EUR
- German TV/radio fee: approx. 19 EUR
- Public transport (Deutschlandticket 2026): approx. 43 EUR
Beyond these fixed costs, additional expenses will vary depending on individual needs, such as travel to visit family or participation in leisure activities.
Additionally, don’t forget potential unforeseen costs, such as the need for a new laptop or mobile phone, etc.
Usually, non-EU students are required to provide proof of sufficient financial means with a blocked account for visa purposes. It should contain approx. 992 EUR per month for up to 12 months.

Description of the above-mentioned fundi.value:
There are different scholarship opportunities for enrolled students in Germany. However, it is very important to understand that scholarships are highly competitive, limited in number, and never guaranteed. Students must ensure they can finance their studies independently and should not rely on receiving a scholarship. Most programmes focus on excellent academic performance, personal engagement, or specific qualifications; financial need is often not the main criterion. Some national scholarships also require German language skills (often B2 level).
THI offers its own scholarship opportunities for international students once a year, announced through the university’s communication channels. Deutschlandstipendium, for example, supports high-performing, committed students regardless of their financial situation.
Also, there are several major national foundations with extensive selection processes for which the university provides guidance and support.

Academic admission requirements.value:
A Bachelor's degree in computer science or a Bachelor's degree with a high proportion of computer science (e.g. Bachelor's degree in artificial intelligence, Bachelor's degree in cyber security, Bachelor's degree in business informatics, Bachelor's degree in aviation and vehicle informatics, etc.) with 180 ECTS credits is required. For details, please refer to the statutes of the programme.
The programme is conducted in English. A language level of B2 (official European reference framework) is required.
By the end of the first semester, students must provide evidence of basic knowledge of German Level A1.
To apply, you must have taken the SAT (Scholastic Assessment Test) and provide the SAT score.
The Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt can only make a legally binding decision about your eligibility for your desired study programme after reviewing the documents you submit with your application. We can’t provide a definitive assessment or evaluate your chances of acceptance until we have your full application, including your educational history.
Furthermore, it is possible to find out if you’re qualified to study in Germany before applying. Detailed information is available at the following link: www.uni-assist.de/en/tools/check-university-admission.
Additionally, you can find out about the qualification requirements via the study and examination regulations (in German: Studien- und Prüfungsordnung = SPO). Find these on the following page under the respective statutes: https://www.thi.de/en/university/university-profile/university-management/legal-department/.
Thank you for your understanding. You are very welcome to apply, and we will check your application documents.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
Whether you can work alongside your studies depends on several factors. At the beginning, it is advisable to focus on your studies and adjust to a new academic and cultural environment. Studying abroad can be challenging due to different learning cultures and the need to catch up on course content.
International students are required to take part in a programme preparing them for the German labour market.
A good command of German at least B2 level is essential for employment opportunities. Students are therefore encouraged to invest time in learning German.
After the first year, students may consider taking on a part-time job. Specialist skills are required to work as a student trainee.
Furthermore, non-EU citizens only have a limited work permit in Germany (see Study and work).

Description/content.value:
MSc COSIB - a continuing education / advanced Master’s programme for international IT talents and career changers with a focus on the German labour market
COSIB programme and module structure
Computer science is a dynamic and continuously evolving discipline. Professionals in this field constantly develop their technical and methodological skills – lifelong learning is therefore a central element of professional practice. In this context, the MSc COSIB has been designed.
The programme is aimed at both aspiring and experienced international IT professionals who are either already active in the German labour market or specifically seeking to enter it. It offers a compact, structured, academically grounded opportunity to further develop existing knowledge and/or acquire new specialist competencies.
For international career changers into IT
You have completed a degree in a STEM field, already gained practical IT experience, and now wish to establish yourself in the IT industry in Germany through a structured academic pathway and a recognised academic qualification.
The MSc COSIB provides you with solid foundations in computer science as well as a deeper understanding of selected specialist areas and supports you in qualifying as an IT professional for the German labour market.
For international IT professionals outside Germany
You already hold a degree in computer science or a closely related field and have gained professional IT experience. You now wish to strengthen your qualifications through a specialised Master’s degree and prepare for a role in the German labour market or advance your career there.
The MSc COSIB offers an academically grounded specialisation that provides competencies applicable across different contexts of IT practice and employability-oriented elements. This allows you to sharpen your professional profile and systematically prepare for your next career step in the German labour market.
For international IT professionals in Germany
You are already working as an IT expert in Germany and would like to expand your knowledge, explore new subject areas, or integrate current research trends into your professional practice.
The MSc COSIB enables academic specialisation and supports you in further developing your expertise within your professional and disciplinary context.
Regardless of individual background, the MSc COSIB is aimed at international IT talent and career changers who wish to build or advance their careers in Germany.

Course organisation.html:
The MSc COSIB is a compact one-year Master's programme that combines basic and/or advanced study in computer science with integrated practical elements. It is designed for students seeking to broaden or complement their academic background while preparing for careers in the German IT sector.

Upon successful completion, graduates are awarded a fully accredited Master of Science degree from the University of Konstanz, recognised both nationally and internationally.

COSIB in brief:

  • Degree options: 
    Master of Science (60 ECTS)
    Diploma of advanced studies (30 ECTS)
  • Standard period of study: 
    Two semesters
  • Form of study: 
    First semester: full-time on-campus study
    Second semester: flexible practical period
  • Practical elements:
    Eight-week professional or research internship, 
  • Special programme features: 
    Data Science profile or individual specialisation e.g. AI
    Alumni mentoring/talks
    Micro-degree certification option (DoAS)

Programme structure: 
In two semesters, students of the MSc COSIB complete 60 ECTS credits:

First semester (30-33 ECTS):

  • Introductory (basic) modules in computer science (0-12 ECTS) and/or specialised in-depth modules (18-30 ECTS)
  • KEY module on labour market orientation/integration (0-3 ECTS)

Students develop either an in-depth understanding of the basic principles of computer science, including the theoretical and practical aspects of algorithms, data structures and programming languages. They learn how to design, analyse and implement efficient algorithms.

Additionally, they have set their own specialisations depending on their previous knowledge and individual interests, such as AI, and choose from pre-defined profiles, such as Data Science.

Second semester (27-30 ECTS)

  • Eight-week professional or research internship (8 ECTS)
  • KEY module on labour market orientation/integration (3-6 ECTS)
  • Thesis and colloquium (16 ECTS)

Students of the MSc COSIB have the opportunity to specialise in Data Science, which can be studied in both the summer and winter semesters.

Integrated internships.value:
The MSc COSIB is a career-oriented degree programme designed to equip students with the advanced skills required to succeed as qualified IT specialists. A key component of the programme is a compulsory internship of at least eight weeks in the second semester, giving students valuable hands-on experience in a company related to their field of study.
Students who are already employed may complete this internship within their current company, provided their work is clearly relevant to computer science.
To further support career development, the department actively connects students with regional companies by offering a range of networking opportunities, including alumni talks, matchmaking events, and mentoring programmes.
Students interested in pursuing an academic career or deepening their expertise in a specific area also have the option to complete a research internship within the department, working closely with one of its research groups.
The Department of Computer Science works closely with the Career Service at the University of Konstanz and the IT-competence network cyberLAGO and other company networks for this purpose.
Ideally, the compulsory internship serves already as an entry point into the German IT job market. Subject to relevance to the field of study and academic approval, the Master’s thesis may also be completed in cooperation with a company.

Academic admission requirements.value:
Our admission committee decides on the basis of the application documents, using defined mandatory criteria and a points system, on the eligibility for the Master's programme in Computer Science for Industry and Business.
Eligibility is granted if all mandatory criteria are met and additionally, at least 20 out of 35 points are achieved in the points system.
In a first formal selection step, mandatory criteria such as a relevant degree, the final grade, proof of relevant prior knowledge in the field of computer science and mathematics, proof of at least one year of relevant professional experience, and sufficient English language skills are evaluated.
If all mandatory criteria are met, points are awarded for the final grade, additional subject-specific knowledge, professional experience, and the study project.
Be sure to familiarise yourself with the admission criteria and language requirements; they are listed in full on this website.

Accommodation.value:
At the University of Konstanz, international students have access to a variety of accommodation options, including student residence halls, shared flats (WGs), and private apartments. Because housing in Konstanz is limited and demand is high, early application and preparation are strongly recommended.
A major provider of student accommodation is Seezeit Studierendenwerk Bodensee, which offers rooms in multiple residence halls across the city. These rooms are usually furnished and available either as single rooms in shared flats or as small studio-style units. In shared flats, students typically have their own private bedroom while sharing kitchen and bathroom facilities with two to six other students, creating a community-oriented living environment. (uni-konstanz.de)
Residence halls vary in size and structure, ranging from smaller shared apartments to larger housing complexes. This allows students to choose between more social living arrangements or quieter, more independent settings depending on availability and preference. (seezeit.com)

Accommodation.html:
At the University of Konstanz, international students have access to a variety of accommodation options, including student residence halls, shared flats (WGs), and private apartments. Because housing in Konstanz is limited and demand is high, early application and preparation are strongly recommended.

A major provider of student accommodation is Seezeit Studierendenwerk Bodensee, which offers rooms in multiple residence halls across the city. These rooms are usually furnished and available either as single rooms in shared flats or as small studio-style units. In shared flats, students typically have their own private bedroom while sharing kitchen and bathroom facilities with two to six other students, creating a community-oriented living environment. Career advisory services and programmes.value:
The MSc COSIB at the University of Konstanz offers a range of employability support services that are closely integrated into the curriculum and designed to prepare students for the IT job market.
A central feature of the programme is its strong focus on labour market integration. Students complete a compulsory, subject-related internship of at least eight weeks, which can serve as a direct entry point into employment in Germany. The department actively supports this process by facilitating contacts with regional companies and organising networking formats such as alumni talks, mentoring programmes, and matchmaking events.
In addition, the MSc COSIB includes structured modules on “labour market orientation and integration,” ensuring that career preparation is an explicit part of the academic programme. Students also benefit from broader university-wide career services.

Description/content.value:
The four-semester Master's programme in Photonics provides in-depth knowledge and skills in photonics and related fields in an integrated form. Photonics is an interdisciplinary field of technology that aims to utilise light in science and technology, with a focus on the quantum nature of light (photons).
Areas of application include information and communication technology, laser material processing, medical technology, the semiconductor industry, life sciences, measurement and sensor technology, quantum technologies, artificial intelligence, aerospace, the automotive industry, mechanical and equipment engineering, and lighting and display systems.
The curriculum is divided into five different areas, each consisting of a different number of modules:
Mathematical and Scientific Fundamentals consists of four modules (Structure of Matter, Mathematical Methods, Theoretical Principles of Photonics I and II).
Engineering Fundamentals consists of five modules (Measurement Technology and Instrumentation, Microtechnologies, Technical Optics I, Laser Technology, and Optical Measurement and Analysis Methods).
Subject-specific Specialisation consists of three modules (Technical Optics II, Laser Material Processing, Applied Photonics).
Profile Development consists largely of currently six elective modules (choices include Optical Simulation in Practice, Bio- and Environmental Photonics, Optics and Photonics on Large Equipment, Ophthalmic Optics, Optical Communication Technology, Applied Quantum Optics, Modelling of Optical Systems, Optical Fibres, Semiconductor Detectors, research and development projects).
Interdisciplinary Content consists of one module, as business and economics subjects have been combined into a single “Management” module.
The programme can be completed entirely in English. It is thus a perfect choice for international students who are interested in studying and possibly working in Germany or Europe. It is also ideal for German or European students who are preparing for an international career in the fields of information and communication technology, optoelectronics, materials processing, manufacturing technology, device technology, measurement technology, semiconductor industry, printing technologies, biotechnology and medical technology, environmental, sensor and microsystems technology, aerospace technology, or the automotive industry.

Academic admission requirements.value:
The admission requirement is a first professionally qualifying university degree worth at least 180 credit points (CP) in accordance with the European Credit Transfer System (ECTS), which must demonstrate a subject-related focus. The aforementioned admission requirement is deemed to be fulfilled for accredited degree programmes in:
Physical Technologies/Energy Systems
Biosystems Engineering/Bioinformatics
Automation Technology
at the Technical University of Applied Sciences Wildau (TH Wildau);
Optometry/Optical Device Technology at the Technical University of Applied Sciences Brandenburg (TH Brandenburg)
Laser Science and Photonics at the Berlin Technical University of Applied Sciences (BHT Berlin)
A Bachelor's degree in related subjects is also welcome. In these cases, the degree programme director will decide on admission.
Graduates of degree programmes with a different focus must provide evidence of course content that is comparable to degree programmes in a related field. This evidence is provided if courses or modules in an adequate form and scope with at least 25 CP in the following subject areas have been successfully completed:
Mathematics
Physics
Optics
Electrical Engineering
Computer Science
These CP must be composed of at least three of the mentioned subject areas. In cases of doubt, the degree programme director will decide on admission.

Description/content.value:
Transform the future of medical informatics – join the English-taught Master's in Medical Informatics at Dortmund University of Applied Sciences and Arts (Fachhochschule Dortmund) together with University Medicine Essen (University of Duisburg-Essen). Study in a very friendly, international environment, with projects turning cutting-edge knowledge into practical experience in the dynamically growing healthcare and high-tech industries of the German Ruhr Valley region.
The Master's in Medical Informatics delivers the competencies to shape the digital revolution in medicine. With the Master’s programme, we focus on the integration of digital solutions in healthcare – especially software & information technologies. We are exploring the relevant artificial intelligence models, cybersecurity and socio-economic impact as well. Our graduates are trained to work in very dynamic, diverse, and agile international teams aiming for solutions that benefit patients and society.
The three pillars of the Master's in Medical Informatics competence model are as follows:
Medical informatics modules covering the relevant processes, methods and tools for developing complex software solutions in healthcare
Research-oriented work in projects of the participating universities
A strong focus on project-oriented, user-centred development processes
Our students have key advantages by studying Medical Informatics at Fachhochschule Dortmund:
Wide research and job opportunities are available for our students and many career opportunities are open to our graduates in German and international companies, e.g. in the companies and hospitals of Ruhr Valley region.
Culturally diverse international teams and class experience
Interactive learning methods
Strong interrelation with DFG funded RTG WisPerMed
International events and conferences as well as a semester abroad exchange programmes
Research opportunities in our medical informatics groups and at University Medicine Essen
Hands-on experience with practical approaches
International networking
For more information on the Master's in Medical Informatics programme, please visit https://www.fh-dortmund.de/studiengaenge/medical-informatics-master.php?loc=en or contact us directly.

Course organisation.value:
The international Master's in Medical Informatics programme is taught in four semesters, including the Master's thesis. The programme has a workload of 3,600 hours and 120 credit points (ECTS).
The first two semesters consist of five modules each. In the second and third semesters, students may study their chosen specialisation. The programme finishes with a Master's thesis.
Master's thesis topics comprise clinical research projects or development/research questions in the healthcare domain. All classes and labs as well as course documentation and exams are in English. (Students can use German for written assignments and write their theses in German, too).
Compulsory modules (each module 6 ECTS):
First semester (when starting in winter semester)
3D Computer Vision and Augmented Reality in Medicine
Advanced Methods in Biomedical Signal and Image Processing
Epidemiology and Applications in Healthcare
Elective 1
Scientific & Transversal Skills 1
Second semester (when starting in winter semester)
Knowledge-Based Systems in Medicine
Advanced Telemedicine Applications and Technologies
Applied Artificial Intelligence in Medicine
Scientific & Transversal Skills 2
Elective 2
Third semester – specialisation and research project
Elective 3
Elective 4
MI team project
Research project (thesis)
Fourth semester
Master's thesis (30 ECTS)
Elective modules (each module 6 ECTS):
Advanced Web Engineering
Machine Learning
Design and Modelling of Complex Software Architectures
Human-Centred Digitalisation
Requirements Engineering
Selected Aspects of Information Security
IT Nets
Distributed and Parallel Systems
Usability Engineering
Formal Methods
Advanced Regression Methods
The didactic model of the programme involves lectures (partly online), practical elements, and scientific components. The practical elements include working with clinical partners and conducting laboratory experiments. These are mostly project-oriented activities carried out in small teams. Elective courses allow specialisation in a topic, such as an application domain or technology. The research project and Master's thesis can be conducted in cooperation with a clinic or company, or as part of a research project at one of the participating universities.

Description/content.value: The Mannheim Master in Finance, Accounting and Taxation programme (MMFACT) combines three areas that are otherwise often taught separately: corporate finance, accounting and taxation. Students not only learn the subject matter in detail, but also how these areas interact and influence strategic decisions. A particular focus is on data analysis and empirical methods, which are indispensable for modern finance and tax issues. The programme thus trains specialists who understand finance from all perspectives and can support companies in making sustainable, well-founded decisions.

Course organisation.value: The programme consists of five main areas: Business Analytics and Economics (24 ECTS credits): The four courses will teach you the fundamentals of data analysis and business economics. CFO Core Competencies (25-35 ECTS credits): This module will provide you with key knowledge of finance, accounting, and taxation. You will acquire precisely the skills that are crucial for a successful career in finance. Finance, Accounting and Taxation (at least 19 ECTS credits): You can customise your profile in accordance with your interests and professional goals. The wide selection of in-depth courses allows you to specialise in your desired area. Complementary Elective (no more than two courses): Broaden your mind and think outside the box. You can take supplementary courses from other areas of business administration or economics. Theses (30 ECTS credits): At the end of your studies, you will complete a research-oriented seminar and write your Master's thesis at one of the participating chairs.

Description/content.value:
Are you searching for the Higgs Boson or Dark Matter? Do you want to tailor materials to your needs? Would you like to cure cancer, study nuclei and their role in the Universe, or look into the heart of matter? Particle accelerators will help you do that.
The “Particle Accelerator Science” MSc study programme is an English-language cooperative programme between Technical University of Darmstadt, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and Goethe University Frankfurt am Main as part of the strategic alliance between the Rhein-Main Universities. In this programme, the next specialist in Particle Accelerator Science is always no more than a one-hour train ride away.
All three partners of the RMU are recognised for their outstanding expertise in the physics and technology of particle accelerators in Germany and beyond. The different areas of research and development at our universities cover a wide technological spectrum and range of applications, from nuclear and particle physics, by way of biology, biophysics, and medical technology, to, e.g. materials research and atomic and quantum, laser and plasma physics.

You will complete the "Practical Introduction to Scientific Research" in the third semester, followed by a Master's thesis in the fourth semester. This gives you the opportunity to work on a research project in the last year of your studies.

Academic admission requirements.html:
Admission to the Master's programme requires the following knowledge for successful study, which can usually be acquired in degree programmes in the natural sciences or engineering with a Bachelor of Science degree.

The following mandatory entry requirements must be demonstrated for admission; they cannot be demonstrated by means of conditions (§ 17a (8) APB), i.e. it is not possible to start the programme without demonstrating these mandatory entry requirements:

  • Selecting suitable physical methods for working on tasks from current research and development in particle accelerators, developing conceptual solutions and implementing them in practice, as well as familiarising oneself with new physical methods;
  • Confident use of the definitions of electric and magnetic fields in electrostatics, magnetostatics and quasi-static electrodynamics; recognising the connection between electricity and magnetism;
  • Identifying, classifying and critically analysing questions from the constituent subjects of accelerator physics and technology, i.e. physics, electrical engineering, information technology and materials science;
  • Confident use of mathematical methods of linear algebra and analysis (including vector analysis) to solve problems and tasks in accelerator science;
  • Fundamental practical knowledge of experimental measurement technology.

Accordingly, compulsory entry-level competencies in the following areas and with the following CP must be proven:

  • at least 20 CP in mathematics and
  • at least 5 CP in the fundamentals of physics and
  • at least 5 CP in theoretical electrodynamics, and
  • at least 4 CP in measurement technology or natural science laboratory practicals.

The CP values are based on the standard credit points system.

Accommodation.value:
TU Darmstadt's International Affairs Department assists international students in their search for accommodation through its Housing Assistance Office. A major science hub, Darmstadt is home to multiple research institutions, three universities, and many high-technology companies, all of which attract people from around the world. A wide variety of accommodations that vary in size, furnishing, and rent are available in Darmstadt and its vicinity. As the university does not own or manage student housing, we support students in finding housing in private and public student dormitories or on the private market. In order to improve your chances in finding the optimal place to live, we recommend that you start your search early. We are happy to assist you in this process. Please make sure to register online on the housing assistance website for international students.
Our services include the distribution of an “Accommodation Guide” that includes links to private and public student dormitories, hotels and youth hostels, and a “Housing Guide” that provides tips on how to search for accommodation in Darmstadt.

Description/content.value:
The Master's degree programme is application-oriented and imparts knowledge in the field of innovative development capabilities with respect to the complete life cycle of battery systems.
It equips graduates with the skills to apply their knowledge on known and new problems and to independently acquire new knowledge and skills in the future. The goal is to acquire expert knowledge and to differentiate existing academic results as well as to identify practical problems and to have the ability to solve them. The students acquire the skills to judge scientific findings and to apply them in practice and do practical research themselves.

Course organisation.value:

Part of the course takes place at the partner institution Kiel University (CAU) and at the Fraunhofer ISIT in Itzehoe. The programme can also be pursued alongside employment, which allows for an individual study plan regarding module attendance and examinations and may result in an extension of the total study duration.

Academic admission requirements.value:
(1) Admission to the Master’s programme “Battery Technologies” is granted to applicants who have completed a Bachelor’s degree in a) Electrical Engineering, b) Mechatronics, or c) Industrial Engineering – Electrical Engineering with a minimum grade of 2.99 (German grading scale).
(2) Admission is also possible for applicants who have completed a first professionally qualifying degree in a closely related field with a minimum grade of 2.99. Closely related programmes are those comprising at least 120 credit points (CP) in fundamental core competencies in mathematics, physics, control engineering, electronics, computer science, digital technology, project management, materials science, low-level programming (e.g. in microcontroller technology, software development for engineering applications I, cyber-physical systems, automation technology, computer-aided tools, or similar areas).
(3) If the previous Bachelor's degree comprises fewer than 210 CP but at least 180 CP, the missing competencies must be acquired subsequently. As a rule, a total of 300 CP should be achieved. The required competencies and the latest possible date for their completion will be communicated in writing to the students by the Examination Board after enrolment at the beginning of the programme. In all other respects, § 7 paragraph 7 no. 9 PVO applies.
Remark: Bachelor's degrees obtained outside the European Higher Education Area (EHEA) are often assessed as equivalent to 180 CP.
(4) Applicants holding a Bachelor’s degree obtained outside the Bologna area (i.e., outside the European Higher Education Area) must additionally provide the following qualification proof: GRE test result with a minimum percentile of 64% in the Quantitative Reasoning section. No exceptions can be made.
(5) Language requirements: see below
(6) Application via uni-assist is also required if the applicant has additionally obtained a Master's degree from an institution within the EHEA. Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit all relevant documents as these may help compensate for competencies missing from the Bachelor's degree.

Description/content.value:
The Master’s programme in Social Work Research focuses on developing research-based and analytical competencies for work in academia and research institutions. Students gain a deep understanding of the theoretical foundations, empirical methods, and ethical principles that shape modern social work research.
The curriculum combines project-based learning with a strong emphasis on empirical research design, data collection and analysis, and theoretical reflection. Throughout the programme, students work in small research groups, engage in interdisciplinary discussions, and participate in ongoing research projects within the university or partner institutions.
Key areas of study include:
Theories and methods of social work research
Quantitative and qualitative empirical research
Research ethics and academic integrity
Project management and teamwork in research settings
Academic writing, presentation, and publication skills
Preparation for teaching and self-administration in academia
Students benefit from close supervision and a collaborative learning environment. Those interested in pursuing a PhD may opt for the Doctoral Track, which allows them to start their doctoral studies while completing the Master’s degree.

The Master’s programme in Social Work Research focuses on developing research-based and analytical competencies for work in academia and research institutions. Students gain a deep understanding of the theoretical foundations, empirical methods, and ethical principles that shape modern social work research.

The curriculum combines project-based learning with a strong emphasis on empirical research design, data collection and analysis, and theoretical reflection. Throughout the programme, students work in small research groups, engage in interdisciplinary discussions, and participate in ongoing research projects within the university or partner institutions.

Key areas of study include:

  • Theories and methods of social work research
  • Quantitative and qualitative empirical research
  • Research ethics and academic integrity
  • Project management and teamwork in research settings
  • Academic writing, presentation, and publication skills

Students benefit from close supervision and a collaborative learning environment. Those interested in pursuing a PhD may opt for the Doctoral Track, which allows them to start their doctoral studies while completing the Master’s degree.

Course organisation.value:
The Master’s programme in Social Work Research is structured to gradually introduce students to academic research in social work through a systematic, step-by-step approach. The curriculum combines theory, empirical research, and practical academic experience across four semesters.
First semester: Students begin with the Master’s Forum, where they learn to critically review and evaluate current research in the field. The semester also includes comprehensive training in both qualitative and quantitative research methods as well as participation in a collaborative research project on a socially relevant topic. Working together with partners from the field, students conduct real-world research that generates practical and socially meaningful outcomes.
Second semester: The focus shifts to academic practice. Students complete a university-based research internship, gaining insight into the daily work of academic institutions. A complementary module on research ethics and academic reflection deepens their understanding of responsible research and academic integrity.
Third semester: Students are introduced to university teaching in social work and apply their methodological knowledge to the analysis of current discourses, practices, and diagnoses in social work studies. A dedicated module on science communication equips them with the skills to present research findings effectively and highlight their social relevance.
Fourth semester: The final semester is dedicated to independent research and writing of the Master’s thesis, allowing students to demonstrate their ability to plan, conduct, and present a substantial academic research project.

Description/content.value:
The Individual Research Master at Leuphana University allows students to design their own personalised, research-oriented curriculum. At the core of the programme is an individually developed research project that students pursue throughout their studies under close guidance from an academic mentor. Students select courses from different disciplines to build an interdisciplinary profile that supports their research focus.
The programme places strong emphasis on developing advanced academic skills, including research design, methodological competence, and scientific reflection. It encourages students to engage in independent scholarly work, ranging from empirical studies to theoretical investigations.
International experiences such as research stays or study periods abroad are integrated into the programme and can significantly enrich the student’s individual research trajectory.

Course organisation.value:
The Individual Research Master is structured around a flexible and highly personalised study plan that students design in close collaboration with an academic mentor. Instead of following a fixed sequence of modules, students assemble an individual curriculum from courses offered across the university that best support their chosen research project.
Throughout the programme, students work continuously on developing, refining, and conducting their independent research, supported by methodological and theoretical coursework. Research forums and mentoring meetings provide an academic framework, ensuring coherence and progress in the individual study path.
International components such as research stays, summer schools, or study periods abroad can be integrated at any point where they meaningfully advance the research project.
The programme culminates in the Master's thesis, which synthesises the research developed over the entire course of study.

Description/content.value:
The programme is aimed at alumnus/alumna of Bachelor's degree programmes in engineering or geosciences who wish to deepen their knowledge of renewable energy systems and pursue an international career in the energy industry or research.
Through practical project work, laboratory exercises, and research collaborations – in particular with the Fraunhofer Institute for Energy Infrastructure and Geothermal Energy (IEG) – students acquire application-oriented skills that prepare them specifically for the challenges of the global energy market.
In the Master's degree programme in Geothermal Energy Systems, you will deepen your knowledge of the scientific, technical, and economic fundamentals of geothermal energy production.
The content focuses on:
Reservoir Engineering & Hydrogeology – Examination of the thermal, hydraulic, and mechanical processes in the reservoir, reservoir evaluation, and optimisation
Drilling and plant technology – Planning and operation of geothermal wells, power plants, heating systems, and heat storage facilities
Geochemistry and geophysics – Analysis of rock and fluid processes, geophysical exploration, and data interpretation
Numerical modelling & simulation – Use of modern tools such as FEFLOW or Modelica for reservoir and system analysis
Energy and environmental policy – Evaluation of the economic, ecological, and regulatory framework conditions of sustainable energy systems
There is a special focus on interdisciplinary project work and the practical application of scientific methods.
Thanks to the international orientation of the degree programme, students also acquire important communication and teamwork skills in intercultural environments.
Description/content.html:
The programme is aimed at alumnus/alumna of Bachelor's degree programmes in engineering or geosciences who wish to deepen their knowledge of renewable energy systems and pursue an international career in the energy industry or research.

Through practical project work, laboratory exercises, and research collaborations – in particular with the Fraunhofer Institute for Energy Infrastructure and Geothermal Energy (IEG) – students acquire application-oriented skills that prepare them specifically for the challenges of the global energy market.

In the Master's degree programme in Geothermal Energy Systems, you will deepen your knowledge of the scientific, technical, and economic fundamentals of geothermal energy production.

The content focuses on:

  • Reservoir Engineering & Hydrogeology – Examination of the thermal, hydraulic, and mechanical processes in the reservoir, reservoir evaluation, and optimisation
  • Drilling and plant technology – Planning and operation of geothermal wells, power plants, heating systems, and heat storage facilities
  • Geochemistry and geophysics – Analysis of rock and fluid processes, geophysical exploration, and data interpretation
  • Numerical modelling & simulation – Use of modern tools such as FEFLOW or Modelica for reservoir and system analysis
  • Energy and environmental policy – Evaluation of the economic, ecological, and regulatory framework conditions of sustainable energy systems

There is a special focus on interdisciplinary project work and the practical application of scientific methods.

Thanks to the international orientation of the degree programme, students also acquire important communication and teamwork skills in intercultural environments.

Academic admission requirements.value:
The prerequisite for admission to the Master's programme in Geothermal Energy Systems is a qualifying degree (Bachelor's or Dipl-Ing degree) from a minimum seven semester (210 credit points) engineering or natural sciences programme with an energy focus, or a minimum seven semester (210 credit points) geosciences programme with a focus on geology, hydrogeology, geophysics, geomechanics, georesources or geothermal energy at a state or state-recognised university with:
an overall grade of 2.5 (up to 2.59) or better
an ECTS grade of B or better, or
an overall grade worse than 2.5 but better than 3.0 (meaning 2.6 to 2.9), if a meaningful assessment of suitability for the Master's programme in Geothermal Energy Systems is submitted. The assessment must have been prepared by a university lecturer who taught the applicant in their first professionally qualifying degree. The examination board decides on the recognition of the assessment and admission to the programme.
Graduates of a Bachelor's programme equivalent to 180 credit points are admitted to the Master's programme with the requirement that they must acquire additional alignment credits (usually 30 credit points) before registering for their Master's thesis.
The decision on the academic comparability of degree programmes is made by the chair of the examination board. The chair of the examination board also determines whether students have to make up for any prerequisites as well as which prerequisites these applicants may have to make up for.

Deep Dives for Specialisation
This Master's degree programme is far more than a specialisation – it is a commitment: to sustainable practice, to children's rights and child protection and to social work that consistently focuses on justice, participation and inclusion. It is for all those who want to act as global citizens and help shape and promote a better future for children and families.
Study track in English or German – the choice is yours! Be part of an international community that brings together local and global aspects of social work.
This consecutive Master's degree programme prepares you to understand challenges for families and children in a globalised world and, with knowledge of international and local social work concepts and approaches, to develop and apply sustainable solution strategies to promote social justice, cohesion and living conditions for children and families. The global sustainability goals and social inequalities must be interpreted and implemented locally from a child- and family-centred perspective and require innovative responses and strategies.
An interdisciplinary view, relevant global sources of knowledge and multilingual student groups enable a sensitisation to international standards, different social, cultural and political contexts and their corresponding complex interactions. Only in this way can children and families be actively involved, a stable basis for long-term commitment and self-responsibility be created and sustainable interventions and equal-opportunity solutions be found.
Please find specific information on our website and in the module handbook.

Description/content.value:
If your enthusiasm for technology and people come together, Sales Engineering is the perfect study programme for you.
Sales Engineering involves selling technically sophisticated products and services – with a deep understanding of technology and a focus on customised customer solutions. Delve into the world of international business to business sales. Learn how digital trends are changing purchasing behaviour and how innovative products are successfully presented worldwide.
Through industry projects, international excursions like to Silicon Valley, and practical work in the Sales and Purchasing Laboratory, you will acquire technical, economic, and sales expertise that will enable you to not only understand international business but also actively shape it. Through elective courses, you can specialise in further areas such as supply chain, materials science, etc.
Unique features
Interdisciplinary blend of technology, sales, digital tools, and AI. Practical application of AI, training and coaching of negotiation techniques in our own Sales and Purchasing Laboratory.
Close collaboration with local and international technology leading companies
Supportive environment, medium class sizes, and approachable lecturers and staff
Opportunities for international study and interdisciplinary projects
Practical internship semester for real-world experience

Course organisation.value: Semesters one through four: In the first four semesters, students study basic and foundation modules in engineering, business economics, sales and marketing as well as language (mathematics, physics, material science, computer science, engineering mechanics, B2B marketing, business administration, personal selling and management, German as a foreign language or technical English, etc.) Semester five: This is a practical semester, during which students complete internships in international industrial companies either in Germany or around the world, where they work independently on projects. Semester six and seven: Within these two semesters, students deepen their knowledge in sales, marketing and technology. A strong emphasis on digitalisation and artificial intelligence ensures that you are well prepared to shape teams, organisations, and processes for the future. Advanced modules are negotiation coaching, digital sales and customer relationship management or AI in B2B sales. Hands-on projects, labs, excursions like to Silicon Valley, and guest lectures connect you to both local and international companies, giving you practical experience and a global perspective. This comprehensive approach makes our graduates highly sought after in the international job market. Through elective courses you can specialise in further areas such as supply chain management, production, procurement, logistics etc. In the seventh semester, students need also to work on the final Bachelor's thesis, which is also mostly done in cooperation with industry. Description/content.value:
The healthcare industry is booming! Developments in the growing healthcare market are immense – as is the associated technological progress. The growing and increasingly technological healthcare market requires highly qualified and well-trained experts, which is exactly where the new Health Technology Management degree course comes in: it teaches medical, scientific, technical and economic expertise. Ready to shape the future of healthcare?
The overarching goal of the Master's programme is to qualify graduates for research- or development-related professional activities at the interface between scientific disciplines in the health sector on the one hand and management on the other. Graduates are prepared to take on leadership roles in health economics and business management.
The Master's programme is broader in scope and more scientifically grounded than a purely subject-specific programme, thus enabling graduates to pursue a wider and more sustainable range of career opportunities. Graduates are equipped with scientific working skills thanks to the challenging projects and case studies carried out during their studies and a corresponding Master's thesis.
Discover what makes studying Health Technology Management at Aalen University so special:
Two semesters in Aalen in a Master's programme taught fully in English
Full flexibility: Write your thesis (six months) at your preferred location
Gain interdisciplinary expertise in health, tech & management
Prepare for leadership roles in healthcare and business sectors
Experience vibrant campus life in a welcoming student city
Live affordably – benefit from low living costs in Aalen
Start working in Germany by effortlessly extending your visa
