Description/content.value:
The Master’s programme in Computational Molecular and Materials Science focuses on modern computational approaches to study and design molecules and materials. Central to the programme are modelling, simulation, and data-driven methods that enable the analysis and prediction of properties at the atomic and molecular scale.
The curriculum combines fundamental concepts from chemistry and physics with advanced techniques in computational chemistry and materials simulation. Students learn to apply quantum mechanical methods, multiscale simulation approaches, and numerical techniques, complemented by tools from data science and machine learning. These methods are used to understand complex systems and to predict their behaviour under different conditions.
A key feature of the programme is its strong application focus. Computational methods are applied to current challenges in areas such as energy conversion and storage, sustainable materials, drug design, and nanotechnology. By integrating theory, simulation, and application, the programme enables students to design and optimise molecules and materials efficiently.
The programme is inherently interdisciplinary, linking chemistry, physics, materials science, and computer science. It prepares graduates for careers in academic research as well as in research-driven industries.

Course organisation.value:
The curriculum of the Master’s programme in Computational Molecular and Materials Science combines a shared academic foundation with opportunities for individual specialisation.
At the beginning, foundational alignment modules (10 ECTS) help to balance different academic backgrounds and establish a common foundation. Building on this, the core modules (30 ECTS) provide essential knowledge in modelling, simulation, scientific computing, and data-driven methods.
These are complemented by practical courses (10 ECTS), where students apply the acquired methods in hands-on settings at an early stage. Within the advanced specialisation area (20 ECTS), students can tailor their profile, for example, in molecular or materials simulation, advanced simulation techniques, or the integration of theory and experiment.
A research project (10 ECTS) enables independent scientific work within a research group. The programme concludes with the Master’s thesis (30 ECTS), typically embedded in ongoing research projects and completed with a presentation.
The Master’s seminar (5 ECTS) provides insights into current research topics and emerging developments in the field. In addition, a free elective module (5 ECTS) from the FAU-wide course catalogue allows for further individual specialisation.

Academic admission requirements.value:
Applicants must hold a Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field from a recognised university.
A Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Molecular Science, or Physics is considered directly relevant. Applicants with closely related degrees may also be eligible if their studies included a strong focus on molecular-based natural sciences (approximately 60% of the curriculum), with coursework in:
Quantum Mechanics (minimum 5 ECTS or an equivalent workload)
Chemistry or Molecular Science (minimum 5 ECTS or an equivalent workload)
Mathematics / Mathematical Methods or Physics (minimum 5 ECTS or an equivalent workload)
Applicants from other natural or engineering science backgrounds may be assessed individually, based on their academic profile and study focus.
Students who have not yet completed their Bachelor’s degree must have completed the equivalent of at least 135 ECTS (approximately 75% of a standard Bachelor’s programme) at the time of application.
Applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency at CEFR level B2 (or equivalent). This requirement is waived if the previous degree was completed entirely in English.
Admission is based on academic performance and subject-specific background. Depending on qualifications and grades, applicants may be invited to an oral interview conducted in English. The interview assesses:
Subject-specific knowledge in chemistry, molecular science, mathematics, physics, and quantum mechanics (50%)
Ability to discuss scientific topics in English (30%)
Motivation and ability to relate prior studies to the Master’s programme (20%)
The final admission decision is made by the programme’s admissions committee.
Applicants whose nationality does not fall under the Lisbon Recognition Convention may be required to meet additional formal criteria. In particular:
The Bachelor’s degree must have been obtained from a university listed as H+ in the anabin database.
Applicants must submit results from a standardised subject-specific test: the GRE (Graduate Record Examination) Subject Test in Physics, with FAU specified as a designated recipient, and a minimum score at the 50th percentile, or the GATE test in Chemistry, reaching a minimum score of 650.

Accommodation.value:
The cities of Erlangen, Fürth, and Nuremberg offer a very good standard of living. They are popular places to live, meaning that accommodation is in high demand but often in short supply. This is particularly the case during the period before the start of a new semester. We therefore recommend that you start looking for accommodation as soon as possible. If you are flexible and also look in the surrounding area, you will have a better chance of finding somewhere affordable to live. The region has an excellent public transport system, so you should not have any problems getting to your place of study or work.
It is worth checking the available accommodation on the Internet every day, as new accommodation becomes available on a day-to-day basis. It pays to be flexible when it comes to the price, location, and available facilities of your accommodation.
Student Services Erlangen-Nürnberg runs its own student accommodation in Erlangen and Nuremberg. You will be informed about how to apply for a room in Student Services accommodation while you are in the process of applying to be admitted to FAU.

Description/content.value:
MULTICOM is the first Master’s degree programme in the data science of human multimodal communication. The programme focuses on the connection between language, thought, and the different modalities of communicative behaviour: gesture, gaze, facial expression, pose, speech articulation, prosody, and more. MULTICOM is an Erasmus Mundus joint degree, co-funded by the European Union and co-awarded by the universities of Murcia (Daedalus Lab) in Spain, Lund (Centre for Languages and Literature) in Sweden, and Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (Big Data Linguistics) in Germany.
MULTICOM integrates humanities, multimodality, data science, and technology. Along with the relevant theories, methods, and statistical and computational techniques, students are trained to combine and influence the key technologies in multimodal data science, such as large language models, body pose detection, automatic speech analysis, eye tracking, motion capture, or articulography. While candidates are expected to have a strong background in language and related disciplines, only basic quantitative skills are required for admission.
Capturing the intricacies of human communication requires integrating complex data into research questions about language, cognition, communication, emotion, social interaction, or culture. But profiles in those areas seldom have the necessary data-science training. They also tend to be unfamiliar with the sophisticated technologies required to analyse video and audio input from communicative exchanges. Moreover, it is quite rare for anyone, from either the sciences or the humanities, to possess language-related training beyond text or the analysis of a single modality, such as speech or gesture.
MULTICOM bridges all three gaps because students are trained in a comprehensive approach to multimodal communication and are required to work in more than one modality, enabling them to engage rigorously with multiple communicative channels. Also, they will receive intensive training in statistics and computing tailored to their needs as multimodal data scientists. Finally, they get hands-on training in all key technologies for the study of multimodal communication, along with the opportunity to influence their development through collaboration with top players across industry and academia.

MULTICOM is the first Master’s degree programme in the data science of human multimodal communication. The programme focuses on the connection between language, thought, and the different modalities of communicative behaviour: gesture, gaze, facial expression, pose, speech articulation, prosody, and more. MULTICOM is an Erasmus Mundus joint degree, co-funded by the European Union and co-awarded by the universities of Murcia (Daedalus Lab) in Spain, Lund (Centre for Languages and Literature) in Sweden, and Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (Big Data Linguistics) in Germany.

MULTICOM integrates humanities, multimodality, data science, and technology. Along with the relevant theories, methods, and statistical and computational techniques, students are trained to combine and influence the key technologies in multimodal data science, such as large language models, body pose detection, automatic speech analysis, eye tracking, motion capture, or articulography. While candidates are expected to have a strong background in language and related disciplines, only basic quantitative skills are required for admission.

Capturing the intricacies of human communication requires integrating complex data into research questions about language, cognition, communication, emotion, social interaction, or culture. But profiles in those areas seldom have the necessary data-science training. They also tend to be unfamiliar with the sophisticated technologies required to analyse video and audio input from communicative exchanges. Moreover, it is quite rare for anyone, from either the sciences or the humanities, to possess language-related training beyond text or the analysis of a single modality, such as speech or gesture.

MULTICOM bridges all three gaps because students are trained in a comprehensive approach to multimodal communication and are required to work in more than one modality, enabling them to engage rigorously with multiple communicative channels. Also, they will receive intensive training in statistics and computing tailored to their needs as multimodal data scientists. Finally, they get hands-on training in all key technologies for the study of multimodal communication, along with the opportunity to influence their development through collaboration with top players across industry and academia.

Course organisation.value:
Semester 1: Introduction to multimodal data science
September to December at the University of Murcia, Spain
Welcome week, inauguration, social programme
Thorough overview of multimodal data science
Intensive training in basic or intermediate quantitative skills
Basic professional skills
Opportunities to pursue key topics in the field, participate in hands-on research, fill in any gaps on language and cognition, or develop further professional and entrepreneurial skills.
Semester 2: The multimodality lab: cognition and learning
January to June at Lund University, Sweden
Welcome week, social programme
Specialised training in laboratory-based methods and on theoretical background for research on multimodality in language, cognition, and learning
Intermediate or advanced training in quantitative skills
Data management, property rights, and ethics
Opportunity to gain further expertise in hands-on experimental research projects, to delve into the connections between multimodality and natural and artificial intelligence, or pursue a key topic in the field
Professional fair
Semester 3: Machine learning and multimodal corpora
September to January at FAU, Erlangen Campus, Germany
Professional project (internship) of at least six weeks between June and October
Specialised training in multimodal corpus linguistics, multimodal language models, and the creation, curation, analysis, and management of large-scale audiovisual data sets
Advanced professional skills
Opportunities to further master key technologies: machine-learning techniques, computer vision, speech analysis, and natural language understanding, or to pursue key topics in the field
Conference at the end of term, co-organised by students and faculty
Semester 4: Research and professional development
January to August at location(s) of choice
Students work on the MA thesis at one or two organisations, beneficiaries or associated partners, chosen by the student and the main supervisor, who must be from one of the three universities. Stays at non-academic partners, as well as professional training related to the thesis research, will be encouraged.
Further professional training for both academic and industry careers
Thesis defence (virtual)
Graduation ceremony
To get more detailed information about the modules taught, please visit https://multicom-em.eu/program/.

Academic admission requirements.value:
1. Leadership, commitment, autonomy and motivation
You should be intrinsically motivated and have a sufficiently mature understanding of what the programme can offer you and of what you can contribute to the MULTICOM community. Through achievements commensurate with your age and career stage, you show leadership, commitment, autonomy, and the ability to thrive in a multidisciplinary and international environment.
2. Language, communication, and thought background
Courses directly related to multimodal communication will be appreciated, but no previous multimodality-related training is required to be considered an excellent candidate, provided that the applicant has an outstanding background in the study of language and thought. Professional experience of demonstrable quality and of specific relevance to the area background will be assessed on an individual basis.
3. Academic/professional excellence
Overall grades and other standard indicators of academic distinction, beyond the specific grades in the relevant areas, should be proven: class valedictorian, top tier of promotion, graduation from prestigious programmes, and similar distinctions, depending on the university system. For candidates with substantial professional experience, indicators of overall quality and distinction include a highly competitive selection process, certified top performance, or any other significant achievements commensurate with their career stage, beyond their experience in relevant areas for multimodal data science.
4. Quantitative background
Excellence in quantitative skills will be rewarded, but training beyond the equivalent of two undergraduate courses will not be considered for applicant selection. While applicants with a stronger quantitative background are encouraged to apply, they should bear in mind that MULTICOM is designed to provide training on multimodality and its related data science to strong profiles in language, communication, and thought.
5. International experience
Although not required, international mobility and intercultural collaboration will be regarded as a factor increasing the likelihood of success in the MULTICOM environment.

Information on the legal conditions relating to part-time jobs for students is available in the brochure "Jobben" (part-time jobs) published by the German National Association for Student Affairs. FAU’s job portal is also updated regularly with new advertisements for part-time jobs.

Accommodation.value:
The cities of Erlangen, Fürth, and Nuremberg offer a very good standard of living. They are popular places to live, meaning that accommodation is in high demand but often in short supply. This is particularly the case during the period before the start of a new semester. We therefore recommend that you start looking for accommodation as soon as possible. If you are flexible and also look in the surrounding area, you will have a better chance of finding somewhere affordable to live. The region has an excellent public transport system, so you should not have any problems getting to your place of study or work.
It is worth checking the available accommodation on the Internet every day, as new accommodation becomes available on a day-to-day basis. It pays to be flexible when it comes to the price, location, and available facilities of your accommodation.
Student Services Erlangen-Nürnberg runs its own student accommodation in Erlangen and Nuremberg. You will be informed about how to apply for a room in Student Services accommodation while you are in the process of applying to be admitted to FAU.

Description/content.value: The Earth System Dynamics and Evolution programme prepares interdisciplinary Earth system scientists with a fundamental understanding of Earth systems, and the interconnectedness between Earth’s spheres across different timescales. Students will gain an understanding of the diverse data sources that represent Earth and life through geological time, alongside strong competencies in modelling and statistics, research design, and project management. In addition, the programme raises awareness of the social and geopolitical dimensions of science, and includes training in science policy and diplomacy. Graduates will be able to reflect critically on the role of science in society, the interface between research and decision-making, and the ethical implications of scientific practices. The programme is funded by the Elite Network of Bavaria.

Description/content.value: Biotechnology at FAU is an engineering degree programme with a focus on industrial and medical biotechnology as well as bioproduct processing. It combines fundamental scientific principles with technical applications. The resulting applications serve the transition from a petroleum-based industry to a bioeconomy and the protection of human health and the environment.
Description/content.html: Biotechnology at FAU is an engineering degree programme with a focus on industrial and medical biotechnology as well as bioproduct processing. It combines fundamental scientific principles with technical applications. The resulting applications serve the transition from a petroleum-based industry to a bioeconomy and the protection of human health and the environment.

Course organisation.value:
The Master's programme in Biotechnology (BT) comprises specialisation, compulsory and elective modules (key skills), a three-week project development course, a twelve-week industrial internship, and a six-month Master's thesis.
Students can choose three specialisations according to their own interests. The following specialisations are available:
Bioprocess engineering
Medical biotechnology
Bioseparation
Mechanical process engineering
Systems biotechnology
Individualised specialisation allows students to choose elective modules from a wide range of current, research-oriented topics. Examples of elective (compulsory) modules are Immune Biotechnology, Food Technology, Pharmaceutical Technology, Biophysics/Biomechanics, Biocompatible Materials and Environmental Bioprocess Engineering.

Clothing: 46 EUR

Description/content.value:
Are you interested in the evolution of organisms? Are you curious about genomics, computational and population biology? Then this Master’s degree programme in evolutionary biology is perfect for you.
This programme will connect you to our expert, globally renowned researchers here at JGU Mainz, and will open doors to thriving careers in international academia, conservation, industry and government. This course of study blends practical laboratory work, theoretical exploration, and advanced computer application to help you develop a wide range of career skills.
Applicants must hold a Bachelor’s degree in biology, molecular biology, mathematics, forensic sciences or bioinformatics. Knowledge of English is essential (including German Abitur of English at level B2). Knowledge of German is not required. Our online interview process ensures alignment with your academic background.
Our programme runs over four semesters and includes hands-on laboratory practicals, cutting-edge computational techniques and lectures, delivered by active researchers in evolutionary biology. In the second semester, you will have the flexibility to specialise your studies, whether you’re focussed on molecular biotic interactions, evolutionary ecology, anthropology or computational and theoretical biology.
Description/content.html:
Are you interested in the evolution of organisms? Are you curious about genomics, computational and population biology? Then this Master’s degree programme in evolutionary biology is perfect for you.

This programme will connect you to our expert, globally renowned researchers here at JGU Mainz, and will open doors to thriving careers in international academia, conservation, industry and government. This course of study blends practical laboratory work, theoretical exploration, and advanced computer application to help you develop a wide range of career skills.

Applicants must hold a Bachelor’s degree in biology, molecular biology, mathematics, forensic sciences or bioinformatics. Knowledge of English is essential (including German Abitur of English at level B2). Knowledge of German is not required. Our online interview process ensures alignment with your academic background.

Our programme runs over four semesters and includes hands-on laboratory practicals, cutting-edge computational techniques and lectures, delivered by active researchers in evolutionary biology. In the second semester, you will have the flexibility to specialise your studies, whether you’re focussed on molecular biotic interactions, evolutionary ecology, anthropology or computational and theoretical biology.

Course organisation.value: The first semester provides a foundation in evolution, ecology and behaviour, evolutionary theory, and population genetics and genomics. From the second semester onwards, students specialise in three areas, including social evolution, species interactions, life history evolution, evolutionary modelling, anthropology, computational biology, molecular genomics, and DNA sequence analysis. Students develop expertise in empirical, experimental and bioinformatic approaches, as well as in theoretical frameworks, through lectures and practical training. The programme also includes elective and soft skill courses in grant writing and publishing, along with field excursions, seminars, and discussions. In the third semester, students acquire the knowledge and methods required for the Master’s thesis, which is completed in the fourth semester with a final oral examination.

Students develop expertise in empirical, experimental and bioinformatic approaches, as well as in theoretical frameworks, through lectures and practical training. Academic admission requirements.value:
Applicants must hold a Bachelor’s degree in biology, another natural science, medicine, mathematics, forensic science, or computer science. They must have completed at least 27 credits in evolutionary biology, biostatistics, or bioinformatics.
Applications are submitted via the Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz portal (JOGU-StINe). For students who got their certificates or degrees abroad, your international school and university certificates have to be recognised during the application period. These applications should thus be submitted about six weeks before the application deadline.
In addition to standard documents, applicants must complete an admission form (“Aufnahmebogen”), which allows assessment of their prior training and eligibility. Candidates who meet the formal requirements are invited to an interview. This interview is not an examination but serves to evaluate qualifications and provide guidance on programme suitability.
Admission decisions are based on a weighted evaluation of the interview and the Bachelor’s grade (ratio 4:6).

Description/content.value:
The Bachelor's degree programme in Applied Natural Sciences is aimed at anyone who is enthusiastic about STEM subjects and is looking for a broad-based, practice-oriented course of study — without having to specialise right from the start.
It combines chemistry and physics with mathematics, electrical engineering and programming, providing a solid, interdisciplinary foundation. On this basis, you will acquire in-depth specialist knowledge that is closely aligned with current, application-oriented issues from research and development.
The programme prepares you specifically for the challenges of modern technologies and innovative fields of work.
From the sixth semester onwards, you will have the opportunity to deepen your individual interests:
By choosing suitable compulsory elective modules, you can specialise in semiconductor and microsystems technology or sensor technology. Alternatively, you can complete your studies without a specialisation and continue with a broad scientific focus.
Description/content.html:
The Bachelor's degree programme in Applied Natural Sciences is aimed at anyone who is enthusiastic about STEM subjects and is looking for a broad-based, practice-oriented course of study — without having to specialise right from the start.

It combines chemistry and physics with mathematics, electrical engineering and programming, providing a solid, interdisciplinary foundation. The programme prepares you specifically for the challenges of modern technologies and innovative fields of work.

Course organisation.value:
The Bachelor's degree programme in Applied Natural Sciences is designed as a full-time programme and comprises a standard duration of study of seven semesters.
Modules in the first year:
Applied natural sciences in practice
Data processing with LabView
Programming
Electrical engineering 1 including practical course
Technical physics 1 and 2
Mathematics 1 and 2
General and inorganic chemistry including practical course
Toxicology
Technical English
In addition to the modules mentioned above, an interdisciplinary module (so-called ZIL module) must be taken.
Modules in the second year:
Technical Physics 3 with practical course
Mathematics 3
Modelling and Simulation with practical course
Physical chemistry
Fundamentals of semiconductor and microsystems technology
Basics of sensor technology
Data Science
Electronic components
Electrical engineering 2 with practical course
Materials science
In addition to the modules mentioned, an interdisciplinary module (known as the ZIL module) is also required.
Fifth semester:
Internship, internship seminar, and practical courses
The internship semester is scheduled for the fifth semester of study. It lasts 20 weeks and offers you the opportunity to apply what you have learned in a company, organisation or institution and gain your first professional experience.
Last academic year:
Students choose a total of nine compulsory elective modules.
In order to choose a specialisation, students must select at least five modules from the field of semiconductor and microsystems technology or sensor technology.
It is also possible to graduate without choosing a specialisation.
Bachelor's thesis
The programme concludes with the Bachelor's thesis, in which a specific scientific question is addressed.

Academic admission requirements.value:
There is no minimum grade requirement.
For admission to OTH Regensburg, international applicants need:
a university entrance qualification
adequate knowledge of German
UNIVERSITY ENTRANCE QUALIFICATION
For an application for a Bachelor’s degree programme at the OTH Regensburg (university of applied sciences) international certificates, transcripts of your educational records and diplomas must first be recognised by uni-assist. Please request a "preliminary review documentation" (in German "Vorprüfungsdokumentation", abbr. VPD). The processing time is four to six weeks, often longer. The VPD must be submitted by the deadline (see "Deadlines" / "Deadline for late submission of certificates"). Submitting the VPD application alone is not sufficient!
Exceptions are applications from the PR China and Vietnam. The recognition is the responsibility of the relevant Academic Evaluation Center. However, if the APS certificate does not show a grade, a VPD is also required. Applicants from India normally require a certificate of the Academic Evaluation Center of India in order to request the VPD from uni-assist.
If you have already attended a preparatory college (Studienkolleg) and have passed the assessment examination (Feststellungsprüfung = FSP), you do not need a VPD from uni-assist any more. Please submit your FSP certificate together with your foreign school-leaving certificate as a university entrance qualification (HZB). If you have a VPD for the Studienkolleg or any other kind of recognition of our school-leaving certificate from abroad, please submit it as well.
If you have an IB Diploma, you do not need to apply for a VPD from uni-assist. Simply upload the diploma as your university entrance qualification.

Description/content.value:
The Master of Engineering in Sustainable Energy (Engineering specialisation) at Europa-Universität Flensburg provides an in-depth, interdisciplinary education in sustainable energy systems and technologies. The programme combines core engineering subjects with a systems perspective on the energy transition, including the integration of renewable energies, energy storage, and grid solutions. Students engage with technical topics such as electrochemical energy technology, power plant systems, wind energy engineering, and energy efficiency, alongside advanced analytical and modelling approaches.
In addition, the curriculum addresses the broader context of energy transitions by incorporating economic, environmental, and policy dimensions, including sustainable and just energy systems. A flexible structure with elective modules allows students to tailor their studies to individual interests and to integrate interdisciplinary perspectives. The programme concludes with an independent research-based Master’s thesis focused on real-world energy challenges.

Description/content.value:
The Master of Engineering in Sustainable Energy (Transition specialisation) at Europa-Universität Flensburg provides an interdisciplinary education focused on the governance, economics, and societal dimensions of energy transitions. The programme combines a systems perspective on sustainable energy with insights from policy, economics, and social sciences.
Students engage with topics such as energy policy and governance, sustainable development, energy economics, and transformation processes, alongside analytical and research methods. The curriculum emphasises the design and implementation of sustainable and just energy systems in different regional and global contexts.
A flexible structure with elective modules allows students to tailor their studies to individual interests and develop interdisciplinary expertise. The programme concludes with an independent research-based Master’s thesis addressing real-world energy transition challenges.

Costs of living.value:
The cost of living in Flensburg is generally slightly lower than in major German cities. A budget of 800 to 1,000 EUR per month should cover the basic cost of living, including rent.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
International students from other countries are allowed to work 140 full days or 280 half days per year. You can find more information about part-time jobs on the DAAD website: https://www.daad.de/en/studying-in-germany/work-career/side-jobs/.
The university offers a wide range of student jobs, which are also open to international students who speak German. The city of Flensburg, being a tourist town, offers lots of part-time job opportunities for people with a good command of the English and German languages. However, it is not as easy to find a student job without German language skills.

Accommodation.value:
The accommodation on campus is administered by a non-profit organisation called the "Studentenwerk". The students must apply directly to them. The link is here: https://studentenwerk.sh/en/dormitories-in-flensburg.
The International Center together with the CampusEngel of Europa-Universität Flensburg, also support and helps students when it comes to finding accommodation.
There are no meal plans, since normally the students have only lunch at the cafeteria. They usually live in shared apartments with a common kitchen. Thus, they prepare breakfast and dinner at home.

Description/content.value:
Sustainability starts with the foundations of our industry — materials and production processes. The English-taught Bachelor’s programme Sustainable Engineering for Materials and Processes (BSc) trains experts who rethink materials and manufacturing: resource-efficient, recyclable, and future-ready.
It provides a broad foundation in natural and engineering sciences: chemistry, physics, mathematics, and computer science form the basis for understanding and optimising materials and processes holistically. From the third semester onward, students choose their focus: those specialising in materials science delve into the analysis and development of sustainable materials — from bio-based alternatives to innovative designs. Students focusing on process engineering explore resource-efficient production, circular economy, sustainable energy and raw material use. Individual specialisation is possible through technical electives, complemented by practical projects and the Bachelor’s thesis, often in cooperation with industry partners.
Thanks to their interdisciplinary expertise, graduates are equipped to drive sustainable innovation and advance the ecological transformation of industry. Thus, they are ideally qualified for entry-level positions in both the industrial sector and public administration, as well as for continuing their academic education in a relevant Master’s programme.
Description/content.html:
Sustainability starts with the foundations of our industry — materials and production processes. The English-taught Bachelor’s programme Sustainable Engineering for Materials and Processes (BSc) trains experts who rethink materials and manufacturing: resource-efficient, recyclable, and future-ready. 

It provides a broad foundation in natural and engineering sciences: chemistry, physics, mathematics, and computer science form the basis for understanding and optimising materials and processes holistically. From the third semester onward, students choose their focus: those specialising in materials science delve into the analysis and development of sustainable materials — from bio-based alternatives to innovative designs. Students focusing on process engineering explore resource-efficient production, circular economy, sustainable energy and raw material use. Individual specialisation is possible through technical electives, complemented by practical projects and the Bachelor’s thesis, often in cooperation with industry partners. 

Thanks to their interdisciplinary expertise, graduates are equipped to drive sustainable innovation and advance the ecological transformation of industry. Thus, they are ideally qualified for entry-level positions in both the industrial sector and public administration, as well as for continuing their academic education in a relevant Master’s programme.

Course organisation.value:
In the first semesters, students build a strong foundation in natural and engineering sciences. Core topics include mathematics, chemistry, physics, materials science and process engineering, providing the essential knowledge required to understand and design sustainable materials and technologies. These fundamentals are complemented by modules on renewable resources, life cycle assessment and sustainable systems, ensuring a holistic perspective from the very beginning of the programme.
From the third semester onwards, students can tailor their studies according to their interests by choosing one of two specialisation tracks: Materials or Processes. The Materials track focuses on the development, characterisation and testing of sustainable and advanced materials, while the Processes track emphasises resource-efficient production technologies, chemical and biotechnological processes, and sustainable energy systems. Both tracks combine theoretical knowledge with laboratory work, projects and practical applications.
A significant portion of the curriculum is dedicated to individual profile building. Through a wide range of technical and general electives, students can deepen their expertise, explore interdisciplinary topics and develop transferable skills. An integrated research internship offers early exposure to scientific research or industrial practice and prepares students for independent project work.
The programme concludes with a Bachelor’s thesis in the sixth semester. Students work independently on a scientific or applied research question in the field of materials or process engineering, often in collaboration with industry or research partners. This final project allows students to consolidate their knowledge, sharpen their specialisation and demonstrate their ability to address complex challenges in sustainable engineering.
Overall, the programme combines a solid scientific foundation with flexibility and practical relevance, enabling students to shape their individual academic profile and prepare for careers in industry, research or further academic studies in sustainability-related fields.

Description/content.value:
Theatre stages have for thousands of years been the home for stories of humans (and other creatures) and their worlds. Theatre and the Performing Arts can permeate the present, the past and the future alike, can build bridges through times, can zoom out or go into close-ups: onto hopes and dreams, enhancing wonders and abysses alike, looking through the surfaces of societies.
Please note: A prerequisite for admission is passing the artistic aptitude test (please see https://eignung.design.fh-dortmund.de/en).
Theatre, as an ever-contemporary art form, has at all times kept a curious and, at the same time, a critical eye on the inventions of new technologies — wondering whether these inventions could be interesting for being incorporated on its stages. Very often, the answer was "yes" (just think of electricity and cameras).
Theatre has always been created by storytellers with different expert knowledge. The Master "Theatre and Digitality" is therefore aimed at students with an either artistic or technical background (or both) — students who are interested in exploring theatrical narratives in context with technologies.
The Master "Theatre and Digitality" is an interdisciplinary, three-semester, English-language study at the Faculty of Design of Fachhochschule Dortmund — University of Applied Sciences and Arts. Graduates will be awarded the Master of Arts degree.
The study is implemented in cooperation of FH Dortmund's Faculty of Design, of the worldwide renowned Academy for Theatre and Digitality and FH Dortmund's Faculty of Computer Science.
Creativity, interdisciplinary expertise and critical thinking: The Master's programme "Theatre and Digitality" includes research and development in the field of digital-technologically supported theatre and performative art. With its curriculum between technology, storytelling, dramaturgy and performance, the study aims to provide students with a broad range of theoretical as well as practical and application-oriented, professionally qualifying skills in the intersection between digital technologies and narratives on analog, virtual and hybrid stages (including topics such as human-machine interfaces or the use of machine learning).

Academic admission requirements.value:
Degree requirements
A diploma or Bachelor's degree in fields such as Design, Architecture, Interior Design, Exhibition Design, Dramaturgy, Acting, Scenography, Object Theatre, Visual Media, Set Design, Performance, Film, Directing, Dance, and Theatre Studies, Applied Computer Science, Machine Learning, Actuators and Robotics, Creative Robotics, Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, Creative Coding, Theatre and Event Technology, Lighting Technology, Sound Technology, Video Technology or a comparable programme at a university that includes scenographic-design or IT-related technical components; or relevant artistic and creative aptitude for the programme.
Language requirement
The MA “Theatre and Digitality” programme is offered in English. Proof of sufficient English skills (C1) has to be provided by the applicants. In exceptional cases, the proof can be provided by an equivalent certificate or document. The respective committee will decide whether there is equivalence.
Artistic aptitude test 
Proof of artistic and creative or technical aptitude is required for enrolment in this Master’s programme. In the assessment procedure, the applicants must prove that they have the artistic-creative or technical aptitude for the course of study, which allows the achievement of the study goals to be expected. The determination of the course-related aptitude is carried out twice a year in a two-level procedure.
The application process for the MA “Theatre and Digitality” has two parallel arches:
1) Registering with the central FH Dortmund application department.  The process there starts with a so called “Self-Registration”.
https://portal.fh-dortmund.de/qisserver/pages/cs/sys/portal/hisinoneStartPage.faces?page=2&sessionlanguage=en
2) Registering with the Design Faculty page for the artistic aptitude examination AND uploading documents.
https://eignung.design.fh-dortmund.de/en

Description/content.value:
Scenography and communication deals with questions such as:
How can I design museum and exhibition spaces across different media?
How can I create narrative qualities in film, theatre and stage spaces?
What potential does the scenography of public spaces offer in terms of shaping social developments?
Which scenographic communication strategies are relevant for the future?
The project studies focus on theatre and stage spaces, museum and exhibition spaces, media and hyper-media spaces, public spaces and temporary spaces for brand staging and corporate communication. You can experiment with individual projects and work in interdisciplinary teams on third-party funded projects.
The three-semester Master's degree programme is offered as a bilingual study programme with a predominantly German-language focus or with a predominantly English-language focus.
Choosing a language track does not result in a division into German- and English-speaking cohorts; it is relevant only for examination purposes.
Courses can be selected regardless of the chosen language focus and are taught bilingually. This means that no one is excluded due to a lack of proficiency in English or German. Because of this mix, most courses are taught in English. All instructors are available in both languages.
The project-oriented course allows you to specialise in the areas of exhibitions, museums, art in public spaces and the stage.
At the same time, you can deepen your knowledge creatively, technically and scientifically at the faculty and in collaborations outside the university. The course offers you the greatest possible freedom. You can implement scenographic projects of your choice in all conceivable fields of creative and artistic spatial and event design.
In the first year of study, you will acquire the necessary knowledge through the modules Experimental Exploration & Design of Scenographic Fields of Work and Scenographic Conceptualisation of Spatial Design and Staging, among others. The second year of study includes the module Project Realisation of a Scenographic Design Project. Learning management skills is also part of the course.
The project-oriented structure leads to numerous collaborations with external funding partners and, as a result, to projects carried out under real-world conditions. Students acquire the necessary competencies through the implementation of projects, not through isolated training in individual aspects of scenography.
The study programme is internationally oriented. Project practice during the course promotes international exchange and contributes to the formation of a worldwide scenographic network.

Course organisation.value:
This is a thematic overview of the course content.
First semester:
01 Scenography + Communication (15 CP)
02 Conception + Design (8 CP)
03 Science (7 CP)
Second semester:
04 Scenography + Communication (15 CP)
05 Conception + Design (8 CP)
06 Science (7 CP)
Third semester:
07 Best practice / foundation (2 CP)
08 Project support for Master's thesis (8 CP)
08 Thesis + Colloquium (20 CP)
The first two semesters of the programme have the same structure and are designed so students can start in either semester. This also doubles the number of project choice options.
In two major design projects (01, 04), which always include a realisation component and very often involve a partnership with an external partner and third-party funder, students go through all phases—including research, analysis, conceptualisation, design, implementation, and documentation—and acquire the necessary skills for each. The projects are often carried out in teams. All students are exposed to all aspects of the process but may also choose to focus on specific areas.
Each of these two modules accounts for half of a semester’s workload.
In two smaller design projects (02, 05), students can adopt a more experimental approach; in module 05, students can also work on independent, self-initiated projects, either individually or in groups.
Two academic courses (03, 06) support the programme by imparting relevant knowledge and enabling students to place their own work in an academic context.
Each of these four modules accounts for a quarter of the semester’s workload.
The third semester is reserved for a final project of the student’s own choosing and a short module designed to prepare students for the transition into the professional world.
With the exception of the last two modules, 08 and 09, all modules can be taken in any order.
A Master’s degree requires 300 credits (BA + MA). For students with a BA degree worth fewer than 210 credits, in addition to the 90 credits from the Master’s programme, there is the option to earn the missing 30 credits by providing proof of relevant internships or professional experience gained after completing the BA degree. Additionally, during this adjustment semester, students have the option to take modules from the Master’s programme in Scenography and Communication or BA courses from any of our BA programmes (Object and Spatial Design, Communication Design, Film and Sound, Photography, and Serious Games).

Description/content.value:
The international, English-language degree programme in Theology / Development Studies complements theological and intercultural competencies with the subject areas of development cooperation and humanitarian aid. The subject focus is approximately two-fifths on development cooperation / humanitarian aid, two-fifths on theology, and approximately one-fifth on interculturality and religious studies. The high practical relevance is emphasised by a compulsory semester abroad as well as an internship semester, which can be carried out in a relevant organisation in Germany or abroad.
The programme equips students with knowledge, skills, and competencies to lead, teach, and respectfully collaborate in teams in their specific field of work. Furthermore, the programme enables students to be self-directed learners and instils an enjoyment of lifelong learning.
The programme is taught in English. If the lecture schedule allows, some courses can also be taken in German. Exams can be taken in German or English, subject to approval by the examiners.

Course organisation.value:
The lower division courses take two years. They teach the basics of Biblical, systematic and intercultural theology as well as development cooperation in 18 courses. All lower division classes conclude with an examination.
The higher division courses, which also take up two years of the programme, include eight compulsory classes and a course catalogue of 18 classes, from which two courses must be completed with an examination. All other courses serve to acquire the required CPs.
A mandatory internship semester (30 CP) takes place in the fifth or sixth semester in a relevant organisation either in Germany or abroad. A semester abroad with the possibility of crediting approx. 24 CPs is also mandatory. Together with the accompanying course "Organising a Study Abroad Semester“ (6 CP), 30 CPs will be achievable during this semester.
Detailed information on the structure and concept of the study programme can be found in the curriculum.

Integrated internships.value:

Description/content.value: The Bachelor's degree programme in "Serious Games & Digital Knowledge" is unique as it takes the fundamental connection of playing and learning seriously — in both digital and non-digital media. Its production-focused approach is interdisciplinary and bilingual (German/English), conjoining expertise from the departments of design, computer science and business studies. Students qualify in all relevant areas of serious game design and development, game-based learning and gamification. Game aesthetics, media theory and pedagogics meet programming and team management with a strong focus on application and team management, using state-of-the-art technologies. Cooperative project work is highly encouraged: within the university's well-equipped workshops, in exchange with students from other design programmes and with external business partners.

Academic admission requirements.value:
This is a short overview. Please make sure to check the details for the required degrees and certificates in your specific case with the International Office:
https://www.fh-dortmund.de/international/international-office/index.php?loc=en
FORMAL QUALIFICATION: You need a degree that qualifies you for a university of applied sciences / arts — preferably with a design-, IT- or education-related focus. Examples include: subject-related entrance qualification, vocational technical diploma, technical / vocational baccalaureate; or higher: GCE A-Levels, upper secondary school leaving certificate, general university entrance qualification. In some cases, an apprenticeship combined with several years of subject-related professional experience will also suffice.
KNOW WHAT YOU'RE GETTING YOURSELF INTO: You need six weeks of practical experience / internship in a subject-related business or institution. Examples of subject-related are design business, software development, publishing, digital media, education, etc. Some school degrees with a subject-related vocational/artistic focus can replace this requirement.
TALENT AND TECHNIQUE: You need to pass a test of your artistic aptitude. It is a combination of your portfolio and two tasks you will receive in February (or along with your first registration). You need to submit all of this by 30 April. We may invite you for an interview afterwards.
Find more details about the programme on our website: https://www.fh-dortmund.de/serious-games?loc=en-US.

Description/content.value:
The work of biomedical engineers centres on addressing medical and biological challenges through the application of technical and engineering principles. The Biomedical Engineering (BMT) Master’s programme is research-oriented. Its primary objective is to provide advanced, interdisciplinary training at the interface of electrical engineering, computer science, and health sciences. This enables graduates to contribute independently and innovatively to research and development in the field of biomedical engineering.
The programme offers a comprehensive and research-focused education covering biomedical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, medicine, psychology, and biology, with particular emphasis on the key research areas of these disciplines.

Description/content.value:
The 21st century is characterised by profound processes of transformation: ecological crises, political conflicts, technological innovations, and more, which are raising fundamental questions of orientation in an increasingly globalised world marked by (religious) pluralism. This is happening at both the personal and the societal levels. The Church and theology are part of these transformation processes. At the same time, theology offers the potential to deal responsibly with transformation processes and the challenges that accompany them.
The new Master’s degree programme addresses this challenge in two ways: On the one hand, the outlined horizon becomes the starting point to get to know Catholic theology in interdisciplinary discourse as a discipline that is relevant to the present context and is itself undergoing change. On the other hand, the transforming world also forms the goal of the programme: Catholic theology is explored as a (self-)critical science that, based on its self-image, influences social discourse and can contribute to the humane shaping of society and the world.

Academic admission requirements.value:
The Master’s programme "Theology for a World in Transformation" is addressed to all Bachelor’s graduates who are interested in critically reflecting on a changing world from a theological perspective. It does not formally require prior studies in theology or religious studies. To pursue the programme with both enjoyment and success, applicants should be motivated to engage with this perspective and demonstrate a fundamental openness to theological thinking. Helpful — though not required — are prior academic experience related to theology (for example in philosophy or cultural studies), as well as biographical experiences with religion and the Church (such as through church-based youth work or internships).
If the Bachelor’s certificate has not been issued at the time of application, proof of at least 150 ECTS credits in total must be provided to facilitate an uninterrupted transition to the Master’s degree programme in the semester immediately following. The certificate must then be obtained by the end of the re-enrolment period for the third subject semester of the TWT Master’s degree programme at the latest.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
Finding part-time employment in Würzburg is a great way to gain experience, make new connections, and supplement your finances while studying. Students from EU and EEA countries enjoy equal terms in the labour market and can work freely during their studies. Students from other countries can work up to 140 full days or 280 half days per year, including voluntary internships. If you wish to work more, you'll need permission from the employment agency ("Agentur für Arbeit") or the immigration office.
It's important to ensure that your studies remain your top priority, so choose a side job that complements your academic schedule. The University of Würzburg offers resources to help you find part-time work, such as the student job portal.

Accommodation.value:
Finding the perfect place to live is an important part of your student experience at the University of Würzburg. Unlike some other countries, students in Germany need to find their own accommodation, as universities do not automatically provide it. At the University of Würzburg, you have two main options: "Studierendenwerk" housing or private rooms/student halls.
The Student Housing Service ("Studierendenwerk") manages 12 student residences in Würzburg, offering a total of 2,887 rooms. These dormitories provide a variety of amenities:
Single and double rooms or apartments shared by two to four students, with communal kitchens and bathrooms
Furnished rooms and apartments are available, though you'll need to bring your own dishes, cooking items, bedding, and towels.
To apply for housing, note the deadlines: 15 June for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester. For more information about private rooms and student halls, visit the Central Student Advisory Service.
In addition to Studierendenwerk housing, there are many private accommodation options available:
Shared apartments ("Wohngemeinschaften" or "WGs"): These are popular among students and offer a great way to meet new people and share living costs.
Private student halls: These are often run by private companies and offer similar amenities to Studierendenwerk dormitories. They can be a bit more expensive but may offer more modern facilities.
Short-term accommodation: If you need a place to stay while you search for permanent housing, consider options like hostels, guest houses, or short-term rentals.
Additional housing opportunities for students on this programme are provided by cooperation partners of the Faculty of Catholic Theology. For more information, please contact theologie-master@uni-wuerzburg.de.

Description/content.value:
GlobalMBA: Four countries. Two Degrees.
Since 2001, the GlobalMBA has united globally forward‑thinking students and distinguished faculty across four continents, creating a truly international dual Master’s experience. The University of Wuppertal is the newest partner within this unique programme.
This immersive 15‑months programme brings together a select cohort that studies, lives, and travels together through four global business hubs:
Semester 1 — Germany: Bergische University Wuppertal (BUW)
Semester 2 — Poland: University of Warsaw (UW)
Summer — Taiwan: Soochow University, Taipei (SCU)
Semester 3 — United States: University of North Florida (UNF)
Across these locations, students follow a shared curriculum centred on international business, intercultural communication, and the economic landscapes of each country. Every semester includes strategic company visits, industry engagement, and professional networking events designed to connect students with global business leaders.
Graduates earn two degrees:
A joint Master’s degree in International Management and Intercultural Communication from the University of Warsaw and Bergische University Wuppertal
An MBA from the University of North Florida
All coursework is delivered in English, and alumni launch careers across sectors, across leadership levels, and all over the world.
Students from any undergraduate background are encouraged to apply; only a few fundamental business prerequisites are required prior to the first semester.
One of the GlobalMBA’s greatest strengths is its worldwide alumni network, representing diverse industries and cultures.
We invite you to join this dynamic community of global professionals: leaders who think across borders, collaborate across cultures, and shape the future of international business.
Please note: a one-time programme fee of 1,350 EUR has to be paid to the University of North Florida. Other than that, only semester fees of the corresponding university (in Wuppertal: appr. 340 EUR per semester) have to be paid.
Your benefit:
The University of Wuppertal reserves places in the halls of residence near the campus for students in this degree programme.

Course organisation.value:
The Master's programme in International Management and Intercultural Communication — GlobalMBA comprises 90 ECTS. The regular duration is three semesters / 15 months of full-time study.
Each university in the consortium selects a small group of students who study and travel together as a single cohort throughout the programme.
Students rotate from one participating university to the other over the course of the programme. At each location, students complete mandatory courses, in total 72 ECTS or 51 U.S. credits of course work.
The Master's Thesis & Defence (18 ECTS) is done as a group project during the course of study, typically by three to four students of different nationalities.
Courses are taught in an interactive style focusing on intercultural team work. Courses are complemented by integrated strategic company visits, industry engagement, and professional networking events designed to connect students with global business leaders.

Costs of living.value:
Housing costs in Wuppertal are typical for a major German city, but they are cheaper than in cities such as Munich, Berlin or Cologne. The monthly rent for a room in a hall of residence is between 200 and 420 EUR, and the monthly rent for a room in a shared flat is between 300 and 500 EUR. An apartment of one's own costs at least 400 EUR.
You should expect to spend around 600 to 1,250 EUR per month on living and studying. In addition to rental costs, you will also need money for living expenses: from food, clothes, books for university and leisure activities to sports, cell phone contracts and going out. The costs for public transport throughout Germany are included in the semester fee and do not have to be paid separately.

Description of the above-mentioned fundi.value:
Life is not always straightforward and without stumbling blocks. Not giving up, facing these challenges on your own path in life requires courage, perseverance, creativity and determination. The Studienstiftung der Bergischen Universität Wuppertal promotes these qualities, the corresponding positive attitude to life and rewards them with its scholarship programme, which is aimed at students whose academic success is at risk for economic reasons.
Scholarships (like the "Deutschlandstipendium" or "Studienabschlussstipendium") are awarded with special consideration given to personal circumstances and/or social commitment.

General services and support for interna.value:
The University of Wuppertal offers lots of support programmes for international students. During the first week of each semester, a welcome ceremony is held accompanied by events such as city tours, pub evenings, or excursions. The International Students Team (IST) offers get-togethers and trips. The university's own language learning institute (SLI) offers preparatory and accompanying courses in German as a foreign language at all levels, including online and/or evening classes.
The In Touch programme includes counselling and mentoring during studies and career. The primary goal is to integrate and further qualify students with a refugee background professionally and interculturally, to lead them promptly to a degree that enables them to position themselves successfully on the regional and global labour market.

Costs of living.value:
The cost of living is roughly 800 EUR per month, which covers accommodation and living expenses.
Included are approximately 140 EUR per month for the compulsory health and care insurance if you are below 30 years of age (this is a special reduced students' rate). If you are over the age of 30, it can cost substantially more (up to a factor of two or three), and the cost greatly depends on the insurance type and company you have chosen.
In addition, a voluntary personal liability insurance is recommended (roughly 70 to 120 EUR per year, also varying greatly by company).
Accommodation is relatively cheap in Köthen in comparison to bigger German cities.
Students from most countries outside the European Union are requested to prove that they have the amount of roughly one year's cost of living and accommodation on a blocked account in order to be entitled to receive the visa that will allow them to enter Germany.

Description/content.value:
Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries (AI4CI) is a European Master's programme which covers:
fundamentals of artificial intelligence and machine learning applied to networked systems
advanced automation systems for industrial networks and robotics
advanced network architectures, IoT and computer systems
Lecturers include world-class academics from our European partners and industry experts.
This programme is supported by the Erasmus+ framework and is offered at the following European universities with different study modalities:
Cnam, Paris (France)
Cnam Grand-Est, Mulhouse (France)
Avignon Université, Avignon (France)
Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya, Barcelona (Spain)
Universitatea Babeș-Bolyai, Cluj-Napoca (Romania)
National Technical University of Ukraine, Kyiv (Ukraine)
The part-time Master's programme AI4CI is designed for professionals in technical, scientific, and engineering fields who wish to expand their knowledge of artificial intelligence and specialise in its application to connected industrial environments. It is particularly suited for professionals working in sectors such as mechanical engineering, robotics, information technology, electronics, automotive engineering, or automation technology who want to acquire hands-on expertise in AI and connected technologies. Both recent graduates and professionals with extensive work experience are welcome. The part-time structure of the programme makes it easier for participants to balance their studies with their professional careers, thereby also accommodating students with family or other commitments.
Description/content.html:
Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries (AI4CI) is a European Master's programme which covers:

  • fundamentals of artificial intelligence and machine learning applied to networked systems
  • advanced automation systems for industrial networks and robotics
  • advanced network architectures, IoT and computer systems

Lecturers include world-class academics from our European partners and industry experts.

This programme is supported by the Erasmus+ framework and is offered at the following European universities with different study modalities: 

  • Cnam, Paris (France)
  • Cnam Grand-Est, Mulhouse (France)
  • Avignon Université, Avignon (France)
  • Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya, Barcelona (Spain)
  • Universitatea Babeș-Bolyai, Cluj-Napoca (Romania)
  • National Technical University of Ukraine, Kyiv (Ukraine)

The part-time Master's programme AI4CI is designed for professionals in technical, scientific, and engineering fields who wish to expand their knowledge of artificial intelligence and specialise in its application to connected industrial environments. It is particularly suited for professionals working in sectors such as mechanical engineering, robotics, information technology, electronics, automotive engineering, or automation technology who want to acquire hands-on expertise in AI and connected technologies. Both recent graduates and professionals with extensive work experience are welcome. The part-time structure of the programme makes it easier for participants to balance their studies with their professional careers, thereby also accommodating students with family or other commitments.

Course organisation.value: The Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries Master’s degree programme with a total of 90 Credit Points (CP) is divided into compulsory modules, compulsory elective modules and free elective modules. There are three groups of compulsory elective modules, from which at least 12 CP must be achieved in each. Free elective modules can be selected either at partner universities or from the programmes Sensor Systems Engineering (Sensorsystemtechnik) and Business Analytics at Ulm University. A minimum of 6 CP must be achieved from the free elective modules group. A list of applicable modules is available from the examination board. The remaining 12 CP can be chosen from the compulsory elective modules and free elective modules.

Description/content.value:
The Master’s programme in Mathematical Data Science is a four-semester, 120-credit programme that combines a strong mathematical foundation with modern data science training. Students take core modules in Mathematics of Machine Learning, Numerical Methods for Data Science and Practical Foundations of Data Science, giving them both theoretical depth and hands-on experience.
The programme also offers substantial flexibility through elective courses, e.g. in functional analysis, mathematical statistics, mathematical data science, and applications, complemented by courses in ethics and interdisciplinary or language skills. At the end of the programme, students complete a 30-credit Master’s thesis.
Overall, Mathematical Data Science is designed for students who want to understand data science at a rigorous mathematical level while developing practical skills for research and applications.

Description/content.value: Ready to take the next step in a digital and globalised economy? The MSc Management and Economics at Ulm University builds on your Bachelor's studies to deepen your expertise in Business Management & Law, Economics, and Digitalisation & Data Science. Tailor your degree by choosing a specialisation profile in Economics, Finance, or Insurance, or sharpen your analytical edge through the Advanced Quantitative Methods Track. Interdisciplinary elective modules broaden your perspective, while small class sizes and direct contact with professors ensure you are known, not just enrolled. Our compact campus offers short distances and a dynamic academic community. Strong international partnerships open the door to a semester abroad. All of this unfolds in Ulm, ranked Germany's most liveable city by Handelsblatt. Join us and design the career you envision.

Course organisation.value:
Programme Structure
The MSc Management and Economics at Ulm University is built around flexibility. Rather than prescribing a fixed list of compulsory courses, the programme defines three core areas — Business Management & Law, Economics, and Digitalisation & Data Science — and specifies only the minimum ECTS credits to be earned in each. You choose the modules that best match your interests and career goals, optionally deepening your expertise through one or more profiles (Insurance, Finance, Economics) or the Advanced Quantitative Methods Track (AQMT).
A typical four-semester path looks like this:
Semesters 1–2: You build foundations across the three core areas and begin shaping your profile through advanced electives. Most students combine lectures from several areas during their first semester.
Semesters 2–3: You deepen your chosen profile(s), take at least one research seminar, and broaden your perspective through interdisciplinary electives offered across the university. Students aiming for the AQMT certificate complete their 30 ECTS in advanced quantitative modules during this phase.
Semester 4: You focus on your Master's thesis, an independent research project of six months, typically connected to one of our research groups or an industry partner.
Course Formats
Teaching combines several complementary formats. Lectures, often paired with accompanying exercise classes, deliver the theoretical and methodological foundations of each subject. Research seminars give you the opportunity to engage with current literature, write an academic term paper, and present your results to peers and faculty. Project courses and applied lab-style modules let you work hands-on with real data, software tools, and case studies, often in small teams. Supervision is close throughout: small class sizes and direct contact with professors are a hallmark of our campus university.
For concrete planning, we provide three sample curricula — one profile, two profiles, or two profiles combined with the AQMT — along with a four-semester overview of all scheduled courses.

Integrated/optional study abroad unit(s).value:
Study without borders and broaden your horizons: a stay abroad offers you the opportunity to get to know new perspectives and deepen your expertise in an international environment. Whether as part of the ERASMUS programme in Europe or at one of our non-European partner universities, Ulm University students can apply for one or two semesters at numerous universities worldwide. Even those who do not wish to attend lectures will find exciting options: internships or final theses abroad offer valuable insights into other academic cultures.
Ulm University has exchange agreements with over 100 universities in 26 countries – take advantage of this diversity to reinforce your intercultural skills and shape your academic path globally.
The Fudan-Shanghai exchange programme exists specifically for the Master's programme in Management and Economics, in which you can obtain a double degree by studying for one year at Ulm University and one year at Fudan University in Shanghai.

Description/content.value:
Are you ready to lead the fight against the world's most pressing challenges — climate change, energy transitions, and environmental crises?
Join TRACEE, a new Master’s programme, offered by the CIVIS European University Alliance!
The programme is designed to train experts in the fight against climate change, in the energy transition and in environmental crisis management. It equips you with the knowledge to understand the complex problems in these areas and provides you with the tools to create innovative solutions. A holistic approach is provided by the integration of different perspectives from the natural sciences, social sciences, humanities, and law into the curriculum.
For detailed information on the programme, the application and selection process and participation costs, visit TRACEE at Stockholm University, the coordinating university of the programme.

Description/content.value: The diversity of the biosphere is shaped by selection and evolution in complex and dynamic environments characterised by a complex mix of biotic and abiotic agents. Since the start of the Anthropogenic Era, it faces accelerating, large-scale anthropogenic changes in land use, pollutants, biological invasions and climate. Students of the Master of Science in “Biodiversity, Ecology and Evolution” develop an in-depth understanding of the processes and service functions associated with biodiversity from molecular to global scales. They can quantify diversity in genes, morphology, behaviour, or community composition and link it with biological function and ecosystem stability. With this integrative view, students learn to predict ecological and anthropogenic effects on biodiversity, and to design, conduct and analyse rigorous empirical investigations under laboratory and field settings. Furthermore, BEE MSc students strengthen their skills to communicate their findings and to contribute actively to ongoing societal debates.

Since the start of the Anthropogenic Era, it faces accelerating, large-scale anthropogenic changes in land use, pollutants, biological invasions and climate. Students of the Master of Science in “Biodiversity, Ecology and Evolution” develop an in-depth understanding of the processes and service functions associated with biodiversity from molecular to global scales. They can quantify diversity in genes, morphology, behaviour, or community composition and link it with biological function and ecosystem stability. With this integrative view, students learn to predict ecological and anthropogenic effects on biodiversity, and to design, conduct and analyse rigorous empirical investigations under laboratory and field settings. Furthermore, BEE MSc students strengthen their skills to communicate their findings and to contribute actively to ongoing societal debates.

Course organisation.value: The Master in Biodiversity, Ecology and Evolution programme is designed for a duration of four semesters (120 ECTS credits). Specifically, the programme focuses on the study, complexity, function, interactive nature and ecological service of organismal diversity in environments under varying degrees of human impact. The programme trains students in dealing with ecological and biological complexity both from a short-term, local, and a long-term, global perspective. It fuses top-down and bottom-up approaches in the study of plasticity, adaptability, evolvability, functionality, resilience, facilitation, and conservation at levels ranging from ecosystems down to populations and their genetic and molecular diversity.

Description/content.value:
Discover the fascinating world of plants — from molecular mechanisms to ecosystem dynamics!
The Faculty of Biology at Würzburg University welcomes motivated and qualified graduates with a background in biology (BSc or equivalent) to join its two-year Master’s programme in Molecular Plant Sciences. This programme is designed for globally minded young scientists eager to deepen their understanding of how plants evolve, grow, adapt, and interact with their environment.
As part of the Julius-von-Sachs-Institute within the JMU Biocenter, you will conduct research and learn from internationally recognised researchers in an environment that fosters curiosity, innovation, and collaboration. Through an inspiring combination of lectures, seminars, and extensive laboratory training – all taught in English – you will acquire advanced, research-oriented training in quantitative molecular plant sciences. You will actively engage in ongoing research projects, often with close one-to-one supervision, gaining real-world experience in cutting-edge scientific practice.
The Master’s programme builds on the strengths of highly interactive plant departments at the JvSI and numerous research groups there working at the forefront of plant topics such as Ecophysiology, Physiology, Plant-Microbe Interactions, Signalling Networks, Adaptation and Evolution, Membrane Biology, Structural Biology, and Chemical Biology. This broad spectrum of expertise and the cooperative network within the entire Faculty of Biology ensure an academically rich and intellectually stimulating curriculum.
Depending on your research interests and goals, you can tailor your Master’s programme by selecting two out of six main topics:
Plant Membrane Biology
Structural Biology
Plant Adaptations to a Changing World
Plant Biotic Interactions
Plant Chemical Biology and Metabolism
Plant Signalling Networks
Graduates of this programme have not only expanded their scientific skill set but are also prepared to engage with pressing global challenges in plant science and sustainability.
The website of the Master of Science programme in Molecular Plant Sciences is the best way to find out more about this programme:
https://go.uniwue.de/molplant
Contact: Prof Ulrich Hammes (ulrich.hammes@uni-wuerzburg.de), Prof Nathalie Lackus (nathalie.lackus@uni-wuerzburg.de), Prof Katharina Markmann (katharina.markmann@uni-wuerzburg.de)
