Course organisation.value: During the two-year Master’s programme in Molecular Plant Sciences, students are required to complete a total of 120 ECTS credits. Within the programme, two of the following six topics may be selected: Plant Membrane Biology, Structural Biology, Plant Adaptations to a Changing World, Plant Biotic Interactions, Plant Chemical Biology and Metabolism, and Plant Signalling Networks. In each selected topic, students complete graded modules summing up to 30 ECTS credits. These comprise two theoretical modules of 10 ECTS credits each and one advanced practical course (F1) worth 10 ECTS credits. Students select one focal topic, in which an additional 15 ECTS credits are obtained via an ungraded Advanced Practical Course 2 (F2). The F2 course lasts twelve weeks and precedes the Master’s thesis (6 months, 25 ECTS) with the final thesis colloquium (5 ECTS). Throughout their studies, students are actively engaged in ongoing research projects. They acquire the ability to plan and conduct independent theoretical and experimental work, to summarise and critically discuss their findings in the written thesis, and to present and defend their results in a final colloquium. The credit line “Additional Qualifications” enables students to broaden their scope beyond the focal topic areas by selecting additional modules amounting to 15 ECTS credits. These extra modules, assessed on a pass/fail basis, allow students to pursue individual academic interests. PDF Download

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
Finding part-time employment in Würzburg is a great way to gain experience, make new connections, and supplement your finances while studying. Students from EU and EEA countries enjoy equal terms in the labour market and can work freely during their studies. Students from other countries can work up to 140 full days or 280 half days per year, including voluntary internships. If you wish to work more, you'll need permission from the employment agency ("Agentur für Arbeit") or the immigration office.
It's important to ensure that your studies remain your top priority, so choose a side job that complements your academic schedule. The University of Würzburg offers resources to help you find part-time work, such as the student job portal.

Accommodation.value:
Finding the perfect place to live is an important part of your student experience at the University of Würzburg. Unlike some other countries, students in Germany need to find their own accommodation, as universities do not automatically provide it. At the University of Würzburg, you have two main options: "Studierendenwerk" housing or private rooms/student halls.
The Student Housing Service ("Studierendenwerk") manages 12 student residences in Würzburg, offering a total of 2,887 rooms. These dormitories provide a variety of amenities:
Single and double rooms or apartments shared by two to four students, with communal kitchens and bathrooms
Furnished rooms and apartments are available, though you'll need to bring your own dishes, cooking items, bedding, and towels.
To apply for housing, note the deadlines: 15 June for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester. For more information about private rooms and student halls, visit the Central Student Advisory Service.
In addition to Studierendenwerk housing, there are many private accommodation options available:
Shared apartments ("Wohngemeinschaften" or "WGs"): These are popular among students and offer a great way to meet new people and share living costs.
Private student halls: These are often run by private companies and offer similar amenities to Studierendenwerk dormitories. They can be a bit more expensive but may offer more modern facilities.
Short-term accommodation: If you need a place to stay while you search for permanent housing, consider options like hostels, guest houses, or short-term rentals.
Remember to start your housing search early and stay positive! With a bit of patience and diligence, you'll find a cosy place to call home.

Description/content.value:
The FAME Master's programme is a completely redesigned, English-language study programme that opens the door to the most challenging and exciting jobs in research, development, and industry. Building on existing engineering knowledge, you will deepen your expertise in areas such as design and production engineering, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, materials science, control engineering, and project management.
In addition to modern laboratories and practical projects, you can expect close cooperation with industry partners and research institutions, including a one-semester internship in industry or at an institute. You will learn to analyse complex systems, develop innovative solutions, and implement them in an economical, sustainable, and technically excellent manner. We also prepare you in terms of language and culture to make it easier for you to start your career and/or life in Germany.
With a Master's degree in mechanical engineering, you will be qualified for creative or management positions in industry, research, or self-employment. You can actively shape the technological progress of our society.

Course organisation.value: The FAME Master’s programme comprises four semesters (120 ECTS), which must be completed in accordance with the examination regulations. The programme is divided into several blocks, each of which offers a wide range of options: Engineering Fundamentals: This module consists of three courses designed to provide a comprehensive foundation in core engineering principles. If your previous Bachelor’s degree did not cover certain subject areas, you can make up for them here. If necessary, the admissions committee will provide guidelines on the subjects you are required to take. Language and Culture: In this section, you choose a subject from the field of work culture and a language that you want to study in depth. For students from abroad, we offer special courses designed to make living and working in Germany easier, and if you come from Germany, there are also other offers to help you broaden your horizons. Focus Fields: In the two focus fields, which you can choose yourself, you can choose from over 140 different subjects, which you can use to develop your individual study focus and personal profile. The subjects cover the entire spectrum of mechanical engineering in Stuttgart and are taught exclusively in English. Each Focus Field is supervised by a professor who is on-hand to answer your questions and provide guidance during your studies. Engineering Practice Term: As an applied science, it is important to us that you also learn about practical life as part of an organisation. For this purpose, one semester of the programme is reserved for either a mandatory internship at a company (please refer to the internship guidelines) or a research project at a university research institute, depending on the profile you wish to pursue. In addition, you will participate in a compulsory supporting module (accompanying seminar) at the university to discuss and reflect on your experiences. Master's thesis: You will complete your studies with a Master's thesis in one of your two focus fields. This will be closely supervised by the staff of the institute you choose for this purpose. Description/content.value:
The Bachelor's programme in International Business and Management prepares you for a career in national or international companies. The programme is taught in German and English, includes a semester abroad and practice-oriented projects, and allows you to choose your own specialisation.
Language Policy
Lectures in the first two semesters are conducted in German; some of them can be replaced by English‑taught classes. From the third semester onward, both German and English are used as languages of instruction. Business English is integrated as a first foreign language, and Spanish, French, Russian or Chinese can be selected as a second foreign language.
Competence Profile
You acquire comprehensive knowledge and competencies in all areas of business management and, after completing the Bachelor's degree, you can work as a junior manager in companies or organisations. You will learn to act in the interest of sustainable value creation and to develop solutions collaboratively for global enterprises.
Didactic Concept
The teaching content is delivered in German and English within small, international study groups. The programme offers opportunities to gain cross-cultural competencies during your studies and to establish contacts worldwide.
Specialisation and Language Options
You can select among various specialisations in business management, economics and business languages, study additional foreign languages, and gain experience abroad.
Study‑Abroad Semester
A semester abroad, usually taken in the fifth semester, is a compulsory, integrated part of the programme. Around 150 partner universities worldwide are available, and the semester abroad may also be undertaken at a non-partner university. One or more additional semesters or study stays abroad are possible.
Double-Degree Options
With a French and a South Korean university, double-degree agreements are in place; after a one-year study period at those institutions you can also obtain the Bachelor’s degree awarded by these institutions.
Practical Relevance and Professional Field
Practice-oriented projects, the integrated semester abroad and work in small, diverse groups strengthen both your professional and intercultural competence. In an increasingly globalised world, professionals with these skills are in high demand. Your knowledge of international markets and sustainable value creation will help you develop innovative solutions for the economic challenges of tomorrow.

We offer student assistant jobs at the university. You can also find jobs through our database (PRAXIKO), where local employers look for student workers and interns.
If you speak German well enough, there are many job opportunities in Osnabrück in bakeries, supermarkets, industry, restaurants, etc.

Mrs Laetitia Godineau will answer your questions around finding a job during your studies as well as about making the transition into the job market after graduation.
Important: If you need to work to support yourself, you should start looking for a student job as early as possible.

Description/content.value:
This degree programme prepares you to become a qualified specialist in the field of mechanical engineering.
The programme lasts three semesters and leads to a Master of Engineering (MEng). The course initially offers advanced modules in general mechanical engineering and modules in management and project management. You also have the opportunity to specialise in the areas of plant engineering, design or production engineering, by choosing from a catalogue of modules in these specialisations. In addition to the lectures, your studies also include a substantial project component. The Master's programme can be studied either entirely in English or in German, but you may also freely choose between English- and German-taught modules.

Course organisation.value: The Master's degree course in Mechanical Engineering is divided into three parts in the first two semesters. One part of the curriculum (10 CP) consists of two modules with 5 CP each, which are compulsory. Here you will learn leadership and project management skills as well as advanced technical fundamentals. Part 1: The compulsory modules are: Advanced Project Management for Engineers 5 CP Lightweight Construction and Innovative Materials 5 CP Part 2: You can specialise in the elective part of the programme. In particular, the specialisations from the Bachelor's degree course in Mechanical Engineering (Plant Engineering, Production Engineering, Design Engineering) and intersections thereof are considered here. You may choose freely from a catalogue, but you must take at least 30 CP (6 modules). For guidance, the modules are marked according to their main subject area (A = plant engineering, P = production engineering, K = design engineering). Examples for elective modules (in English) are: Advanced Vehicle Dynamics Advanced ERP Systems Energy Process Simulation Project Wind Challenge Hyperloop Project Modular Systems and Module Management Advanced Thermodynamics Laser Material Processing Data Science / Software Development Simulation of Production Technology Advanced Control Theory An overview of the modules can be found on the website and in the module handbook. Part 3: The third part of the first two semesters is the project area. Here you will learn how to conduct scientific work in technical projects. The aim is to prepare you for management and project management tasks in industry as well as for research work — for example, during a doctorate. In the third semester, you will complete your Master's thesis, which you can typically carry out in a company or in one of our university's laboratories. PDF Download
Course organisation.html:
The Master's degree course in Mechanical Engineering is divided into three parts in the first two semesters. One part of the curriculum (10 CP) consists of two modules with 5 CP each, which are compulsory. Here you will learn leadership and project management skills as well as advanced technical fundamentals.

Part 1:

The compulsory modules are:

  • Advanced Project Management for Engineers 5 CP
  • Lightweight Construction and Innovative Materials 5 CP

Part 2:

You can specialise in the elective part of the programme. In particular, the specialisations from the Bachelor's degree course in Mechanical Engineering (Plant Engineering, Production Engineering, Design Engineering) and intersections thereof are considered here. You may choose freely from a catalogue, but you must take at least 30 CP (6 modules). For guidance, the modules are marked according to their main subject area (A = plant engineering, P = production engineering, K = design engineering).

Examples for elective modules (in English) are:

  • Advanced Vehicle Dynamics
  • Advanced ERP Systems
  • Energy Process Simulation
  • Project Wind Challenge
  • Hyperloop Project
  • Modular Systems and Module Management
  • Advanced Thermodynamics
  • Laser Material Processing
  • Data Science / Software Development
  • Simulation of Production Technology
  • Advanced Control Theory

An overview of the modules can be found on the website and in the module handbook.

Part 3:

The third part of the first two semesters is the project area. Here you will learn how to conduct scientific work in technical projects. The aim is to prepare you for management and project management tasks in industry as well as for research work — for example, during a doctorate.

In the third semester, you will complete your Master's thesis, which you can typically carry out in a company or in one of our university's laboratories.

Description of other international eleme.value:
As a result of the learning activities, students are given the opportunity to acquire subject-specific and general intercultural skills, with lecturers supporting them through activities that encourage student engagement. These include group assignments and projects in teams comprising students from different disciplinary, ethnic, sociocultural or socio-economic backgrounds. The option to switch between German- and English-taught lectures and the considerable project part in the Master’s programme enhance intercultural collaboration throughout the programme.
In addition, voluntary internships, study abroad semesters and Master's theses abroad are strongly supported by Emden/Leer University of Applied Sciences. Voluntary language courses are offered throughout the programme.

Admission requires a Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial engineering, Energy Efficiency or a comparable degree of seven semesters or 210 ECTS. Further details can be found in the admission regulations. Students who have only 180 ECTS at the beginning of their studies can acquire an additional 30 CP in selected modules. In these cases, the duration of the Master's programme is extended by one semester.
Reliable and certified English or German language skills are required. Proof of English proficiency at B2 level is required: please check the uni-assist English proficiency framework and the admission requirements on our website (one is listed as an example).
Applicants originating from China, India, or Vietnam additionally have to hand in the original certificate of the academic assessment office issued by the German embassy (“Akademische Prüfstelle”). Your application cannot be processed without this certificate. You may find further information here:

Description of the above-mentioned fundi.value:
There are different scholarship opportunities for enrolled students in Germany. However, it is very important to understand that scholarships are highly competitive, limited in number, and never guaranteed. Students must ensure they can finance their studies independently and should not rely on receiving a scholarship. Most programmes focus on excellent academic performance, personal engagement, or specific qualifications; financial need is often not the main criterion. Some national scholarships also require German language skills (often B2 level).
THI offers its own scholarship opportunities for international students once a year, announced through the university’s communication channels. For example, the Deutschlandstipendium supports high-performing, committed students regardless of their financial situation.
There are several major national foundations with extensive selection processes for which the university provides guidance and support.

Academic admission requirements.value:
Requirements include a Bachelor's degree in chemical engineering, process engineering, energy engineering, mechanical engineering, industrial engineering, electrical engineering, civil engineering or equivalent with at least 210 ECTS credits or equivalent degree requirements (a minimum of seven semesters at a German university with a workload of 25 to 30 hours per ECTS).
Specific experience in energy-related topics is an advantage.
Proof of sufficient proficiency in the English language (level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) is a must. After the evaluation of your application documents, an online interview will be conducted with selected applicants.
Admission for applicants with Bachelor's degrees comprising 180 ECTS: For applicants who have a Bachelor's degree with less than 210 credits (but with a minimum of 180 ECTS), an approval of 30 ECTS on the basis of the qualified working experience is possible if the admission board agrees. The extent and nature of the working experience must comply with the rules for a second practical semester at Bavarian applied universities (§ 13 RaPO) and must be documented with a certificate of employment.
The Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt can only make a legally binding decision about your eligibility for your desired study programme after reviewing the documents you submit with your application. We can’t evaluate your chances of acceptance until we have your full application, including your educational history.
Additionally, you can find out about the qualification requirements via the study and examination regulations (=Studien- und Prüfungsordnung = SPO). Please find these on the following page under the respective statutes:
https://www.thi.de/en/university/university-profile/university-management/legal-department/.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
Whether you can work alongside your studies depends on several factors. At the beginning, it is advisable to focus on your studies and adjust to a new academic and cultural environment. Studying abroad can be challenging due to different learning cultures and the need to catch up on course content.
International students are required to take part in a programme preparing them for the German labour market.
A good command of German at least B2 level is essential for employment opportunities. Students are therefore encouraged to invest time in learning German.
After the first year, students may consider taking on a part-time job. Specialist skills are required to work as a student trainee.
Furthermore, non-EU citizens only have a limited work permit in Germany (see Study and work).

Description/content.value:
The programme provides knowledge in a challenging field of technology that is socially and environmentally relevant: autonomous flight systems contribute to sustainability, safety, and resilience (e.g. airspace monitoring, surveillance missions during wildfires, floods, and rescue operations).
The programme is characterised by an interdisciplinary curriculum that covers a broad range of technologies necessary to develop autonomous flight systems, spanning from computer science, systems engineering, and simulation, via robotics and AI (autonomy, path planning, decision-making algorithms) to communication technology.
The programme is designed for students interested in interdisciplinary issues related to the development of autonomous flight systems, who possess a strong affinity for technology and a willingness to innovate. Knowledge required to design and implement components of autonomous, intelligent and networked flight systems is provided. The focus is on acquiring skills needed to develop flight systems that use sensors, planning and control algorithms and Artificial Intelligence to perceive their environment and react to changing situations. Knowledge such as flight dynamics, control of flight systems and avionics is expanded by technologies such as sensor technology, machine learning, autonomous navigation and methods for determining optimal, safe and efficient flight paths for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is imparted. Students will be prepared to master the challenges of UAVs and drones — from urban use to scientific research in remote areas.

Course organisation.value: Differences in prior knowledge are addressed in the first semester by aligning competencies in areas like software development, control engineering, flight mechanics, and flight systems. Theoretical instruction is supplemented by practical exercises. Modules in the following two semesters cover, among other topics, mathematical methods, models, and algorithms for flight control, navigation, environmental perception, and mission planning. Students will learn how to specify and implement software architectures for autonomous flight systems, mission planning and flight control algorithms, as well as the development of communication and coordination concepts. Methods related to systems engineering or to the computation of flight paths and of trajectory planning are applied in laboratory exercises. PDF Download

In addition to tuition fees, students face the following fixed monthly living costs:
- Health insurance: approx. 150 EUR
- Liability insurance: approx. 10 EUR
- Accommodation: approx. 500 to 650 EUR
- Internet and mobile phone: approx. 25 EUR
- Food: approx. 200 to 300 EUR
- German TV/radio fee: approx. 19 EUR
- Public transport (Deutschlandticket 2026): approx. 43 EUR
Beyond these fixed costs, additional expenses will vary depending on individual needs, such as travel to visit family or participation in leisure activities.
Additionally, don’t forget potential unforeseen costs, such as the need for a new laptop or mobile phone, etc.
Usually, non-EU students are required to provide proof of sufficient financial means with a blocked account for visa purposes. It should contain approx. 992 EUR per month for up to 12 months.

Description of the above-mentioned fundi.value:
There are different scholarship opportunities for enrolled students in Germany. However, it is very important to understand that scholarships are highly competitive, limited in number, and never guaranteed. Students must ensure they can finance their studies independently and should not rely on receiving a scholarship. Most programmes focus on excellent academic performance, personal engagement, or specific qualifications; financial need is often not the main criterion. Some national scholarships also require German language skills (often B2 level).
THI offers its own scholarship opportunities for international students once a year, announced through the university’s communication channels. For example, the Deutschlandstipendium supports high-performing, committed students regardless of their financial situation.
There are several major national foundations with extensive selection processes for which the university provides guidance and support.

Applicants with a Bachelor's degree obtained in a non-EU country undergo a selection procedure, provided that the formal admission requirements are met.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
Whether you can work alongside your studies depends on several factors. At the beginning, it is advisable to focus on your studies and adjust to a new academic and cultural environment. Studying abroad can be challenging due to different learning cultures and the need to catch up on course content.
International students are required to take part in a programme preparing them for the German labour market.
A good command of German at least B2 level is essential for employment opportunities. Students are therefore encouraged to invest time in learning German.
After the first year, students may consider taking on a part-time job. Specialist skills are required to work as a student trainee.
Furthermore, non-EU citizens only have a limited work permit in Germany (see Study and work).

Description/content.value:
The international Master’s programme in "Biogeoscience of the Anthropocene" is the scientific response to some of the most pressing global challenges of our time. The programme focuses on investigating how climate change, biodiversity loss, and the crossing of planetary boundaries affect terrestrial ecosystems, above and below ground, their surface-subsurface couplings, and their essential services. Positioned at the interface of biosciences, geosciences, meta-omics and data sciences, students analyse the dynamics of ecosystem functions under anthropogenic pressure.
The curriculum goes far beyond descriptive analysis: a core objective is to develop active, transformative competence. Students are empowered not only to diagnose complex environmental problems with precision but also to actively design intelligent solutions. This includes nature-based solutions and the foundations for innovative technological approaches to strengthen the resilience of the Earth system.
By making use of the excellent research infrastructure of Friedrich Schiller University Jena, and in close cooperation with the Max Planck Institutes for Biogeochemistry and Geoanthropology, students are familiarised with working with complex, short- and long-term datasets and state-of-the-art methodologies.
A unique feature of this programme is the intensive integration of advanced fieldwork within Jena's world-class long-term research sites. Students gain hands-on experience by working in "open-air laboratories" and master modern monitoring techniques—from sampling the unsaturated zone to analysing flux dynamics between soil, the aeration zone and groundwater—to understand the Critical Zone under real-world conditions.
The programme offers applicants with a Bachelor’s degree in geosciences, biosciences, environmental sciences, or related fields a flexible, interdisciplinary structure. Our goal is to train experts who can translate systemic knowledge into proactive action to sustainably secure the vital functions of our planet in the Anthropocene.

Course organisation.value:
The Master's programme covers four semesters with 120 ECTS in total. Compulsory modules (in total 45 ECTS) have to be completed during the first three semesters. Elective modules totalling more than 100 ECTS are offered, of which 45 ECTS must be completed. The fourth semester consists of the Master's thesis (30 ECTS).
Lectures will transmit theoretical knowledge, seminars are featuring discussions and presentations, lab work, field trips / field exercises, and computer exercises convey hands-on training. Project work with individual supervision is designed to apply theoretical and practical expertise.

Description/content.value:
Without modern electrical engineering and information technology, our daily lives would be hard to imagine, and probably quite boring. Just imagine if all devices with a plug or a battery suddenly disappeared: no smartphones, no laptops, no refrigerators, no light switches, no trains, and no medical equipment. Modern life as we know it would be practically impossible.
Rapid progress began about 150 years ago, when the first high-voltage transmission lines were built and electrical energy could be transported over long distances for the first time. This marked the beginning of the triumph of electrical engineering. Electrical energy could now be generated reliably, transmitted efficiently, and used almost everywhere, an essential foundation for industrialisation, prosperity, and technological progress.
Today, alongside energy supply, information technology plays a central role. It ensures that data can be transmitted quickly and reliably, from the internet and mobile communication networks to satellite links. Ultimately, all of this relies on electrical signals that carry information. They deliver messages to our smartphones, control machines in industry, and enable worldwide communication within fractions of a second.
But this is only a small glimpse of what engineers in electrical and information engineering work on. Examples of exciting fields of activity include:
Semiconductor technology, the foundation of computer chips and microcontrollers
Electrical machines and drive systems, for electric cars, trains, and industrial machinery
Modern power transmission and energy networks, from high-voltage direct current transmission to intelligent power grids
Electromobility and energy storage, enabling sustainable energy systems
Communication and telecommunications engineering, for mobile networks, Wi-Fi, and satellite communication
High-frequency engineering and sensor technology, for applications such as radar, medical devices, or autonomous systems
and much more….
Electrical and information engineering therefore shape many of the most important future technologies of our society.
Be part of this future.
By studying this degree programme at HTWG Konstanz, you can help drive progress in areas such as renewable energy systems, secure data transmission, intelligent technical systems with AI applications, and reliable electronics that make our everyday lives easier, more efficient, and more sustainable.

Course organisation.value:
During the first and second semester — known as foundation studies — you will receive broad foundational education and explore important areas of electrical engineering and information technology.
You will enter your main studies in the third semester and expand on your knowledge and competences from the basic studies.
The fourth semester is a practical study semester. You will get to know the structures and processes at a company in the industry. By learning on the job, you will develop your knowledge, gain a clear idea of your future professional field, and you will be able to establish contacts with employers.
From the fifth semester onwards, you will specialise individually in one of the modules of specialisation:
Electrical and Electronic Systems
Information Technologies and AI
Sustainable Energy Systems
You complete your studies with the Bachelor's thesis at the university or at a company.

Description/content.value:
When people think about intelligent mobility systems, many different ideas may come to mind. Most of us probably first think of self-driving cars, such as those developed by companies like Waymo or Google. However, intelligent mobility involves much more than autonomous passenger cars.
The Smart Mobility Systems degree programme focuses on the entire world of modern mobility. This includes, for example, intelligent bicycles equipped with sensors that detect riding conditions and provide safety features such as anti-lock braking systems. It also includes highly-automated automobiles that can perceive their environment, make decisions, and navigate independently. In addition, autonomous ships and ferries, capable of docking precisely and safely at terminals, are part of this technological development. Beyond that, connected transportation systems, intelligent infrastructure, and new mobility concepts are becoming increasingly important.
Engineers who develop such innovative technologies need broad and solid technical knowledge from several fields, for example:
Electrical and information engineering, the foundation of modern technical systems
Control engineering and artificial intelligence, enabling systems to act autonomously
Software engineering and computer science, for developing complex software and algorithms
Sensors and environmental perception, allowing vehicles to reliably detect and interpret their surroundings
Electric drives and modern mobility systems, designed to be efficient, sustainable, and high-performance
and much more.
If you would like to actively shape the mobility of the future, dive into the world of intelligent transportation systems and start your studies in Smart Mobility Systems at HTWG Konstanz. Here you will learn how modern vehicles, sensors, software, and artificial intelligence work together to make transportation safer, smarter, and more sustainable.

Description/content.value:
Even relatively simple technical systems consist of several hundred individual components. A modern mobile phone or computer can contain tens of thousands of parts. These components are developed and manufactured in factories all over the world and must then be brought together to create functioning products.
Over the past decades, free global trade and the increasing globalisation of markets have significantly expanded international supply chains and cooperation between companies worldwide. Components are developed, manufactured, and assembled in different countries. At the same time, quality, costs, logistics, and timelines must be coordinated reliably. As a result, modern technological products are usually created through the close collaboration of many international partners.
This programme prepares you specifically for this global environment. During your studies, you will learn how technical projects are organised in an international context and what needs to be considered when working with global business partners. This also includes understanding how global markets operate, how international supply chains are structured, and which economic, cultural, and organisational factors influence international cooperation.
The programme builds upon the traditional industrial engineering curriculum and expands it with a strong focus on international perspectives and global challenges. In addition to technical and economic subjects, you will explore international markets, intercultural collaboration, and global production and logistics structures.
An important part of the programme is international experience. During your studies, you will spend part of your study time abroad. In addition, our double degree programme offers you the opportunity to earn a second academic degree from one of our international partner universities alongside your degree from HTWG.
This way, you will be well prepared to design and manage technical projects and global supply chains in an interconnected world.

Description/content.value:
We all want electronic devices and technical gadgets that are affordable to purchase and, ideally, work reliably for a long time. Whether it is a smartphone, a laptop, a household appliance, or an electric car, we expect the technology to be powerful, offer many functions, and cost as little as possible.
Electrical engineers primarily focus on developing technical systems that function reliably and offer a wide range of capabilities. However, turning a technical idea into a product that can be used worldwide is still a long journey. Production, component procurement, logistics, distribution, and cost structures are equally important. This is exactly where industrial engineers work, at the intersection between technology and business.
Their goal is to design and organise technical products so that they can be produced efficiently, distributed economically, and made affordable for many people. This includes understanding global supply chains, optimising production processes, and organising companies so that innovation and economic efficiency work together.
Today, the objective is no longer simply to manufacture products at the lowest possible cost. Engineers also carry a responsibility for sustainability, resource conservation, and environmentally compatible production processes. Modern technical products therefore need to be considered across their entire life cycle, from development and manufacturing to usage, reuse, and recycling.
For this reason, industrial engineers require not only a solid technical background, but also knowledge in many additional areas, for example:
how companies are organised and how technical projects are managed
how markets function and the role of competition and innovation
how supply chains are analysed, evaluated, and developed
how economic and environmental factors interact
how sustainable production systems can be designed
how circular economy and recycling concepts can be integrated into modern products
and much more….
This creates a very broad and exciting field of work in which technology, business, and sustainability are closely connected.
If you are interested not only in modern electrical and information engineering, but you also want to understand how technical products can be developed in an economically viable and sustainable way across their entire life cycle, then this degree programme is the right choice.

Course organisation.value:
During the first and second semester — known as foundation studies — you will receive broad foundational education and explore important areas of electrical engineering, information technology and management.
You will enter the main studies in the third semester and expand on your knowledge and competences from the basic studies.
The fourth semester is a practical study semester. You will get to know the structures and processes at a company in the industry. By learning on the job, you will develop your knowledge, gain a clear idea of your future professional field, and you will be able to establish contacts with employers.
From the fifth semester onwards, you will specialise individually in one of the modules of specialisation:
Electrical and Electronic Systems
Information Technologies and AI
Sustainable Energy Systems
Sustainable Global Value Networks
You complete your studies with the Bachelor's thesis at the university or at a company.

Description/content.value:
Are you curious about the world and how it works? Are you interested in the ideas, cultures, and forces that have shaped human societies across time? “Liberal Arts: Culture, History, Society” at the University of Regensburg is an interdisciplinary Bachelor’s programme that invites you to explore the big questions - from the roots of civilisation to contemporary challenges: migration, climate change, gender, social inequality, sustainability and many others that reflect the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Taught entirely in English and with a foundation in the rich tradition of Liberal Arts education — but with a distinct contemporary twist — this seven-semester Bachelor of Arts degree challenges students to think broadly and critically. You’ll engage with history, literature, culture, and the social sciences, building the skills to analyse, communicate, and connect across disciplines.
Description/content.html:
Are you curious about the world and how it works? Are you interested in the ideas, cultures, and forces that have shaped human societies across time? “Liberal Arts: Culture, History, Society” at the University of Regensburg is an interdisciplinary Bachelor’s programme that invites you to explore the big questions - from the roots of civilisation to contemporary challenges: migration, climate change, gender, social inequality, sustainability and many others that reflect the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Taught entirely in English and with a foundation in the rich tradition of Liberal Arts education — but with a distinct contemporary twist — this seven-semester Bachelor of Arts degree challenges students to think broadly and critically. You’ll engage with history, literature, culture, and the social sciences, building the skills to analyse, communicate, and connect across disciplines.

Course organisation.value:
The programme begins with foundational courses in history, social sciences, and cultural/literary studies, alongside academic writing and language training. In the second semester, students take themed interdisciplinary courses and continue developing language and transferable skills.
From the third to fifth semesters, the focus shifts to interdisciplinary, phenomenon-based learning combined with discipline-specific courses and additional skills training. The sixth semester offers either an Erasmus exchange or a stay-home option with an internship and area studies courses. Finally, the seventh semester is dedicated to thesis preparation, a colloquium, and completing the Bachelor’s thesis.

Description/content.value:
The Master's programme in Chemistry comprises three core modules, which can be freely combined from all offered sub-disciplines of chemistry: Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Physical Chemistry, Bioanalysis, Theoretical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Sustainable Chemistry.
Information: https://www.uni-regensburg.de/en/chemie-pharmazie/studieren/im-studium/studiengaenge/msc-chemistry
In addition to free module selection, we offer students the opportunity to choose specialisation studies.
1) MSc Chemistry with a focus on Bioanalysis:
Bioanalysis – an interdisciplinary field providing the methodologies to study fundamental questions of life and to cope with life’s challenges in health diagnostics, pharmacy and medical technology. From probing single cells or molecules to providing point-of-care diagnostics to screening for new pharmaceutical drugs: developing novel bioanalytical tools is the basis of it all. The Master of Chemistry with a focus on Bioanalysis aims at training a next generation of bioanalytical chemists who will have a broad foundation in chemical knowledge and an in-depth understanding of this interdisciplinary field.
Information: https://www.uni-regensburg.de/en/chemie-pharmazie/studieren/im-studium/studiengaenge/msc-chemistry-with-focus-on-bionalysis
2) MSc Chemistry with a focus on Sustainable Chemistry:
Sustainable chemistry is crucial for addressing the growing challenges of environmental protection, resource scarcity, and human health. The conventional chemical industry has historically contributed to pollution, energy consumption, and waste production. To counteract these negative impacts, sustainable chemistry focuses on developing environmentally friendly processes and materials that are ecologically sound, resource-efficient, and safe for human health, as well as promoting the recycling of chemical products. By transitioning to sustainable chemical practices, we can not only reduce our environmental impact but also ensure the long-term availability of raw materials and foster innovative solutions to global challenges such as climate change and pollution.
Information: https://www.uni-regensburg.de/en/chemie-pharmazie/studieren/im-studium/studiengaenge/m-sc-chemistry-with-focus-on-sustainable-chemistry

The Master’s in Media Informatics programme offers an advanced and interdisciplinary approach to understanding, designing, and developing interactive digital technologies. Students explore how humans engage with digital systems and learn to create applications that are both technically robust and user‑centred. The curriculum combines theoretical foundations with hands‑on project work, enabling students to gain expertise in areas such as user experience design, software engineering, interactive media technologies, and data‑driven methods.
A key feature of the programme is its high degree of flexibility. Students can tailor their studies to their academic interests and professional ambitions by selecting from a broad range of elective modules. These include topics such as Usability Engineering, Game Engineering, Digital Humanities, Explainable and Generative AI, as well as advanced courses in Computer Science, Data Science, and related fields. The programme also supports international mobility, allowing students to integrate a semester abroad into their studies.
Graduates leave the programme with a strong methodological background and the ability to conceptualise, prototype, and evaluate innovative digital solutions. They gain experience in interdisciplinary teamwork, research‑oriented thinking, and the practical implementation of interactive systems. This combination of skills prepares them for careers in research institutions, the tech industry, the creative sector, and any field where digital innovation plays a central role.
The programme is structured into two main components:
Core Area (72 ECTS)
The core curriculum consists of four compulsory modules, including the Master’s thesis. Students learn to plan and manage IT projects, develop and evaluate interactive systems, and conduct independent research in Human‑Centred Computing.
Core modules include:
Software Engineering and Project Management
Engineering Interactive Systems
Research Project in Human‑Centred Computing
Master’s Thesis
Elective Area (minimum 48 ECTS)
Students choose at least 48 ECTS from twelve elective modules. This allows them to build a personalised academic profile, ranging from applied media technologies to AI‑driven methods or interdisciplinary digital‑humanities approaches.
Overall, the programme equips students with the expertise needed to contribute to the development of future digital technologies and to assume roles as specialists in academia, industry, and the broader innovation landscape.

Course organisation.value: Our courses You will attend lectures with accompanying labs, seminars, and project seminars or internships. In lectures with accompanying labs, you will be taught knowledge and methods that you can apply yourself in the labs, through which you will acquire subject-specific skills through your own application. In the labs, exercises are usually offered as coursework, which may be compulsory or optional. The examination usually consists of a written or oral examination in which the acquired knowledge and the ability to apply methods are tested. Seminars enable you to independently explore a scientific field of media informatics, to grasp the state of research on a current topic and to design, prepare and critically evaluate scientific presentations and texts. In these cases, a presentation on a selected topic is therefore planned as coursework, while the examination consists of a written paper. Project seminars are offered in which students (in teams) gain experience in applied research and independently carry out a research project in preparation for the final thesis. This research project includes a presentation of the planned project, and a project paper or its documentation is usually required as the examination. Our programme Pursuing the Master’s degree in Media Informatics at our university means joining an advanced programme that focuses on the design, development, and evaluation of interactive digital technologies. Instead of concentrating solely on traditional computer science, the programme integrates human‑centred perspectives, creative digital methods, and modern software engineering practices. You gain a deep understanding of how interactive systems are built and how they can be shaped to meet the needs of diverse users and application domains. PDF Download

Academic admission requirements.value:
If you want to study the MSc Media Informatics at the University of Regensburg, you should have:
A Bachelor's degree with a final grade of 2.5 or better (or at least 138 ECTS in your current Bachelor's degree with a provisional final grade of 2.5 or better)
If you have not already studied media informatics or computer science in your Bachelor's degree, but are burning with interest in media informatics, you can be admitted if you fulfil the other requirements.
Completed credits from the field of media informatics amounting to 54 ECTS (With a total of 30 ECTS from media informatics including 6 ECTS in programming, you can be conditionally admitted.)
Proof of English at level B2 CEFR or a Bachelor's thesis written in English
If the language of instruction during your studies was English, you will still need to provide proof of language proficiency (language test certificate or thesis). Only applicants with English as their first language are exempt from providing proof of English language skills. In this case, it is sufficient to upload a copy of your passport.
If you are pursuing or have completed your first university degree (Bachelor’s) outside of Germany, you must submit a preliminary documentation (VPD) from uni-assist (processing time: up to six weeks) as part of your application on the UR Campus Portal.
If you are pursuing or have completed your first university degree (Bachelor’s) in a country that is not a Signatory State to the so-called Lisbon Recognition Convention, you must also prove your academic knowledge by passing the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) General Test.
Further details regarding the requirements as well as further information on the admission procedure, deadlines and necessary documents are available on our website.

Description/content.value:
Planning transportation systems of the future – data-driven and sustainable: The programme provides in-depth knowledge on collecting and analysing data on mobility behaviour. The programme models the mobility behaviour of transportation users and examines its impact on society, the economy, and the environment. In addition, methods of mobility planning are taught, with a particular focus on environmentally friendly and innovative mobility options.
The research-oriented programme covers general engineering methods as well as content and skills in the planning of mobility and transport systems, the design of roads, paths, and railway infrastructure, public transport, strategic mobility planning, data analysis and modelling of transport systems, the operation and management of transport systems, traffic psychology, traffic ecology, scientific work, and project management in the transport sector.

In addition, methods of mobility planning are taught, with a particular focus on environmentally friendly and innovative mobility options.

The research-oriented programme covers general engineering methods as well as content and skills in the planning of mobility and transport systems, the design of roads, paths, and railway infrastructure, public transport, strategic mobility planning, data analysis and modelling of transport systems, the operation and management of transport systems, traffic psychology, traffic ecology, scientific work, and project management in the transport sector.

Course organisation.value: Study contents The programme begins with five compulsory modules on strategic mobility and transport planning, transport psychology and sustainability, local public transport, road infrastructure, and data analysis in transport. Students can then choose from 11 elective modules to explore these and other topics in greater depth. There are over 30 modules available on mobility and transport systems for road, rail, and air transport, geoinformatics, transport economics, civil engineering, and intelligent transport systems. A research project teaches students how to systematically and scientifically examine a current topic in transport research. A professional internship can be optionally incorporated into the programme. The programme ends in the fourth semester with a Master's thesis on a research-related topic from the field of transportation. Internship during studies A voluntary internship (lasting at least eight weeks) can be completed instead of elective modules.

Academic admission requirements.value:
Admission requirements
The prerequisite for admission to the programme is a first university degree recognised in Germany that qualifies the holder for professional practice, or a degree from a state or state-recognised vocational academy in a field related to transportation science, in particular the fields of transportation engineering, transportation economics, or mobility and transportation systems, or a degree in civil engineering, environmental engineering, or industrial engineering, or another university degree with comparable prior knowledge.
Applicants who do not hold a university degree from a university in the European Union or the European Economic Area must also provide proof of a Graduate Record Examination (GRE) score of at least 162 points in quantitative reasoning and at least 151 points in verbal reasoning. The certificate must not be more than five years old. The deadline is the last possible day for application.
In addition, special aptitude is required. Proof of this special aptitude is provided by means of an aptitude assessment procedure in accordance with the Mobility Systems Aptitude Assessment Regulations.
English language skills at level C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) are required. Proof of this must be provided in the form of certificates or language certificates. These may include, in particular, a certificate of a university degree completed entirely in English or a language certificate (see below).
Aptitude assessment procedure
The participation in an aptitude assessment or selection procedure is a prerequisite for enrolment in this degree programme. Please note that the deadline for submitting an application may be earlier than the application deadlines for the degree programme (see above under application deadlines). The following links will provide you with information on all documents to be submitted within the specified deadline and on the relevant regulations.

Description/content.value:
The Executive MBA in Real Estate International is a part-time, internationally focused programme designed for experienced real estate professionals seeking to strengthen their leadership capabilities and drive sustainable value creation in a global business environment.
The programme equips participants with advanced knowledge of real estate finance, investment, and international markets, enabling them to successfully manage real estate companies and complex projects. With a strong emphasis on the USA, the UK, and Asia, the Executive MBA provides a deep understanding of global market dynamics and cross-border investment strategies.
The IREBS Executive MBA in Real Estate International combines academic rigour with strong practical relevance, delivering state-of-the-art real estate expertise and management skills in an international context. Designed specifically for working professionals, the programme is completed over 15 months.
Modules take place in Regensburg, Eltville (near Frankfurt), and Berlin, and include an overseas residency at renowned partner universities such as Harvard University (USA), the University of Reading (UK), and institutions in Singapore. These international modules provide first-hand exposure to global real estate markets and access to an extensive international professional network.
All lectures are conducted in English. Upon successful completion of the programme and the Master’s thesis, graduates are awarded the degree Master of Business Administration (MBA) by the Faculty of Business, Economics, and Information Systems at the University of Regensburg.
Learning Outcomes
Upon successful completion of the Executive MBA in Real Estate, graduates will be able to:
Analyse international real estate markets and assess economic, financial, and demographic drivers of value
Apply advanced real estate finance and investment techniques in a global context
Develop and implement sustainable real estate strategies aligned with long-term business objectives
Lead and manage real estate organisations effectively, applying modern leadership and corporate governance principles
Evaluate global capital markets and financing structures relevant to international real estate investments
Conduct professional negotiations and make informed decisions in cross-border real estate transactions
Integrate urban economics, city valuation, and planning considerations into strategic real estate decisions
Conduct independent academic research and apply analytical methods to real-world business challenges through the Master’s thesis

  • Analyse international real estate markets and assess economic, financial, and demographic drivers of value
  • Apply advanced real estate finance and investment techniques in a global context

Description/content.value:
The Executive MBA in Real Estate Finance is a part-time programme designed for experienced professionals aiming to strengthen their leadership capabilities and deepen their expertise in real estate finance and investment.
The programme prepares participants to shape the real estate industry in a sustainable and value-driven manner by combining advanced economic, financial, and management knowledge with practical application. It provides a solid foundation in real estate and urban economics, combined with state-of-the-art finance methodologies relevant to both national and international markets.
Spanning 15 months, the programme comprises four modules—Business, General Management, Finance, and the Master’s Thesis—and awards 60 ECTS. Its blended learning format integrates on-campus sessions with online components, allowing participants to balance their studies with demanding professional responsibilities.
Courses take place at four locations in Germany: Regensburg, Kloster Eberbach, Frankfurt, and Munich. Throughout the programme, participants address topics such as global capital markets, real estate cycles, sustainability, digitalisation and Big Data, real estate valuation, investment vehicles, portfolio management, and risk-adjusted decision-making. Leadership-focused content includes negotiation management, corporate strategy, governance, and innovation management. Case studies, simulations, and applied projects ensure strong practical relevance.
The programme concludes with a Master’s Thesis, which may focus on a real-world business challenge from the participant’s professional environment, provided it meets academic requirements. All courses are taught in English, and successful graduates are awarded the degree Master of Business Administration (MBA).
Learning Outcomes
Upon completion of the Executive MBA in Real Estate Finance, graduates will be able to:
Analyse real estate markets using economic, financial, and data-driven approaches
Evaluate, value, and structure real estate investments and financing concepts
Apply international valuation methods and capital market-based portfolio models
Assess risks, returns, and sustainability aspects of real estate investments
Manage and optimise real estate portfolios using quantitative and strategic tools
Integrate digitalisation, Big Data, and innovation into finance and investment decisions
Lead real estate organisations with strong strategic, governance, and negotiation skills
Conduct applied research and translate academic insights into executive decision-making

Description/content.value:
The content of the Master's degree programme in Geoinformatics at TU Dresden covers in-depth fundamentals as well as current development and research trends in geoinformatics. The Master's degree programme offers three areas of specialisation:
Geodata acquisition: laser scanning, photogrammetry, optical 3D measurement methods, GNSS and remote sensing as well as methods of data analysis and data integration
Geodata services: modelling, methods and technologies for geodata infrastructures as well as the development of geoinformation services and web applications
Geodata visualisation: methods of geovisual analysis and cartographic communication, methods of automatic generalisation, as well as mobile and field-based cartography
These focal points are supplemented by content from computer science to expand methodological knowledge (e.g. virtual reality, (geo)databases, (geo)software development) and from the environmental sciences as an essential application domain of geoinformatics (e.g. environmental risks, spatial planning). In-depth seminars and projects deal with current research topics in geoinformatics (e.g. sensor networks, GI usability, web applications for decision support, geodata fusion, etc.) In addition, key qualifications are taught in the following areas: foreign languages, management methods, personnel management, marketing, work organisation, contract law, cultures, rhetoric, presentation. In four semesters, the course comprises six compulsory modules and eight compulsory elective modules, in which courses can be selected from compulsory elective catalogues. This allows students to set their own priorities for individual specialisation. The fourth semester is used to complete and defend the Master's thesis.

Accommodation.value:
It is still relatively easy to find affordable accommodation in Dresden. Accommodation is available either via the "Studentenwerk Dresden" or on the private market. Rent for a single room in a student residence is 250 EUR per month on average.
Private housing can be found online. We recommend that you move into a hall of residence at the beginning of your stay in Dresden. Subsequently, you can look for a place on the private market or in a shared apartment, which is known as a "Wohngemeinschaft" in German.

Description/content.value:
The Bachelor's programme in Tourism Management (TM) at Heilbronn University of Applied Sciences consists of a two-semester foundation phase and a five-semester main study phase, including an optional semester abroad and an internship that can also be completed internationally.
Tourism Management offers business fundamentals with a strong focus on tourism industry challenges. Students choose from five foreign languages (English, French, Spanish, Russian or Arabic) and select business specialisations such as International Finance, Marketing, Human Resource Management or International Management. The programme offers a mix of attendance phases, self-study periods and practical experience through excursions or guest lectures in companies in the tourism industry.
Tourism areas:
Destination Management
Tour Operator Management
Business Travel
Tourism, Regional and Location Development
Specific Aspects in Tourism
Tourism Marketing
Health Tourism
Aviation Management

Description/content.value:
This programme is designed to provide students with in-depth subject knowledge and methodological skills that enable them to successfully address the challenges of a globalised world with limited resources. The goal is to foster transdisciplinary skills for the planning, development, and management of sustainable tourism destinations at various levels and to train professionals in sustainability management for companies across all industries.
Upon completion of the programme, graduates will possess the competencies required in an interdisciplinary environment involving diverse stakeholders. They will be able to carry out research-based planning and consulting projects and apply scientific methods to complex challenges faced by tourism management and planning as well as sustainability management, in various organisational contexts.

This programme is designed to provide students with in-depth subject knowledge and methodological skills that enable them to successfully address the challenges of a globalised world with limited resources. The goal is to foster transdisciplinary skills for the planning, development, and management of sustainable tourism destinations at various levels and to train professionals in sustainability management for companies across all industries.

Upon completion of the programme, graduates will possess the competencies required in an interdisciplinary environment involving diverse stakeholders. They will be able to carry out research-based planning and consulting projects and apply scientific methods to complex challenges faced by tourism management and planning as well as sustainability management, in various organisational contexts.

Course organisation.value: Teaching in small groups enables lively discussions and interaction with the lecturers, which contributes to an intensive examination of the subject matter. In addition, both the selection of lecturers and external partners involved in the programme ensure that the content has practical relevance. The courses are taught in German or English. The first semester comprises the following courses, each worth 5 ECTS credits: Fundamentals of Sustainability Management* Spatial Science Basics of Tourism* Digital Transformation Foundations, Business Models and AI in Tourism Municipal Economics and Public Management* Spatial Planning and Law* Research Methods I *taught in German The second semester comprises the following courses, each worth 5 ECTS credits: Natural & Cultural Heritage Management Sustainable Tourism Management Sustainable Tourism Development Project* Research Methods II Specialised topic in Tourism and Sustainability Management 1 (compulsory elective module according to the elective catalogue) Specialised topic in Tourism and Sustainability Management 2 (compulsory elective module according to the elective catalogue) *taught in German In the second semester, students select two modules (5 ECTS credits each) from an elective catalogue that is compiled each year, e.g.: courses from the second semester of the Master's programme International Business and Intercultural Management courses from the Master's programme Tourism Futures Studies courses from Master's programmes in other faculties: Entrepreneurship Strategic Information Management Supply Chain Management An additional semester of study can be added to create an individualised course of study. Students can use this for internships or a stay abroad at one of our partner universities. An optional third semester increases the total number of ECTS credits to 120. In this case, the Master's thesis is completed in the fourth semester. PDF Download
Course organisation.html:
Teaching in small groups enables lively discussions and interaction with the lecturers, which contributes to an intensive examination of the subject matter. In addition, both the selection of lecturers and external partners involved in the programme ensure that the content has practical relevance.

The courses are taught in German or English.

The first semester comprises the following courses, each worth 5 ECTS credits:

  • Fundamentals of Sustainability Management*
  • Spatial Science Basics of Tourism*
  • Digital Transformation Foundations, Business Models and AI in Tourism
  • Municipal Economics and Public Management*
  • Spatial Planning and Law*
  • Research Methods I

*taught in German

The second semester comprises the following courses, each worth 5 ECTS credits:

  • Natural & Cultural Heritage Management
  • Sustainable Tourism Management
  • Sustainable Tourism Development Project*
  • Research Methods II
  • Specialised topic in Tourism and Sustainability Management 1 (compulsory elective module according to the elective catalogue)
  • Specialised topic in Tourism and Sustainability Management 2 (compulsory elective module according to the elective catalogue)

*taught in German

In the second semester, students select two modules (5 ECTS credits each) from an elective catalogue that is compiled each year, e.g.:

  • courses from the second semester of the Master's programme International Business and Intercultural Management
  • courses from the Master's programme Tourism Futures Studies
  • courses from Master's programmes in other faculties:
    • Entrepreneurship
    • Strategic Information Management
    • Supply Chain Management

An additional semester of study can be added to create an individualised course of study. Students can use this for internships or a stay abroad at one of our partner universities. An optional third semester increases the total number of ECTS credits to 120. In this case, the Master's thesis is completed in the fourth semester.

Description/content.value:
With more than 50 modules and over 100 individual courses, our MSc programme offers a diverse and flexible portfolio that allows you to shape your studies according to your personal interests, strengths, and career ambitions. This wide selection ensures that you can build a truly individualised academic path while gaining both depth and breadth in geosciences.
Within the MSc Geoscience programme, we offer several overarching research directions, each encompassing a range of specialised fields that you can focus on:
Geophysics: including Experimental Geophysics, Earthquake Processes, and Tectonic Geodesy
Applied Geosciences: including Engineering Geology and Rock Mechanics, as well as Hydrogeology and Environmental Geology
Earth Surface Processes: including Geomorphology and Geohazards, Sedimentology and Isotope Geochemistry, and Sedimentary Geochemistry
Geodynamics, Geomaterials, and High-Temperature Processes: including Tectonics and Resources, Structural Geology, Petrology, High-Temperature Geochemistry, and Crystallography
Applied Geothermics: a binational MSc track offered in collaboration with our partner university, UNSJ (Argentina)
This structure enables you to specialise in a focused area while maintaining interdisciplinary connections across the geosciences.
Description/content.html:
With more than 50 modules and over 100 individual courses, our MSc programme offers a diverse and flexible portfolio that allows you to shape your studies according to your personal interests, strengths, and career ambitions. This wide selection ensures that you can build a truly individualised academic path while gaining both depth and breadth in geosciences.

Within the MSc Geoscience programme, we offer several overarching research directions, each encompassing a range of specialised fields that you can focus on:

  1. Geophysics: including Experimental Geophysics, Earthquake Processes, and Tectonic Geodesy
  2. Applied Geosciences: including Engineering Geology and Rock Mechanics, as well as Hydrogeology and Environmental Geology
  3. Earth Surface Processes: including Geomorphology and Geohazards, Sedimentology and Isotope Geochemistry, and Sedimentary Geochemistry
  4. Geodynamics, Geomaterials, and High-Temperature Processes: including Tectonics and Resources, Structural Geology, Petrology, High-Temperature Geochemistry, and Crystallography
  5. Applied Geothermics: a binational MSc track offered in collaboration with our partner university, UNSJ (Argentina)

This structure enables you to specialise in a focused area while maintaining interdisciplinary connections across the geosciences.

Course organisation.value:
At the start of your studies, you will work closely with a prospective thesis adviser to design a personalised study plan tailored to your interests, specialisation, and envisioned Master’s thesis project.
During your first year, you will build a strong foundation of advanced knowledge across multiple geoscience disciplines through a dynamic mix of lectures, hands-on exercises, seminars, introductions to various programming languages, and targeted fieldwork. In your third semester, you will refine your academic focus by selecting further electives and shaping a research- or professional-oriented study path — often including laboratory work and training in our state-of-the-art analytical facilities.
Your individualised MSc thesis project, developed in close collaboration with your adviser, will form the centrepiece of your fourth semester.

Accommodation.value:
In the city of Bochum, you can find different types of accommodation. On average, students in Bochum pay approximately 400 to 800 EUR per month for a single apartment, which is below the average rent in Germany. A room in a shared apartment is usually less expensive.
About 5,000 students in Bochum live in multiple student halls close to the campus, which are run by the Akademisches Förderungswerk (AKAFÖ). In the halls, each student has a single room and shares a kitchen and bathroom with other students, rents an apartment with a private bathroom and kitchen, or shares an apartment with one or several flatmates.
More information on the student halls can be found at https://studium.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/de/wohnen.
In addition, private and church-affiliated student halls accommodate up to 1,000 students: http://www.stuwo.de/wohnheim-region/bochum/.

ACCOMMODATION @ RPTU in KAISERSLAUTERN:
The majority of our students live in residence halls located on or close to campus. The "Studierendenwerk" operates several large halls of residence in Kaiserslautern. Description/content.value:
The English-language Master's degree programme in Mechatronics is designed for alumni of Bachelor’s programmes in engineering who wish to deepen their knowledge in the field of intelligent mechatronic systems. Over the course of four semesters, you will acquire in-depth expertise in classical mechatronics — with a special focus on autonomous robotics and automated driving.
The programme centres on the development, operation, and further advancement of intelligent technical systems. Key future-oriented topics such as artificial intelligence, automation, and modern control technology are specifically addressed in the modules and taught in a practical manner.
A central component of the programme is the one-year laboratory internship in the second and third semesters. In state-of-the-art laboratory facilities, you will work on practical tasks and have the opportunity to set your own individual academic focuses. This will allow you to deepen your knowledge in a targeted manner and gain valuable practical experience in working with complex Mechatronics systems.

International students in Germany are allowed to work part-time during their studies. Non-EU students may work up to 140 full days or 280 half days per year, or up to 20 hours per week during the semester. Exceeding this limit may require additional insurance contributions.

Description/content.value:
The Bachelor Plus STEM programme is an eight-semester (four-year) Bachelor's programme in which students are first introduced to the broad field of STEM subjects (known as MINT subjects in German). After the first year, students choose one main subject, such as physics, chemistry, computer science or mathematics, and pursue their studies in this field (the complete list is available on our website). Upon completion of the programme, students receive a Bachelor of Science degree and are eligible to enrol on the respective corresponding Master's programme, as well as the one-year research Master's BioMed programme.
The programme consists of 240 ECTS credits, 120 to 180 of which (depending on your chosen subject) are dedicated to your main subject. The remaining ECTS credits can be earned through any other courses on campus, meaning that the programme allows students to have a core subject while also pursuing their other interests and learning more about other subjects on campus. Popular additional subjects include economics, philosophy, law and pharmacy. If you have any questions regarding the freedom of choice, please do not hesitate to contact us.
