Description/content.value:
Are you interested in understanding social contexts and conducting your own scientific research? The Master's programme in Sociology enables you to deepen your theoretical knowledge and methodological skills in order to independently analyse and empirically investigate social processes and inequalities.
Special Features & Major Fields of Study
Master's degree qualifying for both professional practice and research
strong emphasis on quantitative methods in empirical social research
option to specialise in Empirical Social Research (indicated on final degree certificate)
systematic integration of theory and empirical research with clear orientation toward the requirements of scientific research practice
strengthening the individual profile through selection of a major field of study
Family, Education and Work
Health, Population and Migration
Globalisation, Media and Digital Transformation
Employment, Organisation and Social Policy
close integration of research and teaching through experienced and internationally recognised lecturers with connections to key research institutes in the region
promotion of research-relevant competencies for scientific work or potential further academic qualification beyond the Master's degree
practical module for applying theoretical and methodological knowledge acquired during the course of study
also available as an international double degree programme
Description/content.html:
Are you interested in understanding social contexts and conducting your own scientific research? The Master's programme in Sociology enables you to deepen your theoretical knowledge and methodological skills in order to independently analyse and empirically investigate social processes and inequalities.

Special Features & Major Fields of Study

  • Master's degree qualifying for both professional practice and research
  • strong emphasis on quantitative methods in empirical social research
  • option to specialise in Empirical Social Research (indicated on final degree certificate)
  • systematic integration of theory and empirical research with clear orientation toward the requirements of scientific research practice
  • strengthening the individual profile through selection of a major field of study
    • Family, Education and Work
    • Health, Population and Migration
    • Globalisation, Media and Digital Transformation
    • Employment, Organisation and Social Policy
  • close integration of research and teaching through experienced and internationally recognised lecturers with connections to key research institutes in the region
  • promotion of research-relevant competencies for scientific work or potential further academic qualification beyond the Master's degree
  • practical module for applying theoretical and methodological knowledge acquired during the course of study
  • also available as an international double degree programme

Course organisation.value:
The two-year Master's degree programme (120 ECTS) usually takes place entirely in Bamberg. Teaching consists of a balanced mix of lectures and seminars.
Apart from the compulsory sociological and methodological programme in the first and second semester (30 ECTS), the programme provides flexibility regarding content and organisation of studies.
The sociological modules (42 to 60 ECTS) offered are based in the fields of Family, Education and Work, Health, Population and Migration, Globalisation, Media and Digital Transformation, Employment, Organisation and Social Policy.
The individual academic profile can be supplemented by classes in related economics and social science disciplines (up to 36 ECTS) or courses taken during an optional semester abroad. This supports the interdisciplinary aspect and extends the chosen area of the main focus, thereby making good use of the large potential of the curriculum available at the Faculty for Social Sciences, Economics, and Business Administration at the University of Bamberg.
The Master's thesis (30 ECTS) has to be written over the course of six months at the end of the programme.
Upon graduation, the faculty will award a Master of Science (MSc) degree in Sociology and Social Research (MSSR).

It is thus advisable to begin looking for a flat as early as possible and to be patient, as the process can take quite a while. It also pays to check listings in the local newspaper (Fränkischer Tag), submit an announcement that you are looking for accommodation, or explore the numerous online housing portals.
www.uni-bamberg.de/en/studies/living-studying/living-in-bamberg/

Description/content.value:
The English-language Master's course in Sustainable Chemistry aims to provide students with the specialist expertise that will enable them to develop well-founded sustainability concepts on a scientific basis. For many of the pressing sustainability goals (energy, climate, environment, nutrition), promising solution strategies can only be developed and solutions found with a sound knowledge of chemistry.
Building on a Bachelor's degree programme in natural sciences, the degree programme will therefore focus on the pressing social issues involved in transforming our current way of life into a sustainable one and address these from the perspective of chemistry. This includes aspects of sustainable ways in the production of chemicals by means of modern synthetic tools such as biocatalysis and flow chemistry as well as the design of "green products" based on renewable feedstocks, e.g. biorenewable-based building blocks for the manufacture of bio-based plastics. Complementing these urgent challenges in the transformation of the chemical industry, further aspects address climate change and renewable energy sources and technologies such as artificial photosynthesis. Besides chemical sciences related to sustainability themes, the programme also contains tools for evaluating the sustainability of chemicals and processes by eco-efficiency analysis tools and environmental metrics. Accordingly, the planned modules will be dedicated to specific sustainability goals, to which the necessary specialised content will be subordinated.

Costs of living.value:
Costs for studying in Germany are relatively high due to the living expenses.
Rent in a room in student halls of residence or a private student hall, in a room or flat comes to approx. 290 EUR per month.
The expected costs for student health insurance and other medical fees are about 140 EUR per month.
Depending on your lifestyle, you might spend about 150 EUR on food each month.
Altogether, monthly costs for food, clothes, leisure activities, social fees, travel expenses, telephone bills, and the other mentioned expenses add up to approx. 992 EUR.
There are several ways of cutting expenses in Bielefeld. For example, it is possible to rent a room in a student residence for about 250 EUR, and a meal at the student canteen (Mensa) costs only about 3 EUR.

Description/content.value:
The Master's degree programme in Physics aims to provide students with advanced specialist knowledge, skills and methods that are required for scientific work and scientifically oriented jobs. The programme enables them to critically classify new scientific findings and use them in their professional careers. Knowledge and skills that are acquired through the Master's programme and developed beyond the Bachelor's level are in particular:
Advanced basic knowledge of physics
Advanced knowledge in several branches of physics
In-depth knowledge at an international level in one field of physics, which leads to the current state of research
Knowledge of modern methodology in one or more specialised areas of physics
The ability to use current scientific material appropriately for one's own work
The ability to work creatively, independently and autonomously
The ability to develop, apply and appropriately present scientific results
The ability to work on a comprehensive and demanding project in a focussed manner using appropriate scientific methods
The ability to organise and carry out an independent project in the context of a larger working group

Course organisation.value: The physics degree programme offers a high degree of flexibility in elective course selection. Typically, the first two semesters focus on core modules in experimental and theoretical physics, complemented by a mandatory physics lab course. Furthermore, students begin advanced specialised courses, a portion of which may be selected from the broader range of STEM (MINT) faculties. The second year is dedicated to the methodology and specialisation modules, culminating in the Master’s thesis. These two preparatory modules are closely integrated with the research phase of the thesis itself.

Expertise in conducting physical experiments and a basic, substantive understanding of the physical relationships in all of the following areas of experimental physics: mechanics, electrodynamics, optics, quantum physics, thermodynamics and atomic physics
Basic understanding of theoretical deductive concepts in all of the following areas of physics: mechanics, electrodynamics, quantum mechanics and statistical mechanics
Substantive skills in calculus and linear algebra, including the ability to conduct proofs in these areas

Description/content.value:
Applied Linguistics is an interdisciplinary field of research and practice, dealing with problems relating to language and communication in society, the media, organisations, business, and politics. Students in this MA programme are given the tools to identify problems and work on solving them by applying linguistic theories and employing empirical and experimental methods.
The programme aims at developing knowledge of the theories and methods used in intercultural communication, second language acquisition, language processing, and translation studies. Course topics include interpersonal communication, regional and social variation in language behaviour, (im)politeness across cultures, pragmatic competence, writing in a second language, and cognitive processes in translating.
Students are given an overview of the field of Applied Linguistics and may choose to specialise in a wide range of subdisciplines. The core modules are intercultural communication, second language acquisition, language processing, and translation studies. Teaching and research supervision are also offered in pragmatics, discourse analysis, genre analysis, sociolinguistics, dialectology, cognitive linguistics, psycholinguistics, and metalexicography.

Academic admission requirements.value:
A BA in English Studies from the University of Bonn is suitable if it includes linguistic modules amounting to at least 18 credit points (ECTS).
Other BA degrees are accepted if they include at least 36 ECTS in relevant areas, i.e., a minimum of 18 ECTS in practical English language courses and 18 ECTS in linguistic subjects.
Please note: One ECTS credit point amounts to 25 - 30 hours of coursework.
Important: This programme focuses on scientific research in linguistics, not practical applications like translation or language teaching. If your BA is in these fields, you must demonstrate a strong background in linguistics.
If you already have a Master’s degree in another field, you can apply if you meet the BA-level linguistic requirements. However, you cannot apply if you already have an MA in Applied Linguistics.

General services and support for interna.value:
The University of Bonn offers a range of different support programmes for international students. The Welcome Days (www.uni-bonn.de/welcomedays) before the start of every semester are an opportunity for new students from abroad to gather information on the most important issues, such as enrolment, registration with the local authorities and opening a bank account. Getting to know fellow international and German students during recreational activities is another benefit of the Welcome Days.
The Study Buddy Programme (www.uni-bonn.de/study-buddy) matches newly arrived international students (“Mentees”) with a University of Bonn student (“Buddy”) who helps them as they start their studies and adjust to life in Bonn.

Description/content.value:
Our programme, accredited by the Technical University of Dortmund, provides you with the essential skills to plan future-oriented sites and infrastructure for sustainable energy systems, with a particular focus on hydrogen technology. As the transition to climate-neutral energy systems presents significant challenges, hydrogen offers a key solution for many industrial and transport applications that still rely on gaseous and liquid fuels.
Hands-on experience is at the heart of our programme. Through immersive projects, partnerships with industry leaders and exposure to current research, you can put your knowledge to work and position yourself as a driving force in the energy transition. We also emphasise the development of your leadership and intercultural skills to prepare you for success in an international environment.
The curriculum combines technological expertise with practical planning skills in scenario development, public participation and fostering societal acceptance. These skills, which are at the heart of our School of Spatial Planning, are crucial to the implementation of effective sustainable energy strategies.
With a multidisciplinary, global perspective on current research topics, you will be fully equipped to tackle real-world projects and independently address complex issues. Join an innovative programme that provides not only the key skills for a career in energy but also the knowledge and tools to help shape a sustainable future. Take advantage of this unique opportunity and start your career in one of the world’s most dynamic industries.

Course organisation.value:
The international MSc in Sustainable Energy and Hydrogen Infrastructure prepares you to play a key role in the global energy transition. Become a sought-after expert in one of today’s most dynamic industries, equipped with in-depth knowledge and practical skills in sustainable energy systems and hydrogen technologies.
Our programme emphasises the development of innovative, practical solutions: you will learn how to actively shape the transition to clean energy, plan infrastructure and combine technical efficiency with sustainability. Through interdisciplinary teamwork and international collaboration, you’ll learn how technological, economic and environmental factors interact — and how to apply them to real-world challenges.
Programme Structure
The three-semester full-time programme is clearly structured and comprises 90 ECTS credits, building on the required 210 ECTS credits of the Bachelor’s degree.
First Two Semesters: In the first and second semesters, students complete ten modules (50 ECTS), including eight compulsory modules on key topics in sustainable energy systems and two compulsory elective modules in the area of "skills for the German labour market". The focus here is on content such as international project management and the development of skills for business consultancy projects, which are specifically tailored to the requirements of the German labour market. A central element of the second semester is the project module (10 ECTS), in which students can choose either a practical or an academic focus. This practical module promotes the consolidation of the acquired professional knowledge and enables the application of theoretical content in real project scenarios in cooperation with the partner companies.
Third Semester: This semester is dedicated to completing the Master’s thesis and participating in a scientific colloquium, worth 20 ECTS credits. Additionally, students complete two elective modules (5 ECTS each) to further broaden their expertise.

Academic admission requirements.value:
Students can only be admitted to the Master’s degree programme "MSc Sustainability Energy and Hydrogen Infrastructure" if they have fulfilled the following:
They must have completed a Bachelor’s degree, a state examination programme, or an equivalent qualification in one of the following fields: preferably engineering sciences (spatial planning, process engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering), natural sciences (geography, physics, chemistry), or economics (specialising in energy management). The examination board decides on equivalence of related subjects.
They must have specialised knowledge in the fields of spatial and infrastructure planning, energy technology, energy economics.
They should demonstrate English language proficiency at B2 level. This must be proven by a recognised language certificate (see details below) or by official confirmation from the applicant’s institution that the undergraduate degree was taught in English. The examination board will decide on the equivalence of other qualifications.
Applicants must be able to provide evidence of at least one year of relevant professional experience. The document should be from the company for which you worked and include the period of employment (start and end dates) as well as your tasks.

Accommodation.value:
In the city of Bochum, you can find different types of accommodation. On average, students in Bochum pay approximately 400 to 800 EUR per month for a single apartment, which is below the average rent in Germany. A room in a shared apartment is usually less expensive.
About 5,000 students in Bochum live in multiple student halls close to the campus, which are run by the Akademisches Förderungswerk (AKAFÖ). In the halls, each student has a single room and shares a kitchen and bathroom with other students, rents an apartment with a private bathroom and kitchen, or shares an apartment with one or several flatmates.
More information on the student halls can be found at https://studium.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/de/wohnen.
In addition, private and church-affiliated student halls accommodate up to 1,000 students: http://www.stuwo.de/wohnheim-region/bochum/.

Description/content.value:
Components of the Master of Arts in English and American Studies include the English language, its description and analysis in the context of current research, and the academic study of anglophone literatures and cultures from the Middle Ages to the present. The curriculum allows students a great deal of flexibility; they can choose to study the field in a broad, all-encompassing manner, or they may specialise in either linguistics or literature and cultural studies. Emphasis is placed on demanding language courses for practical purposes, which means students must have an excellent command of English before starting the programme.
A number of cooperation agreements with other departments, including those of German Linguistics and German Literature as well as the departments of History and Geography, enrich the course offering in the fields of literature and cultural studies. Please note, however, that most of the courses taught by other departments are conducted in German.

Description/content.value:
In the light of the global environmental and resource crises, sustainable development has been adopted internationally as a guiding principle. Today, sustainability or sustainable development means, above all, meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
The "Sustainable Materials Engineering" Master’s programme aims to improve sustainability in the extraction, production, processing, sustainable use, and recycling of materials. This includes knowledge of (a) the synthesis and characterisation of sustainable materials for various applications (particularly regarding their chemical, mechanical, and thermal manufacturing and processing methods), (b) the optimisation of structure-property relationships with regard to the sustainability and performance of the raw materials used, as well as (c) an understanding of the behaviour, durability, degradation, and recyclability of materials under various environmental conditions.
A key objective of the programme is to provide students with a solid technical education in the sustainable use of the world’s limited resources. These concepts are applied to various key materials: polymers, composites, metals, and optical glasses — supplemented by aspects of circular economy. A particular emphasis is placed on new technologies that enable future scientists and engineers to develop more environmentally friendly and sustainable materials and processes.
During their studies, students will acquire the following qualifications:
knowledge and skills for optimising the chemical composition and processing of polymers, composites, and metals
developing techniques to optimise the service life and recyclability of these materials
developing innovative bio-inspired materials
Description/content.html:
In the light of the global environmental and resource crises, sustainable development has been adopted internationally as a guiding principle. Today, sustainability or sustainable development means, above all, meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

The "Sustainable Materials Engineering" Master’s programme aims to improve sustainability in the extraction, production, processing, sustainable use, and recycling of materials. This includes knowledge of (a) the synthesis and characterisation of sustainable materials for various applications (particularly regarding their chemical, mechanical, and thermal manufacturing and processing methods), (b) the optimisation of structure-property relationships with regard to the sustainability and performance of the raw materials used, as well as (c) an understanding of the behaviour, durability, degradation, and recyclability of materials under various environmental conditions.

A key objective of the programme is to provide students with a solid technical education in the sustainable use of the world’s limited resources. These concepts are applied to various key materials: polymers, composites, metals, and optical glasses — supplemented by aspects of circular economy. A particular emphasis is placed on new technologies that enable future scientists and engineers to develop more environmentally friendly and sustainable materials and processes.

During their studies, students will acquire the following qualifications:

  • knowledge and skills for optimising the chemical composition and processing of polymers, composites, and metals
  • developing techniques to optimise the service life and recyclability of these materials
  • developing innovative bio-inspired materials

Course organisation.value:
The international Master’s programme in "Sustainable Materials Engineering" is taught in English, and it offers its contents in either three (full-time) or six (part-time) semesters. It is equally suitable for both domestic and international students with sufficient English proficiency (minimum B2 level). The programme modules focus on specific types of materials, particularly those derived from renewable raw materials. Relationships between (biogenic) material structure and properties, biomimetic development principles, and sustainable production and processing technologies are addressed, taking into account circular value creation.
The modules in the first semester cover various aspects of sustainability in the production, use, and recycling of conventional, bio-inspired, and bio-based polymeric materials. In the second semester, students have the opportunity to focus their studies on different areas — drawn from current research projects — as part of the “Research Lab Course” module. Students can choose to specialise in one of the following four areas:
Sustainable Functional Polymers
Bio-Inspired Functional Materials
Sustainable Optical Materials
Materials of Electrical Engineering
Furthermore, it is also possible to complete the “Research Lab Course” at a (partner) company during the second semester. In the Master’s thesis, students can further deepen their understanding of the chosen focus area. In addition to technical expertise, the thesis also fosters independent, critical thinking and enhances project management skills.

Description/content.value:
The way we produce and consume today determines how liveable our world will be tomorrow. Resources are becoming scarcer, the impact our lives have on the environment is increasing, and many existing economic models are reaching their limits. The circular economy offers a promising solution: it combines technical innovations with economic and organisational strategies to keep raw materials and resources in circulation for as long as possible. To achieve this, products and how we use them need to be reimagined from the very beginning — and this is precisely where the English-language Master’s programme in Circular Engineering and Economy comes in.
The transition to a functioning circular economy is highly complex and it requires a lot of work from everyone who is involved in making it a reality. To master these challenges, we need training that meaningfully combines engineering, economics, and management while focusing on a sustainable circular economy across the entire value chain — from raw material extraction right up to recycling. To make the circular economy a reality, recycling must be factored in as early as the product design stage so that waste streams and our consumption of resources can be reduced. Students in the Circular Engineering and Economy Master’s programme learn to understand processes in their entirety and to make economic decisions that are based on technical expertise. This is because a circular economy is only feasible if economic goals are based on a sound understanding of technical feasibility as well as material- and process-related limitations. Over the course of two years, students acquire a solid, versatile education that prepares them for the challenges of a sustainable future in the best possible way.

To meet the academic prerequisites, applicants must demonstrate the competencies required for successful completion of the Master’s programme in Circular Engineering and Economy in the following subject areas.
A total of 50 CP in engineering and subject-specific fundamentals:

Mechanics
Mechanical Engineering
Electrical Engineering
Thermal Engineering
Process Engineering
Transport Phenomena
Mathematics
• At least 14 credits from the “Specialised Fundamentals” area:
Energy Economics
Introduction to Business Administration
Business Engineering
Quality and Project Management
Communication and Organisational Development
Raw Materials and Energy Law
Quantitative and Numerical Methods
Measurement, Control, and Regulation
Simulation Technology
Introduction to Programming
The proven achievements must be comparable to those of the Bachelor's degree programmes in “Sustainable Raw Materials and Energy Supply” and “Mechanical Engineering” at RWTH Aachen University.
If applicants are required to catch up with more than 30 CP, admission to the Master's programme is not possible.
In addition, proof of sufficient command of the German language must be provided (details below).

Description/content.value:
The Joint Master's programme in Water Security and Global Change offers a truly international learning experience. It immerses students in a dynamic educational environment that addresses the urgent and vital issue of water security, bridging perspectives from both the global South and global North. Drawing on the collective expertise of all partner institutions, the new Master's programme adopts an integrated and comprehensive approach to meet the needs of regional, national, and international stakeholders.
Building upon existing modules, the programme features a modular structure with opportunities for specialisation. Student mobility is coordinated as part of this collaborative effort, alongside the development and implementation of communication, dissemination, and marketing strategies. Courses are taught by experts from the participating institutions, ensuring a high standard of education.
Master's theses are conducted in close collaboration with selected companies, governmental agencies, and NGOs, providing students with practical experience and real-world connections. Through a joint curriculum, the programme is established across three degree-awarding universities (RWTH Aachen, IIT Madras, TU Dresden), with two associated partners (UNU Flores and AIT Bangkok). Upon completion, students receive a joint degree.
What does this programme offer?
Gain comprehensive insight into the hydrological cycle, water system components, and their interactions with the environment, society, and ecosystems
Explore the repercussions of global change on water resources and ecosystems
Gain an understanding of the effects of temperature shifts, precipitation patterns, and sea level rise on water availability and quality
Learn about water resource governance structures, policies, and regulations at various levels and their implications for water security
Study water pollution sources, their impacts on human health and the environment, and strategies for monitoring and enhancing water quality
Develop skills in managing and optimising water resources, including sustainable water use, conservation, and integrated management strategies
Learn to assess and mitigate water-related risks such as floods, droughts, and water scarcity, and build resilience in water systems
Collaborate across disciplines, integrating knowledge from environmental science, engineering, policy, economics, and social sciences to address water security challenges
Enhance research skills and analytical abilities to investigate complex water-related problems and propose evidence-based solutions
Explore ethical, social, and equity aspects of water security, acknowledging access to clean water as a fundamental human right

Course organisation.value:
The Joint Master's programme has a scope of earning 120 ECTS points / 213 IITM credits in total. It consists of three semesters of course work with 90 ECTS points / 159 IITM credits in total and a fourth semester of thesis of 30 ECTS / 54 IITM credits. Each semester consists of 30 ECTS points / 54 IITM credits of course work with courses of 5 or 7.5 ECTS points. 30 ECTS (approx. 51 to 54 IITM credits) per semester may change according to the agreed schedule (see programme timeline table). Coursework consists of mandatory and elective courses, which are offered equally by all three partner universities and sum up to 30 ECTS points / 53 IITM credits provided by each partner university. The programme enables to define up to 30 ECTS points / 53 IITM credits elective courses.

Accommodation.value:
Availability of university accommodation in Aachen is limited. Therefore, participation in individual allocation procedures is usually required. Because of the demand for university accommodation, it can be necessary to switch to the private accommodation market. Especially family and couples apartments are very high in demand, so that accommodation from the private market is seemingly mandatory. The majority of RWTH Aachen University's students are committed to the private accommodation market. There are a number of options for finding private accommodation in and around Aachen; the International Office can provide students with information beforehand or upon their arrival.
Prices for university accommodation vary between 300 EUR and 500 EUR per month, accommodation on the private market is priced between 350 EUR and 600 EUR per month, of course depending on the size and the number of rooms.
For short-term accommodation, there are many hotels, a few youth hostels, and a boardinghouse located in and around Aachen (reservation is recommended).
Please visit https://www.rwth-aachen.de/housing for further information.

Description/content.value:
The Anglophone Postcolonial Studies programme at the University of Potsdam enables students to adopt a non-Eurocentric view of the (English-speaking) world and to examine global phenomena from a postcolonial perspective. The focus is on the complex entanglements between the (postcolonial) past, present and future. Whether dealing with literary works, cultural dynamics, ecological challenges or media and historical phenomena — graduates learn to view these not as isolated events but also to analyse them from multiple perspectives as part of a culturally interwoven complex. Through their engagement with various historical, disciplinary, and regional contexts, they develop transcultural competencies (“transcultural literacy”), which enable them to understand cultures as inherently incomplete, hybrid and co-constitutive entities.
The programme is complemented by practice-oriented elements such as outreach projects, science communication, and project- and media-based work. It qualifies graduates for advanced MA programmes in literary and cultural studies in Germany and abroad, particularly the institute’s own Master’s programme in Anglophone Modernities in Literature and Culture. However, the programme also opens up career opportunities wherever an in-depth understanding of the diverse range of literary, ecological, cultural, historical, and media developments in the English-speaking world (and beyond) is required. Relevant professional fields include specialised journalism, publishing, the non-profit sector, cultural education, advertising and public relations, as well as, for example, human resources in companies. Cooperation with international partner universities and institutions also qualifies graduates for positions in international organisations and in academic management as well as in archives and libraries.

If you are a Master's student, you can only apply if the degree at the University of Potsdam is your first Master's programme. The housing market is very tight, so please start looking for an accommodation as early as possible.

Description/content.value:
The Global Business Management Master's programme offers a range of small group formats, such as projects, seminars, and colloquia, to help you become a competent leader. A key focus is teaching the latest management skills, the ability to develop strategic structures at different levels, tolerance of ambiguity, as well as reflective and critical thinking. Aspects of sustainability management, innovation, and entrepreneurial thinking are at the forefront of the intensive work in small groups. Optional one-on-one coaching by experienced executive trainers is also available on request.
Graduates of the Global Business Management Master's programme are successfully employed in leadership roles at large and established companies and organisations such as Allianz, PwC, Everllence, SAP, the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), and many others. Many also pursue a doctorate in Germany or abroad, or join a start-up after completing the programme.

If necessary, additional modules may have to be completed in individual qualification areas in order to demonstrate the relevant aptitude.

Description/content.value: Major global challenges such as climate change, habitat loss and biodiversity decline require a deep scientific understanding of ecological systems. The international and research-oriented Master's programme in “Ecology and Biodiversity” enables you to gain in-depth knowledge of ecological concepts, evolutionary relationships and the causes and consequences of biodiversity change in terrestrial and aquatic systems, as well as advanced practical skills to analyse biological diversity and ecological processes from the level of individual organisms to complex ecosystems.
Description/content.html: Major global challenges such as climate change, habitat loss and biodiversity decline require a deep scientific understanding of ecological systems. The international and research-oriented Master's programme in “Ecology and Biodiversity” enables you to gain in-depth knowledge of ecological concepts, evolutionary relationships and the causes and consequences of biodiversity change in terrestrial and aquatic systems, as well as advanced practical skills to analyse biological diversity and ecological processes from the level of individual organisms to complex ecosystems.

Course organisation.value: There is a strong emphasis on laboratory- and field-based work using a wide range of modern methodologies and techniques. You will gain experience in ecological data collection, experimental design and advanced statistical analysis. Field studies, excursions and research internships enable you to apply your theoretical knowledge directly in real-world contexts and to conduct your own research projects. A distinctive feature of the programme is its broad elective area, which allows you to shape your individual academic profile. In addition to specialised modules within “Ecology and Biodiversity”, you can choose modules from the Master's programmes in “Molecular and Cellular Biology” and “Synthetic Biology”, enabling you to explore interdisciplinary perspectives across the life sciences. However, this degree programme goes beyond the acquisition of scientific knowledge. Starting with an introductory module for all new Master’s students, the programme strengthens your intercultural awareness and teamwork skills and encourages personal and professional development from the very beginning. Academic admission requirements.value:
The application for the Master's programme in Ecology and Biodiversity is exclusively done via the application portal TUCaN of TU Darmstadt. The application documents must be submitted to Student Service/ Admission International. Only complete application documents will be processed.
The following documents are required for the application:
Proof of a university degree (Bachelor's degree in biology or a related subject)
Equivalency list of required admission competencies as per the template (becomes visible during the application process in TUCaN)
Summary of the content of the Bachelor's thesis (in English, max. one page)
Proof of proficiency in English (details below)
Evidence of at least six weeks of relevant practical laboratory and field experience, if this cannot be demonstrated as part of the Bachelor's degree
Current transcript of records
Diploma supplement (if available)
Online self-assessment
The entrance examination takes place in two stages.
Stage 1:
Applicants' submitted application materials are independently reviewed and scored by two committee members. A score of 0 to a maximum of 100 points is assigned. Applicants with a minimum score of 80 will be directly classified as suitable.
In cases where individual subject requirements from the first degree programme are not met, applicants may be admitted with the requirement to take foundation examinations in additional subjects for the Bachelor's degree programme in biology for a maximum of 30 credits.
Stage 2:
Applicants who do not achieve a score of 80 points and do not fall below 40 points will be invited to an entrance interview. The 30-minute interview with at least two members of the committee will assess the applicant's suitability for the programme based on the entry competencies.

Accommodation.value:
TU Darmstadt's International Affairs Department assists international students in their search for accommodation through its Housing Assistance Office. A major science hub, Darmstadt is home to multiple research institutions, three universities, and many high-technology companies, all of which attract people from around the world. A wide variety of accommodations that vary in size, furnishing, and rent are available in Darmstadt and its vicinity. As the university does not own or manage student housing, we support students in finding housing in private and public student dormitories or on the private market. In order to improve your chances in finding the optimal place to live, we recommend that you start your search early. We are happy to assist you in this process. Please make sure to register online on the housing assistance website for international students.
Our services include the distribution of an “Accommodation Guide” that includes links to private and public student dormitories, hotels and youth hostels, and a “Housing Guide” that provides tips on how to search for accommodation in Darmstadt.

The international and research-oriented Master's programme “Molecular and Cellular Biology” enables you to gain in-depth knowledge and advanced skills to analyse complex biological processes and to contribute to cutting-edge life science research.
Description/content.html: Understanding life at the molecular and cellular level is key to addressing major challenges in medicine, biotechnology and fundamental research. The international and research-oriented Master's programme “Molecular and Cellular Biology” enables you to gain in-depth knowledge and advanced skills to analyse complex biological processes and to contribute to cutting-edge life science research.

Course organisation.value: There is a strong emphasis on laboratory-based work using a broad spectrum of modern molecular and cellular methodologies. In addition, you will deepen your competencies in quantitative data analysis, experimental design and research data management. Through extensive research internships and project-based modules, you will gain hands-on experience and learn how to independently plan and conduct scientific studies. A distinctive feature of the programme is its broad elective area, which allows you to tailor your studies individually. In addition to specialised modules within molecular and cellular biology, you can choose modules from the Master’s programmes in “Synthetic Biology” and “Ecology and Biodiversity”, enabling you to expand your profile across disciplines and explore interfaces within the life sciences. However, this degree programme goes beyond the acquisition of scientific knowledge. Starting with an introductory module for all new Master’s students, the programme strengthens your intercultural awareness and teamwork skills and encourages personal and professional development from the very beginning. Description/content.value: Numerous urgent problems of our time can only be solved with an interdisciplinary approach in an international context. The international and interdisciplinary Master's programme in “Synthetic Biology” will allow you to gain knowledge and skills to address these complex challenges in life science research using the principles of synthetic biology.
Description/content.html: Numerous urgent problems of our time can only be solved with an interdisciplinary approach in an international context. The international and interdisciplinary Master's programme in “Synthetic Biology” will allow you to gain knowledge and skills to address these complex challenges in life science research using the principles of synthetic biology.

Course organisation.value: The English-taught degree programme combines current knowledge from the fields of molecular biology, engineering, and materials sciences. By bringing the disciplines together, an engineering approach can be used to endow biological cells with new molecular functions. There is an emphasis on laboratory-based work using a wide range of modern methodologies and techniques. In addition, you will develop an understanding of mathematical modelling of biological systems and the application of engineering principles to solve biological problems. This degree programme not only teaches scientific knowledge. You will gain the ability to think creatively, be innovative, and work independently. Through our strong focus on practical experience and research, you will be able to transfer your theoretical knowledge into practice and develop your own projects. Project work is completed with training in intercultural and scientific communication.

This degree programme not only teaches scientific knowledge. You will gain the ability to think creatively, be innovative, and work independently. Through our strong focus on practical experience and research, you will be able to transfer your theoretical knowledge into practice and develop your own projects. Project work is completed with training in intercultural and scientific communication.

Description/content.value:
The Life Science and International Health degree programme offers a unique combination of scientific expertise and international health competence. It prepares students for the challenges of a globalised world and lays the foundation for a successful career in research, development and healthcare management.
The programme consists of natural science, health science and data science modules on the one hand, and it includes modules with a legal, business and social sciences background on the other hand, and provides students with comprehensive theoretical and practical education.
The programme has a strong focus on research. In the laboratory courses in particular, the interesting and exciting teaching content is continuously applied and deepened through a complex biomedical issue in order to prepare students for the national and international job market. It combines foundational natural sciences with international public health while providing a solid foundation for advanced Master’s programmes.
Study objectives and content:
The programme combines a broad foundation in biophysics, chemistry, and data science with specialised training in biological subjects such as cell biology, microbiology, molecular biology, and genetic engineering. Additionally, it covers international public health to equip students with the skills to address global health challenges.
Core competencies:
Natural Science foundations: biomedical data science, biochemistry, microbiology, organic chemistry
Biological specialisation: cell biology, molecular biology, genetic engineering
Public health: health promotion, disease prevention, international health systems, legal frameworks
Practical skills: laboratory work, scientific research, experimental methods
Goals of the programme:
Enable independent research and development
Plan and conduct experiments
Coordinate production processes and quality assurance (e.g. GMP in pharmaceuticals)
Build and optimise healthcare systems for disease prevention and health promotion
Prepare for advanced Master’s programmes in biotechnology, biomedicine, or public health

Costs of living.value:
Studies abroad often have different types of expenses from the ones you know from your home country. You are responsible for covering your own living expenses. Accommodation and other essential living expenses will amount to around 780 to 1,000 EUR per month. Of course, this amount depends entirely on individual lifestyle. The following list gives you an idea of some fixed and variable costs that you should take into account for your stay in Germany.
Monthly costs:
rent (including utilities): 250 to 450 EUR
groceries: approx. 160 to 180 EUR
health insurance, medical fees, medication: approx. 145 EUR
miscellaneous (clothing, study materials, other activities): 170 to 220 EUR
Total: 780 to 1,000 EUR
The so-called "Deutschlandticket" included in the semester ticket allows you to travel using all local public means of transportation throughout Germany.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value: There are job opportunities both in town and on campus. Nevertheless, please do not come to Germany expecting to be able to finance your entire studies by working. The study load is high, it is not always easy to find a part-time job and you will need at least basic German skills for many of the available jobs. Students from non-European countries are allowed to work either 120 whole days or 240 half days annually. The 120-day rule is not affected by mandatory internships or student assistance jobs at university. Students from EU member countries, the European Economic Area (EEA) and Switzerland can work without restrictions during their studies in Germany.

Accommodation.value:
BTU Cottbus-Senftenberg is a university with three locations where numerous student dormitories are provided. Students can choose between different room types. The room capacities in our dormitories are limited, thus we recommend to apply as early as you receive your admission letter for an apartment in the dormitories.
In Germany, it is also very common for students to live alone or with friends. If three or more people share an apartment together, this is called a "WG" in German ("Wohngemeinschaft", which means a shared flat). A comprehensive list on student accommodation and housing options at BTU's three locations can be found on our websites, as well as a video about how students live in both Cottbus and Senftenberg.

The BTU Career Center offers extensive support to international students and graduates, ensuring that students experience a smooth transition into the job market. We help students on their journey to a successful career path by offering seminars, workshops and career advisory services to ensure that students succeed in their job application processes and land great positions.

BTU Job Market: online job board for students

Description/content.value:
In the first semester, you will gain a strong foundation in key subject areas such as Medicine and Nursing, Medical Informatics, Artificial Intelligence, and Strategy and Entrepreneurship in Healthcare. You will also develop essential methodological skills that prepare you for interdisciplinary work in this dynamic field.
In the second semester, you will deepen your understanding of data processing, process design, and the ethical and regulatory frameworks of healthcare. Alongside your courses, you will work on a project-based assignment, applying your knowledge to a practical research question.
The third semester focuses on advanced data analysis and the responsible management of AI systems and health data. You will explore a hands-on topic and have the opportunity to develop your own innovative ideas and solutions for real-world challenges in healthcare.
In the fourth semester, you will independently tackle a complex research topic within Medical Informatics, Artificial Intelligence, or Strategy and Entrepreneurship in Healthcare. You will first build the methodological and organisational basis for your Master’s thesis before developing and completing your own research project — demonstrating your ability to approach a specialised problem with scientific rigour, think critically, and present your results with confidence.

Academic admission requirements.value:
Admission requirements in accordance with the university-wide enrolment regulations
Completed university degree with at least 210 ECTS credits in one of the following degree programmes (examples): Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Digital Health, as specified in the annex to the programme regulations
If you hold a Bachelor’s degree with only 180 ECTS credits, the remaining 30 ECTS credits must be compensated by providing evidence of one of the following:
Co-authorship of a research publication (research paper) in German or English, or
At least six months of full-time, verifiable professional experience after completion of the Bachelor’s degree in a role relevant to the programme’s content (to be demonstrated by employment contract and/or reference letters).
Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree from an institution outside the Lisbon Convention must successfully complete a Graduate Record Examination (GRE) General Test.
Language requirements
English level B2 for all applicants
German level A2 (for international applicants)
Besides English-taught elective modules, German-taught elective modules are available (second/third semester). For these, German B2 level is required — which you can acquire during your first semester. This is not an admission requirement.
This degree programme has unrestricted admission.

Accommodation.value:
In the city of Bochum, you can find different types of accommodation. On average, students in Bochum pay approximately 400 to 800 EUR per month for a single apartment, which is below the average rent in Germany. A room in a shared apartment is usually less expensive.
About 5,000 students in Bochum live in multiple student halls close to the campus, which are run by the Akademisches Förderungswerk (AKAFÖ). In the halls, each student has a single room and shares a kitchen and bathroom with other students, rents an apartment with a private bathroom and kitchen, or shares an apartment with one or several flatmates.
More information on the student halls can be found at https://studium.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/de/wohnen.
In addition, private and church-affiliated student halls accommodate up to 1,000 students: http://www.stuwo.de/wohnheim-region/bochum/.

Description/content.value:
For over 35 years, the European Institute for Advanced Behavioural Management (EIABM) at Saarland University has been firmly established as a provider of top-tier continuing education for international executives through the MBA programme European Management. Starting in the 2026/27 winter semester, the institute will expand to include the MBA in Entrepreneurship & Innovation, thereby meeting the growing demand for university-level continuing education programmes specifically tailored to those interested in starting a business and in the field of innovation management.
The MBA in Entrepreneurship & Innovation imparts scientifically grounded and practice-oriented economic competencies with a focus on entrepreneurship and innovation management. The programme specifically prepares students for start-up ventures, corporate management, and the leadership of innovation projects, and it qualifies graduates for a wide range of roles in companies across all industries or in self-employed entrepreneurial activities. The English-language curriculum combines general management with a specialisation in entrepreneurship and is characterised by a strong practical focus, in-person classes, and transfer-oriented teaching formats. The courses are interactive and closely aligned with professional practice, supplemented by case studies, soft skills seminars, and field trips. Enrolment is limited, ensuring direct interaction in all courses between participants and university professors from Germany and Europe, as well as experienced professionals. Guest lectures and practical reports from successful experts in the field enrich the curriculum. Students also benefit from the excellent entrepreneurship ecosystem at Saarland University, which features outstanding partners and infrastructure such as Triathlon.
The degree offers direct support for founders during the start-up process, while also equipping graduates to successfully manage innovation projects within companies, contribute to research and development, or advance corporate spin-offs. Thanks to the specialised and interdisciplinary competencies of the programme and its international orientation, graduates are qualified for diverse professional roles across organisations of all sizes and in various geographical regions.
Career opportunities span entrepreneurship, business management, and the broader economic sector. Both before and after completing the programme, professional pathways are highly diverse; graduates can work in virtually any field or industry, domestically or internationally, and they may assume leadership roles or pursue their own entrepreneurial initiatives. The programme is designed for a wide range of target groups, including founders and those interested in founding a business, practitioners, entrepreneurs and employees as well as PhD students from other disciplines and affiliated institutes.

Course organisation.value: The programme lasts one year and includes 15 courses: Strategic Management, Corporate Sustainability and Social Responsibility, Soft Skills, European Institutions, European Regulations, Economics and Finance, Learning Business by Doing Business, Marketing of Innovations, Prototyping and Agile Project Management, Business Model Development, Data Analytics Project, Consumer Behaviour, Entrepreneurship, Leadership and Human Resource Management, and Entrepreneurial Management. Each course usually runs from Wednesday to Saturday, as a blocked course. All courses are designed to be transfer-oriented and highly interactive, closely aligned with professional practice and complemented by case studies, soft skills seminars, and excursions to business enterprises. At the end of the programme, students write a Master's thesis on an innovative and relevant topic. There is a writing time of three months for full-time students. The entire curriculum of the MBA programme is offered in English. Students at the EIABM come from all over the world. On their way to taking the lead in global teams, they learn the necessary basics of modern management in the MBA programme: economic, legal, and political strategies as well as essential intercultural aspects, through discussions and case studies. Field trips, lectures, case studies and company visits to the institute's European partner universities offer students the opportunity to deepen and apply theoretical knowledge and interact with international students, practitioners and scholars. The programme is very practice-focused. State-of-the-art teaching methods such as interactive case studies, teamwork and real-life examples enhance the study experience. Students get valuable insights into the industrial world on various company visits and networking events with experts from the business world. This offers excellent opportunities to start building their career networks for their successful futures, right from the beginning. Courses are taught by renowned professors from Saarland University as well as from other recognised universities in Germany and other European countries. EIABM chooses its lecturers very carefully from the elite range of leading experts in their fields. An excellent qualification at the highest level is guaranteed by a high degree of practical relevance and internationality in the study programme. EIABM's industry connections and advisory board foster ongoing collaboration with local industries, enhancing networking opportunities and industry relevance. PDF Download

Description/content.value:
Welcome to the Master of European Technology Law!
AI, Autonomous Robots, AR, Big Data, Digital Twins, and the Internet of Things challenge the legal system just as much as the legal system influences how innovative ideas must be designed, tested, and launched to succeed in the market. Understanding both legal and technological terminology and concepts is key to turning technical innovation into reality. That’s why we have created an interdisciplinary Master's programme combining methods and content from law and technology. The programme includes research-oriented theory and practical projects to develop future skills.
Key areas: Our fields of technology cover Smart Factories, Platform Business Models, Logistics, Smart Farming and Smart Cities.
Open-minded: We don't teach national law. All courses are focused on the European Digital Single Market.
Interdisciplinary: Staff and students are mixed groups of lawyers and data professionals. Industry-based workshops enhance the practical application and value.
Small learning group: The programme admits a maximum of 25 students.
Adapted to your needs: The programme includes a thorough alignment phase dependent on the respective background.
Condensed: Based on a condensed schedule (Thursdays and Fridays), the programme can be combined with your current career.
Flexibility: We want to see you on campus! But we offer hybrid formats for those days (up to four) when a class does not fit your schedule.
Multifaceted: Combine the Master of European Technology Law with a PhD. This might be possible for applicants who have completed at least a Bachelor's in law that lasted a minimum of eight semesters and focused on at least two of the following areas: private law, public law and criminal law.
Career prospects: The Master of European Technology Law prepares graduates for careers in international law firms, as in-house lawyers, in IP and IT departments as well as in technology industries.

Description/content.value:
What does it mean to design responsibly in a world defined by climate change, digital disruption and social inequality? Design (MA) at the University of Applied Sciences Potsdam (FHP) — located 30 minutes from central Berlin — is a tuition-free, English- and German-taught Master's programme for graduates who want to go beyond execution and engage with design as a critical, research-driven practice.
At the heart of the programme is a strong studio culture built on co-creation, collaboration and individual exploration. The result is a flexible, modular and interdisciplinary environment that adapts to each student's interests and ambitions. Students choose from two distinct studio pathways, each with its own focus and language of instruction:
Experimental and research-driven studio: This is an exploratory studio that investigates design as a critical and material practice, engaging with cultural, social and aesthetic dimensions of form and communication (taught in German).
Speculative and technology-oriented studio: This is a studio focused on interaction design and digital futures. Students prototype radical new forms of digital experience, drawing on data visualisation, XR, AI, and media theory (taught in English).
Both studios are embedded in an active research environment. Students can collaborate with the Interaction Design Lab (IDL) and the Urban Complexity Lab (UCLAB) — internationally-recognised research groups with expertise in interaction design, data visualisation and human-computer interaction.
The programme is offered as a one-year fast-track (two semesters, German) or a two-year full programme (four semesters, German or English), with the option of a double degree with the National Taipei University of Technology (Taipei Tech) in Taiwan.
Core Subject Areas
Communication Design, Interface Design, Product Design
Design Research & Design Theory
Speculative Design & Design Fiction
Strategic Design & Design Leadership
Futures Literacy & Interdisciplinary Futures
Data Visualisation & Interaction Design
Design in Times of Polycrisis (ecology, society, technology)
The Master's degree programme was re-accredited in 2025, and it gives you access to the higher civil service in Germany.
Please find specific information on our website and in the module handbook.

Course organisation.value:
Programme Structure
One-year track (two semesters | German): The fast-track Master's for graduates of eight-semester Bachelor's programmes (240 ECTS) has a focus on design research, design theory, and aesthetic-artistic practice. The core module includes Studio X. Elective courses include Teaching Experience, Design Leadership, and Interdisciplinary Futures. This track concludes with Master's thesis, colloquium, and public defence.
Two-year track (four semesters | German or English): This is an in-depth exploration of an annually-changing studio theme. Studio acts as thematic and creative core. Semesters one and two include studio module, design research, a reading group, Interdisciplinary Futures, and Design Leadership. Semester three includes teaching/learning concepts, individual in-depth project, and elective courses. Semester four consists of the Master's thesis and thesis seminar.
Double Degree track (four semesters | English): Year one takes place at FH Potsdam, and year two takes place at Taipei Tech (Taiwan). The Master's thesis is completed at Taipei Tech with supervisors from both universities. A scholarship for the second year abroad may be available.
Key Modules:
Studio X: Two-semester interdisciplinary studio project exploring contemporary design, societal, and technological challenges through design research, speculative design, and artistic practice
Reading Group: This includes seminal texts in design theory, AI, robotics, ecological transformation, and post-human-centred design. Critical reading and survey paper writing are cultivated.
Interdisciplinary Futures: Speculative Design, Design Fiction, futures research methods (trend analysis, scenario building, Futures Literacy), technology ethics
Design Leadership: Strategic design management, team leadership, innovation in start-ups/businesses/NGOs, intercultural competencies, entrepreneurship
Teaching Experience: Students design and deliver teaching formats. This also includes didactic concepts, feedback integration, and group facilitation.
Thesis Development I & II: From research question to the Master's thesis proposal, students are introduced to design research methods — qualitative, quantitative and interdisciplinary — alongside ethics, methodology, academic and creative writing, and presentation strategies. The two modules progressively build toward a fully developed research proposal for the Master's thesis.
Master's Thesis: Practice-based or practice-led research; written project, colloquium, public presentation and academic defence

Graduates of eight-semester (240 ECTS) programmes may apply for the two-semester fast-track (German track). Graduates of six-semester (180 ECTS) programmes apply for the four-semester programme.

A passed artistic design entrance exam (aptitude test) is required in addition to the formal degree. The application deadline is the 1 April.

Description/content.value:
The international and transdisciplinary Master’s programme Future Analytics: AI & Audio Worlds is aimed at graduates with a Bachelor’s degree in music (and musicology), cultural and sound studies, as well as computer science, data science and artificial intelligence. They will collaborate to explore, in a specialised, research-oriented approach, how AI and auditory cultures influence, shape, and challenge one another—and how futures can be shaped responsibly. You learn to analyse future-related challenges, critically reflect on them, and actively shape them. The programme is the first to bring these disciplines together in a single transdisciplinary Master's programme.
During your studies, you will acquire both in-depth knowledge in your own field and skills in the complementary field. You learn to analyse complex problems, deal with uncertainty, communicate across disciplines, and develop innovative solutions. Musicians learn to programme — computer scientists engage with music and audio design. Research skills, critical thinking, data literacy, creativity, and reflection on critical social and scientific discourses form an integrated competency profile. The programme views the future not as a fixed state, but as an open arena of negotiation in which agency continuously shifts between people, machines, data, and institutions (shifting agencies). You will work with academic theories, models, and methods, combining analytical thinking with creative practice.
Course Highlights
A central component of the programme is a two-semester student research project conducted in small teams. Building on academic theories, methods, and concepts, you develop your own research questions, future scenarios, or prototypical applications and gain experience in transdisciplinary work. You will learn to bring together different perspectives, develop a shared technical language, and work collaboratively on current future-oriented topics. Together, you organise a Future Topics Conference and link research to socially relevant future challenges.
The Master’s programme focuses on innovative teaching and learning formats such as project-based learning, peer learning, team teaching, as well as portfolio-based assessments and academic mentoring. These enable you to continuously reflect on your development and shape it independently. Through academic mentoring and close supervision by faculty members, you are supported throughout your entire programme.
After completing the programme, you will have a unique skill profile at the intersection of AI and auditory cultures, qualifying you for international careers in research, technology development, the cultural and creative industries, as well as AI ethics, governance, and consulting; or you develop your own scientific and artistic research and project ideas.

Course organisation.value: The two-year Master’s programme Future Analytics: AI & Audio Worlds comprises four semesters with a total of 120 ECTS credits. The programme is structured around a Specialisation Field, a Complementary Field, and a Transdisciplinary Field (Core). In the first semester, you will take courses in both your Specialisation Field (Music/Audio/Sound Studies or AI/Machine Learning) and your Complementary Field (AI/Machine Learning or Music/Audio/Sound Studies). The focus is on the Transdisciplinary Field (Core), which primarily includes an introduction to future-oriented topics, inter- and transdisciplinary studies, labs, and academic mentoring. In the second semester, you will take courses on theories, models, methods, concepts, and analyses in your Specialisation Field and apply your acquired knowledge in labs. In the Transdisciplinary Field (Core), academic mentoring continues, and you will explore transdisciplinary approaches and designs. This semester also marks the start of the two-semester student research project. In the third semester, you will take courses in analysis, creation, and (specialised) communication. Academic mentoring continues in the Transdisciplinary Field. The focus in the Transdisciplinary Field is on continuing the student research project and organising the student Future Topics Conference. Academic mentoring continues this semester. A preparatory seminar for the Master’s thesis will be held to help students prepare for it. In the fourth semester, the Master’s module (Thesis & Colloquium) worth 30 ECTS credits takes place.

Description/content.value:
Model. Compute. Innovate. Engineering a Sustainable Future.
The English-taught Master’s programme Computational Modelling in Engineering is designed for motivated students with a background in engineering, natural sciences, or computer science who want to shape sustainable technologies in an increasingly digital world. The programme offers a strong foundation in mathematical and physical modelling, complemented by advanced numerical and data-driven methods that are essential in modern engineering practice. As a student, you will learn to develop, analyse, and critically evaluate complex computational models while working in interdisciplinary teams that reflect real-world engineering environments. The curriculum combines fundamental theory with practical applications across various engineering domains, equipping you with skills that are both academically rigorous and highly relevant for your future career. A broad range of elective courses allows you to tailor your studies to your personal interests — whether you are passionate about materials science, fluid dynamics, structural mechanics, or innovative data‑centric approaches. Thanks to the close integration of teaching and active research, you will gain insights into current scientific challenges and collaborate with international researchers. Graduates benefit from excellent global career prospects in academia, research institutions, and forward‑thinking industries.

Course organisation.value:
The Master’s programme combines a clear academic framework with a high degree of flexibility. It comprises 120 CP (ECTS) and is designed to be completed within a standard period of four semesters. The curriculum is structured into six coordinated areas:
Core Competencies (24 CP): Build a strong foundation in the compulsory subjects of mechanics, thermodynamics, computational methods, and data science (completion is recommended by the end of the second semester).
Methods (24 CP): Choose modules in fundamental theoretical, numerical, and data-based methods tailored to your individual research interests.
Computational Engineering and Applications (24 CP): Deepen your expertise in specific application fields across various engineering disciplines.
Interdisciplinary Electives (12 CP, ungraded): Broaden your horizons in the areas of Key Competencies, Economics & Law, and Technology & Society (4 CP each).
Project (6 CP): In the third semester, you will work on a specific scientific topic in small groups of up to five students.
Master’s Thesis (30 CP): The thesis marks the conclusion of your studies and can be completed at any of the four participating faculties.
With the exception of the Core Competencies, you can flexibly design your study plan during the first three semesters. Throughout the programme, dedicated academic advising is available to support your individual specialisation and organisational needs.
For the subject Interdisciplinary Electives, students must choose courses in the three areas Key Competencies (4 CP), Economics and Law (4 CP) and Technology and Society (4CP).
In the subjects Methods and Computational Engineering and Applications, students choose modules adding up to 24 CP each from the available offer in the module handbook. Students should decide on an individual focus and implement it in an individual study plan. Study counselling is offered to support the selection process.
The project is planned for the third semester and can be chosen from a list of offered overall topics. Up to five students team up for it, and the title will be set individually depending on the topic.

Description/content.value:
The study of biological processes increasingly requires the use of knowledge and methods from physics; using physical strategies and approaches, comprehensive insights into complex biological processes become possible.
Currently, more initiatives are being taken worldwide to train qualified scientists who work at the intersection of biology and physics. Saarland University is taking on a pioneering role here with its degree programme and the close linking of physics and life sciences.
The Biophysics programme at Saarland University combines a physics degree with the acquisition of basic biological knowledge, on which graduates can easily build specialised knowledge.
Due to their broad and fundamental education, biophysicists have very good career opportunities, e.g. in medical, bio- or environmental engineering as well as in academic research institutions. These fields show a strong demand for highly qualified and broadly educated scientists.
Description/content.html:
The study of biological processes increasingly requires the use of knowledge and methods from physics; using physical strategies and approaches, comprehensive insights into complex biological processes become possible.

Currently, more initiatives are being taken worldwide to train qualified scientists who work at the intersection of biology and physics. Saarland University is taking on a pioneering role here with its degree programme and the close linking of physics and life sciences.

The Biophysics programme at Saarland University combines a physics degree with the acquisition of basic biological knowledge, on which graduates can easily build specialised knowledge.

Due to their broad and fundamental education, biophysicists have very good career opportunities, e.g. in medical, bio- or environmental engineering as well as in academic research institutions. These fields show a strong demand for highly qualified and broadly educated scientists.

Course organisation.value:
In the Master's degree programme in Biophysics, students are required to complete coursework and examinations amounting to 120 credit points (CP).
During the first year of study, the module Theoretical Biophysics provides in-depth training in theoretical biophysics, covering the subfields of nonlinear dynamics, stochastic processes, statistical physics of systems far from equilibrium, and modelling. For students with a Bachelor’s degree in Biology, an alternative introductory lecture on theoretical methods of physical analysis of biological systems is offered.
In the experimental part of the programme, advanced concepts of cellular biophysics are presented within the Experimental Biophysics module. Complementing this module, the Advanced Laboratory course gives students access to modern experimental methods currently used in projects conducted by experimentally oriented research groups.
During the winter semester of their first year, students have the option to study for one semester at the University of Strasbourg within the Erasmus programme, completing all coursework there.
Another important component of the curriculum in the first year is the extensive elective area, which includes both biophysics-specific and interdisciplinary course offerings:
The biophysics elective area (15 CP) serves to prepare students academically for participation in interdisciplinary (research) projects and for the Master’s thesis.
The interdisciplinary elective area (20 CP) focuses on the acquisition of key qualifications, such as foreign languages, business administration (e.g. entrepreneurship), and the organisation of scientific work, or provides insight into the content and methods of other disciplines such as chemistry, computer science, or mathematics.
The second year of the Master’s programme can be characterised as a research phase. In the third semester, students take the modules “Introduction to Scientific Research” and “Laboratory Project” (15 CP) in preparation for the Master’s thesis (30 CP), which constitutes the completion of the degree programme.

Academic admission requirements.value:
Admission to the consecutive Master’s degree programme in Biophysics requires:
a Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent university degree with a focus on biophysics, biology, physics, or a discipline closely related to biophysics, and
suitability for a Master’s programme. This is generally determined by a Bachelor’s degree with an overall grade of 2.5 or higher, or by an entrance examination.
In addition, expertise in nonlinear dynamics, thermodynamics, and statistical physics, as well as in cell and molecular biology and genetics, is required, along with a basic understanding of biochemistry.
As part of the Master’s programme in Biophysics, supplementary courses are offered that enable students to acquire specialised skills not covered in the Bachelor’s programme.
The number of credit points earned in the Bachelor’s programme in lectures and seminars on physics and biology should not be less than 20 CP in each subject. At least 20 CP should have been earned through laboratory courses.
