Description/content.value:
The application-oriented Master’s degree programme in Software Engineering is a consecutive programme based on a seven-semester Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science and leads to a second professional qualification.
The programme is aimed at students who hold a first university degree or a degree from a state or state-recognised university of cooperative education in the field of (Applied) Computer Science or a closely related discipline, particularly from abroad, and who wish to broaden their knowledge and deepen it within one of the offered profile areas.
The consecutive Master’s degree programme in Software Engineering aims to enable graduates to solve complex tasks in software development, software architecture, and software evaluation independently, on a sound scientific basis, and with a strong sense of responsibility. The qualification objectives are aligned with Level 7 of the German Qualifications Framework (DQR) and with the Qualifications Framework for German Higher Education Degrees (HQR) for Master’s degrees.
Graduates of the programme:
Possess an advanced, research-oriented understanding of the theoretical and practical foundations of software engineering, including advanced methods, architectures, and development paradigms.
Are able to analyse complex problems, independently develop solution approaches, implement them, and critically evaluate them. In doing so, they take into account economic, social, ethical, and ecological conditions.
Master scientific methods of computer science and related disciplines, are able to apply and reflect on them in new contexts, and can critically assess and communicate research findings.
Are able to work in interdisciplinary settings, quickly familiarise themselves with new subject areas, and cooperate in international, multilingual teams in a responsible and goal-oriented manner.
Are capable of taking on leadership responsibilities, particularly in the planning, management, and quality assurance of software projects in industrial, public-sector, or research-related contexts.
Are able to develop scientific research questions and pursue them further within research projects or in the context of subsequent doctoral studies.
The programme leads to a professionally qualifying Master’s degree and at the same time prepares graduates for research-related activities as well as for further academic qualification through doctoral studies.
Description/content.html:
The application-oriented Master’s degree programme in Software Engineering is a consecutive programme based on a seven-semester Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science and leads to a second professional qualification.

The programme is aimed at students who hold a first university degree or a degree from a state or state-recognised university of cooperative education in the field of (Applied) Computer Science or a closely related discipline, particularly from abroad, and who wish to broaden their knowledge and deepen it within one of the offered profile areas.

The consecutive Master’s degree programme in Software Engineering aims to enable graduates to solve complex tasks in software development, software architecture, and software evaluation independently, on a sound scientific basis, and with a strong sense of responsibility. The qualification objectives are aligned with Level 7 of the German Qualifications Framework (DQR) and with the Qualifications Framework for German Higher Education Degrees (HQR) for Master’s degrees.

Graduates of the programme:

  1. Possess an advanced, research-oriented understanding of the theoretical and practical foundations of software engineering, including advanced methods, architectures, and development paradigms.
  2. Are able to analyse complex problems, independently develop solution approaches, implement them, and critically evaluate them. In doing so, they take into account economic, social, ethical, and ecological conditions.
  3. Master scientific methods of computer science and related disciplines, are able to apply and reflect on them in new contexts, and can critically assess and communicate research findings.
  4. Are able to work in interdisciplinary settings, quickly familiarise themselves with new subject areas, and cooperate in international, multilingual teams in a responsible and goal-oriented manner.
  5. Are capable of taking on leadership responsibilities, particularly in the planning, management, and quality assurance of software projects in industrial, public-sector, or research-related contexts.
  6. Are able to develop scientific research questions and pursue them further within research projects or in the context of subsequent doctoral studies.

The programme leads to a professionally qualifying Master’s degree and at the same time prepares graduates for research-related activities as well as for further academic qualification through doctoral studies.

Course organisation.value:
The curriculum of the Master’s degree programme in Software Engineering is aligned with the qualification objectives defined for the programme and follows a clear, systematically structured design. It ensures that students are able to acquire subject-specific and methodological competencies as well as social and personal key skills within a coherent and feasible course of study.
In the first and second semesters, students complete 30 ECTS credits each in modules that are thematically coordinated with one another. These include, among other things, content from the areas of IT project management, software architecture, quality assurance, DevOps, advanced analytics, knowledge engineering, as well as ethics and data protection. In doing so, students acquire the ability to analyse, design, implement, and critically evaluate modern software solutions on a sound methodological basis.
A particular focus of the curriculum is on project-based teaching: in both subject semesters, students complete either a research project or a company project worth 5 ECTS credits each. These formats promote both the academic engagement with current topics and the application of acquired knowledge in real-world practical and business contexts.
The integrated language training (German or English) underscores the international character of the degree programme and strengthens communication skills. The teaching of academic methods and writing techniques takes place in the module Scientific Writing and specifically prepares students for the final phase of their studies.
In the third semester, the Master’s thesis takes centre stage and is generally carried out in cooperation with a company or research institution (25 ECTS credits). It serves as proof that students are able to work independently, systematically, and on a sound academic basis on a complex, application-oriented topic. The final semester is complemented by the module IT Security (5 ECTS credits), which addresses security-related aspects of software development.

Erfurt offers comparatively low living costs compared to larger German cities such as Berlin or Munich.
International (non-EU) students usually need to prove financial resources via a blocked account (approx. 934 EUR/month). Living costs in Erfurt are generally within or below this amount.
Estimated monthly costs:
Rent (shared flat/student housing): 250 to 400 EUR
Food: 200 to 300 EUR
Health insurance: 130 EUR
Study materials: 20 to 50 EUR
Personal expenses: 100 to 150 EUR
TOTAL: approx. 700 to 1,030 EUR per month
With careful budgeting, students can cover their expenses comfortably within the required financial framework.
Tips to save money:
Apply early for student dormitory
Shop at budget supermarkets
Use student discounts

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
International students in Erfurt have good opportunities to take on part-time jobs or conduct internships alongside their studies. Typical student jobs include positions in hospitality, retail, logistics, and engineering-related areas.
Some professors within the programme maintain close links with industry partners and may share information on relevant job opportunities. Moreover, the project “Fremde werden Freunde” regularly offers networking events, company visits, and career-oriented activities that can facilitate access to part-time employment.
According to German regulations, non-EU students may work up to 120 full days or 240 half days per year. Important: German language skills are a massive boost to your employability.

Description/content.value:
The BA Political Conflict Studies (PCS) focuses on social and political conflicts – their causes, dynamics, and solutions – from a political science perspective. Combining International Relations, Comparative Politics, and Political Theory, PCS explores conflicts in their full complexity and encourages students to think outside the box.
international and practice-oriented outlook
interdisciplinary exchange within and beyond political science
training in diverse research methodologies
Exemplary questions addressed by the programme include the following: How do democracies manage political conflict and contestation? How does populism affect political processes? What does justice mean and how can it be implemented? What causes civil and international wars and how can such violent conflicts be ended? In what ways can regional integration help to navigate conflict? What challenges do identity, religion, and culture raise in different political and social settings? What role does sustainability play in politics?

Description/content.value:
The postgraduate Master of Compliance and Integrity Management (MACIM) study programme is a unique feature of Viadrina within the German university landscape, characterised by a strong interdisciplinary and practice-oriented approach to Integrity and Compliance Management.
The MACIM is a postgraduate, tuition-based programme that leads to the academic degree of Master of Compliance and Integrity Management (MACIM) and can be completed on a part-time basis. The programme is associated with the Viadrina Compliance Center, an interdisciplinary unit of the European University Viadrina, which has been successfully dealing holistically with the research fields of Ethics, Compliance and Integrity in organisations since 2010 and has established a reputation in Germany and worldwide.
Through the postgraduate Master's programme, students acquire in-depth knowledge in the field of Compliance and Integrity Management as well as the ability to apply this knowledge in professional practice and research. In the course of their studies, students acquire the skills and abilities to develop, implement, test and continuously improve the Compliance and Integrity Management System in any organisation, taking into account current developments in the areas of digitalisation, environmental protection, sustainability, governance and social aspects.
These goals are achieved through the three-stage teaching approach:
1. Learn: The curriculum consists of specialised modules in which all theoretical and practical knowledge and skills required for the implementation and operation of effective and efficient Compliance and Integrity Management (CIM) are learnt along a practical management cycle.
2. Apply: As part of a presentation, students develop new models and methods based on what they have learnt, which have a strong practical relevance. This takes place as part of an in-depth module in a distance-learning format.
3. Prove: As part of the Master's thesis, students demonstrate their theoretical and practical knowledge and their qualification for management positions.
Description/content.html:
The postgraduate Master of Compliance and Integrity Management (MACIM) study programme is a unique feature of Viadrina within the German university landscape, characterised by a strong interdisciplinary and practice-oriented approach to Integrity and Compliance Management.

The MACIM is a postgraduate, tuition-based programme that leads to the academic degree of Master of Compliance and Integrity Management (MACIM) and can be completed on a part-time basis. The programme is associated with the Viadrina Compliance Center, an interdisciplinary unit of the European University Viadrina, which has been successfully dealing holistically with the research fields of Ethics, Compliance and Integrity in organisations since 2010 and has established a reputation in Germany and worldwide.

Through the postgraduate Master's programme, students acquire in-depth knowledge in the field of Compliance and Integrity Management as well as the ability to apply this knowledge in professional practice and research. In the course of their studies, students acquire the skills and abilities to develop, implement, test and continuously improve the Compliance and Integrity Management System in any organisation, taking into account current developments in the areas of digitalisation, environmental protection, sustainability, governance and social aspects.

These goals are achieved through the three-stage teaching approach:

1. Learn: The curriculum consists of specialised modules in which all theoretical and practical knowledge and skills required for the implementation and operation of effective and efficient Compliance and Integrity Management (CIM) are learnt along a practical management cycle.

2. Apply: As part of a presentation, students develop new models and methods based on what they have learnt, which have a strong practical relevance. This takes place as part of an in-depth module in a distance-learning format.

3. Prove: As part of the Master's thesis, students demonstrate their theoretical and practical knowledge and their qualification for management positions.

Course organisation.value:
The programme lasts two semesters and is divided into five modules, four of which are compulsory basic modules and one is a compulsory elective module including independent study and a presentation. The combination of face-to-face and online teaching, which is always offered on selected Fridays and Saturdays, enables working people to take part in the programme. The programme concludes with the completion of a Master's thesis. This allows students to complete a Master's degree in just two semesters.
The degree programme is not only characterised by its innovative curriculum and strong practical focus, but also by teaching soft skills that are highly relevant to compliance and integrity management. The entire Integrity and Compliance Management cycle has been integrated into the degree programme and distributed across the existing modules. MACIM covers the practical design, implementation, testing and improvement of such a system. This is complemented by specialisation options and insights into various industries, including the public sector.
More than 50 highly qualified lecturers from research and practice contribute to the varied teaching format, ensuring the effective implementation of the programme concept. While sound theoretical foundations are taught by professors, renowned experts deliver the modules on practical implementation and specific management tools. The teaching is complemented by further guest lectures from well-known personalities. The small group size of a maximum of 20 participants enables excellent networking among the group and with the lecturers.

Academic admission requirements.value:
The Master's degree programme in Compliance and Integrity Management is designed as a part-time and continuing education programme. Admission to the MACIM Master's programme generally requires: (1) a first professionally qualifying degree (e.g. a Bachelor's, Diploma, state examination) with at least 240 ECTS points, and (2) at least one year of professional experience. For applicants without a first professionally qualifying degree or with fewer than 240 ECTS points, admission may be granted upon successful completion of the entrance examination.
Access and admission are governed by the Framework Regulations for Admission to Studies at the European University Viadrina Frankfurt (Oder).
The number of students in each edition of the programme is limited to 20 in order to ensure high teaching quality in small groups.
If you do not have a first professionally qualifying degree, but you have many years of relevant professional experience, this may be recognised. The same applies to missing or non-relevant professional experience; in such cases, exceptions are possible.

Description/content.value:
This double degree Master's programme in "Marine Transportation" is a cooperation between "Hochschule Wismar" in Germany and “Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember” Surabaya (ITS) in Indonesia. The Master's programme has a duration of four semesters. The first and second semesters will be held at ITS Surabaya in Indonesia, and semester three and four (including Master's thesis) will be held at Hochschule Wismar in Rostock in Germany.
Students acquire sound practical and decision-making skills in dealing with economic and administrative issues. They learn key administrative contexts and processes from both a business and a regulatory perspective and gain an understanding of structures, procedures, and systems. The economic component focuses on understanding financial flows, decision-making criteria for procurement, maintenance, and renewal of facilities and equipment, as well as retrofit measures. Students learn to develop, implement, manage, and evaluate project-specific tasks. They understand the essential importance of human capital and gain in-depth knowledge of various types of business organisations. In the logistics component, logistics and technology are integrated. Students learn the fundamentals of the seaworthiness of maritime vessels, how they are loaded, and the requirements that must be considered during unloading. They gain knowledge of environmental regulations and their interdisciplinary significance in relation to logistics, and they learn the various cargo handling techniques and port equipment required for cargo handling. Students understand the interrelationships in international transport, supply chains, logistics processes, and dependencies. In addition, they develop personal and social skills as well as intercultural competencies and become familiar with recognised business management procedures and strategies in the context of maritime transport science and economics. Students are equipped to navigate the English-speaking business world with confidence and conduct negotiations. The programme is supplemented and rounded out by additional key knowledge and skills in the field of law. The primary focus here is on understanding the legal foundations, acquiring knowledge of regulations, their application and interpretation, and navigating complex, rapidly changing international legal systems. Additionally, they gain advanced proficiency in the German language and a comprehensive understanding of intercultural contexts.
The main benefits of the programme include an excellent study programme in Indonesia and Germany followed by global employment opportunities in government agencies and institutions, port operations, shipping companies, shipyards, and maritime service providers, as well as transportation and freight forwarding companies and commercial enterprises.

First professional degree (Bachelor’s, Diploma, or equivalent) from a German or foreign university in the fields of economics, logistics, or maritime engineering, with a minimum of 180 credit points (ECTS) under the European Credit Transfer System (ECTS)
The overall grade of the certificate confirming this degree must be at least 2.5 for comparable grade systems or a GPA of 3.75/5.0 for non‐comparable grade systems.

Description/content.value:
Are you curious about how global markets operate and the impact companies have in an internationally connected world? Our International Business (BA) programme, with a specialisation in International Management, provides you with essential knowledge of business, intercultural communication, and methodological skills. Over the course of six semesters, you will gain hands-on training that prepares you for exciting management positions in international companies — and equips you to pursue a Master’s degree afterwards.
Throughout your studies, you will develop a thorough understanding of business administration, along with quantitative and qualitative methods, equipping you to make and implement informed business decisions. You will study the fundamentals of sustainable and responsible management, applying scientific methods purposefully to advance your knowledge independently. By enhancing your soft skills, you will also improve your ability to collaborate successfully within teams and organisations. Key topics include, among others:
Fundamentals of Business Administration
Digital Transformation
Entrepreneurship & Business Development
Sustainable Marketing
English Business Communication
International Business and Society
International Trade and Politics

Description/content.value:
The Master's programme in Mathematics offers an opportunity to delve deeper into the fascinating world of modern mathematics. Building on a solid foundation, students can pursue individual specialisations in both pure and applied mathematics – from algebra and geometry to numerical simulation, statistics, and mathematical modelling.
The programme fosters analytical thinking, creativity, and precision – skills that are highly valued in both academia and industry. A Master's degree in Mathematics opens up a wide range of career opportunities, including positions in research, technology, finance, and data analysis.

Course organisation.value:
The mathematics programme in Greifswald is characterised by excellent, personalised support and small study groups and offers a wide range of elective and specialisation options.
Students take modules from four areas:
Algebra, Geometry, and Topology
Discrete Mathematics
Computer Science, Numerical Mathematics, and Optimisation
Mathematical Modelling, Statistics, and Stochastics
They can determine the weighting of these areas themselves.
The programme typically concludes in the fourth semester with a Master's thesis, which students complete under the supervision of an adviser of their choice.

Description/content.value:
Geodata Science reveals what remains hidden at first glance. It helps us better understand our planet and develop solutions to current challenges — for example, in identifying suitable locations for wind turbines, in the early detection and monitoring of wildfires, in the planning of transportation routes, or in flood protection. Through the interplay of geosciences and computer science, a wide variety of data can be integrated to understand and model its dynamics.
International and Interdisciplinary
The international Master’s programme in Geodata Science combines theoretical knowledge with practical application in small groups. The programme focuses on projects involving various types of big geodata, such as satellite data, social media data, statistical data, sensor/IoT data, and data from simulation models. In addition, “Free to Choose” credits allow students to take courses in other disciplines at Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences, thereby receiving an interdisciplinary education.
Extensive Experience — Up-to-Date Curriculum
The study of geodata has a long tradition at at Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences: For 25 years, the university has offered an international Master’s programme in this field. Starting in the winter semester of 2027, the programme will launch under the new name of “Geodata Science” with a revised curriculum that puts current topics such as artificial intelligence and climate impacts at the centre.
We look forward to welcoming you soon!
What to expect:
Practical training in small, international groups
A curriculum focused on current topics such as AI, climate impacts, the Internet of Things, social media data, and various fields of application (climate, satellite imagery, etc.)
Direct contact with professors and faculty
Master’s theses in research and development or industry, either domestically or abroad, are possible
A region with many employers in relevant fields — for a work-study position during your studies or a direct transition into a job afterwards
International exchange programmes with other universities via our International Office
Support and guidance for students provided by the Central Student Advisory Service or the International Office, for example, when facing challenges during the studies
What you should bring:
A strong interest in geoscience topics, (geo)informatics, and physics
Openness and willingness to collaborate in international teams
The ability to work independently, critical thinking, and a critical approach to AI
Good English skills (B2)
6 CP each in programming, GIS, and statistics from your Bachelor’s degree

Programme Summary:
Are you fascinated by life sciences and their role in biomedicine? Would you like to pursue an English-taught Bachelor’s degree in Germany? The Biomedical Sciences (BSc) programme provides you with a solid foundation in molecular biology, biochemistry, immunology, and bioanalytics. The six-semester programme ends with a Bachelor’s thesis, which is completed at a company or a research institute.
Curriculum:
The six-semester study programme combines theory and practice. The first two semesters focus on natural science fundamentals, followed by specialised modules. Later, you deepen your biomedical knowledge and complete a Bachelor’s thesis. Topics include:
Molecular biology
Biochemistry
Immunology
Bioanalytics
Data analysis and bioinformatics
Quality assurance and legal frameworks
Scientific communication and English for science

Description/content.value:
The specialisation in Bioinformatics provides a research-oriented education at the interface of biology, data science and computational modelling. It focuses on the quantitative analysis and interpretation of complex biological data arising from modern high-throughput technologies across multiple molecular layers.
The programme combines a strong theoretical foundation in biostatistics, machine learning and data science with practical training in the analysis of real-world biological datasets. Students learn to formulate and evaluate statistical models, apply machine learning approaches, and critically interpret results in the context of biological systems. Particular emphasis is placed on understanding the assumptions, limitations and interpretability of computational methods.
The coursework consists of interactive lecture and reading courses that develop a deep conceptual understanding of probabilistic modelling, statistical inference and machine learning, complemented by project-based practical courses in which students work with multidimensional and heterogeneous biological data. These include, for example, sequencing-based measurements, imaging data and integrative multi-omics datasets.
Through this combination of theory and application, students acquire the ability to translate biological questions into computational models and to derive meaningful insights from data. The programme prepares graduates for independent research in academia as well as for data-driven roles in biotechnology, pharmaceutical research and related industries.

Accommodation.value:
ACCOMMODATION @ RPTU in KAISERSLAUTERN:
The majority of our students live in residence halls located on or close to campus. The "Studierendenwerk" operates several large halls of residence in Kaiserslautern. Students submit housing applications directly to the Studierendenwerk. For international Master's or PhD students, International Affairs RPTU aims at arranging accommodation in these residence halls or in private accommodation within its pre-arrival service. The halls of residence have modern single, double or shared apartments with kitchenette, bathroom/WC, and modern facilities as well as internet access.
Fully-furnished: kitchenette (no plates & pots, etc.), bed & mattress (no blankets & pillows), wardrobe, shelf, table, chair (no computer)
Rent: approx. 250 to 350 EUR
Since accommodation is not automatically guaranteed with admission, a request for accommodation to International Affairs ISGS is advisable.
Optional: To help international students get started in Kaiserslautern, the "Studierendenwerk" offers a starter package for the apartment. This package can be purchased for 95 EUR: https://www.studierendenwerk-kaiserslautern.de/en/housing/international.
More information:
https://rptu.de/international/master/prospective-students/travel-accommodation/accommodation

Description/content.value:
The Master’s programme in Quantitative Economics for Sustainability (QuESt) is a full economics programme that focuses on the sustainable economy. Based on quantitative methods of economics and in interdisciplinary collaboration with natural sciences, QuESt asks how the economy can and should be transformed towards ecological and social sustainability.
The central focus is on a sustainable economy. QuESt asks how the private and public economy can be transformed to preserve the natural resource base and to be oriented toward intra- and intergenerational justice. Increasingly, the sustainability is understood as quantitatively measurable. For example, the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and their 169 sub-targets are tracked by means of quantitative indicators. Accordingly, QuESt focuses on quantitative methods, specifically:
a) statistical and econometric methods for processing and analysing data from observations and experiments,
b) methods of economic and integrated economic-natural science modelling to study the consequences of different courses of action for the future development of the economy and its natural basis (climate, biodiversity, resources).
Graduates are well prepared for careers in the private sector, public administration, research institutions, NGOs and international organisations. Possible fields of employment include ministries, environmental agencies, planning offices, financial institutions, sustainability departments and data- or risk-analysis roles. At the same time, the programme provides a strong basis for doctoral study and for an academic career, particularly in sustainability economics and related interdisciplinary research fields (e.g. the research training group Economics of Connected Natural Commons: Atmosphere and Biodiversity (ECO-N).

Course organisation.html:
The MSc Quantitative Economics for Sustainability (QuESt) at Leipzig University comprises 120 ECTS credits and is normally completed over four semesters. The curriculum includes 50 ECTS credits of compulsory modules, 20 ECTS credits of compulsory elective modules, 30 ECTS credits in the free elective area, and a Master’s thesis worth 20 ECTS credits.

First semester: students begin by building a strong analytical and methodological foundation in economics and sustainability economics. They take the following modules:

  • Advanced Microeconomics (10 ECTS)
  • Advanced Econometrics and Statistics (10 ECTS)
  • Quantitative Sustainability Economics (10 ECTS)

Second semester: students continue their core training and deepen their chosen profile through further compulsory and compulsory elective modules:

  • Advanced Macroeconomics (10 ECTS)
  • One compulsory elective module (10 ECTS)
  • One compulsory elective module (10 ECTS)

Third semester: students complete the free elective area, which can also be achieved by spending a semester abroad. The free elective area may consist of modules from the faculty of business and economics, other faculties at Leipzig University, or interdisciplinary modules, particularly in cooperation with the faculty of physics and Earth system sciences and iDiv.

  • Free elective modules / semester abroad (30 ECTS)

Fourth semester: students complete the final research phase of the programme:

  • Research Methods in Sustainability Economics (10 ECTS)
  • Master’s thesis (20 ECTS)

For the compulsory elective area, students must choose at least 20 ECTS credits from the following modules:

  • Climate Economics (10 ECTS)
  • Biodiversity Economics (10 ECTS)
  • Environmental Economics (10 ECTS)
  • Institutional Economics of Sustainability Transitions (10 ECTS)

Other modules listed in the programme documents for the free elective area include:

  • Ecological-Economic Modelling for the Sustainable Use and Conservation of Biodiversity (10 ECTS)
  • Interdisciplinary modules on climate change and/or biodiversity change
  • Modules from the MSc Economics
  • Modules from Management Science
  • Modules from Business Information Systems
  • Modules from Business Education and Management Training
  • Modules from other faculties at Leipzig University, particularly under cooperation agreements with the faculty of physics and Earth system Sciences and iDiv

Description/content.value:
***** Accreditation still ongoing *****
The BSc in Sustainable Agriculture and Food Systems (SAFS) is an innovative English-taught programme that prepares you to become part of the solution to one of the world's greatest challenges: feeding a growing global population sustainably. This interdisciplinary programme equips young professionals from across the globe with the knowledge and skills to transform global food systems. Students gain comprehensive knowledge across natural and social sciences while developing critical thinking, problem-solving, and leadership skills essential for careers in the rapidly growing sustainable agriculture and food sectors.
The curriculum combines theoretical instruction, tutorials, practical fieldwork, and internships to ensure graduates are prepared for the complex challenges facing contemporary food systems.
Objectives
The BSc in Sustainable Agriculture and Food Systems develops graduates who master interdisciplinary and systems-based thinking, integrating knowledge from natural and social sciences to understand complex agricultural ecosystems from farm to fork and beyond. Students acquire critical thinking skills, scientific competence in research methods and data analysis, and practical expertise in sustainable food production, resource management, and nature conservation within planetary boundaries. Through challenge-based learning, hands-on experience, and mandatory internships, the programme builds communication, leadership, and entrepreneurial capabilities essential for careers as change-makers, innovators, and entrepreneurs.
Occupational fields
Graduates are qualified for diverse and rewarding career paths across the food system in the food industry and business, agricultural production, farm management, consultancies, governmental and non-governmental agencies, research and policy, among others. The programme prepares you for positions requiring interdisciplinary knowledge, systems thinking, practical competencies, and commitment to sustainability. Whether you're passionate about production, policy, business innovation, or social change, this programme opens doors to meaningful work that makes a difference in Germany and internationally. The programme also prepares you for graduate studies in fields such as:
MSc Agricultural Sciences (“Transformation Management for Sustainable Agri-Food Systems” and “Advisory and Innovation Services in Agri-Food Systems”)
MSc Organic Agriculture and Food Systems
MSc Environmental Protection and Agricultural Food Production
MSc Crop Sciences
MSc Agricultural Economics
MSc Food Systems
MSc Food Science and Technology
MSc Bioeconomy

Course organisation.value: In the first year of study, you complete ten compulsory modules on: Sustainability in Agri-Food Systems Soil as a Resource for Agricultural Systems under Global Change Livestock Farming Systems and Animal Health Ecology and Planetary Health Crop Production and Sustainable Agriculture Economics of Sustainable Agri-Food Systems Ethics and Justice in Agri-Food Systems Food Technology and Sustainability Food Marketing and Consumer Behaviour German Language Course A1 The module will be designed for students without any experience in the German language. Students with a certificate at level A2 or higher cannot attend this module and choose an elective module. Second year of studies In the second year of studies, you complete five more compulsory modules on: International Agri-Food Markets and Value Chains Policies and Governance of Sustainable Agri-Food Systems Digital Innovations for Sustainable Agri-Food Systems Introduction to Human Nutrition Statistical Methods for Analysing Agri-Food Systems In addition to these compulsory modules, in the summer semester of the second year, you can have the opportunity to do i) an internship within or outside Germany or ii) a supervised research project within the university. Third year of studies You can choose eight more elective modules from a large catalogue of subjects. This ensures you will have a solid education in the sub-disciplines of sustainable agriculture and food systems, while at the same time providing sufficient freedom to put together a programme that suits your individual career planning. The academic programme advisers advise you on your choice of modules and in planning your studies to ensure that you progress smoothly and directly. Course organisation.html:
In the first year of study, you complete ten compulsory modules on: 

  • Sustainability in Agri-Food Systems
  • Soil as a Resource for Agricultural Systems under Global Change 
  • Livestock Farming Systems and Animal Health 
  • Ecology and Planetary Health 
  • Crop Production and Sustainable Agriculture 
  • Economics of Sustainable Agri-Food Systems 
  • Ethics and Justice in Agri-Food Systems 
  • Food Technology and Sustainability 
  • Food Marketing and Consumer Behaviour 
  • German Language Course A1
    • The module will be designed for students without any experience in the German language. Students with a certificate at level A2 or higher cannot attend this module and choose an elective module.

Second year of studies 

In the second year of studies, you complete five more compulsory modules on: 

  • International Agri-Food Markets and Value Chains 
  • Policies and Governance of Sustainable Agri-Food Systems 
  • Digital Innovations for Sustainable Agri-Food Systems 
  • Introduction to Human Nutrition 
  • Statistical Methods for Analysing Agri-Food Systems 

In addition to these compulsory modules, in the summer semester of the second year, you can have the opportunity to do i) an internship within or outside Germany or ii) a supervised research project within the university. 

Third year of studies 

You can choose eight more elective modules from a large catalogue of subjects. This ensures you will have a solid education in the sub-disciplines of sustainable agriculture and food systems, while at the same time providing sufficient freedom to put together a programme that suits your individual career planning. The academic programme advisers advise you on your choice of modules and in planning your studies to ensure that you progress smoothly and directly. 

This allows you to design your studies flexibly in the fifth and sixth semesters by choosing modules from a range of over 260 modules offered by the Faculty of Agricultural Sciences in English or German. 

You will also complete your Bachelor's thesis in your third year of studies.

Costs of living.value:
Baden-Württemberg has the highest standard of living in Germany. The downside is that living costs are slightly above the German average. However, the cost of living can vary enormously depending on your personal lifestyle and where you live. It is generally more expensive to live in a bigger city like Stuttgart, where the University of Hohenheim is located. As a rule of thumb, 950 EUR to 1,000 EUR per month should be enough. The largest monthly expense is usually for rent, accounting for a third of the total cost of living for most students. These costs can be cut substantially by sharing a flat or living in a dorm. A typical example of monthly expenses could look like this:
Rent: 350 EUR to 500 EUR
Health insurance: approx. 110 EUR
Public transport: approx. 60 EUR
Study materials: 100 EUR
Food and drink: 150 EUR to 250 EUR
Leisure and hobbies: approx. 100 EUR

Accommodation.value:
Student residences on campus
At the University of Hohenheim, several student residence halls are located on campus. They are managed by Student Services Tübingen-Hohenheim. There is a high demand for these rooms, which is why usually only a small number of applications will be successful.
International (non-EU) students have a much more difficult time than Germans in finding private accommodation at the start of their studies when they are searching from their home countries. Therefore, the university provides a quota of rooms for international students. This enables a larger number of new international students to have a room in a residence hall. To be able to offer this special assistance at the start of studies, the rental duration for these rooms is limited to two years for Master's students.
Additionally, the house-hunting assistance offers support in finding a room on the private market.

Description/content.value: As a statistician, you are urgently needed in a wide range of industries. Since many students discover their enthusiasm for statistics during their Bachelor's degree, our Master's programme is designed in such a way that students with Bachelor's degrees in a wide range of subjects can also complete it: From business administration and economics to psychology and forestry. The programme focuses on practical relevance. You will not only learn the methodology, but also how to practically implement the analysis of complex data in software packages such as R and finally prepare and present it in a generally understandable way. You can do the internship, the project seminar and the final thesis together with a practice partner from the business world to gain first-hand experience and important contacts. To ensure that you are optimally prepared for your desired career, you have the opportunity to specialise in the subsidiary subjects of economics, life sciences, empirical social research and computer science.

Course organisation.value: The Master's programme in Applied Statistics is designed to take four semesters. In semesters one to three, students gain fundamental knowledge of statistical inference, statistical models and statistical modelling in the modules of the compulsory section. In the compulsory elective section, they can deepen their knowledge of statistical modelling and the selected field of application. Economics, life sciences, empirical social research and computer sciences are currently available as choices for the fields of application. In addition to this, the students work out statistical solutions to a given issue within the context of a practical statistical course, in cooperation with a practical partner. The fourth semester is intended for writing the Master's thesis.

The average cost of living in Göttingen is modest compared to other major university cities in Germany. Currently, expenses for accommodation, food, health insurance and books are about 800 to 1,000 EUR per month. Please note that fees for health insurance may vary according to age. Academic admission requirements.value:
Admission to the Master’s programme in Applied Statistics is competitive. Admission into the programme is based on proof of relevance of previous studies.
Proof of relevance of previous studies
A minimum of six semesters of study culminating in a Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent course of study with a minimum of 180 ECTS credits in statistics, mathematics, computer sciences, economics, agricultural economics or a closely related discipline (e.g. empirical social sciences and psychology).
Applicants must have completed at least 150 of the 180 ECTS credits at the time of application. Unfortunately, we cannot consider applications that do not meet this requirement.
Completed 60 ECTS credits and course work in statistics, mathematics, computer sciences, or another quantitative subject
including 24 ECTS credits in statistics, and
a minimum of 12 ECTS from the modules must be from coursework that is of intermediate or advanced levels.
Proof of relevant language skills
English language skills
For a list of accepted documents, see the required application documents.
Please note
If you have not completed your degree at the time of application, the current average score will be calculated.
For courses to be considered intermediate or advanced, the course content must clearly go beyond introductory or basic concepts.
Determining the relevance of previous studies for the MSc in Applied Statistics programme will be based on the documents enclosed in the application (see: "Required application documents").
The selection process is a two-stage process. The initial selection round will evaluate candidates based on their written application. The second round will evaluate candidates based on personal interviews. Further information on the application process and eligibility requirements can be found in the admission regulations ("Ordnung über die Zugangsvoraussetzungen und über die Zulassung") for the Master’s degree in Applied Statistics (see: "Admission regulations").

Description/content.value:
The MSc Economics at Leipzig University is a research-oriented Master’s programme that provides rigorous training in economics with a strong emphasis on analytical, quantitative, and evidence-based approaches. It combines a solid foundation in economic theory with advanced methodological training in microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics, and research methods. Students can specialise in Economic Policy or Quantitative Economics, enabling them to focus either on applied policy fields or on advanced empirical methods.
The programme equips students to analyse economic relationships, critically evaluate data and arguments, and develop scientifically grounded solutions to complex economic problems. They gain strong mathematical, statistical, and econometric skills as well as practical experience with research software such as R and Stata. The curriculum also fosters academic writing and presentation skills, while a flexible elective area allows for interdisciplinary study.
A distinctive feature of the programme is its international and research-oriented profile. It can be completed entirely in English and offers opportunities such as a semester abroad, study options at Keio University in Tokyo, or a double degree with Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne for highly qualified students. In addition, students may undertake a research internship, working on an independent project under academic supervision.
Graduates are well prepared for careers in the private sector (e.g. banking or insurance), public administration (including ministries and central banks), research institutions, NGOs, and international organisations. The programme also provides a strong foundation for doctoral studies and an academic career.

Course organisation.html:
The MSc Economics at Leipzig University comprises 120 ECTS credits and can be completed over four semesters. The curriculum includes 40 ECTS credits of compulsory modules, 30 ECTS credits of compulsory elective modules, 30 ECTS credits in the free elective area, and a Master’s thesis worth 20 ECTS credits.

First semester: students begin by building a strong analytical and methodological foundation in economics. They take the following modules:

  • Advanced Microeconomics (10 ECTS)
  • Advanced Econometrics and Statistics (10 ECTS)
  • One compulsory elective module (10 ECTS)

Second semester: students continue their core training and deepen their chosen profile through further compulsory elective modules:

  • Advanced Macroeconomics (10 ECTS)
  • One compulsory elective module (10 ECTS)
  • One compulsory elective module (10 ECTS)

Third semester: students complete the free elective area, which can also be achieved by spending a semester abroad. The free elective area may consist of modules from the faculty of business and economics or other faculties at Leipzig University:

  • Free elective modules / semester abroad (30 ECTS)

Fourth semester: students complete the final research phase of the programme:

  • Research Methods in Economics (10 ECTS)
  • Master's thesis (20 ECTS)

Following the compulsory modules, students have the option to specialise in Economic Policy or Quantitative Economics.

For the specialisation in Economic Policy, at least 30 ECTS credits must be chosen from the following modules:

  • Topics in International Economic Policy (10 ECTS)
  • Advanced Public Economics (10 ECTS)
  • European and International Monetary Policy (10 ECTS)
  • International Economic Policy (10 ECTS)
  • Financial Intermediation (10 ECTS)
  • Seminar on Economic Policy (10 ECTS)

For the specialisation in Quantitative Economics, at least 30 ECTS credits must be chosen from the following modules:

  • Spatial Econometrics (10 ECTS)
  • Empirical Public Economics (10 ECTS)
  • Time Series Analysis for Macroeconomics and Finance (10 ECTS)
  • Multivariate Data Analysis and Data Mining (10 ECTS)
  • Applied Topics in Monetary Economics (10 ECTS)
  • Microeconometrics (10 ECTS)
  • Seminar Applied Econometrics (10 ECTS)

For the full course organisation, please see the linked PDF.

Description/content.value:
The aim of the study programme is the interactive communication of knowledge about theories and methods of peace and conflict studies. On this basis, students acquire skills and expertise in the analysis of social and political contexts. The curriculum is focused on approaches that interrogate the causes of violent conflicts and make way for possibilities of transforming these conflicts. It is also focused on the investigation of tangible experiences of peaceful cohabitation and opportunities for the stabilisation and enhancement of non-violent conflict resolution mechanisms. The Peace and Conflict Studies programme focuses on the acquisition of theoretical and methodological skills from various disciplines; on the transfer of knowledge about different concepts, institutions, and instruments of peacebuilding, conflict transformation, and human rights policies; and on the development of analytical and practical skills in constructive conflict management. The programme is designed to enable students to closely analyse complex conflicts from different perspectives; to evaluate political strategies and ongoing projects in the fields of security, peacebuilding, and human rights; and to propose alternative methods of conflict resolution.
Having finished this programme, students know how international organisations function and how peaceful forms of politics can be re-established in contexts once ruled by overt violence. Also, students learn about the means and ends of human rights policies in national and international contexts. Furthermore, they are able to develop constructive strategies to overcome stalemates in social conflicts by analysing their causes and discussing different options of solutions. The Peace and Conflict Studies programme in Magdeburg is characterised by a multidisciplinary approach that incorporates not only traditional theories of international relations but also psychological, sociological, anthropological and linguistic components. This allows graduates to assess conflicts from a variety of important perspectives. However, far from advancing a purely additive attainment of knowledge, the lecturers of the programme particularly aim at conveying methodological expertise.
With regard to a future position in relevant occupational fields, the programme thus endeavours to foster the necessary theoretical aptitude as well as practical capacities. In order to acquire these skills, students are familiarised with socio-scientific methods of investigation as well as with political decision-making processes and mediation techniques that they practise in contexts such as operational simulations and conflict-management seminars. An internship in a pertinent institution is also part of the course.

It is also focused on the investigation of tangible experiences of peaceful cohabitation and opportunities for the stabilisation and enhancement of non-violent conflict resolution mechanisms. The Peace and Conflict Studies programme focuses on the acquisition of theoretical and methodological skills from various disciplines; on the transfer of knowledge about different concepts, institutions, and instruments of peacebuilding, conflict transformation, and human rights policies; and on the development of analytical and practical skills in constructive conflict management. The programme is designed to enable students to closely analyse complex conflicts from different perspectives; to evaluate political strategies and ongoing projects in the fields of security, peacebuilding, and human rights; and to propose alternative methods of conflict resolution.

Having finished this programme, students know how international organisations function and how peaceful forms of politics can be re-established in contexts once ruled by overt violence. Also, students learn about the means and ends of human rights policies in national and international contexts. Furthermore, they are able to develop constructive strategies to overcome stalemates in social conflicts by analysing their causes and discussing different options of solutions. The Peace and Conflict Studies programme in Magdeburg is characterised by a multidisciplinary approach that incorporates not only traditional theories of international relations but also psychological, sociological, anthropological and linguistic components. This allows graduates to assess conflicts from a variety of important perspectives. However, far from advancing a purely additive attainment of knowledge, the lecturers of the programme particularly aim at conveying methodological expertise.

With regard to a future position in relevant occupational fields, the programme thus endeavours to foster the necessary theoretical aptitude as well as practical capacities. In order to acquire these skills, students are familiarised with socio-scientific methods of investigation as well as with political decision-making processes and mediation techniques that they practise in contexts such as operational simulations and conflict-management seminars. An internship in a pertinent institution is also part of the course.

Course organisation.value:
The programme comprises the following modules:
1: Theories & Approaches of Peace and Conflict Studies
The module is composed of two parts: a lecture and an associated tutorial. The lecture provides an overview of key theories and approaches in national and international Peace and Conflict Studies, illustrated with current research.
2: Concepts of Securing Peace
This module deals with scientific concepts of securing peace, the advancement of human rights, and democracy and includes reflections on the use of coercive military measures.
3: Conflict Analysis & Theories of Conflict Management
The module is composed of two parts: a seminar on Conflict Analysis and a seminar or a lecture on Conflict Management. In the latter, students gain a broad overview of central terms, approaches, and assumptions within the theoretical field of conflict management (i.e. conflict resolution & conflict transformation).
4: Applied Conflict Management
This module includes practical elements. Students gain insight into the methods of conducting negotiation, mediation, and moderation, as well as related communication strategies, political planning and consultations.
5: Methods
The module comprises a seminar and a compulsory tutorial. Students can choose between a seminar that provides an overview of various qualitative research methods and one that focuses on a single method in depth.
6: Regional and Global Order
The module assumes the increasing relevance of governance beyond nation-states. Thus, it dedicates itself to the political, economic, and normative creation of order at the global and regional levels.
7: Sustainable Development & Resource Management
The aim of this module is to convey knowledge on the anthropogenically caused environmental ramifications of global change, scenarios regarding the limits of growth and global warming in connection with resource scarcity, and the resulting distributional conflicts that not only aggravate the long-existing global North-South constellation but also generate new types of conflict situations.
8: Violence & Media
This module allows for a critical analysis of different forms of legitimation and the mobilisation of direct violence, as well as the cultural, epistemological, or structural violence inherent in some discourses.
9: Global Justice
In this module, students examine the normative aspects of long-term peacekeeping and conflict management.
10: International Module
This module facilitates the transfer of credits earned during international exchanges.

Description/content.value:
Discover the modern science of matter and energy on atomic and subatomic scales at one of the leading German research departments. Gain theoretical understanding and experimental expertise in state-of-the-art techniques and technologies. Work with leading researchers from all over the world and learn from award-winning teachers.
Knowledge & competences gained:
Theoretical foundations and experimental techniques of nonlinear and quantum optics
Physics and experimental tools of ultracold quantum gases, quantum sensing, and quantum computing
Key elements of quantum technology
Theoretical tools in advanced quantum mechanics
Many-body quantum phenomena and their theoretical description
Basic elements of quantum information processing
Six reasons for Advanced Quantum Physics
Qualify for research and development: No matter whether you aim to work in academia, business, or industry, our Master’s programme will provide you with everything you need for your career. Our alumni excel in leading positions in fields ranging from optical technologies and the semiconductor industry to top-level consulting and finance.
Explore the quantum world: Are you fascinated by the surprising and counterintuitive phenomena of quantum physics? Our Master’s programme will allow you to explore the full breadth and depth of such quantum effects, both in theory and in our state-of-the-art laboratories.
Learn the science that will drive tomorrow’s technology: Quantum technology is constantly advancing technologies in communication, computation, sensing, and many other areas. These developments build on enabling technologies such as micro-optics, nanostructuring, and numerical methods. Our Master’s programme will give you a solid background in these areas and prepare you for your future career.
Bring quantum theory into the real world: Our Master’s programme will take you directly into our research groups, where you can study, explore, and realise your own quantum project.
Be part of cutting-edge research and technology: Benefit from close collaboration between theoretical and experimental research at the highest level and see novel predictions come to life in our laboratories. Our Master’s programme will give you access to state-of-the-art equipment in quantum technology and theory to realise your ideas.
Join the worldwide network of quantum researchers: Our research is strongly connected to a large international network. Our Master’s programme will give you access to these connections and open up the global scientific community to you.

Course organisation.value:
General
The curriculum is organised into several modules. While a small number of core lectures are mandatory, the majority can be chosen according to your individual interests and academic goals. The programme has a strong research focus and includes a full year dedicated to research projects.
Modules
https://physik.rptu.de/quantum-master/what-will-you-learn/
Module QT: Quantum Technologies
Quantum physics has already become a reality in various technological applications, and many more will follow. This module will convey the fundamentals of quantum technology and the enabling technologies, including, for example, quantum optics and photonics. We are convinced that you learn technologies best by applying them. Therefore, this module is closely linked to our advanced laboratory courses.
Module MB: Many-Body Quantum Systems
In the quantum world, a many-body system is much more than just the sum of its constituent parts. This is a consequence of quantum correlations, which make quantum systems so special. This module will provide the necessary theoretical background, as well as experimental examples, to describe and understand the fascinating properties of quantum many-body systems.
Module LC: Laboratory Courses
Bridging the gap between theoretical understanding and the realisation of quantum phenomena in cutting-edge research is a crucial step. Our advanced laboratory course offers you the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in areas such as quantum optics and photonics.
Through intensive one- or two-week projects, you will develop essential skills in data acquisition, analysis, and interpretation. This practical training will prepare you to confidently tackle your own research projects and excel in experimental quantum science.
Modules SE and GE: Science Elective and General Elective
Elective courses complement your scientific training in advanced quantum mechanics with valuable interdisciplinary skills and knowledge. You may select courses from areas such as mathematics, computer science, electrical engineering, or even fields like economics or management. By broadening your perspective beyond core physics, these courses help prepare you for a wide range of career paths in academia, industry, and beyond.
Modules RM and MT: Research and Master's Thesis
Do you want to solve your own quantum problem and see quantum phenomena emerge that nobody has seen before? The research module and Master’s thesis will allow you to join one of our leading theoretical and experimental groups and pursue your research topic under close supervision and within the worldwide network of quantum researchers.

Accommodation.value:
ACCOMMODATION @ RPTU in KAISERSLAUTERN: The majority of our students live in residence halls located on or close to campus. The "Studierendenwerk" operates several large halls of residence in Kaiserslautern. Students submit housing applications directly to the Studierendenwerk. For international Master's or PhD students, International Affairs RPTU aims at arranging accommodation in these residence halls or in private accommodation within its pre-arrival service. The halls of residence have modern single, double or shared apartments with kitchenette, bathroom/WC, and modern facilities as well as internet access.
Fully-furnished: kitchenette (no plates & pots, etc.), bed & mattress (no blankets & pillows), wardrobe, shelf, table, chair (no computer)
Rent: approx. 250 to 350 EUR
Since accommodation is not automatically guaranteed with admission, a request for accommodation to International Affairs ISGS is advisable.
Optional: To help international students get started in Kaiserslautern, the "Studierendenwerk" offers a starter package for the apartment. This package can be purchased for 95 EUR: https://www.studierendenwerk-kaiserslautern.de/en/housing/international.
More information: https://rptu.de/international/master/prospective-students/travel-accommodation/accommodation

Description/content.value:
In this more application-oriented Master's degree the graduates continue their education in the fields of modern mathematics and learn in-depth scientific concepts, methods and techniques that enable the graduates to handle challenging and complex mathematical problems in applications.
The Master's programme is characterised by:
scientific orientation
concentration on the specialisations in "mathematics for sustainability", "business mathematics", and "mathematical data science"
particular emphasis on practical relevance project orientation
development and extension of capacity for teamwork, good organisational skills, and leadership skills, and
the Master's thesis as an application-oriented scientific work
The graduates develop the following professional skills and competences: application of knowledge, methods and techniques from diverse subjects of mathematics on concrete problems (further elaboration in mathematical and scientific expertise, scientific working methods, problem-solving competence, and analytical mindset), quick familiarisation in new fields of application which provides experts with high-quality solutions (self-competence, critical thinking, ability to transfer established methods to new problems in practice), procedural approach based on project management methods to handle functional and organisational difficulties appearing in practical questions (organisational skills and social skills), communication skills and well-founded judgement in critical dialogue with experts in practice (communication skills and leadership skills as part of social competencies). These key qualifications empower the graduates to assume managerial positions and leadership responsibilities in the private as well as the public sector ("higher civil service"). Highly qualified graduates are prepared to enter a doctoral studies programme.
Description/content.html:
In this more application-oriented Master's degree the graduates continue their education in the fields of modern mathematics and learn in-depth scientific concepts, methods and techniques that enable the graduates to handle challenging and complex mathematical problems in applications.

The Master's programme is characterised by:

  1. scientific orientation
  2. concentration on the specialisations in "mathematics for sustainability", "business mathematics", and "mathematical data science"
  3. particular emphasis on practical relevance project orientation
  4. development and extension of capacity for teamwork, good organisational skills, and leadership skills, and
  5. the Master's thesis as an application-oriented scientific work

The graduates develop the following professional skills and competences: application of knowledge, methods and techniques from diverse subjects of mathematics on concrete problems (further elaboration in mathematical and scientific expertise, scientific working methods, problem-solving competence, and analytical mindset), quick familiarisation in new fields of application which provides experts with high-quality solutions (self-competence, critical thinking, ability to transfer established methods to new problems in practice), procedural approach based on project management methods to handle functional and organisational difficulties appearing in practical questions (organisational skills and social skills), communication skills and well-founded judgement in critical dialogue with experts in practice (communication skills and leadership skills as part of social competencies). These key qualifications empower the graduates to assume managerial positions and leadership responsibilities in the private as well as the public sector ("higher civil service"). Highly qualified graduates are prepared to enter a doctoral studies programme.

Academic admission requirements.value:
The Master's programme in Mathematics for Sustainability, Economics, and Data Science builds consecutively on a first professionally qualifying university degree with a standard period of study of six semesters (180 credit points/ECTS) from a university in mathematics or mathematics for sustainability, economics, and data science. The programme can also build on a first professionally qualifying university degree with a standard period of study of six semesters (180 credit points/ECTS) in a related programme. In this case, the first professionally qualifying university degree must contain mathematical components, particularly in the areas of:
Analysis
Stochastics
Financial Mathematics
Actuarial Mathematics, and
Operations Research
to an approximately equal extent as the undergraduate programme "Mathematics for Sustainability, Economics, and Data Science" at the Technische Hochschule Mittelhessen. The Examination Board decides on the fulfilment of these requirements.
Access to the Master's programme in the English-language version is only possible if a first professional university degree can be proven in accordance with these requirements, and the overall grade of this first professional university degree is at least "good" (2.0; at least 80 percentage points according to Section 9, Paragraph 2 of Part I of the Examination Regulations).
For international applicants who have obtained their first professional university degree in a non-German-language programme, proof of German language proficiency is required in accordance with the "Framework Regulations on German Language Examinations for Studying at German Universities" in its currently valid version by the end of the enrolment period set by the THM at the latest. If proof of language proficiency cannot be submitted by the application deadline, proof of the missing requirements is to be provided, at the latest, by the enrolment deadline for the Master's programme in Mathematics for Sustainability, Economics, and Data Science set by the THM.

Description/content.value:
The Master's study programme in Crop Science is a research-oriented study programme with the aim of imparting theoretical and methodological skills for carrying out independent and innovative research work in the field of crop science in the field of agriculture and horticulture. Students are involved in research projects and choose one of the three specialisations: "Production Ecology and Resource Conservation", "Digital Agriculture" or "Molecular Crop Science", each with a wide range of elective modules.
Mandatory courses encompass Data Analysis and Visualisation, Technology and Sensors in Precision Crop Production, Resource Conservation, Production Ecology, Crop Physiology, Crop Breeding Research, Advanced Scientific Writing and Communication.
The elective courses cover a wide range of specialised as well as interdisciplinary topics in crop sciences, such as:
General topics: sustainable production, renewable resources, horticultural production, ecosystems, agroecology, agroecosystems, sustainability, cropping systems, decision analysis, forecasting in agriculture, modelling (crops, soil, rhizosphere), crop management, tree phenology, population and quantitative genetics, crop assessment, climate change
Agricultural and horticultural production systems and management: organic agriculture, sustainable production and farming, agroforestry, decision analysis, future competent agricultural and food systems
Plant Health, plant stress, plant pathology and plant protection: entomology, nematology, crop stress, stress perception and signalling, plant-pathogen interactions, forecasting
Soil sciences: soil ecology, soil protection, soil microbiology
Crop physiology and molecular biology: plant nutrition, molecular crop physiology, crop functional genomics, plant biochemistry, plant biotechnology, plant breeding, genome analysis, genomics
Digital agriculture and advanced methods: sensors in agriculture and horticulture, sensor technology, plant phenotyping, biometry, robotics
Agricultural and horticultural ecology: agrobiodiversity, ecosystem-atmosphere interactions, climate-smart ecosystem management, element cycles, nature conservation, risk and transformation, crop ecology, water management, geobotany, ecological climatology

Description/content.value:
In the first semester of your studies, you will lay the foundations for your future success: you will attend classes on the impact environmental factors have on the wind industry, on technical maths and technical writing in English.
The second semester of your studies will focus almost entirely on wind turbines, from aerodynamics to rotor structures. You will also broaden your engineering expertise further.
In the third semester, you will choose one of four majors:
Mechanical Engineering - dynamics, materials and rotor blades
Electrical Engineering - electrical machines and system integration
Structural Engineering - tower and structure design
Project Development - wind farm planning and project development
Something that all majors share is a project in which you will design a wind turbine together with other students.
In the fourth semester, you will focus on your Master’s thesis.
Description/content.html:
In the first semester of your studies, you will lay the foundations for your future success: you will attend classes on the impact environmental factors have on the wind industry, on technical maths and technical writing in English.

The second semester of your studies will focus almost entirely on wind turbines, from aerodynamics to rotor structures. You will also broaden your engineering expertise further.

In the third semester, you will choose one of four majors:

  • Mechanical Engineering - dynamics, materials and rotor blades
  • Electrical Engineering - electrical machines and system integration
  • Structural Engineering - tower and structure design
  • Project Development - wind farm planning and project development

Something that all majors share is a project in which you will design a wind turbine together with other students.

In the fourth semester, you will focus on your Master’s thesis.

Disciplines included in the Master's are Egyptology, Ancient Near Eastern Studies, Classical Archaeology, Prehistoric Archaeology, Near Eastern Archaeology, Archaeoinformatics, and the History of Science in the Ancient World.

Applicants also need to be proficient in German (DHS 2/C1) and English (B2).

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
There are many ways of earning money while you study, for example as wait staff, academic assistants, or private tutors. Knowledge of German will improve your chances of finding a part-time job, but it isn’t necessarily required. However, it is important to be aware of the legal regulations.The student support service at the university, called "studierendenWERK Berlin", and the local representative of the "Bundesagentur für Arbeit" (Federal Employment Agency) can provide information about jobs for students.
When searching for a job, look at online job boards, notice boards on campus, and ads in local newspapers.
You can also work on campus. The Freie Universität Berlin regularly offers positions for students in science, teaching support and administration that you can find on our careers portal.

Accommodation.value:
You have the option to stay in a public/private student dormitory or in a private (shared) apartment. Student dormitories are not administrated by the university itself, so Freie Universität Berlin does not have any on-campus housing. However, it works together with "studierendenWERK Berlin" regarding student accommodation.
If you do not wish to stay in a student dormitory, you can try to find a room or an apartment on the private housing market. Many students in Berlin live in shared apartments ("WGs"). You can find these offers online (e.g. WG-Gesucht or Kleinanzeigen) or on notice boards on campus.
Available rooms/apartments near the university are rare. Therefore, students mostly commute from other parts of the city. The commute via public transportation usually takes between 30 minutes and an hour, which is considered a normal travel time in Berlin due to the size of the city.

Description/content.value:
Bioeconomy aims at the conversion of the raw material base from fossil to biogenic raw materials and builds a bridge between technology, ecology, society and economy as well as their interactions. This structural change involves the production and use of biological resources to provide products, processes and services in all economic sectors within the framework of a sustainable economic system. The courses of study in Bioeconomics train experts who can understand, accompany and shape this change. Overall, there are several areas of work for the bioeconomy.
In order to be able to accompany economic and social transformation processes, it is first necessary to understand the processes involved and the actors involved. This understanding of the bio-based economic system does not end at national borders, but includes regional considerations as well as the global effects of local action.
Secondly, the use of biogenic resources is not per se sustainable. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of sustainability and sustainable development as well as other concepts and strategies existing alongside the bioeconomy are required to achieve this. This includes in particular the approaches of closed-loop management and industrial ecology.
Thirdly, bioeconomics requires the participation of various scientific disciplines and their successful cooperation. These disciplines come from the social and economic sciences, the engineering sciences and the natural sciences.
Bio-based and bio-inspired innovations form the basis for advancing structural change. The potential of innovative products and markets as well as technologies for their implementation on the basis of biological resources are to be harnessed for industry and society.
The aim of the programme is to train innovative graduates who have an understanding of the complexity of a necessary structural change. By combining topics from micro- and macroeconomics, chemistry, engineering and life sciences with comprehensive knowledge in the field of the efficient and sustainable use of biogenic resources, graduates will have an interdisciplinary understanding and will be able to develop solutions. They are able to adopt regional, national and global perspectives.
