Course organisation.value: In the first two semesters, important mathematical, natural science, environmental economics, and macroeconomic fundamentals are taught. From the third semester onwards, knowledge from the main areas of chemistry, physics, biology, and business administration / economics is deepened. In the fifth semester, a focus is set based on elective modules. The tandem module combines two subject areas, enabling a structured and interdisciplinary approach to solving a specific problem. The programme concludes with a Bachelor’s thesis. First semester: Mathematics, Statistics, Microeconomics, Management Science, Physics, Environmental Resources in a Changing World Second semester: Organic Chemistry, Fundamentals of Thermodynamics, Empirical Research Methods, Macroeconomics, Material Flow Analysis and Life Cycle Assessment, Elective Foundations of Management (total 6 ECTS) Third semester: Foundations of Biology, Wood-based Resources, Production of Biogenic Resources, Foundation of Programming, Intermediate Microeconomics, Environmental Management Fourth semester: Introduction to Process Engineering, Policy and Innovation, Circular Economy, Introduction to Environmental and Resource Economics, Green Chemistry, Elective Foundations of Management (total 6 ECTS) Fifth semester: Governance of Bioeconomy, Technical Electives (total 23 ECTS) Sixth semester: Evidence-Based Management and Policy, Project on Public Discourses and Scientific Solutions, General Elective Module (total 3 ECTS), Bachelor's thesis Elective Foundations of Management Six credits must be obtained from the following list: Entrepreneurship, Supply Chain, Organisational Behaviour, Strategic and International Management, Innovation Management Technical Elective Modules From the following list, 23 credits must be obtained: Seminar in Behavioural Economics, Biochemistry, Biomass Utilisation, Biopolymers, Introduction to Development Economics, Behavioural Economics, Modelling and Optimisation, Seminar in Innovation and Technology Management, and Project Study. General Elective Modules Three credits must be obtained from the following list: can be chosen from the total range of courses offered by TUM.

Description/content.value:
INNOVATIVE. SUSTAINABLE. SMART.
Are you dreaming of a technical career in Germany and want to prepare ideally? Discover the Bilingual Electrical Engineering programme at THM.
Imagine programming the artificial intelligence of the future, developing the smart buildings of tomorrow, and driving the energy transition forward.
Our digital and sustainable future needs YOU!
At the THM, you will dive into hands-on projects, exchange ideas with local students, and learn German at no extra costs. After nine semesters you will hold a recognised Bachelor's degree, offering you many opportunities.
The goal of our programme is to equip students with the ability to actively shape the process of digitalisation in industry and society and to advance it with professional expertise.
Depending on your chosen specialisation (after the fifth semester), our Bachelor’s programme has an open admission policy and lets you learn how to advance modern power electronics and energy storage systems (specialisation in General Electrical Engineering), plan and implement complex automation systems for modern and sustainable buildings (specialisation in Building Automation) or, for example, deepen your knowledge in the field of networks and networked systems (specialisation in Technical Computer Science).
Graduates are able to independently design, implement, and maintain electrical engineering products and processes, as well as complex systems in the fields of energy, building, automotive, and systems engineering. This includes the collection, storage, and processing of information in digital form and the transmission of energy. Or you can go down a different route and pursue an academic career after graduation. Continue e.g. with our English-taught Master’s in Control, Computer and Communications Engineering (CCCE) or our consecutive Master’s in "Elektro- und Informationstechnik" (EIT).
The German equivalent programme, "Elektro- und Informationstechnik" was successfully re-accredited in 2021 by the "Stiftung Akkreditierungsrat" (German Accreditation Council). The accreditation also includes the introduction of the "Bilingual Electrical Engineering" variant in 2025 and has been confirmed by the Accreditation Council.

Course organisation.value: The Bilingual Electrical Engineering programme extends the standard duration of study by two semesters. Duration: nine semesters (one extra year for a relaxed start and smooth language integration) including the Bachelor's thesis and defence Study the first four semesters in English Learn German in parallel – without extra fees Switch to German-taught courses after four semesters Curriculum: Total of 210 credit points In the first four semesters, students are required to take an additional language course designed to improve their German language skills (German B1.1, B1.2, C1.1, C1.2). Starting in the second semester, students are required to attend supplementary courses e.g. technical courses in mathematics, programming, physics, digital electronics or even courses in literature research. The supplementary courses are conducted in German but are not graded. They are individually selected based on previous knowledge and supportive needs. A certificate of participation is issued at the end of the semester. Starting in the fifth semester, courses are taught in German and exams are administered in German, unless otherwise specified in the course description. In semesters six to eight, electives are chosen based on the chosen specialisation and individual interests. Currently, the following specialisations are offered: General Electrical Engineering Technical Computer Science Building Automation During the ninth and final semester, a “Professional Practice Phase (BPP)”, a mandatory internship lasting 13 weeks, is integrated into the curriculum. Through this experience, students are able to apply theoretical knowledge in a practical setting relevant to their specialisation. It serves to provide career guidance, facilitate project work, and help students establish professional contacts. The final requirement for graduation is a final project which is the Bachelor's thesis and an accompanying defence. PDF Download

Starting in the second semester, students are required to attend supplementary courses e.g. technical courses in mathematics, programming, physics, digital electronics or even courses in literature research. The supplementary courses are conducted in German but are not graded. They are individually selected based on previous knowledge and supportive needs. A certificate of participation is issued at the end of the semester.

Starting in the fifth semester, courses are taught in German and exams are administered in German, unless otherwise specified in the course description.

In semesters six to eight, electives are chosen based on the chosen specialisation and individual interests. Currently, the following specialisations are offered:

  • General Electrical Engineering
  • Technical Computer Science
  • Building Automation

During the ninth and final semester, a “Professional Practice Phase (BPP)”, a mandatory internship lasting 13 weeks, is integrated into the curriculum. Through this experience, students are able to apply theoretical knowledge in a practical setting relevant to their specialisation.

It serves to provide career guidance, facilitate project work, and help students establish professional contacts.

The final requirement for graduation is a final project which is the Bachelor's thesis and an accompanying defence.

Description/content.value:
The Institute of Organismic Biology at the University of Bonn is the only institution in Germany offering a Master of Science programme in Palaeontology. This programme is designed around interdisciplinary, research-oriented courses in both the geosciences and biosciences, with a focus on understanding the patterns and processes that have shaped the evolution of life and its environments throughout Earth’s history. The Institute is dedicated to excellence in teaching, learning, and research, and is committed to preparing future leaders across the natural sciences.
A distinctive strength of the Master's programme lies in its diverse faculty, whose expertise spans vertebrate palaeontology, invertebrate palaeontology, micropalaeontology, and palaeobotany. Students can also elect modules in geoscience, organismic evolution and palaeobiology. This breadth of specialisation allows the programme to offer a wide range of courses that equip students with knowledge and skills highly valued in both academia and beyond.
The Master's programme is primarily intended for applicants with a strong interest in palaeontology, evolutionary biology, and the history of life on Earth. Proficiency in English is essential for attending lectures, participating in exercises, fieldwork, and student projects, as well as for completing examinations.

Description/content.value:
The focal area Engineering Physics is designed for students with a strong interest in physics-based approaches within engineering. It focuses on electromagnetically-dominated and multiphysical systems in which electric and magnetic fields, waves, particles, transport processes, material properties, and non-linear dynamics are strongly coupled.
The programme combines a solid foundation in electromagnetic field theory, quantum mechanics, plasma technology, photonics, and microsystems technology with modern methods of theoretical analysis, modelling, simulation, experimental diagnostics, and laboratory work. Students learn to analyse complex physical and technological systems theoretically, investigate them experimentally, model them quantitatively, and contribute to their technological realisation.
The focal area includes courses on plasma technology, photonics, quantum mechanics, fields, waves and particles, microsystems, and plasma diagnostics and laboratory experiments. Students can further specialise in competence areas such as plasma engineering, photonics, microsystems technology, and modelling and simulation.
Engineering Physics provides a research-oriented profile within the Master's programme in Electrical Engineering and Information Technology. It prepares students for scientific and industrial careers in modern high-technology fields, including plasma and surface technology, optical technologies, semiconductor and microsystems technology, numerical simulation, and related areas of applied physics and engineering.

Course organisation.value:
The Master’s programme is research-oriented and spans two years and encompasses 120 ECTS credits. It aims to equip you with advanced knowledge and skills needed to excel in the dynamic fields of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology. Engineering Physics is one of three areas of specialisation offered entirely in English.
The programme is designed to provide a balanced and in-depth learning experience, divided into four key areas, each worth 30 CP:
Compulsory courses (30 CP)
The compulsory courses, typically completed in the first two semesters, lay the foundation for your specialised studies. These courses ensure a solid understanding of the fundamental principles that underpin your chosen area of specialisation.
Compulsory elective courses (30 CP)
The compulsory elective courses allow you to tailor your education to your interests and career goals. Choose from a variety of courses that align with your academic passions. Additionally, participate in a seminar (3 CP) and a laboratory practical (3 CP) to gain hands-on experience in our state-of-the-art research labs and engage in cutting-edge scientific discourse.
Free elective area (30 CP)
Broaden your horizons by selecting from the diverse offerings at the Ruhr-Universität Bochum and the University Alliance Ruhr. You can choose further courses in your field of specialisation or another engineering discipline, or focus on soft skills such as language courses, intercultural competence, etc. This area is also well-suited for a study abroad experience, for example, through one of our numerous co-operations within the Erasmus programme.
Master’s thesis (30 CP)
The Master’s thesis is a capstone project where you demonstrate your ability to tackle complex engineering challenges with innovative solutions. Over a six-month period, you will independently conduct research using scientific methods, applying both technical and interdisciplinary skills. You will document your findings in a comprehensive written report and present your key results in a colloquium lecture to showcase your presentation and argumentation skills.

Accommodation.value:
In the city of Bochum, you can find different types of accommodation. On average, students in Bochum pay approximately 400 to 800 EUR per month for a single apartment, which is below the average rent in Germany. A room in a shared apartment is usually less expensive.
About 5,000 students in Bochum live in multiple student halls close to the campus, which are run by the Akademisches Förderungswerk (AKAFÖ). In the halls, each student has a single room and shares a kitchen and bathroom with other students, rents an apartment with a private bathroom and kitchen, or shares an apartment with one or several flatmates.
More information on the student halls can be found at https://studium.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/de/wohnen.
In addition, private and church-affiliated student halls accommodate up to 1,000 students: http://www.stuwo.de/wohnheim-region/bochum/.

Description/content.value:
The Bachelor’s programme in Geodesy and Earth Observation focuses on the precise monitoring, measurement, and mapping of the Earth and its habitats. Using state‑of‑the‑art methods for data acquisition, modelling, and processing, students learn how high‑quality geoinformation is generated — information that is essential for a wide range of scientific, societal, and technical applications.
The data collected and analysed by geodesists ensures legal certainty in official surveying and forms a reliable basis for planning, regulation, and land management. Beyond this, geodetic measurements and Earth observation techniques provide indispensable data for disaster management, environmental risk assessment, and research into the Earth system, global change, and planetary processes.
The central aim of geodesy and Earth observation is the detailed recording and analysis of the human environment. Through precise measurement techniques, structured processing of geospatial information, and targeted visual presentation, geodesists describe our surroundings, classify them according to relevant characteristics, and contribute their expertise to shaping and managing change in a sustainable way.
Students gain hands‑on experience with classical measurement instruments such as theodolites, laser scanners, and cameras, while also working with modern information systems, satellite technologies, and digital remote sensing sensors. An important focus of the programme is the development and application of automated, computer‑aided methods for acquiring, processing, analysing, and visualising spatial data.
The field of Geodesy and Earth Observation is broad and diverse, covering applications ranging from satellite‑based global Earth measurements and air‑borne regional terrain surveys to terrestrial, locally focused engineering surveys of buildings, infrastructure, and machines. In addition, geodetic measurement methods play a key role in disaster response, environmental monitoring, risk assessment, and Earth system research.
The Bachelor’s programme provides a strong scientific and technical foundation and prepares students for advanced studies or entry into a wide range of professional fields related to geospatial data and Earth observation.
Education in geodesy therefore plays an important role in society. The use of digital technologies and modern analysis strategies is an integral part of the Bachelor's programme in Geodesy and Earth Observation and provides an integrated, comprehensive foundation in the entire field.

Course organisation.value:
The standard period of study for the Bachelor's programme in Geodesy and Earth Observation (GEObs) is six semesters (180 ECTS), with studies beginning in the winter semester. The credit load for each semester is 30 ECTS, with no more than six exams to be taken per semester. The programme comprises five categories of modules: basic and orientation exams (GOPs), GEObs core modules, GEObs elective modules, free elective modules, and a Bachelor's thesis. GOPs, GEObs core modules, and the Bachelor's thesis are compulsory, while GEObs electives and free electives can be freely chosen from a catalogue of electives provided.
Study Structure & Content
The basic and orientation exams (GOPs) must be successfully passed within the first two semesters. In semesters one to four, there are 18 core GEObs modules to be completed. They define the fundamentals of all disciplines of geodesy and Earth observation, from modern engineering geodesy to photogrammetry, remote sensing from the ground, air, and space, satellite geodesy, Earth surveying and modelling, cartography, and geoinformatics to land management. They build on each other to some extent, starting with the basics, which are expanded upon with more in-depth knowledge and advanced methodological approaches. The content is then further deepened in the GEObs electives, which allow students to focus on individual topics, methods, and skills.
GEObs elective modules can be chosen in semesters four to six. The elective areas give students the opportunity to orient themselves in a specific direction in order to prepare for a Master's degree in their individual field of interest or to pursue a professional profile in a specific subject area. The list of GEObs elective modules includes various modules offered in the summer and winter semesters. Students must select at least 10 of these modules.
The degree programme concludes with a Bachelor's thesis, in which the methodological, technical, and practical skills acquired are brought together in their application.

Description/content.value:
Digitalisation has created many new legal questions that go far beyond the regular curriculum. The “Digitalisation & Law” Master's programme at JMU aims at addressing these legal problems in a specialised programme.
It is designed for professionals seeking a specialisation in the field of digitalisation and IT law. A previous IT background is not required; the necessary technical knowledge will be imparted in the courses.
All courses are taught in English and will be held by renowned professors and specialised lawyers in the historic city of Würzburg.
The first semester consists of six compulsory courses: Introduction to Informatics, Introduction to German IT Law, Machine Ethics, Fundamental Rights and Data Protection, Cybercrime I, and Procedure Law.
In the second semester, the students can choose six of the following courses: Company Law and Digitalisation, Legal Tech, Competition Law in the Digital Age, IP Law, Cybercrime II, Robot Law / AI Law, E-commerce / Consumer Protection, Public Law in the Digital Age and Labour Law and Digitalisation.
The third semester is reserved for the Master's thesis and the oral examination.
After a successful completion of the programme, the University of Würzburg awards graduates with the academic degree of "Master of Laws" (LLM). For practising lawyers in Germany, the University of Würzburg can award graduates with a certificate for the theoretical part of the specialist lawyer in IT Law (Fachanwalt IT-Recht, § 14k FAO).

Course organisation.value:
The LLM is structured as a 90-ECTS Master’s programme. The first two semesters each count for 30 ECTS, and the Master’s semester also counts for 30 ECTS, with 25 ECTS awarded for the Master’s thesis and 5 ECTS for the oral examination.
Although the LLM is described as a full-time programme, it can be studied alongside a job. Lectures are held on weekday evenings and as block courses on Friday evenings and Saturdays.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
Finding part-time employment in Würzburg is a great way to gain experience, make new connections, and supplement your finances while studying. Students from EU and EEA countries enjoy equal terms in the labour market and can work freely during their studies. Students from other countries can work up to 140 full days or 280 half days per year, including voluntary internships. If you wish to work more, you'll need permission from the employment agency ("Agentur für Arbeit") or the immigration office.
It's important to ensure that your studies remain your top priority, so choose a side job that complements your academic schedule. The University of Würzburg offers resources to help you find part-time work, such as the student job portal.

Finding the perfect place to live is an important part of your student experience at the University of Würzburg. Unlike some other countries, students in Germany need to find their own accommodation, as universities do not automatically provide it. At the University of Würzburg, you have two main options: "Studierendenwerk" housing or private rooms/student halls.
The Student Housing Service ("Studierendenwerk") manages 12 student residences in Würzburg, offering a total of 2,887 rooms. These dormitories provide a variety of amenities:
Single and double rooms or apartments shared by two to four students, with communal kitchens and bathrooms
Furnished rooms and apartments are available, though you'll need to bring your own dishes, cooking items, bedding, and towels.
To apply for housing, note the deadlines: 15 June for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester. For more information about private rooms and student halls, visit the Central Student Advisory Service.
In addition to Studierendenwerk housing, there are many private accommodation options available:
Shared apartments ("Wohngemeinschaften" or "WGs"): These are popular among students and offer a great way to meet new people and share living costs.
Private student halls: These are often run by private companies and offer similar amenities to Studierendenwerk dormitories. They can be a bit more expensive but may offer more modern facilities.
Short-term accommodation: If you need a place to stay while you search for permanent housing, consider options like hostels, guest houses, or short-term rentals.
Remember to start your housing search early and stay positive! With a bit of patience and diligence, you'll find a cosy place to call home.

Description/content.value:
This international Master’s programme combines advanced academic training with an exceptional level of clinical practice. Designed for experienced dentists, its compact part-time format allows you to deepen your specialisation without stepping away from your practice or personal commitments.
Weekly online sessions provide the flexibility to integrate your studies into your professional routine. The clinical training forms the core of the programme: around 75 hours of hands-on sessions across three intensive clinical blocks in Dresden (Germany) and Ferrara (Italy) give you the opportunity to apply advanced techniques directly under the guidance of internationally recognised specialists.
From diagnostics and evidence-based treatment planning to periodontal therapy and implantology, the programme focuses on skills that can be transferred directly into everyday clinical practice. Health psychology and scientific research complement the curriculum, enabling you to approach complex cases from both a clinical and academic perspective. This distinctive combination of flexible online learning, intensive clinical training, and international expertise sets the programme apart from many comparable Master’s programmes in Europe. You will expand your treatment portfolio, strengthen the positioning of your practice, and build a valuable professional network across Europe. At the same time, you will gain access to further academic opportunities, including the possibility of publishing your Master’s thesis in an international peer-reviewed journal.

Course organisation.value:
Programme structure
The “Periodontology and Implant Therapy (M.Sc.)” degree programme has a modular structure. Over the course of four semesters, students build advanced knowledge in periodontology and implant therapy while systematically expanding their scientific, diagnostic, and clinical competencies.
The curriculum combines foundational knowledge, evidence-based diagnostics, non-surgical and surgical therapy concepts, implantology, interdisciplinary treatment planning, and scientific work. In this way, the programme connects academic depth with direct relevance for clinical practice.
Students learn to assess complex periodontal and implant-related cases, make evidence-based treatment decisions, and apply modern therapeutic concepts in a way that is structured and professionally responsible. At the same time, they strengthen their ability to critically evaluate research, develop academic projects, and transfer scientific findings into everyday professional practice.
Study schedule
First to third semester: Students complete the taught modules of the degree programme. These cover the foundations of periodontology and implant therapy, diagnostics and treatment planning, scientific work, pathology and therapy concepts, implant therapy, interdisciplinary treatment approaches, and project work.
The programme combines weekly online sessions with guided self-study and clinical in-person phases. Three clinical weekends in Dresden and Ferrara (Italy) provide hands-on training, supervised clinical exchange, and direct interaction with experienced specialists from across Europe.
Fourth semester: Master’s thesis phase, including the preparation, writing, presentation, and defence of the Master’s thesis

Description/content.value:
Globalisation processes are strongly linked to issues of peace and security as well as stability and development — not only in Africa. Globalisation processes, including colonisation, de-colonisation, the end of the Cold War, effects of 9/11, the 2008 economic and financial crisis, the so-called Arab Spring, the climate crisis and other current international developments have created particular challenges, risks, threats and vulnerabilities for the African continent.
Globalisation is affecting Africa in specific ways, and globalisation processes (past and present) have implications for security in Africa. The increase in civil wars, intra-state and cross-border conflicts following the end of the Cold War is just one example. Durable peace and stability in Africa have been identified as preconditions for the development of the continent in a constantly globalising world. As such, peace and security research is of special interest to the region. The creation of the Peace and Security Council (PSC) of the African Union and other related policy and research institutions are further point to this need. Linking the subject of “Peace and Security” to the field of “Global Studies” not only allows us to analyse the spatial context but also the global dimensions of peace and security in Africa.
The aim of the programme is the interdisciplinary and transnational training of experts in peace and security issues, particularly on the African continent, with special consideration of the new global configurations in which these conflicts take place. Accordingly, the curriculum goes beyond the traditional focus of peace and security studies, integrating it with the knowledge scope of global studies.
This unique Master's programme combines the expertise of two partner institutes in the fields of globalisation research (GESI) and "Peace and Security in Africa" (IPSS).
The learning targets of the programme are as follows:
to become familiar with different academic ways of looking at processes of globalisation
to learn about how concepts of globalisation operated in the past and today in various world regions, specifically in Africa, and how processes of globalisation interact with aspects of peace and security
to work with concepts from different analytical and theoretical perspectives
to systematically compare socio-political concepts and configurations as well as to investigate their mutual interactions
to gain insights into the production of social science knowledge and to relate knowledge production to concepts of globalisation and peace and security
to become aware of one's own rootedness in a specific discipline and academic culture

Course organisation.value:
The Master's in "Global Studies with a Special Emphasis on Peace and Security in Africa" is a two-year Master's divided into four phases (two winter and two summer semesters). The programme has a modular structure in line with the European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS), as initiated by the Bologna Process. It is made up of 120 credits (30 credits each semester), which is equivalent to a study workload of 900 hours per semester or 1,800 hours per year. It combines established teaching methods (lectures, seminars, tutorials, group work, etc.) with practical experiences such as research internships.
The programme combines on-site and online elements. While lecturers from Leipzig University teach the students in block courses on-site in Addis Ababa, the students also have the opportunity to attend some course elements online.
The first, third and fourth semesters take place at Addis Ababa University with lecturers from Leipzig and Addis Ababa teaching courses together. The second semester takes place at Leipzig University, linking the students' studies in Ethiopia directly to their training in Germany.

The programme combines on-site and online elements. While lecturers from Leipzig University teach the students in block courses on-site in Addis Ababa, the students also have the opportunity to attend some course elements online.

The first, third and fourth semesters take place at Addis Ababa University with lecturers from Leipzig and Addis Ababa teaching courses together. The second semester takes place at Leipzig University, linking the students' studies in Ethiopia directly to their training in Germany.

Description/content.value:
The MBA programme in “AI, Regulatory Affairs & Transformation in Medical Technology (MBA)” at Dresden International University (DIU) combines artificial intelligence, digital medical technologies, regulatory affairs, quality management, and leadership. It is designed for experienced professionals who want to understand, evaluate, and shape AI-enabled transformation in healthcare and medical technology under real regulatory conditions.
The programme provides advanced theoretical and practice-oriented competencies to assess digital healthcare systems, manage AI-enabled medical device development, understand regulatory frameworks such as MDR, IVDR, and the EU AI Act, and lead transformation processes in complex healthcare environments.
Please note: A positive accreditation report has been issued, and applications are already being accepted. The Accreditation Council will grant accreditation in September 2026.
Description/content.html:
The MBA programme in “AI, Regulatory Affairs & Transformation in Medical Technology (MBA)” at Dresden International University (DIU) combines artificial intelligence, digital medical technologies, regulatory affairs, quality management, and leadership. It is designed for experienced professionals who want to understand, evaluate, and shape AI-enabled transformation in healthcare and medical technology under real regulatory conditions.

The programme provides advanced theoretical and practice-oriented competencies to assess digital healthcare systems, manage AI-enabled medical device development, understand regulatory frameworks such as MDR, IVDR, and the EU AI Act, and lead transformation processes in complex healthcare environments.

Please note: A positive accreditation report has been issued, and applications are already being accepted. The Accreditation Council will grant accreditation in September 2026.

Course organisation.value:
Programme structure
The AI, Regulatory Affairs & Transformation in Medical Technology MBA is structured as a modular part-time degree programme. The curriculum combines scientific research and leadership with healthcare technology, medical technology development, regulatory affairs, and AI-enabled transformation. Students develop the strategic, analytical, regulatory, and technological skills needed to evaluate innovations and lead transformation processes across healthcare and the MedTech sector.
The programme covers areas such as scientific research, leadership in digital healthcare, healthcare delivery models, medical technology development, medical device regulation, and the digital transformation of healthcare, product development, and regulatory processes. Students also gain essential competencies in data, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, interoperability, health IT systems, quality management, and risk assessment.
A particular focus is placed on connecting technological innovation with regulatory requirements and organisational implementation. Practice-oriented assignments, case studies, and interdisciplinary exchange prepare students to manage AI-enabled medical technologies throughout their life cycle and take on strategic leadership roles in healthcare, medical technology, regulatory affairs, quality management, and digital transformation.
Study schedule
Classes on-site and online: three online sessions per month and nine consecutive days on-site in Dresden
Language of instruction: English
Additional components: scientific working, empirical research, statistics, leadership development, and team competence

Description/content.value:
The research-oriented Master’s programme in Physics leading to the Master of Science (MSc) degree provides students with in-depth technical knowledge, skills and methods that enable them to work independently in science, to develop innovative ideas, to critically classify scientific findings and to act responsibly.
Students receive a comprehensive education in physics as well as an insight into the content and methods of related sciences. The education in the Master's programme includes modules in theoretical and experimental physics. Connections to neighbouring disciplines or applications of physics in engineering, life sciences or in medicine are established through the non-physics elective. Interdisciplinary key qualifications and content are also taught as part of the programme, e.g. an introduction to the planning and coordination of scientific projects or training in skills for the comprehensible communication of scientific findings.
Description/content.html:
The research-oriented Master’s programme in Physics leading to the Master of Science (MSc) degree provides students with in-depth technical knowledge, skills and methods that enable them to work independently in science, to develop innovative ideas, to critically classify scientific findings and to act responsibly.

Students receive a comprehensive education in physics as well as an insight into the content and methods of related sciences. The education in the Master's programme includes modules in theoretical and experimental physics. Connections to neighbouring disciplines or applications of physics in engineering, life sciences or in medicine are established through the non-physics elective. Interdisciplinary key qualifications and content are also taught as part of the programme, e.g. an introduction to the planning and coordination of scientific projects or training in skills for the comprehensible communication of scientific findings.

Course organisation.value:
In the first year of study, students acquire advanced knowledge in the subfields of quantum mechanics and statistical physics as part of the theoretical physics curriculum (module “Theoretical Physics V”).
In the experimental component of the programme, more advanced concepts in solid-state physics and atomic physics are covered (module “Experimental Physics V”). This includes the application of modern experimental methods in research lab courses and current projects conducted by experimentally oriented research groups.
The second year of the Master’s programme can be characterised as a research phase. In the third semester, students are prepared for the Master’s thesis, which constitutes the completion of the degree programme.

Academic admission requirements.value:
Admission to the consecutive Master’s degree programme in Physics requires both of the following:
a Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent university degree with a focus on physics or a subject closely related to physics
specific aptitude for a Master’s programme, which is generally demonstrated by a Bachelor’s degree with an overall grade of 2.5 or better, or by passing an aptitude assessment test
For the Physics degree programme, subject-specific competencies are required in the areas of mechanics, electrodynamics and optics, thermodynamics and statistics, atomic and molecular physics, condensed matter physics, nuclear and particle physics, as well as quantum mechanics. The number of credit points earned in lectures and tutorials in experimental physics, theoretical physics, and mathematical foundations should be at least 30 CP in each area. At least 20 CP should have been obtained through physics laboratory courses.

Description/content.value:
The Master’s programme in Process Management and Resource Efficiency combines innovative management approaches with technical expertise to make industrial processes more efficient, sustainable and future-ready. Students develop key competencies in process optimisation, lean management, project management, digitalisation, quality management, energy efficiency and sustainability.
The programme focuses on a holistic approach to production and business processes – from analysing existing workflows and reducing waste to developing sustainable and innovative solutions. Methods such as agile project management, Six Sigma, value analysis and process controlling are taught and applied in a practical context.
Through the close integration of theory and practice at Hochschule Landshut and the Technology Centre for Production and Logistics Systems (TZ PULS) in Dingolfing, students gain hands-on experience in a realistic learning and demonstration factory and work on current challenges from industry and business.
The programme prepares graduates to manage complex transformation processes, use resources efficiently and support companies in achieving greater sustainability, innovation and competitiveness.
Description/content.html:
The Master’s programme in Process Management and Resource Efficiency combines innovative management approaches with technical expertise to make industrial processes more efficient, sustainable and future-ready. Students develop key competencies in process optimisation, lean management, project management, digitalisation, quality management, energy efficiency and sustainability.

The programme focuses on a holistic approach to production and business processes – from analysing existing workflows and reducing waste to developing sustainable and innovative solutions. Methods such as agile project management, Six Sigma, value analysis and process controlling are taught and applied in a practical context.

Through the close integration of theory and practice at Hochschule Landshut and the Technology Centre for Production and Logistics Systems (TZ PULS) in Dingolfing, students gain hands-on experience in a realistic learning and demonstration factory and work on current challenges from industry and business.

The programme prepares graduates to manage complex transformation processes, use resources efficiently and support companies in achieving greater sustainability, innovation and competitiveness.

Course organisation.value: The Process Management and Resource Efficiency degree programme has a standard duration of five semesters. In the first three semesters, you will take part in seminars from the module areas of business administration, technology, practice and integration. In the fourth and fifth semesters, you will write your Master's thesis, in which you will work intensively and in detail on answering a scientific question related to your degree programme. Each semester includes one to two on-campus weeks with practical modules conducted at the learning and demonstration factory TZ PULS or at campus Landshut. The rest of the semester consists of online study, including virtual courses according to the lecture timetable and self-study. Academic admission requirements.value:
Admission requirements according to the study and examination regulations are:
Domestic or foreign university degree with, as a rule, at least 210 ECTS points or an equivalent qualification. (If you have a university degree with fewer ECTS points, please contact us so that we can show you solutions for admission).
Proof of at least one year of qualified professional practice; qualified activities include at least one of the following areas: project work; system analysis; system design; system testing; project support activities in purchasing, marketing and sales, controlling, production, development or resource management; professional or disciplinary management of employees
English language skills, at least level C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages
If you have any questions about admission, we will of course be happy to advise you individually and show you how to provide evidence.

Description/content.value:
Do you want to study in an English-speaking study programme with a focus on business and leadership at one of the largest universities of applied sciences in Germany?
Do you want to develop leadership skills and gather intercultural experience to construct your future career in a responsible and future-proof manner?
Do you want to learn an additional widely used business language (German, Chinese or Spanish) to improve your chances in an increasingly globalised job market?
Then the International Business and Leadership (BSc) is the right choice for you.
The degree programme places a special emphasis, both in terms of content and methodology, on leadership skills and intercultural collaboration in business. Graduates are able to responsibly manage global developments and their regional consequences as leaders. In addition to imparting subject-specific skills, the teaching and learning formats aim to empower students to take personal responsibility for their individual academic success and for their collaboration as a peer group. Modules for foreign language acquisition complement the subject-specific and interdisciplinary skills and promote student collaboration. Language tandems are an integral part of the curriculum. They offer students flexibility in terms of content while simultaneously giving them responsibility for the joint development of the programme.

Description/content.value: The Bachelor's in Mechanical System Engineering is a modern degree designed to bridge the gap between traditional mechanical engineering and digitalisation. The programme targets both international students who want to enter the German job market and local students seeking an international edge, focusing heavily on AI, machine learning, and simulation. Students begin with engineering basics like CAD and materials science before specialising in virtual engineering methods and mechatronics. The curriculum is highly practical, featuring hands-on lab work with humanoid robots and electric race cars, a mandatory internship semester in the industry, and a final thesis completed at a company to build direct professional networks. Through integrated language training and a "digital-first" approach, the programme prepares graduates for high-demand roles in the evolving global industry.

Description/content.value: The programme in microbiology addresses all aspects of microbiological research, including prokaryotic and eukaryotic systems. Bacterial and fungal systematics, biotechnology, physiology, ecology, molecular biology, cell biology, applied microbiology, genetics, interactions with other organisms, and environmental interactions are covered. The study programme is based on interdisciplinary research and involves cooperation with the Leibniz Institute for Natural Product Research and Infection Biology — Hans Knöll Institute, the Max Planck Institute for Chemical Ecology, and associated biotechnology companies.

Course organisation.value: The degree programme is structured in modules. Individual modules consist of lectures, seminars, exercises, practical courses, field courses, excursions, project work, tutorials, laboratory classes, colloquia, independent studies, and examinations. Each module is a combined learning and assessment unit. Each module extends over one semester or an academic year. The modules for the first academic year provide a basis for further development of previously acquired knowledge and for preparation of independent project work as well as for developing skills in presenting scientific results. Therefore, the first academic year comprises three basic modules (compulsory) as well as three advanced modules (compulsory elective). Additional modules may be recognised following evaluation by the board of examiners.

A Bachelor of Science degree in biology entitles the applicant to apply for the Master's programme in microbiology. Admission is based on selection criteria and grades, and a letter of motivation is taken into consideration. The following application documents are to be submitted as certified copies by the set deadline:
a) proof of having passed academic examinations and detailed documentation of completed studies in the first degree programme leading to a professional qualification
b) if relevant, proof of research experience (research activities, publications, research work, periods spent abroad carrying out research or studying)
c) if relevant, proof of relevant professional experience (e.g. as a biology technician, industrial experience)

Description/content.value:
Are you looking to open doors to an international career in the fields of business, sustainability, and innovation? Welcome to MIBAS.
Study sustainable business
MIBAS offers you a rigorous education in the fields of international business, sustainability and innovation. The programme combines a strong base of generalist knowledge within these three pillars with a broad variety of electives that allow you to focus your studies in line with your interests.
What does that mean? Are you interested in things like the following?
How businesses can make true sustainability profitable
How innovation and entrepreneurship can make a social impact
What opportunities sustainable investing and finance offer
The fundamentals and fine points of sustainability reporting
Then you’re in the right place (and of course, this is just the beginning). As a MIBAS student, you’ll confront and debate these types of issues and many more on a daily basis — at the number-one ranked university for sustainability in Germany.

Study sustainable business

MIBAS offers you a rigorous education in the fields of international business, sustainability and innovation. The programme combines a strong base of generalist knowledge within these three pillars with a broad variety of electives that allow you to focus your studies in line with your interests.

What does that mean? Are you interested in things like the following?

  • How businesses can make true sustainability profitable
  • How innovation and entrepreneurship can make a social impact
  • What opportunities sustainable investing and finance offer
  • The fundamentals and fine points of sustainability reporting

Course organisation.value:
MIBAS is divided into four semesters and six modules spanning a broad range of subject areas and 120 ECTS credits.
Courses are designed to provide you with a rigorous foundation in the core areas of the programme — business, sustainability, and innovation management — and support you in developing and pursuing specialised knowledge in your areas of interest. After you’ve completed the programme, you’ll be equipped to take on a role in international management and navigate the complexity of today’s globalised business landscape.
Semester 1: Modules I and II provide a foundation in business administration and research methods.
Semester 2-3: Modules III-VI deepen and specialise your knowledge in sustainability and innovation in the context of management, finance and accounting. Room for electives allows you to further individualise your studies.
Semester 4: The last semester is devoted to your Master’s thesis, a significant research project allowing you to use the skills and knowledge you’ve developed during the programme to explore a research question of your choice.
The programme content is outlined in detail in the following:
Subject-Specific Provisions (Fachspezifische Bedingungen)
Examination Regulations (Prüfungsordnung)
Course catalogue
Please note that the exact course offering varies each semester; all courses listed on this page are subject to change.

Academic admission requirements.value:
To be admitted to MIBAS, you’ll need to meet the following eligibility requirements:
A Bachelor’s degree (at least 180 ECTS) in socioeconomics or in a comparable interdisciplinary socio-economic degree programme, business administration, law, social sciences, sociology, economics or business studies. In exceptional cases, graduates of other academic degree programmes may also be admitted, provided that they can usefully build on their knowledge from their previous studies. If you’re currently completing the last semester of your Bachelor’s programme, you can still apply and receive conditional acceptance. See admissions for details on applying while completing your final Bachelor’s semester.
A proof of completion of one of the following study aptitude tests:
Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT) Focus Edition with a total score of at least 545 points or
Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT) Tenth Edition with a total score of at least 570 points or
Graduate Record Examination (GRE) General Test with a scaled score of at least 151 points in Verbal Reasoning and a scaled score of at least 156 points in Quantitative Reasoning or
Graduate Test for programmes in Economics, Business and Social Sciences (GTEBS; former name: TM-WISO (Test für Masterstudiengänge in den Wirtschafts- und Sozialwissenschaften)) with an achieved test value (standard value) of at least 95 points: The English language version of GTEBS must be taken.
(Note: Submission of proof of English language proficiency e.g. TOEFL or IELTS is not an admission requirement. Your English proficiency is automatically tested through the successful completion of a study aptitude test (GMAT, GRE, GTEBS) — see minimum required scores above.)

Description/content.value:
BECOME A MICROELECTRONICS ENGINEER AND BE PART OF THE MOST IMPACTFUL DEVELOPMENTS IN TECHNOLOGY
Microelectronics Engineering is not only already one of the pillars of our modern world, but also the key to the future of technology. Just in 2025, Germany proclaimed microelectronics engineering as one of only six key enabling technologies in the national High-Tech Agenda, underlining the strategic goal of Germany and Europe to re-establish a strong ecosystem in microelectronics. Become part of this development and take the chance to dive into microelectronics at TU Braunschweig!
The specialisation in “Microelectronics Engineering” is part of the Master’s degree programme in “Electrical Engineering” at TU Braunschweig, and it provides a broad insight into fascinating quantum technologies, including both silicon CMOS as well as Gallium Nitride-based microelectronics and photonics.
WHAT IS SPECIAL ABOUT TU BRAUNSCHWEIG?
TU Braunschweig has established an internationally visible centre for microelectronics, the Nitride Technology Center (NTC) together with its regional partners Leibniz Universität Hannover and Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt Braunschweig (PTB), the second largest national metrology institute worldwide. NTC is a well-known hub for technology exchange between academia, start-ups and industry.
With the “Microelectronics Engineering” specialisation, you will become a part of this network and get a sound introduction to microelectronics, including front-end and back-end chip processing as well as chip design. Discover both, the world of silicon as well as Gallium Nitride technology in a hands-on fashion. Our strong ecosystem in microelectronics offers an early contact to the global microelectronics industry as well as regional start-ups, giving you ideal starting conditions for your professional career.

Description/content.value:
The study programme envisages an obligatory thematic concentration on the following study profiles:
The Applied African Linguistics study profile: Language Education and Language Planning offers advanced courses in all areas of language management, status and corpus planning and related field of language in education. While a strong focus is placed on the aspect of societal multilingualism in Africa and its relevance to the educational sector, the informal educational background of people coming from African countries is also considered. Graduates acquire the appropriate qualifications for Africa-related responsible jobs in education, governmental or non-governmental cooperation and international organisations.
The Linguistic Analysis and Language Documentation study profile offers advanced courses in all areas of formal grammar and linguistic field methods. Topics include elicitation, transcription, annotation and analysis of linguistic data from un(der)described African languages. It also covers aspects of documentary linguistics, the production of linguistic-ethnographic records through annotated audio and video data.
The Ethiopian and Eritrean Studies study profile develops and deepens the graduates’ knowledge of Ethiopian and Eritrean languages, literatures, cultures and religions. It gives the opportunity to learn the philological method and to apply it to the texts transmitted in manuscripts. The students will be able to analyse texts in Ethiopian and Eritrean languages, both linguistically and philologically, and thus gain insight into such areas of knowledge as history with focus on ancient and pre-modern history, historical linguistics, religious history of Ethiopia and Eritrea, literature, and manuscript studies. Ethiopian and Eritrean Studies is primarily oriented to the study of linguistics, philology, history, and literature. It considers the oral as well as the manuscript traditions of Ethiopia and Eritrea.
The Language in Culture study profile allows students with a BA in African Languages & Cultures or a degree in a similar programme to improve their methodological skills and theoretical knowledge in the field of mono- and multilingual communication, language use and knowledge transfer in Africa. Language in culture and communication in African societies are treated from a broad perspective based on the insight that social interaction and collective transmission of knowledge in African cultures can only be captured adequately by a deeper understanding of language and codifications of verbal interaction. A focus of this study programme is placed on communication in multilingual settings and the construction of social meaning in culturally diverse societies. Graduates acquire the appropriate qualifications for Africa-related responsible jobs in the media, education, and in the field of documenting or communicating African cultures.

Academic admission requirements.value:
University degree
A Bachelor's degree from a German or recognised foreign university in a major subject from African or Semitic studies or related fields
If you have not received your degree certificate yet, you can submit this by the end of the first semester of your Master’s programme. Please see the “Documents to submit” section below for details.
Additional special admission requirements
Certificate of linguistic knowledge in English at Level B2 (CEFR) or
Official Medium of Instruction certificate (MOI)
Depending on the selected profile, the following admission requirements must be fulfilled:
Profiles Linguistic Analysis and Language Documentation and Applied African Linguistics:
Proof of fundamental knowledge in phonetics/phonology, morphology and syntax with a minimum of 45 ECTS as well as competences in an African language with a minimum of 16 ECTS (language proficiency equivalent to 16 ECTS can be submitted on request until the end of the second semester). The proof of these competences is usually provided by a transcript of records.
Profile Ethiopian and Eritrean Studies:
Proof of competence in Semitic, Philological, Christian Oriental or African studies with a minimum of 45 ECTS and basic knowledge of Geez (Ancient Ethiopic) is required, with a minimum of 8 ECTS (language proficiency equivalent to 8 ECTS can be submitted on request until the end of the second semester). The proof of these competences is usually provided by a transcript of records.
Profile Language in Culture:
Proof of competences in African linguistics or African Studies with a minimum of 45 ECTS as well as competences in an African language with a minimum of 16 ECTS is required (language proficiency equivalent to 16 ECTS can be submitted on request until the end of the second semester). The proof of these competences is usually provided by a transcript of records.

Description/content.value:
This Bachelor's degree programme combines four important subject areas, guaranteeing professional success on the international stage: engineering and the natural sciences, business and economics, communication and intercultural knowledge, and foreign languages. The programme is taught in English and is offered by two universities - Merseburg University of Applied Sciences in cooperation with the Martin Luther University, Halle-Wittenberg.
There are four profile-forming thematic fields.
Engineering
The curriculum begins with a solid foundation in the natural sciences through mathematics, physics, and chemistry. Building on this, students master engineering basics including material science, transport phenomena, thermodynamics, mechanics, and electrical engineering. Advanced coursework focuses on process engineering, covering specialised areas such as process control, equipment design, and sustainable energy supply. Through electives, students can further specialise in biotechnology, environmental technology, CAD, or plant engineering. These modules are highly application-oriented and emphasise hands-on practical experience.
Business and Economics
This part of the programme draws on modules from the BSc Business Economics at Martin Luther University, providing students with in-depth economic expertise. The curriculum covers essential subjects such as financial accounting, statistics, cost accounting, and Principles of Investment. A wide selection of electives is also available, allowing students to explore the full spectrum of business and economics. To complement this, Merseburg University of Applied Sciences provides specialised modules in logistics and supply chain management, ensuring a well-rounded professional profile.
Communication and Intercultural Knowledge
Effective communication is vital in a globalised professional environment. Because intercultural awareness is a prerequisite for successful international collaboration, the programme includes a dedicated module specifically designed to develop these essential soft skills. This training ensures that students are well-prepared for the challenges of working in diverse, multinational teams and provides them with the tools needed to navigate complex cultural nuances in a professional setting.
Language
Language is the primary key to academic and professional integration. The degree programme is taught in English; however, it incorporates specific language tracks based on the students' backgrounds. International students complete five semesters of German as a Foreign Language (DaF), earning 5 ECTS per semester. Conversely, German-speaking students undertake intensive courses in Business and Technical English. Additionally, the programme offers the opportunity to study Spanish as a second foreign language over the course of three semesters to further enhance global mobility.

Description/content.value:
Are you fascinated by the intricate workings of living organisms at the molecular level? Do you want to be at the forefront of the biotech revolution, utilising cutting-edge techniques to manipulate and enhance biological systems? If so, then our Master's programme in Molecular Biotechnology is perfect for you.
Our comprehensive programme covers everything from gene editing and recombinant DNA technology to protein engineering and synthetic biology. Experts from academia and industry prepare you for a career in research, development, production and commercialisation of biotech products.
You'll graduate with a strong background in molecular biology and understanding of ethical awareness and regulatory issues surrounding biotechnology. Our programme provides plenty of opportunities for hands-on research, including collaborations with industry partners and internships experience in state-of-the-art laboratories and research facilities.
Join us to lead in the dynamic world of molecular biotech!

Course organisation.value: The four-semester Master’s programme is divided into two phases and begins with advisory support even before the semester starts. First and second semesters: In the first semester, all students complete an advanced module on molecular biotechnology, covering key biomolecules and core concepts from academic and industrial perspectives. You will also take three methods modules in (i) bio/chemical analytics, (ii) cell engineering, and (iii) computational biology, each including two hands-on workshops in modern laboratory techniques. In the second semester, experts from industry teach biotechnological production, from target identification to clinical trials, regulatory approval, and quality control. You will also study bioprocess engineering and gain business and legal basics for developing biotech products in collaboration with MAFEX (the Marburg Institute for Innovation Research and Start-up Support). Third and fourth semesters: You will complete internships at universities, research institutions, or in industry in Germany or abroad, or participate in competitions such as iGEM. The programme concludes with an experimental Master’s thesis in molecular biology.

Academic admission requirements.value:
To be eligible for the Molecular Biotechnology programme at Marburg University, applicants must have a C1 level proficiency in English, as all teaching and exams are conducted in English. Detailed information on the C1 level requirements can be found on the university's webpage.
Applicants will be evaluated based on their Bachelor's degree grades, as well as the number of credit points earned from courses taken in biological sciences (a minimum of 30 ECTS) and supporting sciences such as physics and mathematics (a minimum of 12 ECTS). Additional subject-specific qualifications documented by successfully completing relevant advanced and/or final modules in bioscience and biotechnology will allow students to earn extra credits.
In addition to providing academic transcripts, applicants must also submit a CV and a letter demonstrating their subject-specific aptitude for the programme. Applicants who meet the admission score level will be invited to participate in an interview, during which a committee will make the final admission decision.

Accommodation.value:
The market situation for accommodation is not easy in Marburg. However, the university assists international students in finding suitable and affordable accommodation. The student services office ("Studierendenwerk Marburg") maintains student residence halls with a total of approx. 2,100 units. Apart from single rooms, there are two- to three-room flats for student families. Only students registered at Marburg University are entitled to a place in a residence hall. The "Konrad Biesalski House", in which handicapped and non-handicapped students live together, offers round-the-clock assistance. A bus service and services such as physiotherapeutic exercises and massage baths are offered. Many students live in private accommodation or shared flats. The supply of flats in the centre of Marburg is limited, especially in the Old Town ("Oberstadt"). The situation on the outskirts of Marburg and in the immediate vicinity is better. There are good bus connections. Experience shows that demand for accommodation is highest at the beginning of each semester (April, October), so you should start looking for accommodation around the end of the previous semester (February, July) if possible.
https://www.uni-marburg.de/en/studying/life-at-umr/housing

Description/content.value:
Global Change Ecology (MERGE) is a double degree programme offered jointly by the University of Bergen (UiB) in Norway and the Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg (JMU) in Germany. This international Master's programme offers in-depth, interdisciplinary training in ecology, conservation biology, and global change biology. Students will gain a strong foundation in key areas such as applied ecology, remote sensing, and evolutionary biology, while examining how species, populations, and ecosystems interact in a world shaped by rapid environmental change. From the first semester, students will dive into the principles of ecological and evolutionary theory, learn observational and experimental methods, and engage with cutting-edge research across a variety of ecological disciplines. Through hands-on projects and lab work, students will develop the skills to critically assess and conduct ecological research in both field and laboratory settings.
A defining feature of the programme is the MSc research project, in which students join active research teams to work on real-world topics under co-supervision from both universities, while developing the skills to independently design, conduct, and communicate original scientific work in their Master's thesis. Master of Science (MSc) degrees from both JMU and UiB can be awarded.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
Finding part-time employment in Würzburg is a great way to gain experience, make new connections, and supplement your finances while studying. Students from EU and EEA countries enjoy equal terms in the labour market and can work freely during their studies. Students from other countries can work up to 140 full days or 280 half days per year, including voluntary internships. If you wish to work more, you'll need permission from the employment agency ("Agentur für Arbeit") or the immigration office.
It's important to ensure that your studies remain your top priority, so choose a side job that complements your academic schedule. The University of Würzburg offers resources to help you find part-time work, such as the student job portal.

Accommodation.value:
Finding the perfect place to live is an important part of your student experience at the University of Würzburg. Unlike some other countries, students in Germany need to find their own accommodation, as universities do not automatically provide it. At the University of Würzburg, you have two main options: "Studierendenwerk" housing or private rooms/student halls.
The Student Housing Service ("Studierendenwerk") manages 12 student residences in Würzburg, offering a total of 2,887 rooms. These dormitories provide a variety of amenities:
Single and double rooms or apartments shared by two to four students, with communal kitchens and bathrooms
Furnished rooms and apartments are available, though you'll need to bring your own dishes, cooking items, bedding, and towels.
To apply for housing, note the deadlines: 15 June for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester. For more information about private rooms and student halls, visit the Central Student Advisory Service.
In addition to Studierendenwerk housing, there are many private accommodation options available:
Shared apartments ("Wohngemeinschaften" or "WGs"): These are popular among students and offer a great way to meet new people and share living costs.
Private student halls: These are often run by private companies and offer similar amenities to Studierendenwerk dormitories. They can be a bit more expensive but may offer more modern facilities.
Short-term accommodation: If you need a place to stay while you search for permanent housing, consider options like hostels, guest houses, or short-term rentals.
Remember to start your housing search early and stay positive! With a bit of patience and diligence, you'll find a cosy place to call home.

Description/content.value:
The University of Siegen offers a Master’s programme in Physics with a duration of four semesters. Students can tailor their curriculum to our three focus areas: particle physics, solid state physics, and quantum optics and quantum information.
General Information: The MSc in Physics is a research-oriented study programme. During the first year, students attend elective lectures, lab courses, and seminars. In the second year, students carry out a project in one of the research groups, leading to the Master's thesis. The programme language is English. Admission is possible each year in spring and autumn.
Research: At the Department of Physics, about 300 students and 20 professors work together, resulting in an outstanding student-to-staff ratio. Our research groups work on:
Experimental particle & astroparticle physics
Theoretical particle physics
Experimental quantum optics with trapped ions
Experimental quantum & nano-optics
Theoretical quantum optics & quantum information theory
Experimental solid state physics
Experimental x-ray methods
We are part of numerous international collaborations, giving young students the chance to work directly on challenging problems in cutting-edge research, such as:
Exploring the fundamental nature of matter and new phenomena in strong and weak interactions, as part of the cluster of excellence "color meets flavor"
Challenging the Standard Model of particle physics through precision calculations for experiments at the energy and intensity frontier, as part of the CRC "particle physics phenomenology after the Higgs discovery"
Exploring and developing novel concepts and methods for quantum information processing with trapped ions, in cooperation with the local quantum industry pioneers at eleQtron GmbH and research partners worldwide
Probing the limits of quantum theory with matter waves and macroscopic quantum effects, together with leading experimental groups in Europe
Detector development for the world’s largest particle accelerator at CERN, the world’s largest cosmic rays experiment in Argentina, and for medical imaging
Understanding the nature of entanglement, its role in quantum networks, and practical applications, as part of European quantum information science initiatives
Development of quantum sensors and single-photon sources based on colour centres and optical nanostructures
Preparing and characterising novel, ultra-thin 2D materials as the ultimate limit of device miniaturisation
Facilitating the development of new materials with cutting-edge x-ray methods at large-scale x-ray facilities in Germany, Europe and the world
Description/content.html:
The University of Siegen offers a Master’s programme in Physics with a duration of four semesters. Students can tailor their curriculum to our three focus areas: particle physics, solid state physics, and quantum optics and quantum information.

General Information: The MSc in Physics is a research-oriented study programme. During the first year, students attend elective lectures, lab courses, and seminars. In the second year, students carry out a project in one of the research groups, leading to the Master's thesis. The programme language is English. Admission is possible each year in spring and autumn.

Research: At the Department of Physics, about 300 students and 20 professors work together, resulting in an outstanding student-to-staff ratio. Our research groups work on:

  • Experimental particle & astroparticle physics
  • Theoretical particle physics
  • Experimental quantum optics with trapped ions
  • Experimental quantum & nano-optics
  • Theoretical quantum optics & quantum information theory
  • Experimental solid state physics
  • Experimental x-ray methods

We are part of numerous international collaborations, giving young students the chance to work directly on challenging problems in cutting-edge research, such as:

  • Exploring the fundamental nature of matter and new phenomena in strong and weak interactions, as part of the cluster of excellence "color meets flavor"
  • Challenging the Standard Model of particle physics through precision calculations for experiments at the energy and intensity frontier, as part of the CRC "particle physics phenomenology after the Higgs discovery"
  • Exploring and developing novel concepts and methods for quantum information processing with trapped ions, in cooperation with the local quantum industry pioneers at eleQtron GmbH and research partners worldwide
  • Probing the limits of quantum theory with matter waves and macroscopic quantum effects, together with leading experimental groups in Europe
  • Detector development for the world’s largest particle accelerator at CERN, the world’s largest cosmic rays experiment in Argentina, and for medical imaging
  • Understanding the nature of entanglement, its role in quantum networks, and practical applications, as part of European quantum information science initiatives
  • Development of quantum sensors and single-photon sources based on colour centres and optical nanostructures
  • Preparing and characterising novel, ultra-thin 2D materials as the ultimate limit of device miniaturisation
  • Facilitating the development of new materials with cutting-edge x-ray methods at large-scale x-ray facilities in Germany, Europe and the world

Course organisation.value: Structure and content: In the first year, students can choose elective lectures and courses according to their specialisation. We offer courses focused around the following topics: Experimental solid state physics Quantum information theory and foundations of quantum mechanics Theoretical quantum optics and quantum thermodynamics Experimental quantum optics and nano-optics Theoretical particle physics Experimental particle and astroparticle physics Machine learning and computational methods in physics The second year is devoted to the MSc thesis, which is prepared in one of the research groups. The aim of the thesis is to deliver a contribution to current research in theoretical or experimental physics. The outstanding student-to-staff ratio at the department implies direct supervision of each student, and results from MSc theses are regularly published in international scientific journals. An MSc degree is a precondition for entering a doctoral programme in Germany. The PhD research is then performed in one of the research groups and prospective PhD students have to find a professor who is willing to supervise their work. Typically, PhD theses last three to four years and PhD students receive financial support. Costs of living.value:
The city of Siegen has very moderate costs for accommodation, offering attractive living conditions for students. Living expenses range from only 800 EUR to 1,000 EUR per month, including rent, health insurance, food, clothing, learning materials, phone/Internet, travel expenses, entertainment, and sports. This estimated cost of living can vary depending on lifestyle, type of accommodation, budget, and spending habits.
It is important that students plan and manage their finances throughout the duration of the degree programme to ensure they have enough funds to cover semester contributions and living costs.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value: Students can find part-time jobs with the help of the job placement service of the university. Siegen and the surrounding area are home to a large number of medium-sized industrial enterprises (SMEs), or so-called hidden champions in electrical and mechanical engineering. Some bigger examples include the companies SMS and Achenbach Buschhütten. A lot of smaller, yet very successful and quickly growing high-tech companies are located here as well, for instance, PMD Technologies and Asentics, which are spin-off companies of the university. Therefore, there are employment prospects in the region, particularly for positions that are available during the semester break and following graduation.

Accommodation.value:
There are student residences (dormitories) of the "Studierendenwerk" (student services) close to the university. The rent for a room is between 240 EUR and 460 EUR. Please be aware that German universities do not usually have campus systems like universities in some other countries, where all students can find accommodation directly on the university property. Therefore, some students might have to find rooms on their own. The private accommodation costs per room are 400 EUR on average. Detailed information concerning general accommodation can be found here.
Early application/search is advisable.

Description/content.value:
This Master’s programme aims to educate specialists and executive staff for optical industry and related areas of expertise. The programme is strongly geared toward practical experience and combines scientific and engineering skills. This is supported by several lectures from experts in the optical industry at their companies.
The course focuses on technical optics and how to design and characterise optical systems, optical metrology, optical materials and coatings, quality control, special optics as well as important mathematics for better understanding.
We highly encourage our students to cooperate with companies, which can be involved in ongoing research and education and each Master's student can connect to the optical industry at an early stage of their career, as we are located near a large optical industry region in Germany.
The collaboration of the faculties during study time bridges the gap between scientific competencies, technical applications of optics and individual interests.
Upon successful completion of the Master's programme, you will be a specialist and ready to work in the field of optical technology, one of the key technologies of the 21st century.
For further information: https://www.thm.de/site/en/studies/our-courses/optical-system-engineering
