Course organisation.value:
This Master's programme curriculum offers a clear structure and allows for flexibility in pursuing individual interests. Over all three semesters, students gain hands-on practical experience and learn theory.
In the first two semesters, all modules are completed. Three compulsory modules are offered in each of the first two semesters. These modules are independent of each other and are partly taught by external lecturers from industry.
In addition, students take subject-oriented elective modules. These are selected from the entire THM module pool according to the students' individual interests and strengths, and can cover a broad spectrum ranging from computer science, natural sciences and mechanical engineering to sustainability and innovation management. These modules make up two-thirds of the overall coursework.
The third semester is devoted to applied research and development work to complete the Master's thesis, culminating in the thesis defence. We encourage our students to cooperate with national and international partners.
Throughout the whole programme, communication skills, team-working and methodological work skills are developed.
For further information: https://www.thm.de/site/en/studies/our-courses/optical-system-engineering
Compulsory Modules:
Optical Design and Layout of Optical Systems
Measurement Technology, Tolerancing and Quality Control of Optical Systems
Special Laser Technology
Modern Optical Manufacturing Technology and Special Optics
Optical Coatings and Optical Materials
Numerical Methods in Optics
Organisation:
Beginning: Every winter and summer semester (1 October and 1 April)
Duration: Three semesters including Master's thesis & defence
Curriculum: Total of 90 credit points
Language of instruction: English

Description/content.value:
The Master’s programme in Computational Mechanical Engineering (MSc) is designed for students who want to take mechanical engineering to the next level and are interested in using digital methods, working with precision, and are future-oriented. The programme provides an education in advanced mathematics, engineering foundations, and modern computational methods in mechanical engineering. The academic foundation is specifically linked to the faculty’s application-oriented research and development projects.
Students learn to independently model and simulate complex engineering problems and implement innovative solutions in accordance with scientific and industrial requirements. Graduates are therefore well prepared for demanding positions in research, development, and the high-tech industry.
Description/content.html:
The Master’s programme in Computational Mechanical Engineering (MSc) is designed for students who want to take mechanical engineering to the next level and are interested in using digital methods, working with precision, and are future-oriented. The programme provides an education in advanced mathematics, engineering foundations, and modern computational methods in mechanical engineering. The academic foundation is specifically linked to the faculty’s application-oriented research and development projects.

Students learn to independently model and simulate complex engineering problems and implement innovative solutions in accordance with scientific and industrial requirements. Graduates are therefore well prepared for demanding positions in research, development, and the high-tech industry.

These may be completed in the context of a working group at the university or in external research organisations or companies.

Description/content.value:
The consecutive Master’s programme in Mathematics is a research-oriented study programme designed to deepen and extend the knowledge acquired during a Bachelor’s degree in Mathematics. It provides students with a solid foundation in advanced mathematical theory as well as the opportunity to engage with current research topics.
The programme offers a wide range of specialisation areas, including Algebra, Analysis, Differential Geometry, Geometry, Numerics, Statistics, and Stochastics. Students can flexibly combine courses across these fields and thereby develop an individual academic profile tailored to their interests and career goals.
A particular emphasis is placed on analytical thinking, abstraction, and the ability to solve complex mathematical problems independently. In addition to subject-specific modules, the programme allows students to take courses in related disciplines such as computer science, economics, or physics. This interdisciplinary component enhances both academic development and career prospects.
All Master‘s courses can be taught in English upon request, making the programme accessible to international students. Furthermore, the programme includes an international double degree option in cooperation with the University of Bern (Switzerland), providing students with the opportunity to gain international experience and benefit from two academic environments.

Course organisation.value:
The Master’s programme in Mathematics is a full-time programme with a standard duration of four semesters (120 ECTS credits). It is characterised by a flexible and modular structure that combines lectures, seminars, and independent work.
The curriculum consists of the following components:
Main modules (18 ECTS), providing fundamental knowledge in the chosen specialisation areas
Specialisation modules (13.5 ECTS), offering advanced and research-oriented courses
Mathematical elective modules (27 ECTS), allowing students to deepen and broaden their expertise
Mathematical or non-mathematical elective modules (27 ECTS), supporting interdisciplinary study
Seminar (4.5 ECTS), focusing on presentation and discussion of current research topics
Master’s thesis including presentation (30 ECTS), representing an independent research project
Coursework is usually completed during the first three semesters. The fourth semester is primarily dedicated to the Master’s thesis, which is supervised by a faculty member and typically related to the chosen specialisation.
Within the double degree option with the University of Bern, students spend the first academic year in Konstanz and the second year in Bern. The Master’s thesis is jointly supervised by one advisor from each institution. Upon successful completion, students are awarded Master’s degrees in Mathematics from both universities.

Academic admission requirements.value:
Applicants must hold a Bachelor’s degree in Mathematics or a related subject from a university, a recognised university of cooperative education (Berufsakademie), or an equivalent higher education institution in Germany or abroad.
Applicants must also have sufficient academic preparation in Mathematics to ensure a successful start to the programme. As a rule, this requires at least 120 ECTS credits in coursework and examinations comparable to the level of the Bachelor’s programme in Mathematics at the University of Konstanz. This includes advanced knowledge in at least one of the specialisation areas offered in the Konstanz Bachelor’s programme.
If applicants are missing some subject-specific qualifications, they may be admitted on condition that they make up to 30 ECTS credits in Mathematics during the first year of study and pass the required examinations within the specified period. In such cases, applicants are strongly advised to contact the Student Advisory Service at an early stage.
International applicants must provide proof of German or English language proficiency. Accepted proof of German or English language skills corresponds to at least B2 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.
Alternatively, English language proficiency may be demonstrated by one of the following:
successful completion of at least four courses taught in English within a degree programme in the European Economic Area or Switzerland
a secondary school diploma or Bachelor’s degree obtained at an English-language institution
at least one semester spent abroad in an English-speaking academic environment
Recognised countries in this context include the USA, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Description/content.value:
Freie Universität Berlin’s Master’s degree programme “Ottoman and Turkish Studies“ focuses on the history and culture of the Ottoman Empire and modern Turkey. Students gain knowledge of and experience with the basic tenets of academic and scientific work as well as good scientific practice. During their studies, they receive an introduction to academic and scientific work, which involves thinking critically about the contexts, preconditions, theories, and methods in the field.
The Master’s degree programme covers knowledge of the Turkish and Ottoman language, an overview of the history and culture of the Ottoman Empire and Turkey, advanced knowledge of fundamental topics in Ottoman and Turkish history as well as current topics, especially regarding the following: pre-modern statehood and social organisation; modernisation under the conditions of global interdependence and power structures; political, social, and cultural approaches to plurality and diversity; gender as a social, cultural, and political category; migration, mass violence, and genocide; and approaches to historical and cultural heritage.
The programme also addresses contemporary issues of politics, society and culture in Turkey. It has an interdisciplinary approach covering theories and methods of history, anthropology and the political, social and cultural sciences. It also perceives Ottoman and Turkish Studies as entangled and comparative, thus including trans-Ottoman perspectives and post-Ottoman societies as well as topics concerning the migrant communities from Turkey in Germany.
Graduates of the Master’s degree programme are qualified to pursue doctoral studies. The skills and knowledge gained in the programme prepare graduates for work in governmental and non-governmental organisations that deal with the languages, history, and cultures of Turkey and other Turkic-speaking regions, as well as with migrant communities. In addition to careers in academic research and science, other possible occupations include work at non-university research institutions, academic and non-academic educational institutions, in the media, politics, diplomatic service, development aid, for non-governmental organisations or cultural organisations, in public administration or publishing, at libraries or museums, or in intercultural social work.

Course organisation.value:
The Master’s degree programme consists of three phases: the introductory phase, the specialisation phase, and the completion phase.
The structure and progression of the programme is laid out in the degree programme regulations, which also includes detailed descriptions of the contents and learning objectives of the individual modules, as well as a standard curriculum plan. The examination regulations define the types of assessments and coursework required in the different modules and for the final Master’s degree assessment. The regulations stipulate the number of credit points required for each module (and/or course) as well as the workload (in hours) for the entire degree programme.
The Master’s thesis should show that students are able to conduct independent research using scientific/academic methods and present their work. Upon successful completion of the Master’s degree programme, the student will receive a Master of Arts (MA) university degree.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
There are many ways of earning money while you study, for example as wait staff, academic assistants, or private tutors. Knowledge of German will improve your chances of finding a part-time job, but it isn’t necessarily required. However, it is important to be aware of the legal regulations.The student support service at the university, called "studierendenWERK Berlin", and the local representative of the "Bundesagentur für Arbeit" (Federal Employment Agency) can provide information about jobs for students.
When searching for a job, look at online job boards, notice boards on campus, and ads in local newspapers.
You can also work on campus. The Freie Universität Berlin regularly offers positions for students in science, teaching support and administration that you can find on our careers portal.

Accommodation.value:
You have the option to stay in a public/private student dormitory or in a private (shared) apartment. Student dormitories are not administrated by the university itself, so Freie Universität Berlin does not have any on-campus housing. However, it works together with "studierendenWERK Berlin" regarding student accommodation.
If you do not wish to stay in a student dormitory, you can try to find a room or an apartment on the private housing market. Many students in Berlin live in shared apartments ("WGs"). You can find these offers online (e.g. WG-Gesucht or Kleinanzeigen) or on notice boards on campus.
Available rooms/apartments near the university are rare. Therefore, students mostly commute from other parts of the city. The commute via public transportation usually takes between 30 minutes and an hour, which is considered a normal travel time in Berlin due to the size of the city.

Description/content.value:
The Master's degree programme in "Engineering and Management of Space Systems" (EMSS) provides students with essential systems engineering and management competencies required for the planning, design, implementation and management of space missions. This includes all necessary systems/facilities (Flight System, Ground System & Test Facilities, Launch System) following the current standards of the European Cooperation for Space Standardization (ECSS) and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).
The increasing digitisation, distribution and networking of technical systems lead to the necessity of a degree programme that teaches “the systems view” and interdisciplinary methods and skills. Furthermore, it is necessary to consider the entire life cycle of the systems starting with the requirements analysis to design, integration, verification, operation and maintenance. This, supplemented by management and social skills, forms a solid foundation for mastering the steadily growing complexity of technical systems in practice.
Since interdisciplinary approaches and internationality are essential for engineering and management of space systems, a joint interdisciplinary international double degree Master’s programme “Engineering and Management of Space Systems” was established as a cooperation between Hochschule Bremen (HSB) — City University of Applied Sciences, Germany, and Gdańsk University of Technology (Gdańsk Tech), Poland. The first semester (summer) is conducted at the Gdańsk Tech. The second semester (winter) is conducted at HSB. The third semester is reserved for the Master's thesis and can be done at one of the both universities, usually in cooperation with the industry. The degree programme is carried out in English.
The curriculum is oriented to the international systems engineering certification standards of the International Council on Systems Engineering (INCOSE) and its German Chapter, Gesellschaft für Systems Engineering (GfSE).
It includes theoretical principles and concepts of systems engineering and management as well as practical projects concentrating on space systems and projects.
Prof Dr-Ing Jasminka Matevska on the HSB side and Prof Dr hab inż Zbigniew Łubniewski on the Gdańsk Tech side are responsible for this degree programme.

Description/content.value: In this English-language degree programme, you will explore the physical Earth system in all its facets: from the Earth's interior to the climate and the oceans. Topics such as earthquakes, climate change and extreme weather events such as hurricanes are not only exciting, but also highly relevant to society. You will learn how to use physical and mathematical methods to investigate the dynamics of the solid Earth, the atmosphere and the oceans — in other words, how our planet "ticks". In the process, you will develop skills in measurement methods, data analysis and computer modelling. Even during your studies, you can participate in current research projects and thus help shape real science. Thanks to a flexible election of courses, you can focus on your areas of interest — whether in geophysics, meteorology or oceanography, or you can opt for a broad education in all areas of physical Earth system sciences.

In the process, you will develop skills in measurement methods, data analysis and computer modelling. Course organisation.value:
Understanding the dynamic processes of the Earth system requires a sound education in mathematics and physics. These foundations are combined with an introduction to Earth system sciences in the first three semesters. Beginning in the third semester, there is a steadily growing proportion of core elective courses, which enables students to choose modules within the Earth system sciences or to specialise in a field of their interest. A large fraction of additional free electives allows cross-disciplinary education beyond Earth system physics. In the third year of study no compulsory modules are scheduled. The fifth semester is ideally suited for a stay abroad. In the sixth semester, students write a Bachelor’s thesis on a research topic of their choice. Embedded in a research group and under supervision they investigate and document a current question in the field of Earth system physics.
An overview is given here.

Description/content.value:
The Master’s programme in Biomedical Engineering focuses on the interdisciplinary collaboration of engineering, natural sciences, and medicine to develop advanced diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Students gain comprehensive theoretical and practical knowledge in imaging techniques, signal processing, and image analysis, with a strong emphasis on applications in medical technology as well as engineering fields such as the automotive industry and process engineering. Students explore modules such as Tomographic Imaging, Ultrasound Imaging, Digital and Statistical Signal Processing, Biomedical Systems, and Image Processing. They gain expertise in electromagnetic and acoustic wave fields, modelling and simulations, sensor technology, measurement instrumentation and control engineering, stochastic signal processing, image reconstruction and processing, pattern recognition and machine/deep learning, and information technology.
Through the Master’s seminar and practical training, students engage in scientific literature reviews, specialised knowledge acquisition, and the application of engineering principles to address medical needs. They practice critical reflection, systematic concept implementation, and the development of innovative solutions.
The international academic environment offers students the opportunity to gain intercultural work experience, enhancing their soft skills, and preparing them for a global career. This programme provides a solid foundation for students aiming to work in medical engineering research and development, preparing them to address critical health challenges through early detection, accurate diagnosis, effective therapy, and disease prevention leading to impactful careers in improving human health and well-being.
Graduates are well-prepared to tackle complex technical and scientific problems in various industries, also beyond medical technology, e.g. automotive and process engineering, or to pursue a PhD to become independent researchers in the respective fields. They are equipped to independently analyse, solve, and document research and development challenges, using current technical language and terminology to communicate their findings effectively.

Course organisation.value:
The research-oriented Master’s programme spans two years and encompasses 120 ECTS credits. It aims to equip you with advanced knowledge and skills needed to excel in the dynamic fields of electrical engineering and information technology. Biomedical Engineering is one of three areas of specialisation offered entirely in English.
The programme is designed to provide a balanced and in-depth learning experience, divided into four key areas, each worth 30 CP:
Compulsory courses (30 CP)
The compulsory courses, typically completed in the first two semesters, lay the foundation for your specialised studies. These courses ensure a solid understanding of the fundamental principles that underpin your chosen area of specialisation.
Compulsory elective courses (30 CP)
The compulsory elective courses allow you to tailor your education to your interests and career goals. Choose from a variety of courses that align with your academic passions. Additionally, students participate in a seminar (3 CP) and a laboratory practical (3 CP) to gain hands-on experience in our state-of-the-art research labs and engage in cutting-edge scientific discourse.
Free elective area (30 CP)
Broaden your horizons by selecting from the diverse offerings at the Ruhr-Universität Bochum and the University Alliance Ruhr. You can choose further courses in your field of specialisation or another engineering discipline, or focus on soft skills such as language courses, intercultural competence and so on. This area is also well-suited for a study abroad experience, for example, through one of our numerous co-operations within the Erasmus programme.
Master’s thesis (30 CP)
The Master’s thesis is a capstone project that allows you demonstrate your ability to tackle complex engineering challenges with innovative solutions. Over a six-month period, you will independently conduct research using scientific methods, applying both technical and interdisciplinary skills. You will document your findings in a comprehensive written report, and you will present your key results in a colloquium lecture to showcase your presentation and argumentation skills.

Accommodation.value:
In the city of Bochum, you can find different types of accommodation. On average, students in Bochum pay approximately 400 to 800 EUR per month for a single apartment, which is below the average rent in Germany. A room in a shared apartment is usually less expensive.
About 5,000 students in Bochum live in multiple student halls close to the campus, which are run by the Akademisches Förderungswerk (AKAFÖ). In the halls, each student has a single room and shares a kitchen and bathroom with other students, rents an apartment with a private bathroom and kitchen, or shares an apartment with one or several flatmates.
More information on the student halls can be found at https://studium.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/de/wohnen.
In addition, private and church-affiliated student halls accommodate up to 1,000 students: http://www.stuwo.de/wohnheim-region/bochum/.

Description/content.value:
The goal of the specialisation in Communication Systems is to train graduates who are familiar with the diverse methods and techniques of communication engineering, machine learning, optimisation and data science, and who can appropriately select and apply those most suitable for a given application.
The following areas of study are of particular importance:
Systems thinking: Knowledge of methods for describing linear and non-linear (physical) systems, theory of signals, information processing and machine learning, analysis and simulation methods, principles of human-to-human and human-system interaction.
Problem-solving approaches combined with application-oriented examples: theoretical and practical knowledge of components, devices, and systems; transmission methods; all types of signal processing from source to sink; methods of fault diagnosis and fault tolerance.
Tools and resources: Sound programming skills at both macro and micro levels (software engineering), statistical methods, optimisation techniques, machine learning methods and software frameworks, knowledge of computer architectures and methods for circuit analysis, synthesis, and simulation
Interdisciplinarity: Applications in medical technology, acoustics and acoustic signal processing, methods of control engineering, basic knowledge of management/logistics and economics, and understanding the interactions of people, technology, and organisations
This specialisation is based on the following mandatory courses:
Digital Signal Processing
Mobile Communication Systems
Communication Acoustics
Wireless Communications
Optimisation
Advanced Topics in Machine Learning
It also offers many additional elective subjects.

Accommodation.value:
In the city of Bochum, you can find different types of accommodation. On average, students in Bochum pay approximately 400 to 800 EUR per month for a single apartment, which is below the average rent in Germany. A room in a shared apartment is usually less expensive.
About 5,000 students in Bochum live in multiple student halls close to the campus, which are run by the Akademisches Förderungswerk (AKAFÖ). In the halls, each student has a single room and shares a kitchen and bathroom with other students, rents an apartment with a private bathroom and kitchen, or shares an apartment with one or several flatmates.
More information on the student halls can be found at https://studium.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/de/wohnen.
In addition, private and church-affiliated student halls accommodate up to 1,000 students: http://www.stuwo.de/wohnheim-region/bochum/.

Description/content.value:
This English-taught Master's programme provides a forward-thinking education in the areas of automation, robotics and control. The initial theory courses serve as the groundwork for the more practice-oriented modules later on. All courses are conducted by researchers actively engaged in the field.
The foundational knowledge is provided by the general compulsory modules, which include Mathematics for Engineering Science, Advanced Linear Control, Learning Dynamical Systems, Autonomous Systems and Robots, Modelling and Control. Building upon these compulsory subjects, the programme offers various opportunities for further specialisation in the areas of Automation, Robotics and Control.
The study programme is completed with the Master's thesis in the final semester.

Description/content.value:
The programme is equivalent to 120 ECTS, (one ECTS equals around 30 hours of workload) according to the European system.
The first, second and third semesters consist of core and elective modules, and the fourth semester is dedicated to the Master's thesis:
Core modules (compulsory modules) cover 40 ECTS
Elective modules (compulsory optional modules from the catalogue “Method & Tools” and the thematic catalogues “IWRM”, “REM”, “NRM”) cover 50 ECTS
Master's thesis and colloquium cover 30 ECTS
One part of the programme consists of basic core modules, such as “Management of Natural Resources Systems”, “Natural Resources Economics and Governance”, ”International Cooperation and Development” and “Project and Business Management” with the aim of providing an overview of water management, economics, project management, and the regional and institutional context.
In addition to the core modules, the students select ten specialised elective modules related to topics of water management, emphasising the particular situation and experiences in Germany or the MENA region.
The elective modules are organised into „Methods and Tools“ and three thematic blocks: „Integrated Water Resources Management“ (IWRM), „Natural Resources Management and Development“ (NRM) and „Renewable Energy Management“ (REM). Students select a total of ten elective modules from the respective module catalogue IWRM (minimum 25 ECTS), the module catalogue „Methods and Tools“ (minimum of 10 ECTS), and any module catalogue, including the catalogues of the adjoining Master’s programmes of NRM and REM (a maximum of 15 ECTS). The students will study three out of the five IWRM elective modules at GJU during their exchange (third) semester.
The fourth semester is dedicated to the Master's thesis research that addresses a present research or management problem in the MENA region. Internships and research stays predominantly in an Arab country guarantee the practical orientation of the Master’s research, which is preferably done in cooperation with an ongoing project of an institution or company. Through their Master’s research work, the students apply the knowledge and competencies acquired in the previous semesters to demonstrate their ability to identify and analyse a research problem and conclude on policy and research implications. They also demonstrate the ability to plan, design, execute, and document a research project systematically and independently.
In the Project modules, students will have the chance to apply the new knowledge received in the basic or specialised modules to an interdisciplinary case study.

Please note that student jobs may require German language skills depending on the field and type of job.

Students who wish to pursue a career in Germany can take part in TH Köln's "Ready, Study, Go" programme. The programme offers students useful workshops and activities to prepare them for the German labour market.

Accommodation.value:
Being Germany's fourth largest city, Cologne is a highly attractive place to live. The increasing influx of people can make the search for adequate accommodation quite difficult. Dozens of apartment hunters often compete for one single apartment. This is why we strongly recommend that you start looking for a place to live as soon as possible.
Cologne's most convenient and economical housing option is often a student dormitory. A public student services association called "Kölner Studierendenwerk" (KSTW) operates 88 student dorms offering roughly 4,800 rooms. The seemingly large number of dorm rooms is misleading; as the dormitories are open to the roughly 90,000 students enrolled at all Cologne universities, they are in extremely high demand. Please be aware that TH Köln does not allocate the rooms in these dorms. Please apply directly to the KSTW: https://www.kstw.de/wohnen. You do not yet need a letter of admission in order to apply.
The fierce competition in the private housing market has resulted in above-market rents – particularly in proximity to the city centre. We therefore encourage you to be flexible. Try to look for apartments outside the centre or share an apartment – and the cost of rent – with other students: www.th-koeln.de/accommodation.

Description/content.value:
The part-time Master's degree course in Implantology and Dental Surgery offers specialised, practice-oriented further training at the highest international level. In cooperation with the International Medical College (IMC), the programme combines scientific excellence, state-of-the-art clinical procedures and a consistently international orientation. The aim is to prepare dentists in a targeted manner for the complex requirements of modern implantology and oral surgery practice.
The degree programme imparts sound theoretical knowledge and comprehensive practical skills in the fields of implantology, dental surgery, bone and soft tissue management and interdisciplinary treatment planning. Thanks to the close integration of research, evidence-based medicine and clinical application, students benefit from a structured, scientifically sound curriculum taught by internationally experienced lecturers.
The cooperation with the International Medical College (IMC) opens up a global academic network for participants and enables exchange with experts from different healthcare systems. Graduates of the Master's degree course not only acquire a recognised academic qualification, but also the professional and clinical confidence to carry out implantological and surgical treatments independently at the highest level.

Description/content.value:
In the Master's programme in Business Innovation and Entrepreneurship, you will deepen your knowledge of innovation, entrepreneurship and strategic management. The Master's programme combines scientific foundations with a consistent practical orientation and provides you with a clear content profile in the following areas:
Innovation & Business Transformation
Start-up & Corporate Entrepreneurship
Entrepreneurial Finance & Investment
Leadership & Change Management
Project-based teaching formats, interactive seminars and real-world innovation projects promote analytical thinking and entrepreneurial implementation skills. You will work systematically with scientific methods and develop the ability to translate complex economic issues into viable business models. Courses are usually taught in clusters. This compact structure creates space for intensive project work, exchange in the innovation environment and the independent development of start-up and innovation projects.
You will be accompanied by experienced professors and practical experts from the innovation and start-up environment. Personal support in small, international cohorts enables intensive exchange and individual feedback. At the Kemnath study location, you will benefit from an innovative learning environment in a rural area with close links between science, business and regional development.

Description/content.value:
The part-time Master's degree programme in Restorative and Aesthetic Dentistry offers specialised, practice-oriented and scientifically sound further training in the field of modern restorative and aesthetic dentistry. In cooperation with the International Medical College (IMC), the programme combines innovative treatment concepts, evidence-based materials science and the highest aesthetic standards in an internationally oriented study format.
The degree programme provides in-depth knowledge in the functional and aesthetic rehabilitation of the stomatognathic system. The focus is on direct and indirect restorative procedures, adhesive dentistry, aesthetic prosthetics, digital workflows and interdisciplinary treatment planning. The close integration of theoretical training, practical exercises and clinical application enables students to confidently implement complex restorative and aesthetic treatment concepts.
The cooperation with the International Medical College (IMC) gives participants access to an international academic network and lecturers with extensive clinical and scientific expertise. Graduates of the Master's degree course in Restorative and Aesthetic Dentistry acquire a recognised academic qualification and develop the professional competence to independently carry out high-quality restorative and aesthetic treatments at the highest international level.

The close integration of theoretical training, practical exercises and clinical application enables students to confidently implement complex restorative and aesthetic treatment concepts.

The cooperation with the International Medical College (IMC) gives participants access to an international academic network and lecturers with extensive clinical and scientific expertise. Graduates of the Master's degree course in Restorative and Aesthetic Dentistry acquire a recognised academic qualification and develop the professional competence to independently carry out high-quality restorative and aesthetic treatments at the highest international level.

Description/content.value:
The part-time Master's degree programme in Periodontology offers in-depth, scientifically sound and practical training in the field of modern periodontology. In cooperation with the International Medical College (IMC), the programme combines current research, evidence-based therapeutic approaches and clinical excellence in an internationally oriented study concept.
The degree programme provides comprehensive knowledge in the diagnosis, prevention and treatment of periodontal and peri-implant diseases. In addition to systematic periodontal therapy, the focus is on regenerative procedures, soft tissue management, the treatment of peri-implant diseases and interdisciplinary cooperation with related specialist areas. The close integration of theory and clinical practice enables students to directly apply the knowledge they have acquired in their everyday professional lives.
Thanks to the cooperation with the International Medical College (IMC), participants benefit from an international academic environment, highly qualified lecturers and a global network of experts. Graduates of the Master's degree course in Periodontology acquire a recognised academic qualification and at the same time develop the professional competence to carry out periodontological treatments independently and responsibly at the highest scientific and clinical level.

Description/content.value:
The part-time Master's degree programme in Advanced General Dental Practice offers comprehensive, scientifically sound and practice-oriented further training for dentists who wish to develop their clinical skills to an advanced level. In cooperation with the International Medical College (IMC), the programme combines modern dentistry, evidence-based treatment concepts and an international academic orientation.
The degree programme provides in-depth knowledge in all central areas of general dentistry. These include conservative and restorative dentistry, periodontology, endodontics, prosthetics, implant basics as well as preventive and functional treatment approaches. A special focus is placed on structured treatment planning, interdisciplinary thinking and the safe implementation of complex clinical cases in everyday practice.
Thanks to the cooperation with the International Medical College (IMC), participants benefit from an international teaching environment, experienced lecturers and a global professional network. Graduates of the Master's degree programme in Advanced General Dental Practice acquire a recognised academic qualification and at the same time develop the professional confidence to manage a modern general dental practice at a high scientific, clinical and patient-oriented level.

Description/content.value:
In the Information Technology and Business Transformation Master’s programme, you will deepen your knowledge at the intersection of information technology, business strategy and organisational transformation.
You will learn how to analyse complex digital ecosystems, design enterprise architectures and develop transformation strategies that align technology with business objectives. Through the programme’s cooperation with SAP, you will also gain insights into enterprise software platforms and real-world digital transformation environments.
Typical topics covered during your studies include:
digital transformation strategies and governance
enterprise, business and data architecture
IT systems and digital technologies
transformation programme management
organisational change and innovation management
Through practical projects, case studies and collaborative work, you will learn how to work on complex transformation initiatives in organisational contexts.

In the Information Technology and Business Transformation Master’s programme, you will deepen your knowledge at the intersection of information technology, business strategy and organisational transformation. 

You will learn how to analyse complex digital ecosystems, design enterprise architectures and develop transformation strategies that align technology with business objectives. Through the programme’s cooperation with SAP, you will also gain insights into enterprise software platforms and real-world digital transformation environments.

  • digital transformation strategies and governance

Through practical projects, case studies and collaborative work, you will learn how to work on complex transformation initiatives in organisational contexts.

Description/content.value:
Spatial and temporal aspects are at the heart of many pressing societal problems (e.g. achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals), and there is a lack of experts capable of dealing with them properly. The overall aim of the International Master's Programme in Geospatial Technologies is thus to prepare students to exploit new geospatial technologies to support environmental and societal decision-making affecting the future of our planet.
The University of Münster (UM), Germany, the Universitat Jaume I (UJI), Spain, and the Universidade Nova de Lisboa (UNL), Portugal, are complementary institutions with expertise in key research areas and teaching in the field of geospatial technologies. Consequently, the programme can cover interdisciplinary and current topic areas such as informatics, data analytics, remote sensing, spatial statistics and Geographic Information (GI) Science while also providing students with the opportunity to apply these to relevant problems in practical (team) projects.
The partners have been cooperating in several international projects for more than 15 years, including in a previous EMJM as well as in a European PhD programme (International Training Network) on Smart Open Cities. This expertise in running international training programmes, the composition of the consortium, and the tightly integrated structure of the degree programme, ensure that the course content is up-to-date, teaching is delivered to a high standard and essential transferable skills are acquired by the students.
The standard period of study is three semesters, including all examination requirements and the Master's thesis. The International Master's programme requires 90 ECTS credit points. Based on the successful Master's examination, the three universities will award the joint degree “Master of Science” (MSc) with the designation “in Geospatial Technologies”.

Course organisation.value: For detailed information, please check our website. The Master’s programme will be conducted with up to 32 students. Half of them attend their first semester at UJI, half at UNL. Intentionally, UJI and UNL offer courses with a different focus, in order to address the different backgrounds and requirements of the incoming students. Both partners offer basic modules in GI, although with different levels of intensity. The programme at UJI stresses the computing aspects of GI such as computer graphics and web services, whereas the programme at UNL is more oriented towards the processing and modelling aspects of geographic information, including topics such as “Remote sensing” and “Geospatial data mining”. As for the other modules, UJI is more informatics-oriented (modules “Informatics and mathematics” and “New technologies”). UNL provides modules in “Mathematics and statistics” and “Data modelling”. UNL offers different paths within its modules by means of alternative courses, e.g. a student with a background in social sciences such as geography and some previous know-how in informatics would rather choose “Descriptive statistics” and “Data analysis", whereas a more informatics-related student would choose “Mathematical statistics” and “Data mining”. For the second semester, all students attend the courses at UM. The first module covers “Fundamentals in GI Science”. The second module “Advanced topics in GI Science” covers knowledge on ongoing research and research projects, thus preparing the students for their own research in the Master's thesis. Optionally, courses of this module can be replaced by an annual summer school organised by UM, UJI, or UNL, or by work in ongoing research projects of one of the partners’ research groups. The third module mediates additional “Core competences” the students will need for their Master's thesis as well as for their future professional careers: “Research methods in GI Science” and “Project management in GI projects”. As for the third semester (Master's thesis), students can choose one of the three universities, whereas the applicants will be distributed equally to the three partners. If a student did not attend courses of one of the three partner universities before, one of the supervisors or co-supervisors has to be from that university. With the Master's thesis, the candidate shows that she/he is capable to independently handle a defined scientific problem within a defined schedule, and in a way that it is ready to be published. Typically, the Master's thesis will be integrated into an ongoing research project at one of the partners. PDF Download

Description/content.value: Safety and environmental protection are indispensable elements of any industrial activity. In a modern society, technical processes will only be accepted if the emerging hazards are identified and kept under control and if the environmental impact is reduced to an acceptable minimum. To achieve these aims, experts are needed who possess both an in-depth understanding of process engineering and specific knowledge of safety and environmental technologies. The Master's programme in Process Safety and Environmental Engineering aims to educate experts for industry as well as for authorities, research organisations, and higher education. Graduates from the programme are versed in the natural scientific fundamentals of technical processes, especially those related to safety and the environment and think and act holistically in the assessment of safety and environmental concerns and their prevention and mitigation. They are able to apply their engineering know-how to safety and environmental problems and to develop appropriate solutions.

Description/content.value:
The interdisciplinary degree programme Bachelor of Fine Arts encompasses all artistic and scholarly disciplines represented at HFBK Hamburg. Students have access to all areas of specialisation and all workshops.
As part of the Bachelor’s programme, students are free to decide whether they wish to combine different departments or concentrate on a single field. This openness offers a high degree of flexibility and enables the development of an individual artistic and/or scholarly profile.
Description/content.html:
The interdisciplinary degree programme Bachelor of Fine Arts encompasses all artistic and scholarly disciplines represented at HFBK Hamburg. Students have access to all areas of specialisation and all workshops.

As part of the Bachelor’s programme, students are free to decide whether they wish to combine different departments or concentrate on a single field. This openness offers a high degree of flexibility and enables the development of an individual artistic and/or scholarly profile.

Course organisation.value:
In the first two semesters, students receive close guidance that familiarises them with various methods and forms of work and provides an initial orientation for their further studies. Later on, learning and research are shaped by the students’ own artistic projects, and their individual artistic approaches emerge through the interplay of practical and conceptual work. Throughout this process, they receive intensive support from the professors in individual and group discussions. At the same time, the broadly based academic curriculum encourages students to think through their artistic development projects with precision, to deepen them theoretically, to articulate them reflectively, and to present them convincingly. A scholarly focus is also possible.
In the numerous artistic workshops, students can acquire knowledge of materials and fields of application within the various disciplines and develop the necessary craft and technical skills. They learn to create their own works whose experimental character generates aesthetic arguments, statements, and intensities. Students can acquire manual techniques and skills that allow different artistic ideas to be articulated, refined, and further developed. They gain knowledge of art history and theoretical concepts that enable reflection on the status of their own work and inspire as well as intensify artistic productivity.
Students with a scholarly focus additionally learn to formulate theoretical problems, develop arguments, and work out theses or conclusions. The programme also includes the acquisition of skills for presenting one’s own work publicly and showcasing it across different media. The standard period of study is eight semesters and concludes with the Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA).

The promotion of internationality is very important for HFBK Hamburg. This is reflected not only in the high number of international students — almost 50⁠ ⁠% of students have an international background — but also in the numerous exchange programmes, international project collaborations, special international scholarships and regular invitations of artists in residence to the HFBK.

Description/content.value: HFBK Hamburg offers the Master of Fine Arts programme, which focuses on student-driven artistic and/or scholarly development projects. In this programme, research questions, working methods, and creative processes are critically reflected upon, deepened, and refined.
Description/content.html: HFBK Hamburg offers the Master of Fine Arts programme, which focuses on student-driven artistic and/or scholarly development projects. In this programme, research questions, working methods, and creative processes are critically reflected upon, deepened, and refined.

Course organisation.value:
Students are provided with workspaces and receive intensive supervision from faculty through individual and group consultations. The academic curriculum sharpens their critical reflection regarding their own research questions, methods, and processes, while also supporting further research projects. Through exhibition projects and events both within and beyond the university context, students develop a professional approach to presentation formats and distribution methods.
Upon completion of the programme, students present their artistic and/or scholarly work to a broader public, accompanied by documentation in a publication. They deepen and refine their artistic and/or scholarly competencies, creating work whose experimental character generates aesthetic arguments, statements, and intensities. Students learn to purposefully employ technical methods to express, refine, and further develop their artistic ideas.
They acquire extensive art-historical knowledge and theoretical concepts that enable reflection on the status of their own work and serve to inspire and intensify their artistic productivity. Students with a scholarly focus are capable of formulating theoretical problems in a nuanced manner, developing them argumentatively, and deriving theses or conclusions.
The standard period of study is four semesters, culminating in the degree Master of Fine Arts (MFA).

Academic admission requirements.value:
Students are entitled to study the Master’s degree programme in Fine Arts (Master of Fine Arts) at HFBK Hamburg if they can demonstrate an independent artistic position in an entrance examination in accordance with Section 39 (3) of the Hamburg Higher Education Act and have a university degree (including degrees from a university of applied sciences) of 240 ECTS points.
The entrance examination committee decides on the basis of the work submitted whether an independent artistic position exists.
Applicants who do not yet have a university degree at the time of the application deadline, but will obtain one in the six months following the application deadline, may apply and must provide proof of their university degree by the start of the programme at the latest.
Applicants whose university degree comprises fewer than 240 ECTS credits (e.g. 180 ECTS credits in the case of a three-year Bachelor’s degree) are still encouraged to apply and are asked to submit evidence of at least one year of artistic practice, activities in the field of cultural and artistic institutions, internships or previous studies. Outstanding artistic achievements can also be recognised by the admissions committee amounting to 60 ECTS.
Proof of German language skills is not required. However, we strongly recommend that you have knowledge of German in order to be able to take full advantage of the courses on offer (seminars, lectures, group and individual discussions, workshops and more).

Description/content.value:
The Mechanics of Sustainable Materials and Structures Master’s programme is a unique, international, research-oriented, multiple-degree programme. It is offered through joint training activities by the Department of Architecture and Civil Engineering at TU Dortmund University (Germany), the Department of Civil, Environmental, and Mechanical Engineering at the University of Trento (Italy), and the Department of Mechanics, Materials, and Civil Engineering at Ecole Centrale de Nantes (France).
The programme qualifies graduates for research-related and technical professional activities in the areas of:
Advanced Mechanics for Innovative Materials and Structures
Materials and Structures under Extreme Conditions
Materials and Structures in their Environment
The programme also prepares students for PhD studies on advanced research topics related to the mechanics of materials and structures in the field of civil engineering.
With Erasmus Mundus scholarships available, the MS² programme enables students to study in multiple countries while benefiting from an integrated curriculum that combines theory, experimentation, and advanced simulations. Apply now to join a cutting-edge network of students and researchers shaping the future of sustainable structures.
For more information, visit ms2master.com.

Course organisation.value: The Master's degree programme MS² consists of a standard period of study of four semesters (two years). Admission is only possible in the Winter Semester. It requires a high degree of mobility since all students will study in three different countries: Germany, Italy and France. The students of each cohort study at TU Dortmund University in the first semester, at the University of Trento in the second semester and at École Centrale de Nantes in the third semester. The fourth semester is devoted to the Master's thesis work, which takes place either at one of the three universities or at an international partner institution associated with the programme. The following qualifications will be awarded to students that successfully complete all programme requirements: Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Civile (class LM 23) from the University of Trento Master of Science (MSc) from TU Dortmund University Master Sciences, technologies, santé, mention génie civil / Civil engineering from École Centrale de Nantes PDF Download

Academic admission requirements.value:
The admission requirements are set out in the examination regulations §3 of this degree programme. Admission and enrolment are subject to the following requirements: A first-cycle degree qualification according to the European Qualifications Framework, or an equivalent degree in Civil Engineering is required. The equivalence of qualifications must be assessed by the programme’s Admission Board.
The qualifying degree must be completed with an average grade of at least B in the ECTS grading system (corresponding to the top 35% of students), or an equivalent grade of up to 2.8 (“good”) in the German grading system.
English language proficiency is required, demonstrated either by native speaker proficiency or at least level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR).

Description/content.value:
Studying the Master's in Mechanical Engineering provides significant advantages, including access to cutting-edge research facilities and strong industry connections. The programme emphasises practical, hands-on learning, ensuring students gain both theoretical knowledge and the skills needed to excel in today’s competitive marketplace.
Students can specialise in one of three fields or opt for a comprehensive general track:
Mechanical Design and Development: This specialisation focuses on advanced design principles using sophisticated tools like finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to create innovative and sustainable engineering solutions.
Energy and Process Engineering: Concentrates on thermodynamics, heat transfer, and fluid mechanics, emphasising efficient energy conversion systems. The curriculum includes renewable energy technologies and process optimisation to address global energy needs.
Production Engineering: Covers essential manufacturing processes and technologies, focusing on manufacturing systems, automation, and circularity topics. Students learn to integrate circular economy principles, optimising resource use and reducing waste.
The general engineering track offers balanced coursework across core disciplines, providing flexibility for a range of career paths.
For more details on specialisation options and the programme structure, please visit the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering’s website:
https://www.maschinenbau.uni-hannover.de/studium/studiengaenge/maststudiengaenge/mechanical-engineering-english-track

Students can specialise in one of three fields or opt for a comprehensive general track:

  1. Mechanical Design and Development: This specialisation focuses on advanced design principles using sophisticated tools like finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to create innovative and sustainable engineering solutions.

Course organisation.value:
The English Track in the Master's programme in Mechanical Engineering is based on mandatory focus modules that cover key areas of each of the three specialisations "Mechanical Design and Development", "Energy and Process Engineering", and "Production Engineering".
Students can opt for a specialisation by selecting compulsory and elective subjects that match their interests and career goals. The programme also includes a student research project, offering hands-on experience in tackling real mechanical engineering challenges. A pivotal component is an industrial internship lasting at least 12 weeks, where students apply their theoretical knowledge in practical settings, crucial for their career development in preparation for the job market.
For international students, a German language course is mandatory to equip them with basic language skills necessary for daily and professional life. Additionally, an advanced German course can be taken voluntarily as part of the "Studium Generale" module.
The programme concludes with the development and defence of a Master's thesis. The thesis is completed under the guidance of faculty experts, allowing students to delve deeply into a specific area of mechanical engineering.

Description/content.value:
Polymer Materials Science is an interdisciplinary English-language Master's programme in the field of polymer science. You will obtain a multifaceted education in one of the central industrial growth sectors. Nowadays, polymer research is performed as a multidisciplinary collaboration among physicists, chemists, and engineers who are seeking new knowledge on making, characterising, processing, and understanding the molecular basis of novel functional materials. Our course programme is research-oriented and offers a polymer synthetic or a polymer physical specialisation. It thus qualifies you for work in industry as well as advanced training on the PhD level.
Faculty of Natural Sciences II – Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics
Our faculty, with its two Institutes of Chemistry and Physics, is prominently oriented towards research in the broad area of condensed matter and materials science. About one quarter of the 30 chairs and research groups work in the area of macromolecular science and soft matter. Synthetic polymers are the main topic of the Experimental and Theoretical Polymer Physics Groups, the Macromolecular Chemistry Group, the Physical Chemistry of Polymers Group, the Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) Group as well as the Materials Science Group. Several other groups at the Max Planck and Fraunhofer Institutes, as well as at the Centre of Engineering Sciences and the Life Science Faculties, have activities in the polymer field and are actively contributing to the teaching provided within the Master's programme.
Main focus:
General introduction to polymer science
Polymer synthesis and characterisation
Polymer physics
Polymer processing and application
Independent research and industry cooperation
Additional research and studies can be carried out at other institutions in Halle, e.g. the Fraunhofer Institute for Materials Mechanics, the Max Planck Institute for Microstructure Physics, etc. For detailed information, e.g. curriculum, course contents, etc., please visit our website.

Description/content.value: The goal of the university programme is to provide students with a subject-specific education in academic, personal, and social terms. The Master’s programme builds upon the foundational knowledge and specialisations gained in a prior Bachelor’s programme, enabling students to acquire an in-depth academic education in mechanical engineering with a specialisation in materials science. Students are actively involved in research throughout the programme. In addition, through elements such as the internship conducted alongside the programme and the Master’s thesis with colloquium, key competencies – including communication and teamwork skills, presentation and public speaking abilities, and project management – as well as the ability to utilise modern information technologies, are further developed. Within the specialisation modules, students are integrated into engineering research. Through the colloquium at the conclusion of the Master’s thesis, students consolidate their ability to present engineering projects at the Master’s level. The programme prepares students for career paths that require advanced qualifications as mechanical engineers. It aims to train both professionals in leadership roles within the development and research departments of commercial enterprises and the next generation of scientists, as it generally opens the door to pursuing a doctorate in engineering upon completion of the Master’s programme.

The city of Siegen has very moderate costs for accommodation, offering attractive living conditions for students. Living expenses range from only 800 EUR to 1,000 EUR per month, including rent, health insurance, food, clothing, learning materials, phone/Internet, travel expenses, entertainment, and sports. This estimated cost of living can vary depending on lifestyle, type of accommodation, budget, and spending habits.
It is important that students plan and manage their finances throughout the duration of the degree programme to ensure they have enough funds to cover semester contributions and living costs.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value: Students can find part-time jobs with the help of the job placement service of the university. Siegen and the surrounding area are home to a large number of medium-sized industrial enterprises (SMEs), or so-called hidden champions in electrical and mechanical engineering. Some bigger examples include the companies SMS and Achenbach Buschhütten. A lot of smaller, yet very successful and quickly growing high-tech companies are located here as well, for instance, PMD Technologies and Asentics, which are spin-off companies of the university. Therefore, there are employment prospects in the region, particularly for positions that are available during the semester break and following graduation.

Please be aware that German universities do not usually have campus systems like universities in some other countries, where all students can find accommodation directly on the university property. Detailed information concerning general accommodation can be found here.
Early application/search is advisable.

Additionally, the offers of the "Alumniverbund" provide a good opportunity to network and to benefit from the experiences of former students.

Description/content.value:
The LLM programme Comparative and Global Law at the Faculty of Law of the University of Münster is a two-semester programme for students who wish to broaden their legal training with a comparative, internationally-oriented perspective. It is taught in English by the faculty's professors, with an internationally composed student cohort.
Substantively, the programme covers a broad range of comparative-law questions. A first focus area is legal history: how legal institutions change across borders and centuries, and what explanatory power historical analysis holds for understanding the law as it currently stands. A second focus area is constitutional law in a comparative perspective, covering separation of powers, federalism, fundamental rights and constitutional adjudication across continental European, Anglo-American and non-European traditions. A third focus area is business law in a comparative perspective, covering company, contract and commercial law as it arises in German, European and Anglo-American law.
Beyond these three core areas, students can deepen their profile in further fields, including private law (e.g. Roman law and comparative property law), public law (e.g. German public law and common-law constitutional traditions) as well as public international law and human rights (e.g. including human-rights protection in global supply chains). This breadth allows students to sharpen an individual profile, while applying comparative methodology to a field of their own choosing.
This offering is complemented by a continuous focus on independent research competence: critical discussion of current research, the basics of research design and academic writing, and the application of these skills in an independent research project. The programme thus combines a broad substantive selection with a clear methodological common thread: a comparative-law and legal-historical perspective on one hand, and the systematic development of academic research skills on the other.

A second focus area is constitutional law in a comparative perspective, covering separation of powers, federalism, fundamental rights and constitutional adjudication across continental European, Anglo-American and non-European traditions. This breadth allows students to sharpen an individual profile, while applying comparative methodology to a field of their own choosing.

Course organisation.value: The programme is designed as a consecutive two-semester course of study comprising a total of 60 ECTS, divided equally (30 ECTS each) between the first and second semesters. It is organised into three modules: the Foundation Modules (10 ECTS), the Elective Modules (20 ECTS) and the Research Modules (30 ECTS). First semester (30 ECTS): In the first semester, students complete two Foundation Modules (5 ECTS each) and two Elective Modules (5 ECTS each). In parallel, the Research Module already begins with the Colloquium (10 ECTS), in which international guest lecturers present their research and invite students into discussion, giving students their first insights into current research and introducing them to academic discussion. The first semester thus serves both to build the methodological foundation and to make an initial substantive choice, while also introducing students to academic research work. Second semester (30 ECTS): In the second semester, two further Elective Modules follow (5 ECTS each), through which students complete their substantive specialisation. In addition, the Research Module Seminar (5 ECTS) specifically prepares students in the methodology of research work and academic writing. By far the largest share of the second semester is taken up by the Research Module Research Paper — the Master's thesis (15 ECTS), in which students bring together the knowledge and skills acquired throughout the programme in an independent research project. The distribution of modules makes clear that the programme's temporal centre of gravity shifts from the first to the second semester: while the first semester is more strongly characterised by building the methodological and substantive foundation, the second semester increasingly concentrates on independent research work, culminating in the thesis. The Research Module itself, unlike the Foundation and Elective Modules, runs continuously through both semesters and thus forms the structural backbone of the entire course of study.

Academic admission requirements.value:
Applicants must have completed one or more relevant academic degrees with a total duration of at least eight semesters, such as a LLB, a LLM or another professional qualification (e.g. state examination), at a recognised research university. The degree(s) must include a minimum of 240 ECTS credits (or an equivalent).
Typically, applicants will have completed their degree in law. However, students with degrees in other programmes that demonstrate sufficient legal knowledge are welcome to apply as well. If the first degree is not specifically in law, at least 120 of the required 240 ECTS credits must have been earned in that field.
Degrees obtained from universities outside the European Union will be assessed for equivalency.
Applicants who do not fully meet the above criteria, may still be admitted if they have completed a relevant degree programme of at least 180 ECTS and can provide evidence of additional preparatory studies or equivalent credits amounting to 60 ECTS points.

Accommodation.value:
As in all popular university cities in Germany, accommodation is in high demand and not easy to find in Münster – but it's not impossible either! Like most German universities, we do not have our own student halls of residence. However, the "Studierendenwerk", a governmental organisation, offers student halls in Münster. You can find additional information on housing options here and here (only in German).
When contacting about private offers, be careful! Please make sure that you never transfer money before you sign the rental contract. Ideally, you should be able to talk personally to the potential landlord, even if you are still abroad (via phone, video call, etc.) If you are not sure whether an offer is real or possibly a fraud, please feel free to contact the team of our International Office and send us the offer.

Description/content.value:
The Master’s programme in Polymer Technology and Management (MEng) provides students with comprehensive knowledge and skills in the field of polymer materials, plastics processing technologies, and industrial management. The programme combines engineering expertise with management competencies to prepare graduates for leadership positions in the plastics and polymer industry.
The curriculum covers key areas such as polymer materials, plastics processing technologies, simulation and design, quality management, sustainability, and innovative production methods. Students gain in-depth knowledge of the development, processing, and application of polymer-based materials, including practical experience through laboratory courses and industry-oriented projects.
In addition to technical subjects, the programme focuses on business administration, project management, and strategic management to enable students to understand and manage interdisciplinary challenges in modern industrial environments.
A strong practical orientation, close cooperation with industry partners, and application-oriented teaching prepare students to develop innovative solutions for current challenges in the polymer and plastics sector, including resource efficiency, digitalisation, and sustainable materials development.

Course organisation.value:
The Master’s programme Polymer Technology and Management (MEng) is designed as a three-semester full-time programme. The course structure combines theoretical foundations, practical applications, and interdisciplinary management skills.
In the first semester, students acquire advanced knowledge in polymer materials, plastics processing technologies, engineering fundamentals, and management-related subjects. The focus is on building a comprehensive understanding of polymer technology and its industrial applications.
The second semester deepens students’ technical and interdisciplinary competencies through advanced courses, practical laboratory work, project-based learning, and application-oriented seminars. Students work on complex tasks related to polymer development, processing, quality assurance, sustainability, and industrial management.
The third semester is dedicated to the Master’s thesis. Students apply their acquired knowledge to an independent research or industry-related project, often in cooperation with external partners. The thesis enables students to demonstrate their ability to solve complex engineering and management challenges independently.
The programme includes different types of courses, such as lectures, seminars, laboratory courses, exercises, and project work. Lectures provide theoretical knowledge and scientific foundations, while seminars and practical courses promote discussion, application, and problem-solving skills. Laboratory courses and industry-oriented projects enable students to gain hands-on experience with modern polymer technologies and processing methods.
Through the combination of lectures, practical training, and interdisciplinary projects, the programme ensures a strong connection between academic knowledge and professional practice.

Description of other international eleme.value:
The Master’s programme in Polymer Technology and Management (MEng) has an international orientation through its English-language curriculum and its focus on a globally relevant industrial field. Polymer technologies, sustainable materials, and plastics processing are international areas of research and business with strong global connections.
Students work with international technical literature, scientific publications, and current research topics throughout the programme. This enables them to engage with international developments and challenges in the polymer industry.
The programme prepares students for professional activities in internationally operating companies by combining advanced engineering knowledge with management skills. Topics such as sustainability, digitalisation, innovation management, and global industrial trends are addressed from an international perspective.
The programme benefits from close cooperation with industry partners, including companies with international activities. Through practical projects, laboratory work, and application-oriented courses, students gain insights into internationally relevant technologies and industrial requirements.
Depending on available opportunities and individual study planning, students may participate in international exchange activities or study-related stays abroad through the university’s existing international cooperation network.
The international environment is further supported by the use of English as the language of instruction, which enables students from different cultural backgrounds to participate and contributes to intercultural exchange within the programme.

Depending on available opportunities and individual study planning, students may participate in international exchange activities or study-related stays abroad through the university’s existing international cooperation network.

The international environment is further supported by the use of English as the language of instruction, which enables students from different cultural backgrounds to participate and contributes to intercultural exchange within the programme.

Possibility of finding part-time employm.value:
International students in the Master’s programme in Polymer Technology and Management (MEng) have opportunities to find part-time employment alongside their studies.
Possible positions include working student jobs, research assistant positions, or student assistant roles at the university, research institutions, or companies in the region. The availability of part-time employment depends on individual qualifications, language skills, and the current job market. International students must comply with the legal regulations for employment during their studies in Germany.

Course organisation.value:
In the Master's degree programme Mechanical Engineering International, you will deepen your engineering expertise, building on a relevant Bachelor’s degree.
Thanks to a flexible selection of modules rather than fixed specialisations, you can develop your professional profile to suit your individual needs. This allows you to tailor your studies specifically to your personal career goals whilst simultaneously building interdisciplinary expertise.
The programme includes mandatory modules such as Advanced Dynamics, Project Management, Smart Manufacturing Systems, Structural Optimisation, Product Lifecycle Management, Smart Robotics, Structural Health Monitoring and Intercultural Training. The programme is complemented by elective modules, project work or extended project work, and the Master's thesis with a colloquium.
