Description/content.value:
Understand migration, develop solutions, become a changemaker
PATHS Forced Migration: Europe in a Global Context addresses the urgent and complex challenges of forced migration, driven by geopolitical instability, environmental pressures, and socio-economic factors. PATHS Forced Migration provides a unique blend of interdisciplinary and intercultural perspectives within a cohesive curriculum, combining mobility pathways, research opportunities, and close collaboration with local, national, and international organisations. As a PATHS Forced Migration student, you can select one out of three paths: European Border Regimes, Inclusion of Children and Minors, Politics and Policies of Migration. Each path takes place at three different universities. You will also have the opportunity to expand your learning through extracurricular courses offered by ERUA partner universities. Thereby, the European Reform University Alliance (ERUA) paves the way for a new model of European higher education.
In the European Border Regimes path, starting at Viadrina, you will examine how global inequalities as well as ecological and geopolitical instability shape forced migration. You will gain a deep understanding of the legal, technological, and social dimensions of European border regimes, and analyse the interactions between migration policies and global as well as racialised inequalities. The curriculum combines theoretical knowledge, methods training, empirical research, practical internships, and transnational mobility between partner universities in Germany, Poland, and Greece — enabling you to explore border management, refugee reception, and migration policy from local, national, and global perspectives. You will develop the critical skills needed to design ethical, socially just, and evidence-based solutions.
Description/content.html:
Understand migration, develop solutions, become a changemaker

PATHS Forced Migration: Europe in a Global Context addresses the urgent and complex challenges of forced migration, driven by geopolitical instability, environmental pressures, and socio-economic factors. PATHS Forced Migration provides a unique blend of interdisciplinary and intercultural perspectives within a cohesive curriculum, combining mobility pathways, research opportunities, and close collaboration with local, national, and international organisations. As a PATHS Forced Migration student, you can select one out of three paths: European Border Regimes, Inclusion of Children and Minors, Politics and Policies of Migration. Each path takes place at three different universities. You will also have the opportunity to expand your learning through extracurricular courses offered by ERUA partner universities. Thereby, the European Reform University Alliance (ERUA) paves the way for a new model of European higher education. 

In the European Border Regimes path, starting at Viadrina, you will examine how global inequalities as well as ecological and geopolitical instability shape forced migration. You will gain a deep understanding of the legal, technological, and social dimensions of European border regimes, and analyse the interactions between migration policies and global as well as racialised inequalities. The curriculum combines theoretical knowledge, methods training, empirical research, practical internships, and transnational mobility between partner universities in Germany, Poland, and Greece — enabling you to explore border management, refugee reception, and migration policy from local, national, and global perspectives. You will develop the critical skills needed to design ethical, socially just, and evidence-based solutions.

Course organisation.value: The curriculum combines general courses for all students with path-specific courses. The European Border Regimes path follows a structured four-semester curriculum totalling 120 ECTS. You start at the European University Viadrina with two joint introductory courses as well as foundational courses on forced migration and border regimes, equipping you with comprehensive knowledge in areas such as migration control and negotiation, access to protection, and effects of externalisation. For your second semester, you move to SWPS University, where you will deepen your skills in research methods. You will also complete a professional internship at leading organisations such as UNICEF and UNHCR to put your knowledge into practice. The third semester takes place at the University of the Aegean, focusing on refugee reception, border management, and the politics of non-refoulement. In this semester, you take part in a research colloquium designed to prepare you for your Master’s thesis in the fourth semester. All modules combine lectures, seminars, practical exercises, and independent research, ensuring theoretical grounding, methodological competence, and professional experience across multiple European contexts. Description/content.value:
The Master of Science in Psychology & Management is a comprehensive programme that combines psychological principles with business management practices. During three to four semesters, you will be prepared for roles that require expertise in both psychology and business.
In this business psychology degree programme, you will be trained in the main professional fields for business psychologists – psychology, market analysis, consulting and human resources.
In the first semester of the Master's in Business Psychology, you will receive a general and broad education in applied psychology in a business context. In the second semester, you will deepen your expertise in workplace psychology, market and media behaviour, and human resources management, while gaining practical research and industry experience through a hands-on project and an internship. In the third semester, you will gain international exposure via a semester abroad, and in the fourth semester, you will work on your Master’s thesis project.

Description/content.value:
The Master’s programme QIT offers a distinctive interdisciplinary curriculum at the interface of mathematics, computer science, and physics. Its special profile lies in its focus on the mathematical and computational foundations of quantum information, rather than on the physical construction of quantum hardware. In this sense, the programme addresses the theoretical “software side” of quantum technologies. No prior knowledge of quantum physics is required. The relevant concepts are introduced within the programme, allowing students to approach quantum information theory from a mathematical and computational perspective.
The Master’s programme comprises 120 credit points (CP) according to the European Credit Transfer System. Of these, at least 102 CP and at most 106 CP must be completed as graded coursework and examinations. As a rule, students complete 30 CP per semester.
The programme is divided into the following areas:
Quantum Information Theory (40 CP): Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Information Theory, Quantum Algorithms, specialised lectures and a project in QIT
Interdisciplinary Study Area (26–30 CP): lectures in Mathematics, Computer Science and Physics
Master’s Thesis Module (42 CP): Master's thesis in QIT
Elective Modules (8–12 CP): e.g. language courses, tutoring and other modules
The project can be carried out at one of the research groups affiliated with the Center for Quantum Technologies, as well as in collaboration with companies.

Description/content.value:
In our Master's degree programme in Computer Science, you will deepen your knowledge of modern software systems, intelligent applications and data-driven technologies. The programme combines advanced topics in software engineering, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data engineering, enabling you to understand, design and evaluate complex computer science solutions for research and industry.
From software engineering to artificial intelligence, deep learning, big data and data engineering, you will engage with both the theoretical foundations and the practical implementation of current computer science methods. You will learn how to develop reliable and scalable software systems, analyse and process large and heterogeneous data sets, and apply intelligent methods to real-world problems. In this way, you will gain a comprehensive understanding of current technologies and their effective use in demanding application contexts.
A special feature of our programme is the opportunity to specialise in a concentration area. Depending on your interests, you can choose a concentration in Media Informatics or IT Security. In IT Security, you will focus on identifying vulnerabilities, analysing threats and developing suitable technical measures for securing modern software and system environments. In Media Informatics, you will explore novel forms of human-computer interaction, immersive media and user-centred digital experiences. Since the modules in the concentration area can be adapted, the programme remains closely aligned with current technological developments.

Description/content.value:
Our programme consistently focuses on achieving strong environmental sustainability and is shaped by a sense of social responsibility. With a transdisciplinary and holistic approach, we offer you a dynamic learning environment where you can contribute your own ideas.
The Master’s programme has a standard duration of three semesters, each worth 30 ECTS credits. The first two semesters consist of theoretical instruction and practical application in the form of project work. A total of 24 ECTS credits must be earned from the required-elective modules in both the first and second semesters. The third semester is devoted to writing a Master's thesis. This thesis should primarily be completed in collaboration with a partner from industry, business, or research and should prepare students for future professional work or qualify them to pursue a doctoral degree.
Courses in the Programme
Collaboration and the Potential of Teamwork
Sustainability Marketing and Stakeholder
Management in the Food Industry
Psychology and Behavioural Sciences for Sustainable Nutrition
Systemic Management and Transformation
Sustainable Food Production and Resource Use
21st-Century Skills for Food Systems Circular
Economy and Life Cycle Assessment
Strategic Impact Analyses in Food Systems
Sustainable Value Chains and Logistics
Sustainable Corporate Management and Innovative Business Models
Impact Projects
General Elective Modules
Master’s Thesis with Oral Examination
Why study CERES?
Practical and transfer oriented: Apply what you learn directly in case studies and projects and gain valuable practical experience.
Mentoring: Benefit from working with experts from industry and research.
Specialisation and profile: Create a profile for your degree – specialise with a practical or research orientation.
Fast track to a doctorate: A research-oriented Master’s thesis will lay a foundation for doctoral studies.
Interdisciplinary programme: The programme combines management and economics with nutrition, science, and sustainability, opening doors to diverse career opportunities.
Personal supervision: Small groups and direct contact with faculty means beneficial supervision and support.
You will learn to integrate perspectives from economics, science, and society to develop innovative, forward-thinking solutions. The programme also opens up pathways to an academic career, preparing you to become a transdisciplinary researcher. Join us and play an active part in driving change and building a more sustainable future!

Description/content.value:
KLU – ranked among the world's top five percent of business schools (AACSB) – is your launchpad for a future-proof career in any industry you dream of. Our BSc in Business Administration gives you far more than core business skills: you develop KLU's unique operations mindset – critical, data-driven and action-oriented, ideal for the fast-changing, AI-driven economy. You'll study fully in English in small classes with classmates from across the world, enjoying a vibrant campus life that's both fun and full of purpose.
Choose from four specialisations:
Digital Management & Innovation
International Management
Supply Chain Management
Sustainable Management
An integrated internship and semester abroad give you hands-on experience and a global perspective, while KLU's strong employer ties help you move confidently into top Master's programmes or the job market.
Why Study Business Administration at KLU?
Unique Approach to Business: Develop an operations mindset, a unique skill set that will make you stand out from the crowd and give you an advantage in the future business world.
Small Classes, Big Impact: This is your chance for a smooth transition into university. Benefit from a close community, and hands-on innovative learning with the newest technologies, including AI.
Truly International: Our BSc in Business Administration is one of the few in Germany taught 100% in English. With a diverse campus, over 100 destinations for your semester abroad, and our international hub in Saigon, you'll be ready to launch a global career.
Ready for the AI Era: Our programme combines cutting-edge technologies, including AI tools and projects, with an operations mindset and specialisation options, giving you a competitive edge over other graduates.
Future-Proof Career: At KLU, you'll get top-notch career guidance from day one through our Career Skills Course, your integrated internship, and student consulting projects.

Course organisation.value:
Course Organisation
The standard track spans six semesters and 180 ECTS, structured around a strong core in business fundamentals combined with an in-depth specialisation of your choice. In the first two semesters, you build your foundation with core modules such as Fundamentals of Accounting, Statistics, Mathematics for Business & Economics, Marketing, Fundamentals of Management and Strategy, Introduction to Digital Management, Logistics and Supply Chain Management Fundamentals, Human Resource Management, Microeconomics, and Personal Skills, while also beginning your first specialisation modules.
Following an initial break, semesters three and four deepen both your core knowledge — with modules like Corporate Finance, International Business Law, and Macroeconomics — and your chosen specialisation: Digital Management & Innovation, International Management, Supply Chain Management, or Sustainable Management. A mandatory internship, supported by KLU's Career Services team, connects your studies to real industry practice, and your semester abroad at one of KLU's 100+ partner universities lets you complement your studies with courses in areas such as Data Science, Innovation, Leadership, Luxury Management, Psychology, or Sustainability.
You will round off your degree in semesters five and six with further specialisation modules, a Seminar, Personal Skills courses, and finally the Deep Dive Business Challenge — a hands-on consulting-style project tackling a real business problem — together with your Bachelor's thesis, in which you will dive deep into a topic of your choice.

Description of the above-mentioned fundi.value:
At KLU, we believe in educating talented minds regardless of financial background, offering scholarships and tuition financing covering up to 100% of our fees. Our Brain Capital model lets you defer part or all of your tuition until after graduation, with income-based repayments once you've entered the workforce. Multiple loan schemes are also available to cover living expenses.
We offer a limited number of merit-based and need-based scholarships, plus sports scholarships for German and international top-athletes. Students with grants from recognised gifted-education institutions (Begabtenförderwerke) can apply for a full tuition fee waiver, and we proudly support students from refugee communities in Hamburg. Check each scholarship's specific criteria to find your best fit.

Career advisory services and programmes.value:
At KLU, we believe in preparing you for a career with purpose. Our dedicated Career Services help you launch a successful career through a fully integrated curriculum that includes a strategic Career Skills Course, personalised 1:1 career coaching, and industry-focused guest lectures. You'll benefit from exclusive networking events, an active alumni network, and exclusive internship and job offers, plus the chance to showcase yourself in our annual CV book, shared with top employers. All of these services are seamlessly woven into your studies to give you a competitive edge.
KLU's business network includes companies such as Accenture, Airbus, BASF, Beiersdorf, DB Schenker, IBM, Kühne+Nagel, Lufthansa Group, and Siemens.

Description/content.value:
MBA in Leadership & Supply Chain Management
The MBA follows a coherent learning journey designed to support confident and consistent professional growth. It begins with Management Essentials, a foundation covering core disciplines such as strategy and competitive positioning, financial decision-making, customer and market management, and operations and supply chain fundamentals. This phase strengthens analytical thinking across functions, develops a shared management language, and builds a holistic understanding of how organisations create value in international settings.
Building on this foundation, the programme moves into the Transformational Leadership Programme, shifting the focus from managing systems to leading people, organisations, and change. Participants strengthen their leadership capabilities in areas such as change management, ethics and responsible leadership, diversity and inclusion, conflict resolution, and leading teams in international environments.
In parallel, participants deepen their expertise through one of two complementary specialisations: Digital Operations, focusing on intelligent automation, foundations of AI and machine learning, process mining, data strategy, and risk sensing and scenario planning; or Organisational Resilience, focusing on circular supply chains, sustainability hotspots, ESG regulation and compliance, and responsible sourcing.
A central element of the programme is the Impact Project, a real business challenge from the participant's own organisation that runs throughout the MBA, translating classroom insights directly into professional practice. Two integrated international study trips — to destinations such as Universidad de los Andes in Colombia and KLU's campus in Vietnam — provide first-hand exposure to global trade dynamics and emerging markets. The programme concludes with a Master thesis, in which participants apply their acquired knowledge to a specific topic of their choice.

Course organisation.value:
Course Organisation
The part-time MBA runs over 18 months in a monthly block-seminar format: participants attend intensive four-day sessions (Friday to Monday) on KLU's Hamburg campus, allowing them to study alongside their full-time role. The curriculum follows four consecutive phases:
Phase 1 – Management Essentials: Core disciplines such as strategy and competitive positioning, financial decision-making, customer and market management, and operations and supply chain fundamentals.
Phase 2 – Transformational Leadership Programme: A shift from managing systems to leading people, organisations, and change, covering topics such as change management, ethics and responsible leadership, diversity and inclusion, and conflict resolution.
Phase 3 – Specialisation: Participants choose one of two paths — Digital Operations or Organisational Resilience — and deepen their expertise through targeted modules, practical applications, and two integrated international study trips to destinations such as Colombia and Vietnam.
Phase 4 – Master's Thesis: Participants dive deep into a specific topic of their choice, supported by faculty guidance, applying everything they've learned throughout the programme.

Description of the above-mentioned fundi.value:
KLU offers several ways to finance the MBA. The Brain Capital model lets you defer part or all of your tuition until after graduation, repaying based on your income once you're back in the workforce. Many participants are also supported by their employer through sponsorship or a learning budget.
We offer a limited number of scholarships: Logistics Excellence (50%, for AGA/BVL/LIHH members), Women in Logistics Leadership (50%), Social Impact & Sustainability (75%, for NGO/social enterprise experience), Digitalisation & AI (50%), and Global Supply Chain Future Leaders (25%). Scholarships require prior programme acceptance; early applications improve your chances. Tuition is also reduced by up to 15% for early applications, tiered by deadline.

Description/content.value:
The study programme Robotics and Machine Intelligence prepares graduates for careers in fields where engineering, software and intelligence come together. Graduates can work on robotic systems, automation solutions, multi-axis production machines, embedded software, autonomous devices, sensor-based applications and intelligent technical systems.
The programme is particularly relevant for students who want to work close to real technology. Its combination of software development, robotics, AI and engineering fundamentals prepares graduates for roles that require not only programming skills, but also a deep understanding of technical systems and their physical environment.
Description/content.html:
The study programme Robotics and Machine Intelligence prepares graduates for careers in fields where engineering, software and intelligence come together. Graduates can work on robotic systems, automation solutions, multi-axis production machines, embedded software, autonomous devices, sensor-based applications and intelligent technical systems.

The programme is particularly relevant for students who want to work close to real technology. Its combination of software development, robotics, AI and engineering fundamentals prepares graduates for roles that require not only programming skills, but also a deep understanding of technical systems and their physical environment.

Course organisation.value:
The curriculum is designed as a step-by-step pathway into modern robotics. In the first study phase, students build essential knowledge in informatics, mathematics, and engineering basics. These foundations are important for understanding robotic systems not only as software applications, but as real technical systems with sensors, actuators, control mechanisms and physical behaviour. In parallel, German language courses and Technical German are integrated into the curriculum.
In the next phase, the focus shifts towards programming, artificial intelligence, robotics, sensor technology, software engineering, simulation and autonomous systems. Students learn how to connect computational methods with engineering applications and how to develop software for machines that interact with the real world.
The later semesters include an internship semester, advanced robotics and AI topics, technical electives and the Bachelor’s thesis. This allows students to apply their knowledge in practical contexts and to develop an individual profile in fields such as embedded AI, autonomous systems, industrial robotics or sensitive and medical robotics.

Description/content.value: The Master’s programme in "Life Science (MSc)" provides advanced knowledge of the organisation and pathways of life at the molecular and cellular level in both molecular-biomedical ("Molecular and Biomedical Life Science") and environmentally relevant ("Environmental Life Science") contexts. The curriculum places a particular emphasis on (bio)analytical methods and experimental training, enabling students to investigate complex biological processes and systems using modern analytical and quantitative approaches. The programme is designed for graduates of Bachelor’s programmes with a strong interest in research-oriented topics at the interface of chemistry and biology.
Description/content.html: The Master’s programme in "Life Science (MSc)" provides advanced knowledge of the organisation and pathways of life at the molecular and cellular level in both molecular-biomedical ("Molecular and Biomedical Life Science") and environmentally relevant ("Environmental Life Science") contexts. The curriculum places a particular emphasis on (bio)analytical methods and experimental training, enabling students to investigate complex biological processes and systems using modern analytical and quantitative approaches. The programme is designed for graduates of Bachelor’s programmes with a strong interest in research-oriented topics at the interface of chemistry and biology.

Course organisation.value: The Master's programme in "Life Science (MSc)" comprises four semesters of full-time study during which participants are required to obtain a total of 120 ECTS. Ultimately, a total of 300 ECTS are required for the award of the MSc degree. Compulsory courses are organised into two main categories: "Molecular and Biomedical Life Science" and "Environmental Life Science" (60 ECTS). Elective modules (15 ECTS) offer students the opportunity to deepen their knowledge in line with their individual interests. The practical phase emphasises research-oriented learning and consists of a research project (15 ECTS) as well as the Master‘s thesis including a final oral exam (30 ECTS). During these phases, students conduct an independent research project and gain practical experience in scientific investigation and data analysis.

Academic admission requirements.value:
To be enrolled in the Master's programme "Life Science”, students must have graduated from any study programme in the subjects chemistry, biology, biochemistry, or biotechnology, in which the following content was included:
a. Basics and applications of general and inorganic chemistry
b. Substance classes and reaction mechanisms of organic chemistry
c. Basics of biodiversity, taxonomy and phylogeny, microbiology and ecotoxicology
The graduation grade of the respective Bachelor's programme must be 2.5 or better. In addition, there should be basic experience concerning practical work in the organic or biochemistry lab of 10 ECTS.
Exceptions from the above prerequisites are to be decided by the board of examinations upon an application of the student. Exceptions might be a grade in the Bachelor's thesis of 1.5 or better or at least one year of professional working experience in chemistry, biochemistry or biotechnology.

Description/content.value:
The Master of Science (MSc) degree in Architecture at the University of Kassel is an intensive professional academic programme. The course of study allows for interdisciplinary skill-building within the Architecture, the Urban Planning and the Landscape Architecture programmes (ASL). The academic programme culminates with a supervised independent Master's thesis project that allows each participant to frame problems relevant to their specific focus.
The programme consists of two years of study, including three design studios, required coursework, and electives, with an emphasis on extending foundational professional knowledge. The degree is awarded upon successful completion of the required courses and the public presentation of a Master’s thesis project demonstrating the candidate’s ability to develop conceptual and practical design skills through an independent project.
All candidates choose one specialised field of study. The available fields taught in English are Design Research and Architecture Cities Economies (Construction Management / Project Development).
Design Research:
This field of study strengthens design competence as well as analytical skills and supports independent working methods to develop innovative spatial solutions to complex architectural tasks, with particular attention to resource and climate-aware spaces, structures, and programmes.
Architecture Cities Economies (Construction Management / Project Development):
This field of study combines planning and design strategies with high design standards and a focus on political economy, aiming towards a socio-ecological transformation in building economy and project development. The central research objectives is to reach a profound understanding of economic interrelationships in the construction industry between land policy, ownership structures, material logistics and built structures, as well as resource use and planning instruments.

Description/content.value:
The MA Inclusion Studies combines Educational Science, Social Sciences and Sociology, as well as Psychology and Social Work with a clear international perspective on inclusive education. The degree programme offers academic depth and strong practical relevance. Alongside theories of inclusion and methods of empirical social research, inclusion is examined from a comparative perspective as a key challenge facing European societies and education systems, and this is complemented by insights into professional practice within inclusive organisations and fields of activity.
The programme is designed as a multiple degree: Graduates will receive three separate degrees at once.
The programmes takes place across three locations at European partner universities:
Ostrava in Czechia (first semester, starting with a joint summer school)
Bielefeld in Germany (second semester)
Suceava in Romania (third semester)
All students in a year group complete the relevant semester together on site at each location; the Master’s thesis is written in the fourth semester with a free choice of location.
This MA is international and interdisciplinary in nature. At each of the three locations, the Faculty of Educational Sciences provides the core framework. At the partner university in Ostrava, the Faculty of Social Sciences and the Department of Sociology within the Faculty of Arts are also involved.
Career prospects
The programme provides foundational skills in project and team leadership, consultancy, and strategic concept development. Graduates of the programme are trained as experts in inclusion, equipped with advanced theoretical, conceptual, and methodological skills as well as international experience.
Possible career paths include:
EU-level coordinator
project manager
consultant
NGO staff member
conceptual expert
researcher
education policy specialist
ethics lobbyist

Course organisation.value:
Within the first semester, the foundations cover methodology:
Theories and methodologies in the context of inclusion and exclusion 1: The courses "Thinking Inclusion/Exclusion" and "Doing Inclusion" explore the topic through theoretical frameworks and practical applications in labour market integration, health, and gender.
Inclusion and exclusion in societies 1: "Inclusion in the Context of Social Work" and "Inclusion in Housing and Disadvantaged Neighbourhoods" emphasise social work and housing, focusing on preventing social exclusion through diversity theories and systemic barriers.
Practices of inclusion 1: The courses "Inclusive Education in Schools and Society" and "Inclusive Education: Ethics, Policy and Research" address social inequalities and supportive classroom strategies while promoting personal growth and critical reflection on pedagogy and policy.
Within the second semester, the focus is on actors, dynamics and comparatistics:
Theories and methodologies in the context of inclusion and exclusion 2: Systematic and methodological reflections​ within the courses "Structures, Institutions and Actors in Inclusive Education" and "Dynamics of Inclusion and Exclusion"
Inclusion and exclusion in societies 2: Focusses on (re-)negotiating inclusive education in changing societies within the courses "Inclusion and Exclusion in Childhood and Youth" and "Citizenship Education: Challenges for Inclusive Societies"
Practices of inclusion​ 2: Contains two courses "Comparative Practices of Inclusive Education in the Educational System" and "Practices of Inclusive Education at the Intersection of Educational Actors, Institutions and Other Support Services"
Within the third semester, a psychological and technical perspective is taken with a strong practical focus:
Promoting well-being in inclusive contexts​: Looks at the aspects "Emotional Education and Well-being Promotion in Inclusive Contexts", "Promoting Resilience through Education​" and "Positive Psychology and Education"
Skills and tools for inclusion and interculturality: Contains the "Emotional Education and Well-being Promotion in Inclusive Contexts​" and "Applying Technology into Inclusive Education" as well as elective study contents
Fourth semester: Master's thesis

Description/content.value:
The Master’s programme “AI and Digital Technology in Learning and Instruction”, situated at the intersection of computer science and educational psychology, systematically prepares students for the scientific analysis, design, and evaluation of AI-based and digital technologies in educational processes.
The programme is designed as a consecutive and interdisciplinary degree and is aimed at graduates holding either a BSc in Psychology or a BSc in Computer Science. In addition to introductory modules, students in the first year acquire targeted foundational knowledge of the respective other discipline through advanced modules. Building on this foundation, joint specialisation modules further develop the core competencies required for AI-supported educational processes. A practical module also provides insights into potential future career fields.
Over the course of the programme, students acquire in-depth subject knowledge, methodological expertise, and practice-oriented skills for qualified professional activities in the field of AI and digital education. They will be able to develop and evaluate AI-supported learning systems, analyse and optimise educational processes based on data, and advise organisations on the strategic implementation of educational technologies, for example in educational administration or in the EdTech sector.

Description/content.value:
The Master's in International Law, Politics and Economics (LLM) covers six modules over two semesters and consistently combines in-depth legal study with political, economic and practical perspectives. Throughout the programme, you will work on real-world cases where legal, political and economic interests intersect, and learn to analyse and contextualise international decisions from different perspectives. You will study in Berlin — a hub of political and international activity where ministries, embassies, think tanks, associations and NGOs operate in close proximity to one another. This opens up a wide range of opportunities for professional exchange, networking and gaining insights into potential international career paths. Three core modules provide the academic foundations. Building on these, you will choose five specialisation modules and four skills modules, thereby setting your own individual focus. You will deepen your knowledge in areas such as negotiation, crisis management and leadership, and learn to translate complex analyses into clear recommendations for action. At the end of the programme, you will explore a topic of your own choosing in depth in your Master’s thesis.

Description/content.html:
The Master's in International Law, Politics and Economics (LLM) covers six modules over two semesters and consistently combines in-depth legal study with political, economic and practical perspectives. Throughout the programme, you will work on real-world cases where legal, political and economic interests intersect, and learn to analyse and contextualise international decisions from different perspectives. You will study in Berlin — a hub of political and international activity where ministries, embassies, think tanks, associations and NGOs operate in close proximity to one another. This opens up a wide range of opportunities for professional exchange, networking and gaining insights into potential international career paths. Three core modules provide the academic foundations. Building on these, you will choose five specialisation modules and four skills modules, thereby setting your own individual focus. You will deepen your knowledge in areas such as negotiation, crisis management and leadership, and learn to translate complex analyses into clear recommendations for action. At the end of the programme, you will explore a topic of your own choosing in depth in your Master’s thesis.

Core Modules

  • Advanced International Politics
  • Advanced International & EU Law
  • Advanced International Economics

Specialisation

  • Multipolar Security
  • Human Rights & Democratic Regression
  • Trade Wars
  • LPE of International Crime
  • Regulating Critical Raw Materials
  • LPE of Energy/Sanctions and Export Controls
  • China and the EU/EU external relations
  • Law and the Digital Economy
  • Demography & Migration
  • LPE of Cyberwar and Arms Trade

Skill Modules

  • Onboarding & Academic Skills
  • Project Management
  • Policy Entrepreneurship
  • AI & Complexity Thinking — Internationale Wirtschaftspolitik
  • Policy Strategy & Diplomacy
  • Crisis Management
  • Leadership

Course organisation.value:
The programme is structured around six blocks spread over two semesters. Thanks to a wide range of optional modules, you can tailor the programme to your individual interests. In total, you will choose five specialisation modules and four skills modules during the course. In addition, there are three core modules and your thesis.
You will work on cases in which legal, political and economic interests converge. Guest lectures, fireside chats and practical projects will connect you with experts from diplomacy, ministries, international organisations, law firms and consultancies.
You will develop skills in negotiation, crisis management and leadership and learn to translate complex analyses into persuasive recommendations. This will enable you not only to assess international decisions from a legal perspective, but also to understand how they arise, evaluate their consequences and develop viable solutions. Learn more...

Academic admission requirements.value:
Begin your application by submitting the following documents:
A university degree in law with at least 240 ECTS
At least 30 ECTS must have been completed in core law subjects
Proof of English language proficiency
If your application documents meet our admission requirements, we will invite you to an individual interview. During this interview, we will assess your motivation and social skills. The decisive factors are your motivation to perform and learn, your social communication profile, your willingness to take on social responsibility and your initiative.

Career advisory services and programmes.value:
The Career Services Center of the EBS is at the interface between the university, its students and the business world. We support you when you take your first successful steps into the working world through professional preparation, individual consultation, and many opportunities to engage with our comprehensive network.
When it was founded in 1971, the EBS was Germany's first private, state-recognised business school. We have a closely interwoven and successful worldwide alumni network, and our contacts in the business world are diverse and numerous. The mission of EBS is to empower you to use this great network to shape your career success.
